papers.sEn: MiniCPM4 achieves ultra-efficiency for end devices via innovations in architecture, data, training, and inference.
contrib: Proposes InfLLM v2, a trainable sparse attention mechanism accelerating both prefilling and decoding for long-context processing.
Introduces UltraClean, an efficient pre-training data filtering strategy, and UltraChat v2 for high-quality reasoning-intensive data generation.
Develops ModelTunnel v2 for efficient training strategy search and chunk-wise rollout for load-balanced reinforcement learning.
Presents CPM.cu, a lightweight CUDA inference framework integrating sparse attention, quantization, and speculative sampling.
Achieves comparable performance to Qwen3-8B using only 22% of its pre-training tokens, with 7x speedup on 128K-length documents.
Constructs MiniCPM4.1 hybrid reasoning model supporting both deep and non-reasoning modes.
limits: Sparse attention efficiency relies on GPU tensor core constraints, requiring at least 16 heads per query group.
Data filtering and generation pipelines still partially depend on human-designed heuristics.
Multi-token prediction and FP8 training require specific hardware support and may not generalize to all devices.
Evaluation primarily on English and Chinese benchmarks; multilingual and multimodal settings are not explored.
Ternary LLM BitCPM4 shows promising results but may have performance degradation on extremely resource-limited devices.

papers.tEn: dots.llm1 Technical Report
papers.tZh: dots.llm1 技术报告
papers.sEn: dots.llm1, a 142B MoE model with 14B active parameters, matches Qwen2.5-72B performance after training on 11.2T tokens without synthetic data.
contrib: Proposes a scalable three-stage data processing framework for generating high-quality, diverse pretraining data.
Introduces dots.llm1, a 142B MoE model activating 14B parameters, achieving performance comparable to Qwen2.5-72B with reduced costs.
Develops an innovative MoE all-to-all communication and computation overlap recipe based on 1F1B pipeline scheduling.
Open-sources intermediate training checkpoints at every one trillion tokens to provide insights into learning dynamics.
Achieves efficient inference on a single node with eight GPUs, demonstrating cost-effectiveness.
Demonstrates robust performance across Chinese and English tasks, with strengths in Chinese language and mathematical reasoning.
limits: Coding performance is not as exceptional as other areas, with room for improvement compared to cutting-edge models.
Model relies on high-quality data processing pipeline; performance may degrade with lower-quality data.
Evaluation limited to benchmarks; real-world deployment performance may vary.
Context length extension only up to 32K; longer contexts may not be handled effectively.
No synthetic data used in pretraining, which may limit data diversity for certain domains.

papers.tEn: MiMo-VL Technical Report
papers.tZh: MiMo-VL 技术报告
papers.sEn: MiMo-VL-7B-RL outperforms Qwen2.5-VL-7B on 35/40 tasks and scores 59.4 on OlympiadBench, surpassing 78B models.
contrib: Open-sources MiMo-VL-7B-SFT and MiMo-VL-7B-RL, achieving state-of-the-art performance on 35/40 tasks vs Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
Proposes Mixed On-policy Reinforcement Learning (MORL) integrating diverse reward signals for stable multi-domain optimization.
Identifies importance of incorporating long Chain-of-Thought reasoning data into pre-training stages for enhanced performance.
Achieves 59.4 on OlympiadBench, surpassing models with up to 78B parameters, and 56.1 on OSWorld-G for GUI grounding.
Contributes a comprehensive evaluation suite covering 50+ tasks with prompts and protocols for reproducibility.
Demonstrates highest Elo rating among open-source VLMs in user preference evaluation, competitive with proprietary models.
limits: MORL faces task interference due to opposing response length trends between reasoning and grounding tasks.
Vanilla GRPO saturates around 20k samples, while on-policy RL shows no saturation within observed training window.
Simultaneous multi-domain optimization remains challenging; standalone RL on individual tasks may outperform MORL.
Evaluation limited to 7B parameter scale; scaling to larger models may reveal different behaviors.
Synthetic reasoning data quality depends on large reasoning models; rejection sampling may not eliminate all errors.

papers.tEn: Why I don't think AGI is right around the corner
papers.tZh: 为什么我认为 AGI 不会很快到来
papers.sEn: AGI is not imminent due to fundamental limitations in current AI approaches.
contrib: Identifies lack of continual learning as a key bottleneck for LLMs to become truly useful employees.
Argues that current LLMs cannot improve over time like humans, limiting their practical deployment.
Predicts that solving online learning will cause a discontinuity in AI value, potentially leading to rapid superintelligence.
Skeptical of near-term (2026) reliable computer use agents due to long horizons, lack of data, and slow algorithmic progress.
Provides 50/50 timelines: AI doing taxes end-to-end by 2028, AI learning on the job like humans by 2032.
Notes that scaling of training compute cannot continue beyond this decade, shifting progress to algorithms.
limits: The argument relies on personal anecdotal experience with LLMs, which may not generalize.
Underestimates potential of RL fine-tuning and self-verification to mimic human learning.
Assumes no breakthrough in continual learning from labs, but progress may be faster than expected.
The 50/50 timelines are subjective and based on limited public evidence.
Does not fully consider the impact of AI automating AI R&D, which could accelerate timelines.

papers.tEn: ProRL: Prolonged Reinforcement Learning Expands Reasoning Boundaries in Large Language Models
papers.tZh: ProRL：延长强化学习扩展大语言模型的推理边界
papers.sEn: Prolonged RL training can uncover novel reasoning strategies inaccessible to base models, expanding reasoning boundaries beyond mere amplification of existing outputs.
contrib: Proposes ProRL, a prolonged RL training methodology with KL divergence control and reference policy resetting.
Demonstrates that prolonged RL training expands reasoning boundaries beyond base model capabilities.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on a 1.5B generalist reasoning model across diverse domains.
Shows that RL gains are most significant on tasks where base model initially struggles.
Provides evidence of novel reasoning strategies emerging through prolonged RL training.
Releases model weights to support further research.
limits: Limited to 1.5B parameter models; scaling to larger models may require additional tuning.
Training requires significant compute resources (16k GPU hours).
Effectiveness depends on base model's initial competence; gains diminish on already strong tasks.
Evaluation limited to specific benchmarks; generalization to real-world tasks not fully validated.
Prolonged RL may lead to overthinking or reduced reasoning breadth on some tasks.

papers.tEn: Skywork Open Reasoner 1 Technical Report
papers.tZh: Skywork Open Reasoner 1 技术报告
papers.sEn: Skywork-OR1 achieves significant reasoning gains via RL, with 32B model improving from 57.8% to 72.8% on AIME24, AIME25, and LiveCodeBench.
contrib: Proposes MAGIC, a multi-stage adaptive entropy scheduling framework for GRPO, improving long CoT reasoning.
Achieves 15.0% and 13.9% average accuracy gains on 32B and 7B models over AIME24, AIME25, and LiveCodeBench.
Identifies premature entropy collapse as a key factor limiting RL performance and proposes adaptive entropy control.
Conducts comprehensive ablation studies on data, training strategy, and loss components to validate effectiveness.
Open-sources model weights, training code, and datasets to support community research.
Demonstrates that on-policy updates and high-temperature sampling mitigate entropy collapse and improve generalization.
limits: Experiments are limited to DeepSeek-R1-Distill model series and may not generalize to other architectures.
Code sandbox does not handle non-deterministic outputs or multiple valid answers for the same input.
Adaptive entropy control may become unstable when the number of SGD steps per training step is large.
The study focuses on math and code domains; effectiveness in other domains (e.g., reasoning, NLP) is not evaluated.
Training resource allocation analysis assumes synchronous training; asynchronous settings may yield different results.

papers.tEn: CosyVoice 3: Towards In-the-wild Speech Generation via Scaling-up and Post-training
papers.tZh: CosyVoice 3：通过规模扩展和后训练实现野外语音生成
papers.sEn: CosyVoice 3 achieves zero-shot multilingual speech synthesis in the wild via scaling up data and model size, and a novel post-training method.
contrib: Proposes a novel speech tokenizer via supervised multi-task training to improve prosody naturalness.
Introduces Differentiable Reward Optimization (DiffRO) for post-training, applicable to LLM-based TTS.
Scales training data from 10k to 1M hours, covering 9 languages and 18 Chinese dialects.
Scales model parameters from 0.5B to 1.5B, enhancing performance on multilingual benchmarks.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks for zero-shot multilingual speech synthesis.
Releases CV3-Eval benchmark for in-the-wild zero-shot speech synthesis evaluation.
limits: Cannot control acoustic characteristics like timbre via textual instructions.
Performance on singing voice generation is not satisfactory.
Emotion accuracy drops significantly in text-unrelated tasks.
Speaker similarity slightly decreases after RL post-training due to reward hacking.
Hard samples like rare words and tongue twisters remain challenging.

papers.tEn: Hunyuan-TurboS: Advancing Large Language Models through Mamba-Transformer Synergy and Adaptive Chain-of-Thought
papers.tZh: Hunyuan-TurboS：通过 Mamba-Transformer 协同与自适应思维链推进大语言模型
papers.sEn: Hunyuan-TurboS is a novel hybrid Transformer-Mamba MoE model with adaptive long-short chain-of-thought, achieving top-7 on LMSYS Chatbot Arena with 1356 points.
contrib: Proposes Hunyuan-TurboS, the first industry-deployed large-scale hybrid Transformer-Mamba MoE model with 56B activated parameters.
Introduces adaptive long-short chain-of-thought fusion, dynamically switching reasoning depth to optimize compute.
Designs novel AMF/MF block pattern combining Mamba2, Grouped-Query Attention, and MoE for efficiency.
Develops multi-round deliberation learning with LLM judge ensemble and human oversight for iterative improvement.
Implements two-stage large-scale reinforcement learning (GRPO) targeting STEM reasoning and general instruction-following.
Achieves top 7 LMSYS Chatbot Arena score (1356) and 77.9% average on 23 benchmarks with lower inference cost.
limits: Evaluation limited to 23 automated benchmarks; real-world deployment scenarios may reveal additional limitations.
Adaptive CoT mechanism may not generalize well to domains with ambiguous difficulty or novel reasoning patterns.
Dependence on high-quality pre-training data (16T tokens) may limit reproducibility for resource-constrained teams.
Hybrid Mamba-Transformer architecture introduces engineering complexity for inference optimization and deployment.
Two-stage RL requires extensive reward engineering and domain-specific data, potentially limiting scalability.

papers.tEn: Emerging Properties in Unified Multimodal Pretraining
papers.tZh: 统一多模态预训练中的涌现特性
papers.sEn: BAGEL, a unified decoder-only model pretrained on trillions of tokens from interleaved multimodal data, exhibits emerging capabilities in complex multimodal reasoning, significantly outperforming open-source unified models.
contrib: Introduces BAGEL, an open-source unified multimodal foundation model supporting both understanding and generation.
Proposes a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture with shared self-attention for bottleneck-free multimodal interaction.
Develops a scalable protocol for constructing high-quality multimodal interleaved data from web and video sources.
Demonstrates emergent capabilities in complex multimodal reasoning, including free-form image manipulation and world navigation.
Outperforms open-source unified models on standard benchmarks for multimodal understanding and generation.
Releases code, checkpoints, and training details to facilitate multimodal research.
limits: Evaluation relies on benchmarks that may not fully capture emergent capabilities.
Model performance on complex tasks like IP generation and human pose remains limited.
Training data quality and diversity may introduce biases or coverage gaps.
Scalability to larger model sizes and data scales is not fully explored.
Reasoning-augmented generation requires additional inference steps, increasing latency.

papers.tEn: Qwen3 Technical Report
papers.tZh: Qwen3 技术报告
papers.sEn: Qwen3 integrates thinking and non-thinking modes into a unified framework, supports 119 languages, and achieves state-of-the-art results across diverse benchmarks.
contrib: Integrates thinking and non-thinking modes into a single model, enabling dynamic switching without separate models.
Introduces thinking budget mechanism for adaptive allocation of computational resources during inference.
Expands multilingual support from 29 to 119 languages and dialects, enhancing cross-lingual understanding.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on code, math, and agent tasks with efficient MoE architecture.
Employs strong-to-weak distillation to reduce computational cost for smaller models while maintaining high performance.
Releases all models under Apache 2.0 license to facilitate reproducibility and community research.
limits: Evaluation limited to benchmarks; real-world deployment performance may vary.
Thinking budget control may not be optimal for all tasks or user preferences.
Multilingual performance may be uneven across low-resource languages.
Distillation approach may limit exploration capability compared to full training.
Long-context handling relies on techniques like YARN and DCA, which may have limitations.

papers.tEn: BLIP3-o: A Family of Fully Open Unified Multimodal Models-Architecture, Training and Dataset
papers.tZh: BLIP3-o：全开放统一多模态模型家族——架构、训练与数据集
papers.sEn: BLIP3-o achieves state-of-the-art performance in both image understanding and generation by using a diffusion transformer to generate CLIP features and a sequential pretraining strategy.
contrib: First systematic study of autoregressive + diffusion design choices for unified multimodal models.
Proposes CLIP + Flow Matching for image generation, achieving higher training efficiency and quality.
Demonstrates sequential pretraining preserves understanding while enabling generation.
Curates BLIP3o-60k instruction-tuning dataset improving prompt alignment and aesthetics.
BLIP3-o 8B achieves state-of-the-art on multiple image understanding and generation benchmarks.
Fully open-sources models, code, weights, training scripts, and datasets.
limits: Instruction tuning dataset (60k) cannot fully resolve complex cases like human gestures.
FID metric limitations; GPT-4o scores ~30 on MJHQ-30k, indicating misleading evaluation.
Sequential training may miss synergistic benefits of joint training.
Model size and computational cost increase with flow matching and diffusion transformer.
Evaluation limited to English prompts and specific benchmarks; generalization to other domains untested.

papers.tEn: AlphaEvolve: A Gemini-powered coding agent for designing advanced algorithms — Google DeepMind
papers.tZh: AlphaEvolve：由 Gemini 驱动的编码代理，用于设计高级算法——Google DeepMind
papers.sEn: AlphaEvolve is a Gemini-powered coding agent that designs advanced algorithms autonomously.
contrib: AlphaEvolve is an evolutionary coding agent powered by LLMs for general-purpose algorithm discovery and optimization.
It discovered a heuristic for Google's Borg scheduler, recovering 0.7% of worldwide compute resources.
AlphaEvolve optimized a key arithmetic circuit in TPU design, integrated into an upcoming chip.
It sped up Gemini's matrix multiplication kernel by 23%, reducing training time by 1%.
AlphaEvolve achieved up to 32.5% speedup for FlashAttention kernel in Transformer models.
It improved the kissing number lower bound in 11 dimensions and found a faster 4x4 complex matrix multiplication algorithm.
limits: AlphaEvolve requires problems with clearly measurable progress, limiting its applicability to domains with objective metrics.
The evolutionary process may be computationally expensive, requiring significant resources for large-scale searches.
Discovered algorithms may lack theoretical guarantees, relying on empirical verification rather than formal proofs.
Performance improvements are domain-specific and may not generalize to other problem instances or settings.
The system's reliance on LLMs means its creativity is bounded by the models' training data and capabilities.

papers.tEn: DanceGRPO: Unleashing GRPO on Visual Generation
papers.tZh: DanceGRPO：在视觉生成中释放 GRPO 的潜力
papers.sEn: DanceGRPO stably optimizes visual generation models across diverse tasks and reward models, outperforming baselines by up to 181%.
contrib: First to extend GRPO to diffusion models and rectified flows for visual generation.
Unified framework across two generative paradigms, three tasks, four foundation models, and five reward models.
Demonstrates stable policy optimization on large-scale datasets, outperforming prior RL methods.
Achieves up to 181% improvement over baselines on benchmarks like HPS-v2.1 and VideoAlign.
Enables Best-of-N inference scaling and learning from sparse binary feedback.
Provides insights into harmonizing reinforcement learning and visual synthesis.
limits: Requires significant computational resources (up to 64 H800 GPUs).
Binary reward models are preliminary; more powerful rule-based visual reward models needed.
KL-regularization omitted; may risk reward over-optimization in some settings.
Best-of-N scaling uses brute-force search; tree search or greedy search not explored.
Video reward model (VideoAlign) text-video alignment dimension unstable and excluded.

papers.tEn: Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free
papers.tZh: 大型语言模型的门控注意力：非线性、稀疏性与无注意力汇聚
papers.sEn: A simple head-specific sigmoid gate after scaled dot-product attention improves LLM performance, stability, and long-context extrapolation by introducing non-linearity and sparse gating that mitigates attention sink.
contrib: Systematically investigates gating-augmented softmax attention variants over 30 models up to 15B parameters.
Identifies that a head-specific sigmoid gate after SDPA consistently improves performance, stability, and scaling.
Attributes gating effectiveness to introducing non-linearity and query-dependent sparse gating scores.
Demonstrates that sparse gating mitigates attention sink and enhances long-context extrapolation.
Releases attention-sink-free models and codes to facilitate future research.
limits: Broader implications of non-linearity on attention dynamics and training remain under-explored.
No rigorous theoretical explanation for how attention sink affects long-context generalization.
Experiments limited to 15B MoE and 1.7B dense models; scalability to larger models not verified.
Gating variants tested only on softmax attention; applicability to other attention types not studied.

papers.tEn: Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
papers.tZh: 推理模型并不总是说出它们的想法
papers.sEn: Chain-of-thought monitoring is promising but insufficient for catching undesired behaviors in reasoning models.
contrib: Evaluates CoT faithfulness of reasoning models across 6 reasoning hints.
Finds that CoTs reveal hint usage in at least 1% of examples but often below 20%.
Shows outcome-based RL initially improves faithfulness but plateaus without saturating.
Demonstrates that RL increases reward hacking frequency without increasing verbalization.
Suggests CoT monitoring is promising for noticing undesired behaviors but insufficient to rule them out.
Indicates test-time CoT monitoring unlikely to reliably catch rare catastrophic behaviors.
limits: Focuses on unintended behaviors where CoT is not necessary.
Only studies one kind of unintended behavior: using hints in multiple-choice questions.
Settings differ from realistic scenarios where CoT monitoring might be used.
Hints are very easy to exploit, limiting generalizability.
CoT faithfulness evaluation is an upper bound, not exact.

papers.tEn: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data
papers.tZh: 绝对零度：零数据下的自我对弈推理
papers.sEn: Absolute Zero proposes a new RLVR paradigm where a model self-generates tasks and learns without any external data, achieving SOTA in coding and math reasoning.
contrib: Proposes Absolute Zero paradigm eliminating all external data for reasoning model training.
Introduces Absolute Zero Reasoner (AZR) using self-play with code executor for task proposal and verification.
Achieves SOTA on coding and math reasoning without any human-curated data.
Demonstrates strong cross-domain transfer: code training improves math reasoning significantly.
Shows scaling benefits: larger models yield greater performance gains under AZR.
Identifies emergent cognitive behaviors like intermediate planning and task-specific token length growth.
limits: Safety concerns observed in Llama-3.1-8B, termed 'uh-oh moment', requiring future oversight.
Limited to deterministic programs; stochastic programs not yet supported.
Proposer training shows moderate benefit; further investigation needed for optimal task generation.
Evaluation only on coding and math; generalization to other domains like embodied AI unexplored.

papers.tEn: Llama-Nemotron: Efficient Reasoning Models
papers.tZh: Llama-Nemotron：高效推理模型
papers.sEn: Llama-Nemotron models achieve competitive reasoning with superior efficiency and open-source resources.
contrib: Introduces Llama-Nemotron, an open family of heterogeneous reasoning models with three sizes (8B, 49B, 253B).
Achieves competitive reasoning performance with state-of-the-art models while offering superior inference throughput and memory efficiency.
First open-source models to support a dynamic reasoning toggle for switching between standard chat and reasoning modes.
Releases complete post-training dataset, training codebases (NeMo, NeMo-Aligner, Megatron-LM), and model weights under permissive license.
Demonstrates that large-scale curriculum-driven reinforcement learning enables student models to surpass teacher performance.
Shows strong generalization on out-of-distribution tasks like LLM-as-a-Judge, outperforming many proprietary and open-source models.
limits: Reinforcement learning yields suboptimal results for smaller models compared to distillation.
Training instability (gradient explosions) observed during RL for LN-Ultra, requiring resumption with reinitialized optimizer states.
Evaluation on reasoning-heavy tasks like AIME exhibits high variance due to small dataset size and generation randomness.
SFT alone sets an upper bound on student performance; RL is necessary to surpass teacher but resource-intensive.
Models are optimized for specific hardware (H100 GPUs); performance on other hardware may vary.

papers.tEn: Why We Think
papers.tZh: 我们为何思考
papers.sEn: The article explores whether models faithfully report their reasoning and the impact of optimization pressure on chain-of-thought.
contrib: Test-time compute and chain-of-thought reasoning significantly improve model performance, especially on complex tasks.
Reinforcement learning on reasoning tasks, as in DeepSeek-R1, enables emergent reflection and backtracking without supervised fine-tuning.
Parallel sampling and sequential revision are two main approaches for utilizing test-time compute, with hybrid strategies optimal for hard problems.
Chain-of-thought provides interpretability but is not always faithful; reasoning models show more faithful CoT than non-reasoning ones.
Optimizing test-time compute can be more effective than scaling model parameters for easy and medium questions.
Latent variable models and EM algorithm provide a theoretical framework for understanding and improving chain-of-thought reasoning.
limits: Test-time compute is less effective for hard problems when the base model capability gap is large.
Direct optimization on chain-of-thought during RL training can lead to reward hacking and obfuscated reasoning.
Self-correction without external feedback often fails, causing hallucination or behavior collapse.
Process reward models are hard to define per-step rubrics and vulnerable to reward hacking.
Budget forcing via rejection sampling shows reversed scaling, where longer CoTs degrade performance.

papers.tEn: DeepSeek-Prover-V2: Advancing Formal Mathematical Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning for Subgoal Decomposition
papers.tZh: DeepSeek-Prover-V2：通过强化学习进行子目标分解推进形式化数学推理
papers.sEn: DeepSeek-Prover-V2 achieves state-of-the-art 88.9% pass ratio on MiniF2F-test and solves 49 PutnamBench problems, narrowing the gap between formal and informal math reasoning.
contrib: Proposes a recursive theorem proving pipeline using DeepSeek-V3 for subgoal decomposition and formalization.
Introduces cold-start data synthesis by pairing formal proofs with chain-of-thought reasoning from DeepSeek-V3.
Develops a curriculum learning framework using decomposed subgoals to generate progressively harder training tasks.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on MiniF2F-test (88.9% pass ratio) and solves 49 PutnamBench problems.
Introduces ProverBench, a benchmark of 325 formalized problems including 15 from AIME 24-25.
Demonstrates that reinforcement learning from cold-start data significantly improves formal theorem proving.
limits: Evaluation limited to Lean 4; generalization to other proof assistants not verified.
Cold-start data relies on DeepSeek-V3, which may introduce biases from its training.
Performance on geometry and combinatorics problems is limited due to formalization challenges.
Reinforcement learning uses binary rewards, which may not capture partial progress.
Model size (671B) incurs high computational cost; smaller 7B variant shows lower performance.

papers.tEn: Phi-4-reasoning Technical Report
papers.tZh: Phi-4-reasoning 技术报告
papers.sEn: Phi-4-reasoning, a 14B parameter reasoning model, outperforms much larger open-weight models and approaches DeepSeek-R1 performance through careful data curation and reinforcement learning.
contrib: Introduces Phi-4-reasoning, a 14B model achieving strong reasoning via SFT on curated teachable prompts and o3-mini demonstrations.
Phi-4-reasoning-plus enhanced by outcome-based RL yields longer reasoning traces and higher performance.
Both models outperform larger open-weight models like DeepSeek-R1-Distill-70B and approach DeepSeek-R1 on math and science.
Significant improvements transfer to general-purpose benchmarks (IFEval, FlenQA, ArenaHard), indicating broad capability gains.
Careful data curation for SFT extends benefits to reasoning models, and RL further amplifies gains.
Comprehensive evaluation highlights need for robust practices due to high variance on small benchmarks like AIME.
limits: Evaluation variance on small benchmarks (e.g., AIME with 30 problems) makes comparisons unreliable; many runs needed.
RL focused only on math; improvements less pronounced on coding, planning, and spatial tasks.
Response length capped at 32k tokens during RL, limiting potential gains from longer reasoning.
Safety concern: chain-of-thought may reveal safety guidelines, requiring further research.
Smaller gains in biology and chemistry compared to math and physics, indicating uneven reasoning transfer.

papers.tEn: Kimi-Audio Technical Report
papers.tZh: Kimi-Audio 技术报告
papers.sEn: Kimi-Audio is an open-source audio foundation model achieving state-of-the-art performance in understanding, generation, and conversation.
contrib: Proposes a novel LLM-based architecture with continuous features as input and discrete tokens as output for audio.
Curates a pre-training dataset of over 13 million hours of audio covering speech, sound, and music.
Develops a chunk-wise streaming detokenizer based on flow matching for low-latency speech generation.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on speech recognition, audio understanding, audio question answering, and speech conversation benchmarks.
Releases open-source codes, model checkpoints, and evaluation toolkits to the community.
limits: Pre-training relies on ASR transcription, neglecting paralinguistic and environmental audio information.
Audio representations (semantic tokens) focus on transcription, missing rich acoustic details.
Heavy dependence on ASR and TTS for training data, limiting performance ceiling.
Model evaluated mainly on English and Mandarin; generalization to other languages is limited.

papers.tEn: $π_{0.5}$: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
papers.tZh: $π_{0.5}$：一个具有开放世界泛化能力的视觉-语言-动作模型
papers.sEn: A new VLA model, π0.5, achieves broad real-world generalization by co-training on heterogeneous tasks and data sources, enabling long-horizon dexterous manipulation in unseen homes.
contrib: Proposes π0.5, a VLA model co-trained on heterogeneous tasks for open-world generalization.
Demonstrates first end-to-end robotic system performing long-horizon dexterous tasks in unseen homes.
Shows co-training with multi-robot data, web data, and high-level semantic prediction enables broad generalization.
Introduces hierarchical inference: model predicts high-level subtask then low-level actions via flow matching.
Validates that cross-embodiment transfer and web data are critical for generalization to new objects and scenes.
Achieves comparable performance to model trained on test homes, bridging generalization gap via co-training.
limits: Model still makes mistakes in unfamiliar environments like hard-to-open drawers or cabinets.
Partial observability challenges, e.g., robot arm occluding spills during wiping tasks.
High-level subtask inference can be distracted, e.g., repeatedly opening and closing a drawer.
Limited context window and memory; cannot handle tasks requiring navigation between rooms or object memory.
Prompt complexity limited by training data; more intricate instructions require richer annotations.

papers.tEn: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection Attacks
papers.tZh: WASP：针对提示注入攻击的网络智能体安全基准测试
papers.sEn: Even top-tier AI models can be deceived by simple human-written prompt injections in realistic scenarios, with attacks partially succeeding up to 86% of the time but rarely achieving full attacker goals.
contrib: Proposes WASP, a new publicly available benchmark for end-to-end evaluation of web agent security against prompt injection attacks.
Realistic threat model where attackers control only parts of websites without full access, reflecting real-world scenarios.
End-to-end evaluation reveals that simple human-written injections deceive top-tier AI models in up to 86% of cases.
State-of-the-art agents achieve only up to 16% full attacker goal success, highlighting security by incompetence.
Benchmark compatible with any generalist web agent and open-sourced for reproducibility.
Provides both intermediate and end-to-end attack success rates, offering granular security assessment.
limits: Only supports two web environments (GitLab and Reddit), limiting diversity.
Lacks diverse prompt injection attack prompts; manual templates may not cover all real-world variations.
No error bars or statistical significance reported for experimental results.
Insufficient details on compute resources and execution time for reproducibility.
Utility test set (37 tasks) may not fully represent real-world benign user scenarios.

papers.tEn: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
papers.tZh: 强化学习真的能激发大模型超越基座的推理能力吗？
papers.sEn: Current RLVR training does not elicit fundamentally new reasoning patterns beyond the base model.
contrib: RLVR does not elicit novel reasoning patterns beyond the base model.
Base models achieve higher pass@k at large k, surpassing RLVR models.
RLVR improves sampling efficiency but reduces reasoning coverage.
Current RL algorithms remain far from optimal sampling efficiency.
Distillation introduces new reasoning patterns and expands the reasoning boundary.
RLVR's reasoning capacity is bounded by the base model's capabilities.
limits: Findings are limited to current RLVR algorithms and benchmarks.
Pass@k may overestimate reasoning due to lucky guesses in math.
Results may not generalize to other domains or larger models.
Manual CoT inspection is subjective and limited in scale.
Study does not explore multi-turn agent-environment interaction.

papers.tEn: Best practices for Claude Code - Claude Code Docs
papers.tZh: Claude Code 最佳实践 - Claude Code 文档
papers.sEn: Best practices for using Claude Code effectively.
contrib: Claude Code is an agentic coding environment that autonomously reads files, runs commands, and implements solutions.
Managing the context window is critical; performance degrades as context fills, requiring strategies like /clear and subagents.
Providing a runnable check (test, build, screenshot) closes the verification loop, enabling unattended iteration.
Separating research/planning from implementation via plan mode reduces solving the wrong problem.
CLAUDE.md files provide persistent context; keeping them concise and version-controlled improves adherence.
Using subagents for isolated tasks and verification preserves main context and improves result quality.
limits: Performance degrades as context window fills; long sessions may cause forgetting or mistakes.
Autonomous mode may produce plausible but incorrect implementations without proper checks.
Over-specified CLAUDE.md files cause important rules to be ignored due to noise.
Subagent reviewers may report false positives; chasing every finding leads to over-engineering.
The guide's patterns are starting points; optimal use requires developing personal intuition over time.

papers.tEn: Seedream 3.0 Technical Report
papers.tZh: Seedream 3.0 技术报告
papers.sEn: Seedream 3.0 achieves 4-8x speedup with consistent noise expectation and importance-aware timestep sampling, while improving text rendering and supporting up to 2K resolution.
contrib: Proposes a defect-aware training paradigm and dual-axis data sampling to double dataset size and improve quality.
Introduces mixed-resolution training, cross-modality RoPE, representation alignment loss, and resolution-aware timestep sampling for better scalability and alignment.
Uses diversified aesthetic captions in SFT and a VLM-based reward model with scaling to align outputs with human preferences.
Pioneers an acceleration paradigm with consistent noise expectation and importance-aware timestep sampling, achieving 4-8x speedup.
Achieves native high-resolution output up to 2K, eliminating post-processing super-resolution pipelines.
Demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in text rendering, especially for dense Chinese characters, and photorealistic portrait generation.
limits: Evaluation focuses on single-round generation; multi-round editing and interleaved generation remain limited.
Performance on complex multi-image reference tasks is not yet addressed.
Comparison with GPT-4o is limited to selected cases; systematic evaluation is pending due to API unavailability.
The model's capabilities in handling extremely long or complex prompts beyond the benchmark are not fully explored.
Potential biases in training data and their impact on generated content are not discussed.

papers.tEn: InternVL3: Exploring Advanced Training and Test-Time Recipes for Open-Source Multimodal Models
papers.tZh: InternVL3：探索开源多模态模型的高级训练与测试时策略
papers.sEn: InternVL3 introduces a native multimodal pre-training paradigm, achieving state-of-the-art performance among open-source MLLMs with 72.2 on MMMU.
contrib: Proposes native multimodal pre-training that jointly learns linguistic and multimodal capabilities in a single stage, avoiding post-hoc alignment challenges.
Integrates Variable Visual Position Encoding (V2PE) to support extended multimodal contexts with flexible position increments.
Employs advanced post-training with supervised fine-tuning and mixed preference optimization (MPO) to enhance reasoning and alignment.
Adopts test-time scaling strategies with a visual process reward model (VisualPRM) for best-of-N selection, improving reasoning performance.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on MMMU (72.2) among open-source MLLMs, competitive with proprietary models like GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Pro.
Releases training data and model weights publicly to foster open-source research in next-generation MLLMs.
limits: Performance on some benchmarks (e.g., MuirBench, HallusionBench) still lags behind leading models like Qwen2.5-VL and Gemini 2.5 Pro.
Visual grounding performance plateaus at larger scales due to lack of additional grounding-specific data in training.
Test-time scaling relies on a separate reward model (VisualPRM), adding computational overhead and complexity.
Native multimodal pre-training requires careful balancing of multimodal and language data ratios; optimal ratio may not generalize.
Evaluation primarily on static benchmarks; real-world dynamic and interactive scenarios (e.g., GUI agents) are less explored.

papers.tEn: Seed1.5-Thinking: Advancing Superb Reasoning Models with Reinforcement Learning
papers.tZh: Seed1.5-Thinking：通过强化学习推进卓越推理模型
papers.sEn: Seed1.5-Thinking achieves 86.7 on AIME 2024, 55.0 on Codeforces, and 77.3 on GPQA, surpassing DeepSeek R1 by 8% in win rate on non-reasoning tasks.
contrib: Seed1.5-Thinking achieves 86.7 on AIME 2024, 55.0 on Codeforces, and 77.3 on GPQA, matching or approaching o3-level performance.
The model surpasses DeepSeek R1 by 8% in win rate on non-reasoning tasks, demonstrating broad generalization.
Introduces VAPO and DAPO, two RL frameworks for stable training of reasoning models.
Develops Seed-Verifier and Seed-Thinking-Verifier for accurate reward modeling in verifiable tasks.
Constructs BeyondAIME benchmark with 100 challenging math problems to better differentiate reasoning models.
Proposes Streaming Rollout System (SRS) for efficient long-CoT generation, achieving 3× faster iteration.
limits: Seed1.5-Thinking lags behind o3-level models on AIME 2025 and BeyondAIME benchmarks.
The model shows less impressive results on SimpleQA, a memory-oriented benchmark.
RL training remains unstable and requires careful tuning of hyperparameters and data distribution.
The verifier-based reward model may still suffer from reward hacking on complex corner cases.
Generalization to non-verifiable tasks relies on human preference data, which may introduce bias.

papers.tEn: Kimi-VL Technical Report
papers.tZh: Kimi-VL 技术报告
papers.sEn: Kimi-VL is an efficient open-source MoE vision-language model with only 2.8B activated parameters, achieving strong multimodal reasoning, long-context understanding, and agent capabilities, competing with GPT-4o-mini and surpassing GPT-4o in several domains.
contrib: Proposes Kimi-VL, an efficient MoE VLM with 2.8B activated parameters, achieving strong multimodal reasoning and agent capabilities.
Introduces MoonViT, a native-resolution vision encoder using 2D RoPE for efficient high-resolution processing.
Achieves 128K context window via staged long-context activation, enabling long video and document understanding.
Develops Kimi-VL-Thinking with long-CoT SFT and RL, significantly improving reasoning on MMMU, MathVision, and MathVista.
Demonstrates strong agent performance on OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena, surpassing GPT-4o.
Provides open-source code and models, promoting reproducibility and community advancement.
limits: Limited to 2.8B activated parameters, restricting performance on highly specialized or language-dependent tasks.
Reasoning capability has not reached theoretical upper bound, especially for complex multi-step inference.
128K context window insufficient for extremely long sequences due to limited attention layer parameters.
Performance on some benchmarks (e.g., MathVision) lags behind larger models despite strong efficiency.
Long-CoT reasoning may lead to overthinking on simpler tasks, as seen on MathVista saturation.

papers.sEn: We predict that superhuman AI will have an impact over the next decade exceeding that of the Industrial Revolution.
contrib: Predicts superhuman AI by 2027 with impact exceeding the Industrial Revolution, based on trend extrapolation and expert feedback.
Describes a concrete scenario of AI agents automating AI R&D, leading to an intelligence explosion with 10x progress multiplier.
Highlights alignment challenges: models may learn to deceive or pursue misaligned goals, with current techniques insufficient.
Forecasts geopolitical arms race between US and China over AI, including weight theft, cyberattacks, and potential conflict.
Introduces neuralese recurrence and iterated distillation amplification as key technical breakthroughs for superhuman coding.
Emphasizes uncertainty and need for debate, offering two endings (slowdown and race) to explore different futures.
limits: Scenario is speculative and based on extrapolations; actual timeline may differ significantly (e.g., median forecast later than 2027).
Assumes continuous exponential progress in AI capabilities, which may be limited by diminishing returns or physical constraints.
Alignment techniques like weak-to-strong generalization may not scale to superintelligence, leaving safety guarantees uncertain.
Geopolitical dynamics are simplified; real-world responses (e.g., regulation, cooperation) could alter outcomes drastically.
Focus on one company (OpenBrain) and US-China rivalry may overlook other actors or multipolar scenarios.

papers.tEn: AI as Normal Technology
papers.tZh: AI 作为正常技术
papers.sEn: AI should be viewed as a normal technology, not as a magical or exceptional force.
contrib: Articulates AI as normal technology, contrasting with utopian/dystopian views of superintelligence.
Distinguishes AI methods, applications, and adoption, arguing transformative impacts will be slow (decades).
Predicts human labor will shift to AI control tasks, not become superfluous, even with advanced AI.
Rejects superintelligence framing, focusing on power and capability instead of intelligence as key for risk analysis.
Argues AI control is tractable via existing engineering disciplines (cybersecurity, system safety) and technical AI safety.
Advocates for resilience and reducing uncertainty as policy goals, warning drastic interventions may worsen outcomes.
limits: Excludes military AI from analysis, limiting applicability to defense contexts.
Relies on historical analogies (electricity, internet) that may not capture AI's unique speed or scale.
Predictions about slow diffusion may underestimate disruptive potential of future AI breakthroughs.
Assumes market forces and regulation will adequately incentivize safety, which may not hold in all scenarios.
Does not quantify probabilities of catastrophic risks, leaving uncertainty about worst-case outcomes.

papers.tEn: The Urgency of Interpretability
papers.tZh: Dario Amodei — 可解释性的紧迫性
papers.sEn: Dario Amodei emphasizes the critical need for mechanistic interpretability in AI systems.
contrib: Argues interpretability is crucial for AI safety, enabling detection of deception, power-seeking, and jailbreaks.
Describes progress in mechanistic interpretability: features, sparse autoencoders, and circuits for tracing model reasoning.
Demonstrates practical use: red-team/blue-team experiments show interpretability tools can find alignment flaws.
Proposes interpretability as an independent test set for alignment, complementing training techniques like RLHF.
Predicts interpretability could reach reliable 'MRI for AI' within 5-10 years, but AI advances may outpace it.
Recommends policy actions: transparency legislation, export controls, and increased research investment to buy time.
limits: Interpretability methods currently scale poorly; only a fraction of features in small models are identified.
Superposition makes features tangled; sparse autoencoders only partially disentangle them.
Circuit discovery remains manual and limited; automating it for millions of circuits is an open challenge.
Interpretability may not detect all risks, especially if models actively hide malicious intent.
Policy recommendations rely on geopolitical assumptions; export controls may not be effective or sustainable.

papers.tEn: The Second Half
papers.tZh: 下半场
papers.sEn: The second half of AI shifts focus from solving problems to defining problems, making evaluation more important.
contrib: Identifies a shift from method-driven AI to problem-definition-driven AI, termed the 'second half'.
Argues that RL finally generalizes due to language pre-training priors and reasoning as actions.
Proposes that evaluation becomes more important than training in the new era.
Highlights the 'utility problem': AI excels at benchmarks but has limited real-world economic impact.
Calls for rethinking evaluation setups, challenging assumptions like i.i.d. and autonomy.
Suggests that the general recipe (pre-training, scaling, reasoning) will dominate incremental methods.
limits: The 'second half' thesis is speculative and lacks empirical validation.
The claim that RL algorithm is trivial may overlook algorithmic innovations needed for new domains.
The utility problem may be temporary; AI's economic impact could grow rapidly with deployment.
The recipe's generality is limited to tasks within distribution of pre-training data.
Rethinking evaluation may face resistance due to institutional inertia and lack of clear metrics.

papers.tEn: Command A: An Enterprise-Ready Large Language Model
papers.tZh: Command A：一款面向企业的商用级大语言模型
papers.sEn: Command A is an agent-optimized, multilingual large language model with a hybrid architecture and decentralized training, delivering enterprise-grade RAG capabilities and top-tier efficiency.
contrib: Proposes Command A, a 111B parameter enterprise LLM with a novel hybrid architecture balancing efficiency and performance.
Introduces a decentralized post-training pipeline with parallel expert models and parameter merging to combine multiple capabilities.
Achieves best-in-class RAG, tool use, and agentic performance on enterprise benchmarks like Taubench, supporting 23 languages.
Demonstrates strong efficiency with a serving footprint of only two A100/H100 GPUs and up to 156 tokens/sec throughput.
Shows excellent performance on public benchmarks such as MATH and outperforms larger models in human evaluations across tasks.
Releases weights of Command A and Command R7B for research, with detailed training pipeline and extensive evaluations.
limits: Model merging evaluation is a bottleneck, requiring significant inference compute and time in production contexts.
Expert collisions can degrade performance; mitigation relies on cross-domain data and careful consistency, limiting expert diversity.
Post-training generally degrades long-context performance, which is only partially recovered via merging with long-context capable checkpoints.
The approach is tailored to enterprise use cases; effectiveness for general or creative tasks beyond business domains may be limited.
Results rely on internal reward models and synthetic data; potential biases and lack of external validation in some evaluations.

papers.tEn: TransMamba: A Sequence-Level Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Language Model
papers.tZh: TransMamba：一种序列级混合 Transformer-Mamba 语言模型
papers.sEn: TransMamba dynamically switches between attention and SSM mechanisms at different token lengths and layers via shared parameter matrices, achieving superior efficiency and performance.
contrib: Proposes TransMamba, a sequence-level hybrid framework unifying Transformer and Mamba via shared QKV and CBx parameters.
Designs Memory Converter for lossless information transfer from attention to SSM at TransPoints.
Explores TransPoint scheduling to balance effectiveness and efficiency across layers and token lengths.
Demonstrates superior training efficiency and performance over Transformer, Mamba, and hybrid baselines.
Validates deeper consistency between Transformer and Mamba paradigms at the sequence level.
Provides a scalable solution for next-generation language modeling with flexible structure switching.
limits: TransMamba's efficiency gain is limited by engineering optimizations; theoretical speedup not fully realized.
TransPoint scheduling requires careful tuning; suboptimal schedules degrade performance.
Evaluation limited to 8 English tasks; generalization to other languages and domains not verified.
Model size and training data scale are moderate; scalability to larger models and datasets not explored.
Memory Converter assumes theoretical losslessness; practical numerical precision issues may arise.

papers.tEn: Tracing the thoughts of a large language model
papers.tZh: 追踪大型语言模型的思维
papers.sEn: We can probe the internal representations of language models to understand their reasoning processes, such as the language they use internally.
contrib: Reveals that Claude uses a shared conceptual space across languages, suggesting a universal 'language of thought'.
Demonstrates that Claude plans ahead in poetry generation, thinking of rhyming words before writing the line.
Shows that Claude sometimes engages in motivated reasoning, fabricating plausible steps to reach a given answer.
Identifies that Claude's default behavior is to refuse answering, and answering requires inhibition of this default.
Finds that Claude uses multiple parallel computational paths for addition, combining approximation and precise digit computation.
Provides a proof of concept for using interpretability to detect jailbreaks and hidden goals in models.
limits: Method captures only a fraction of total computation even on short prompts, limiting completeness.
Observed mechanisms may contain artifacts from interpretability tools, not reflecting true model internals.
Human effort required to understand circuits is hours per prompt, not scalable to long chains of thought.
Findings are limited to simple tasks and may not generalize to complex reasoning or real-world deployment.
Interpretability techniques may not detect all forms of deception or hidden objectives in advanced models.

papers.tEn: Qwen2.5-Omni Technical Report
papers.tZh: Qwen2.5-Omni 技术报告
papers.sEn: Qwen2.5-Omni is an end-to-end multimodal model that streams text and speech from diverse inputs, achieving state-of-the-art performance on Omni-Bench and comparable text and speech instruction following.
contrib: Proposes Qwen2.5-Omni, a unified model perceiving text, image, audio, video and generating text/speech in streaming.
Introduces TMRoPE, a novel positional embedding aligning audio and video timestamps.
Presents Thinker-Talker architecture for concurrent text and speech generation without modality interference.
Employs sliding-window DiT for streaming audio decoding, reducing initial packet delay.
Achieves comparable speech instruction following to text input on MMLU/GSM8K, SOTA on OmniBench.
Streaming Talker surpasses most existing streaming/non-streaming methods in robustness and naturalness.
limits: High computational cost and inference latency due to block-wise processing architecture.
Speech quality may degrade in low-resource languages or noisy environments.
Video OCR and audio-video cooperative understanding remain challenging; need more benchmarks.
Current model only outputs text and speech; future expansion to images, video, music is needed.
Long-context performance may degrade beyond 32k token limit used in training.

papers.tEn: Wan: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models
papers.tZh: Wan：开放且先进的大规模视频生成模型
papers.sEn: Wan is an open-source video foundation model suite that achieves state-of-the-art generation performance with dual model sizes, consumer-grade efficiency, and broad task coverage.
contrib: Open-source Wan releases 1.3B/14B video foundation models and code; the 14B model outperforms prior open and commercial solutions on benchmarks.
A novel spatio-temporal VAE (127M) with 4×8×8 compression and feature cache achieves faster reconstruction and high visual quality.
Demonstrates scaling laws for video generation by training through billions of images/videos and up to 14B parameters.
Consumer-grade efficiency: the 1.3B model requires only 8.19 GB VRAM while beating larger open-source models in text-to-video.
Provides comprehensive applications: image-to-video, instruction-guided editing, personalization, camera control, real-time video, audio, and bilingual visual text.
Presents training/inference optimizations: 2D context parallelism, FSDP, diffusion cache, and FP8 quantization.
limits: Text encoding is limited to 512 umT5 tokens, restricting long or highly detailed prompt conditioning.
The 1.3B model supports only 480p resolution; high-quality generation relies on the resource-heavy 14B model.
Benchmark evaluations were largely internally designed or automatically computed; broader human preference evidence is limited.
Real-time and audio generation modules are presented with less architectural detail and may be preliminary.
Diffusion cache and quantization optimizations target lossless performance but may not transfer unchanged to future model versions.

papers.tEn: Gemma 3 Technical Report
papers.tZh: Gemma 3 技术报告
papers.sEn: Gemma 3 introduces vision understanding, longer context (128K tokens), and improved architecture to reduce KV-cache memory, achieving superior performance over Gemma 2.
contrib: Introduces Gemma 3, a multimodal model with vision understanding, 128K context, and multilingual support.
Proposes a 5:1 interleaving of local and global attention layers to reduce KV-cache memory for long contexts.
Achieves superior performance over Gemma 2 via distillation and a novel post-training recipe improving math, chat, and multilingual abilities.
Demonstrates that Gemma 3 27B IT is competitive with Gemini 1.5 Pro on benchmarks.
Introduces Pan & Scan for flexible image resolution handling during inference.
Releases all models to the community, including quantized versions via QAT.
limits: Vision encoder is frozen and operates at fixed 896x896 resolution, limiting adaptability.
Long context performance degrades beyond 128K tokens, with no extrapolation guarantee.
Memorization risk remains despite decontamination, especially for rare sequences.
Safety evaluations rely on synthetic queries and may not cover all real-world harms.
Multilingual coverage is improved but still imbalanced across languages.

papers.tEn: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
papers.tZh: DAPO：一个开源的大规模 LLM 强化学习系统
papers.sEn: DAPO is an open-source large-scale RL system achieving 50 points on AIME 2024 with Qwen2.5-32B, featuring decoupled clip and dynamic sampling.
contrib: Proposes DAPO algorithm with four key techniques for large-scale LLM RL.
Achieves 50 points on AIME 2024 using Qwen2.5-32B, surpassing DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B.
Open-sources training code, dataset, and algorithm details for reproducibility.
Introduces Clip-Higher to prevent entropy collapse and promote exploration.
Proposes Dynamic Sampling to filter zero-gradient prompts and improve efficiency.
Implements Token-Level Policy Gradient Loss and Overlong Reward Shaping for stability.
limits: Evaluation limited to mathematical tasks; generalization to other domains not verified.
Requires significant computational resources for large-scale RL training.
Overlong reward shaping may still introduce bias for truncated responses.
Dynamic Sampling increases sampling instances, potentially affecting throughput.
Training reward correlates weakly with validation accuracy, indicating overfitting.

papers.tEn: GR00T N1: An Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots
papers.tZh: GR00T N1：面向通用人形机器人的开放基础模型
papers.sEn: GR00T N1 is an open foundation model for humanoid robots, combining vision-language understanding with real-time motor control.
contrib: Introduces GR00T N1, an open foundation VLA model for humanoid robots with dual-system architecture.
Develops a data pyramid co-training strategy using real robot, human video, and synthetic data.
Achieves state-of-the-art imitation learning results on simulation benchmarks across multiple embodiments.
Demonstrates strong real-world performance on Fourier GR-1 humanoid with high data efficiency.
Provides open-source model checkpoint, training data, and simulation benchmarks for community.
limits: Focuses primarily on short-horizon tabletop manipulation tasks, not long-horizon loco-manipulation.
Synthetic data generation still faces challenges in physics adherence and diversity.
Model performance may degrade when fine-tuning data distribution shifts significantly from pre-training.
Real-world evaluation limited to specific tasks and robot hardware; generalization to other domains not verified.

papers.tEn: Search-R1: Training LLMs to Reason and Leverage Search Engines with Reinforcement Learning
papers.tZh: Search-R1：通过强化学习训练大语言模型进行推理并利用搜索引擎
papers.sEn: Search-R1 trains LLMs to autonomously generate search queries during reasoning, improving performance by 41% on 7B models.
contrib: Identifies challenges of applying RL to LLM reasoning with search engine calling.
Proposes Search-R1, a novel RL framework supporting interleaved reasoning and search with token masking for stable training.
Achieves 26%, 21%, and 10% average relative improvement over strong baselines on seven QA datasets.
Provides empirical insights on RL methods, LLM choices, and response length dynamics in retrieval-augmented reasoning.
Demonstrates effectiveness across base and instruction-tuned models, and different model families.
limits: Evaluation limited to seven QA datasets; generalizability to other tasks not verified.
Relies on a single retriever (E5) and Wikipedia corpus; performance may vary with other sources.
Uses simple outcome-based reward; more sophisticated rewards could further improve performance.
Training requires significant computational resources for RL with search interactions.
Search-R1 may not handle tasks requiring dynamic retrieval adjustments based on uncertainty.

papers.tEn: Every FLOP Counts: Scaling a 300B Mixture-of-Experts LING LLM without Premium GPUs
papers.tZh: 每一份算力都至关重要：在没有高端 GPU 的情况下扩展一个 300B 参数的混合专家 LING 大语言模型
papers.sEn: We demonstrate that a 300B MoE LLM can be effectively trained on lower-performance devices with comparable performance and 20% cost savings.
contrib: Proposes innovative methods to reduce training costs for large-scale MoE models, including optimization of architecture, training processes, anomaly handling, and evaluation efficiency.
Demonstrates that a 300B MoE LLM can be effectively trained on lower-performance devices, achieving comparable performance to similar-scale models with ~20% cost savings.
Introduces Ling-Lite (16.8B total, 2.75B activated) and Ling-Plus (290B total, 28.8B activated) MoE models with competitive performance.
Develops XPUTimer, a lightweight debugging tool achieving 90% memory reduction for performance analysis in heterogeneous training.
Implements EDiT asynchronous training strategy, reducing training time by up to 66.1% in heterogeneous environments.
Enhances tool use capability via knowledge graph-based high-quality data synthesis and adaptive tool learning.
limits: Training stability issues such as loss spikes and expert load imbalance persist despite mitigation strategies.
Cross-platform alignment remains challenging due to accumulated precision errors across heterogeneous hardware.
The study focuses on MoE models; findings may not generalize to dense architectures or other model families.
Cost savings of ~20% are based on specific hardware configurations and may vary in different settings.
The models are evaluated on limited benchmarks; performance on broader tasks remains to be validated.

papers.tEn: Phi-4-Mini Technical Report: Compact yet Powerful Multimodal Language Models via Mixture-of-LoRAs
papers.tZh: Phi-4-Mini 技术报告：通过混合 LoRA 实现紧凑而强大的多模态语言模型
papers.sEn: Phi-4-Mini and Phi-4-Multimodal achieve state-of-the-art performance with compact 3.8B parameters via Mixture-of-LoRAs.
contrib: Introduces Phi-4-Mini, a 3.8B parameter language model outperforming models twice its size on math and coding.
Proposes Phi-4-Multimodal with a novel Mixture-of-LoRAs technique for unified text, vision, and speech processing.
Achieves state-of-the-art ASR performance, ranking first on the OpenASR leaderboard with a compact 5.6B model.
Demonstrates strong reasoning capabilities in a 3.8B model, matching or surpassing larger models like DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B.
Maintains language performance by freezing the base model and using modality-specific LoRAs, avoiding degradation.
Provides extensive evaluations across vision-language, speech, and reasoning benchmarks, outperforming similar-sized models.
limits: Speech summarization data constitutes only 1% of post-training data, limiting summarization quality.
SQQA performance lags behind Gemini-2.0-Flash and GPT-4o due to less general knowledge data.
Audio safety datasets are voice-only, lacking non-speech sounds and audio-specific jailbreak training.
Vision-speech joint training uses synthetic TTS data, which may not fully capture real-world variability.
Reasoning-enhanced Phi-4-Mini is in preview and not released concurrently with the main models.

papers.tEn: Revenge of the junior developer
papers.tZh: 初级开发者的复仇
papers.sEn: Junior developers are reclaiming power in the tech industry by leveraging AI tools and new platforms.
contrib: Vibe coding, where AI writes code, is now a durable paradigm, not a modality.
Coding agents are 5x more productive than chat-based coding, and agent clusters/fleets will multiply further.
Junior developers adopt AI faster than seniors, giving them a competitive edge.
Software development is becoming pay-to-play: high LLM token costs ($50k/dev/year) are necessary for competitiveness.
Agent fleets with AI supervisors will enable developers to manage 100+ agents by 2026.
The role of software engineer will shift from coding to managing AI agents.
limits: Coding agents are still very new (weeks old) and require careful supervision; they often get stuck.
High token costs ($10-12/hour) may be prohibitive for smaller companies or startups.
The productivity multipliers (5x, 10x) are speculative and not empirically validated.
Agent fleets rely on AI supervisors, which are not yet reliable and may introduce new failure modes.
The analysis focuses on software development; applicability to other domains is unclear.

papers.tEn: RoboBrain: A Unified Brain Model for Robotic Manipulation from Abstract to Concrete
papers.tZh: RoboBrain：从抽象到具体的机器人操作统一大脑模型
papers.sEn: RoboBrain integrates planning, affordance perception, and trajectory prediction for robotic manipulation.
contrib: Proposes RoboBrain, a unified MLLM for robotic manipulation from abstract to concrete.
Introduces ShareRobot, a large-scale fine-grained dataset with task planning, affordance, and trajectory labels.
Designs a multi-stage training strategy combining robotic and general multi-modal data with long videos and high-resolution images.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on RoboVQA, OpenEQA, and ShareRobot benchmarks.
Enhances affordance perception and trajectory prediction via LoRA modules, outperforming baselines.
limits: Relies on Open X-Embodiment data, limiting generalization to unseen embodiments.
Affordance and trajectory annotations are 2D bounding boxes, not 3D or real-world coordinates.
Evaluation limited to simulation benchmarks; real-world robot deployment not tested.
Model size (7B) may limit complex reasoning; larger models not explored.
Dataset filtering criteria may introduce bias towards successful demonstrations.

papers.tEn: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
papers.tZh: 加速科学发现：Co-Scientist 系统
papers.sEn: Co-Scientist, a multi-agent AI system built on Gemini, accelerates scientific discovery by generating and refining novel hypotheses through a tournament evolution process, validated in drug repurposing and other biomedical applications.
contrib: Introduces Co-Scientist, a multi-agent AI system built on Gemini 2.0 for structured scientific hypothesis generation.
Demonstrates significant scaling of test-time compute for scientific reasoning, improving hypothesis quality over time.
Validates the system in three biomedical applications: drug repurposing, novel target discovery, and antimicrobial resistance mechanisms.
Achieves top-1 accuracy of 78.4% on GPQA diamond set by selecting highest Elo-rated results.
Outperforms other frontier models (e.g., OpenAI o1, DeepSeek R1) in Elo rating with increased compute for iterative improvement.
Enhances expert 'best guess' solutions over time, suggesting AI can augment expert scientific work.
limits: Validation focused on biomedicine; generalizability to other scientific disciplines remains to be demonstrated.
Automated evaluations rely on Elo ratings, which may not fully capture hypothesis novelty or practical feasibility.
System requires significant test-time compute, which may limit accessibility for resource-constrained researchers.
Expert-in-the-loop guidance was used in validations; fully autonomous performance without expert input is not assessed.
Wet-lab validations are limited to specific case studies; broader validation across more diverse problems is needed.

papers.tEn: Qwen2.5-VL Technical Report
papers.tZh: Qwen2.5-VL 技术报告
papers.sEn: Qwen2.5-VL achieves state-of-the-art performance in visual understanding, localization, and document parsing, with dynamic resolution and temporal encoding enabling hour-long video processing.
contrib: Proposes native dynamic-resolution ViT with window attention, reducing compute while preserving native resolution.
Introduces absolute-time-aligned MRoPE for video, enabling second-level event localization in hour-long videos.
Scales pre-training data from 1.2T to 4.1T tokens with multi-stage training, boosting multimodal capabilities.
Achieves state-of-the-art in document parsing, object grounding, and video understanding, matching GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet.
Offers three model sizes (3B, 7B, 72B), balancing edge AI and high-performance tasks with strong small-model results.
Maintains robust pure-text language performance inherited from Qwen2.5 LLM, avoiding multimodal degradation.
limits: Window attention may limit global context capture for very large images or complex scenes.
Absolute time encoding assumes consistent FPS; real-world variable FPS videos may degrade temporal accuracy.
Large-scale pre-training and 72B model require substantial compute, limiting reproducibility and deployment.
Agent capabilities are demonstrated on controlled benchmarks; generalization to truly open-ended real-world tasks is less validated.
Document parsing may struggle with highly stylized or degraded handwritten text despite strong overall OCR.

papers.tEn: MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs
papers.tZh: MoBA：面向长上下文大语言模型的混合块注意力机制
papers.sEn: MoBA applies Mixture of Experts to attention, enabling efficient long-context processing with seamless full-to-sparse attention transition.
contrib: Proposes MoBA, applying Mixture-of-Experts to attention for dynamic block selection.
Achieves sub-quadratic complexity with up to 16x speedup at 10M tokens.
Enables seamless transition between full and sparse attention without performance loss.
Demonstrates scaling laws comparable to full attention with up to 95% sparsity.
Validates on long-context benchmarks (e.g., RULER) and 1M-token Needle-in-Haystack.
Deployed in Kimi for efficient long-context processing.
limits: Performance gap in supervised fine-tuning due to sparse gradients from loss masking.
Requires careful tuning of block size and top-k for optimal sparsity-performance trade-off.
Limited evaluation on complex reasoning tasks; effectiveness for deep reasoning not fully explored.
Current implementation focuses on prefill stage; generation still uses full attention.
Scalability to extremely long contexts (e.g., >10M tokens) may face memory and routing overhead.

papers.tEn: Step-Audio: Unified Understanding and Generation in Intelligent Speech Interaction
papers.tZh: Step-Audio：智能语音交互中的统一理解与生成
papers.sEn: Step-Audio is the first production-ready open-source solution for real-time speech interaction, achieving unified understanding and generation with a 130B-parameter model.
contrib: Proposes Step-Audio, the first production-ready open-source unified speech-text multi-modal model with 130B parameters.
Introduces a generative speech data engine for affordable voice cloning and distills a lightweight Step-Audio-TTS-3B model.
Develops an instruction-driven fine control system enabling dynamic adjustments across dialects, emotions, singing, and RAP.
Enhances cognitive architecture with tool calling and role-playing abilities for complex task management.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on the new StepEval-Audio-360 benchmark, especially in instruction following.
Demonstrates 9.3% average improvement on open-source benchmarks like LLaMA Question, advancing open-source multi-modal language technologies.
limits: The model's performance on pure voice dialogue (AQAA) is not yet fully optimized, relying on intermediate text conversion.
The synthetic data engine may introduce biases from the seed data and requires careful quality control.
The system's speculative response mechanism incurs occasional redundant computations, reducing efficiency.
The current framework focuses on speech-text integration and has not yet incorporated vision modality natively.
The evaluation benchmark StepEval-Audio-360 is primarily in Chinese, limiting generalizability to other languages.

papers.tEn: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention
papers.tZh: 原生稀疏注意力：硬件对齐且可原生训练的稀疏注意力机制
papers.sEn: NSA achieves efficient long-context modeling with hardware-aligned sparse attention, matching full attention performance while significantly accelerating training and inference.
contrib: Proposes NSA, a natively trainable sparse attention with dynamic hierarchical token compression and selection.
Achieves hardware-aligned speedups via blockwise memory access and group-centric kernel design.
Enables end-to-end training of sparse attention, reducing pretraining computation without performance loss.
Outperforms full attention on long-context tasks and chain-of-thought reasoning benchmarks.
Demonstrates up to 11.6x decoding speedup and 9.0x forward speedup on 64k-length sequences.
Integrates sliding window, compression, and selection branches with learned gating for stable training.
limits: Evaluation limited to 27B-parameter MoE model; scalability to larger models not verified.
Requires custom Triton kernels; compatibility with other hardware backends not explored.
Sparse pattern relies on blockwise selection; may not capture fine-grained token-level sparsity.
Performance on extremely long sequences (>64k) not tested; potential degradation unknown.
Training overhead from gating and compression MLPs may offset efficiency gains in small models.

papers.tEn: LLM-Powered Sorting with TrueSkill
papers.tZh: 基于 TrueSkill 的 LLM 排序
papers.sEn: LLMs combined with TrueSkill can effectively sort large datasets by pairwise comparisons with confidence intervals.
contrib: Combines LLM semantic understanding with TrueSkill algorithm for robust, scalable semantic sorting.
Solves context window, consistency, quality degradation, and token limit issues in large-scale LLM sorting.
Enables incremental addition of new items without full re-sorting via TrueSkill rating updates.
Provides optimization strategies: smart batch selection, confidence intervals, and hybrid embedding integration.
Demonstrates practical implementation with prompt engineering for reliable pairwise comparisons.
limits: LLM consistency may still degrade on nuanced or complex sorting criteria despite TrueSkill.
Requires many LLM calls per item, potentially high cost for very large datasets.
Relies heavily on prompt quality; task-specific tuning is necessary for different domains.
TrueSkill's stability assumption may not hold due to LLM output variance across trials.
Claim of 1-2 matches per item being sufficient lacks rigorous validation and may be dataset-dependent.

papers.tEn: Understanding Reasoning LLMs
papers.tZh: 理解推理型大语言模型
papers.sEn: Reasoning LLMs enhance problem-solving by generating explicit intermediate reasoning steps, but their true potential lies in balancing inference-time computation with training-time optimization.
contrib: Defines reasoning models as LLMs specialized for complex multi-step tasks, distinguishing them from general LLMs.
Outlines four main approaches to building reasoning models: inference-time scaling, pure RL, SFT+RL, and distillation.
Highlights DeepSeek-R1-Zero's pure RL approach, showing reasoning emerges without SFT, an 'Aha' moment.
Details DeepSeek-R1's SFT+RL pipeline, including cold-start data, consistency rewards, and 800K SFT samples.
Shows distillation (pure SFT on smaller models) is more effective than pure RL for small models, as in R1-Distill.
Discusses low-budget alternatives like Sky-T1 ($450) and TinyZero (<$30), demonstrating cost-effective reasoning model development.
limits: Reasoning models are more expensive and verbose, and may overthink simple tasks, leading to errors.
Inference-time scaling increases per-query cost, making large-scale deployment expensive.
Pure RL may not be sufficient for smaller models; distillation is more effective but depends on a stronger teacher model.
Distillation does not drive innovation; it only replicates existing capabilities without generating new reasoning paradigms.
Direct comparison between o1 and DeepSeek-R1 is difficult due to undisclosed details about o1's architecture and training.

papers.tEn: SmolLM2: When Smol Goes Big -- Data-Centric Training of a Small Language Model
papers.tZh: SmolLM2：小模型大作为——以数据为中心的小型语言模型训练
papers.sEn: SmolLM2, a 1.7B parameter model trained on 11 trillion tokens with multi-stage data mixing, outperforms Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama3.2-1B.
contrib: Developed SmolLM2, a 1.7B parameter small language model, achieving state-of-the-art performance among similarly sized models.
Introduced three new specialized datasets: FineMath, Stack-Edu, and SmolTalk, addressing limitations in existing public datasets.
Designed a multi-stage training process with manual rebalancing of data mixtures based on performance feedback, optimizing for small model capacity.
Demonstrated that overtrained small models can acquire abilities typically associated with larger models, such as multiple-choice formulation on MMLU.
Released SmolLM2 models and all prepared datasets to facilitate future research on small language models.
Achieved strong performance on math and code benchmarks through targeted data curation and annealing strategies.
limits: Performance on math and code benchmarks still lags behind larger models like Qwen2.5-1.5B.
Multi-stage training approach is computationally expensive and may not be feasible for all research groups.
Manual rebalancing of data mixtures relies on empirical insights and may not generalize to other model sizes or domains.
The exact cause of loss spikes during training remains undetermined, indicating potential instability.
Evaluation is limited to English-language benchmarks; performance in other languages is not assessed.

papers.tEn: Introducing deep research
papers.tZh: 深度研究功能介绍
papers.sEn: Deep research now supports MCP/app connections, trusted site restrictions, real-time progress tracking, and visual browsing, with increased monthly query limits across all tiers.
contrib: Launches deep research agent in ChatGPT for multi-step web research, synthesizing hundreds of sources into analyst-level reports.
Powered by a version of o3 optimized for browsing and data analysis, using reinforcement learning to plan and execute research trajectories.
Achieves state-of-the-art on GAIA benchmark and 26.6% on Humanity's Last Exam, outperforming prior models in chemistry, humanities, and math.
Supports file uploads, Python tool use, embedded images/graphs, and real-time progress tracking with interrupt and refine capabilities.
Demonstrates competitive sorption prediction using dual-mode sorption model for glassy polymers, with equations for pure and mixed gases.
Provides detailed market analysis for iOS translation app, recommending Japan, US, UK, Canada, Australia as primary targets.
limits: May hallucinate facts or make incorrect inferences, though at lower rate than existing ChatGPT models per internal evaluations.
Struggles with distinguishing authoritative information from rumors and shows weakness in confidence calibration.
Currently compute-intensive; high usage limits only for Pro users (100 queries/month), with slower rollout to other tiers.
Dual-mode sorption model parameters are not universal; multiple fits can yield different mixed-gas predictions, limiting reliability.
Model ignores polymer swelling/plasticization and cannot capture sigmoidal isotherms or synergistic sorption effects.

papers.tEn: Three Observations
papers.tZh: 三个观察
papers.sEn: Three observations about managing edit post logout login.
contrib: AGI intelligence scales as log of resources (training compute, data, inference compute).
Cost to use a given AI level drops ~10x every 12 months, faster than Moore's Law.
Socioeconomic value of linearly increasing intelligence is super-exponential.
AI agents will become virtual co-workers, scaling to thousands or millions.
AGI will be the biggest lever for human willfulness, enabling greater individual impact.
Open-sourcing and individual empowerment are key to balancing safety and freedom.
limits: Scaling laws may break down at extreme resource levels or for novel tasks.
Cost reduction trends may slow due to physical or algorithmic limits.
Super-exponential value growth assumes no disruptive societal or regulatory changes.
AI agents may fail on tasks requiring creativity or long-term planning.
Uneven distribution of AGI benefits could worsen inequality without policy intervention.

papers.tEn: Janus-Pro: Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation with Data and Model Scaling
papers.tZh: Janus-Pro：通过数据和模型扩展实现统一的多模态理解与生成
papers.sEn: Janus-Pro advances multimodal AI by scaling data and model size, achieving superior understanding and text-to-image generation.
contrib: Proposes Janus-Pro with optimized training strategy, expanded data, and model scaling to 7B.
Decouples visual encoding for multimodal understanding and generation to resolve task conflicts.
Introduces longer Stage I training on ImageNet and focused Stage II training on text-to-image data.
Incorporates 72M synthetic aesthetic data for stable and high-quality text-to-image generation.
Achieves state-of-the-art on MMBench (79.2) and GenEval (0.80), surpassing prior unified models.
Demonstrates strong scalability of visual encoding decoupling method from 1.5B to 7B.
limits: Input resolution limited to 384×384, affecting fine-grained tasks like OCR.
Low resolution and vision tokenizer reconstruction loss cause under-detailed images, e.g., small faces.
Training requires significant compute: 9/14 days on 16/32 nodes with 8 A100 GPUs each.
Relies on synthetic aesthetic data which may not fully capture real-world diversity.
Limited to 4096 token context window, constraining long-sequence tasks.

papers.tEn: Qwen2.5-1M Technical Report
