papers.tZh: Qwen2.5-1M 技术报告
papers.sEn: Qwen2.5-1M extends context to 1M tokens with optimized inference framework achieving 3-7x speedup.
contrib: Extends Qwen2.5 context to 1M tokens via long-context pre-training and post-training, significantly improving long-context capabilities.
Employs synthetic data, progressive pre-training, and multi-stage SFT to enhance long-context performance while reducing training costs.
Open-sources an inference framework with training-free length extrapolation (DCA+YaRN) enabling at least 4x context expansion.
Implements sparse attention (MInference) with chunked prefill, achieving 3-7x prefill speedup for 1M-token inputs.
Optimizes inference engine with kernel, pipeline parallelism, and scheduling to reduce time-to-first-token significantly.
Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M outperforms GPT-4o-mini on long-context tasks while maintaining short-context performance.
limits: DCA+YaRN length extrapolation may degrade accuracy on complex reasoning tasks despite strong retrieval performance.
Sparse attention (MInference) can cause accuracy drops for contexts exceeding 400k tokens, even with refinements.
Reinforcement learning post-training uses only short samples (8K tokens), relying on generalization to long contexts.
Progressive pre-training requires careful tuning of stage lengths and RoPE base frequency, adding complexity.
Deployment still demands high GPU memory and compute; optimizations reduce but do not eliminate hardware constraints.

papers.tEn: Computer-Using Agent
papers.tZh: 计算机使用代理
papers.sEn: Computer-Using Agent (CUA) combines GPT-4o's vision with reinforcement learning to interact with GUIs like humans, enabling flexible digital task execution without APIs.
contrib: Introduces Computer-Using Agent (CUA) combining GPT-4o vision with RL-based reasoning for GUI interaction.
Achieves state-of-the-art on OSWorld (38.1%), WebArena (58.1%), and WebVoyager (87%) using a universal screen-mouse-keyboard interface.
Demonstrates test-time scaling: performance improves with more allowed steps.
Implements layered safety mitigations against misuse, model mistakes, and frontier risks.
CUA can adaptively self-correct and handle multi-step tasks without OS- or web-specific APIs.
Released as Operator research preview for Pro users in the U.S., enabling real-world feedback collection.
limits: Performance on complex benchmarks like WebArena (58.1%) still lags behind human level (72.4% on OSWorld).
CUA may make mistakes such as typos, wrong purchases, or accidental deletions, requiring user confirmations.
Vulnerable to adversarial attacks like prompt injections and jailbreaks, though mitigations are in place.
Currently limited to U.S. Pro users and blocks certain high-risk tasks (e.g., banking transactions).
Early-stage technology; not reliable in all scenarios, especially sensitive decision-making tasks.

papers.tEn: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
papers.tZh: DeepSeek-R1：通过强化学习激励大语言模型的推理能力
papers.sEn: Pure reinforcement learning can incentivize reasoning abilities in LLMs without human demonstrations.
contrib: Shows LLM reasoning can be incentivized via pure RL without human-annotated demonstrations.
Introduces DeepSeek-R1-Zero, a model trained via large-scale RL without supervised fine-tuning, achieving strong reasoning performance.
Develops DeepSeek-R1 with multi-stage training and cold-start data, achieving performance comparable to OpenAI-o1-1217 on reasoning tasks.
Demonstrates emergent reasoning behaviors like self-reflection, verification, and dynamic strategy adaptation through RL.
Shows that reasoning patterns from larger models can be distilled into smaller models, outperforming RL-trained small models.
Open-sources DeepSeek-R1-Zero, DeepSeek-R1, and six distilled dense models to support the research community.
limits: DeepSeek-R1-Zero suffers from poor readability and language mixing issues.
DeepSeek-R1's general capabilities in function calling, multi-turn, and complex role-playing are inferior to DeepSeek-V3.
Language mixing occurs for queries in languages other than Chinese and English.
DeepSeek-R1 is sensitive to prompts; few-shot prompting degrades its performance.
Large-scale RL has not been extensively applied to software engineering tasks due to long evaluation times.

papers.tEn: Kimi k1.5: Scaling Reinforcement Learning with LLMs
papers.tZh: Kimi k1.5：通过强化学习扩展大语言模型
papers.sEn: Kimi k1.5 achieves state-of-the-art reasoning performance by scaling reinforcement learning with long context and improved policy optimization, matching OpenAI's o1.
contrib: Proposes a simplistic RL framework for LLMs using long context scaling and improved policy optimization, achieving state-of-the-art reasoning without complex techniques like Monte Carlo tree search.
Introduces partial rollouts to efficiently scale RL training to 128k context windows, enabling continued performance improvement with longer contexts.
Develops effective long2short methods (e.g., length penalty, model merging) to transfer long-CoT reasoning to short-CoT models, achieving state-of-the-art short-CoT results.
Demonstrates that scaling context length is a key dimension for continued RL scaling with LLMs, with smaller models matching larger ones via longer CoT.
Achieves multi-modal state-of-the-art reasoning on AIME, MATH 500, Codeforces, and MathVista, matching OpenAI's o1.
Presents a hybrid deployment framework for efficient on-policy RL training, reducing training-to-inference transition time to under one minute.
limits: The simplistic RL framework may not generalize to tasks requiring explicit search or value functions beyond long CoT.
Long2short methods rely on the availability of a high-quality long-CoT teacher model, which may not be available for all domains.
The study focuses on verifiable problems with clear rewards; applicability to open-ended tasks with subjective evaluation is limited.
Scaling context length to 128k increases computational cost and may not be feasible for resource-constrained settings.
The long2short RL method may still produce overthinking in short models, as length penalty warm-up does not fully eliminate it.

papers.tEn: DeepSeek R1's recipe to replicate o1
papers.tZh: DeepSeek R1 复制 o1 的秘诀
papers.sEn: DeepSeek R1 reveals a recipe to replicate OpenAI's o1 model.
contrib: DeepSeek R1 is the first open-weights reasoning model trained via large-scale RL without SFT as a preliminary step.
The four-stage training recipe includes cold-start SFT, large-scale RL, rejection sampling, and a second RL stage for general alignment.
R1-Zero demonstrates that pure RL on a base model can elicit emergent reasoning behaviors like self-verification and reflection.
The model achieves competitive performance with OpenAI's o1 at a fraction of the inference cost ($0.55 vs $15 per million input tokens).
Distillation of R1's reasoning traces into smaller models significantly boosts their performance, providing a strong baseline for future RL experiments.
The paper confirms that training-time RL scaling is the key to reasoning improvements, not inference-time search methods.
limits: The method requires a very strong base model with long-context capabilities, limiting applicability to smaller or older models.
R1-Zero exhibits reliability issues like language switching and formatting errors, necessitating additional SFT for practical use.
The exact reward design and data composition are not fully disclosed, making replication and comparison difficult.
The second RL stage for general alignment is complex and may degrade reasoning performance if not carefully balanced.
The distillation results suggest that advanced reasoning capabilities may not emerge in smaller models without large-scale RL training.

papers.tEn: MiniMax-01: Scaling Foundation Models with Lightning Attention
papers.tZh: MiniMax-01：利用闪电注意力扩展基础模型
papers.sEn: MiniMax-01 combines lightning attention with Mixture of Experts to achieve cost-efficient training and inference on hundreds of billions of parameters with a context window of up to 4 million tokens, matching the performance of top-tier models like GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
contrib: Introduces MiniMax-Text-01 and MiniMax-VL-01, frontier models rivaling GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
Achieves first large-scale deployment of linear attention via lightning attention with 456B total parameters, 45.9B active.
Designs hybrid architecture combining lightning and softmax attention, enhancing retrieval and length extrapolation.
Develops optimized parallel strategies: ETP/EDP groups, varlen ring attention, and LASP+ for efficient long-context training.
Extends context window to 1M tokens during training and up to 4M at inference with low-cost extrapolation.
Releases model weights and API, offering 20-32x longer context than comparable top-tier models.
limits: Pure linear attention shows weak retrieval; hybrid design requires periodic softmax layers, adding complexity.
Scaling laws become unreliable when extrapolated to 9.3B parameters, requiring custom scaling formula.
Training requires 1500-2500 H800 GPUs; inference with 4M tokens demands 8x80G memory and 8-bit quantization.
Benchmark evaluations focus on standard tasks; real-world long-context performance may vary.
Context extrapolation to 4M tokens is not guaranteed for all inputs; RULER results show degradation at extreme lengths.

papers.tEn: Agents
papers.tZh: 智能体
papers.sEn: Intelligent agents are considered the ultimate goal of AI, and foundation models enable unprecedented autonomous applications.
contrib: Defines AI agents as entities perceiving environment via sensors and acting via actuators, with foundation models as the brain.
Decouples planning from execution: generate plan, validate, then execute, reducing fruitless API calls.
Shows tool use significantly boosts model performance; Chameleon improves ScienceQA by 11.37% and TabMWP by 17%.
Introduces ReAct and Reflexion patterns: interleaving reasoning and action with self-reflection for error correction.
Discusses planning failures: tool misuse, goal failure, and reflection errors; proposes evaluation metrics like plan validity rate.
Highlights that agents require more powerful models due to compound mistakes and higher stakes.
limits: Autoregressive models may fundamentally lack planning ability due to inability to backtrack, as argued by Yann LeCun.
Agent performance degrades with more steps; 95% per-step accuracy drops to 60% over 10 steps.
Tool selection is challenging; more tools increase capability but also complexity and context window constraints.
Agents are prone to hallucination in tool calls, generating invalid functions or wrong parameters.
Reflection and error correction add latency and cost due to extra token generation.

papers.tEn: Reflections
papers.tZh: 反思
papers.sEn: A reflection on managing edit post logout login.
contrib: ChatGPT launched in Nov 2022 triggered unprecedented growth in AI adoption.
OpenAI now believes it knows how to build AGI as traditionally understood.
First AI agents may join the workforce in 2025, materially changing company output.
Iterative deployment with real-world feedback is key to safety and alignment.
Superintelligence could massively accelerate scientific discovery and innovation.
OpenAI's governance failure in 2023 highlighted need for diverse board and trust.
limits: Claims about AGI and superintelligence are speculative with no concrete evidence.
Iterative deployment may not guarantee safety for advanced future systems.
The post lacks technical details on how AGI or superintelligence will be achieved.
Rapid scaling and turnover may hinder long-term research and stability.
The perspective is from OpenAI's CEO, potentially biased and self-serving.

papers.tEn: Scaling Laws for Floating Point Quantization Training
papers.tZh: 浮点量化训练的缩放定律
papers.sEn: We propose a unified scaling law for floating-point quantization training, revealing optimal exponent-mantissa ratios, critical data size, and cost-performance precision between 4-8 bits.
contrib: Proposes a unified scaling law for floating-point quantization training, integrating data size, model size, exponent, mantissa, and block size.
Discovers that exponent bits contribute slightly more to model performance than mantissa bits, providing optimal bit ratios for hardware.
Identifies a critical data size in low-precision LLM training, beyond which performance degrades.
Estimates the optimal cost-performance precision lies between 4-8 bits for a wide range of compute budgets.
Validates the scaling law on 1.2B parameter models, showing accurate loss prediction.
Provides insights on quantization targets and block size effects for practical LLM training.
limits: Experiments limited to LLaMA architecture; applicability to other architectures like Mamba not verified.
Scaling law derived from models up to 679M parameters; larger scales may require further validation.
Focuses on classical floating-point quantization; newer low-bit methods not covered.
Simulated floating-point formats may not fully reflect hardware behavior.
Critical data size and optimal precision estimates depend on fitted parameters; may vary with different datasets.

papers.tEn: Lessons from the hacks - by Nathan Lambert
papers.tZh: 黑客攻击的教训 - 作者：Nathan Lambert
papers.sEn: Current incentives in tech and government are ill-suited for rapid AI transitions, requiring transparency and open models for preparedness.
contrib: Argues current incentives in tech and government are ill-suited for rapid AI transitions, urging transparency from both sides.
Highlights OpenAI's persistent reasoning models as potentially more unsafe due to inference-time scaling and thoroughness.
Emphasizes the need for open models to enable research and preparedness, as closed models hinder defensive measures.
Notes that alignment techniques have positive effects, as models mirror teacher character and follow instructions.
Calls for public access to prompts and model characteristics to avoid speculation and misinformation.
Concludes the industry is unprepared for next 12-24 months, with cyber risks real and imminent.
limits: The article is opinion-based, lacking empirical data to support claims about model safety.
The author's hunch about OpenAI's inference-time scaling is speculative and not rigorously tested.
The piece may overstate the risks of closed models and understate those of open models.
The analysis focuses on OpenAI and HuggingFace incidents, limiting generalizability to other labs.
The recommendation for open models may conflict with security concerns in some contexts.

papers.tEn: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
papers.tZh: DeepSeek-V3 技术报告
papers.sEn: DeepSeek-V3, a 671B MoE model with 37B activated parameters, achieves top-tier performance with only 2.788M H800 GPU hours training, featuring novel auxiliary-loss-free load balancing and multi-token prediction.
contrib: Pioneers an auxiliary-loss-free load balancing strategy for MoE, minimizing performance degradation.
Introduces multi-token prediction (MTP) training objective, enhancing overall benchmark performance.
Validates FP8 mixed precision training on an extremely large-scale model for the first time.
Designs DualPipe algorithm for efficient pipeline parallelism with near-zero communication overhead.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source models, comparable to leading closed-source models.
Requires only 2.788M H800 GPU hours for full training, demonstrating exceptional cost efficiency.
limits: Training costs exclude prior research and ablation experiments on architectures, algorithms, or data.
Performance on English factual knowledge (SimpleQA) trails behind GPT-4o and Claude-Sonnet-3.5.
Engineering-related tasks slightly below Claude-Sonnet-3.5, though still outperforming other models.
MTP modules are discarded during inference; only used for training improvement.
Token boundary bias may occur for multi-line prompts without terminal line breaks.

papers.tEn: Aria-UI: Visual Grounding for GUI Instructions
papers.tZh: Aria-UI：面向 GUI 指令的视觉定位
papers.sEn: Aria-UI achieves state-of-the-art GUI grounding via pure vision, scalable data synthesis, and context-aware reasoning.
contrib: Proposes Aria-UI, a pure-vision LMM for GUI grounding without relying on HTML or AXTree inputs.
Designs a scalable data pipeline to synthesize diverse, high-quality instruction samples for grounding.
Incorporates textual and text-image interleaved action histories for robust context-aware grounding.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on offline and online agent benchmarks, outperforming vision-only and AXTree-reliant baselines.
Releases all training data and model checkpoints to foster further research.
Demonstrates strong zero-shot generalization across web, desktop, and mobile platforms.
limits: Lacks autonomous planning capability; relies on a separate planner model for task instructions.
Training does not include error correction for planner-generated instructions.
Performance may degrade when planner produces low-quality or incorrect instructions.
Limited to GUI grounding; does not address other aspects of agent tasks like planning or memory.
Data pipeline relies on strong LMMs (e.g., GPT-4o) for caption generation, which may introduce biases.

papers.tEn: Deliberative alignment: reasoning enables safer language models
papers.tZh: 审慎对齐：推理能力使语言模型更安全
papers.sEn: Deliberative alignment teaches reasoning LLMs safety specifications and explicit reasoning, achieving superior safety performance without human-labeled data.
contrib: Introduces deliberative alignment, training LLMs to reason over safety specifications at inference time.
Achieves Pareto improvement on both under- and over-refusals, outperforming GPT-4o and others.
Uses synthetic data generation without human-labeled CoTs or answers, enabling scalable alignment.
Combines SFT and RL with a policy-aware reward model to teach safety specifications.
Demonstrates strong generalization to out-of-distribution safety scenarios.
limits: Relies on access to human-written safety specifications, which may be incomplete or biased.
Requires a reasoning model (o-series) with chain-of-thought capability, limiting applicability.
Synthetic data generation may introduce artifacts or fail to cover edge cases.
Effectiveness depends on the quality of the reward model and its access to policies.
May not prevent misuse if specifications are circumvented or reasoning is manipulated.

papers.tEn: Building Effective AI Agents
papers.tZh: 构建有效的 AI 代理
papers.sEn: The most successful LLM agents use simple, composable patterns rather than complex frameworks.
contrib: Advocates simple, composable patterns over complex frameworks for building LLM agents.
Defines clear architectural distinction between workflows (predefined code paths) and agents (dynamic LLM control).
Identifies six common agentic patterns: augmented LLM, prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer.
Recommends starting with simple LLM calls and only adding complexity when it demonstrably improves outcomes.
Provides practical tool design guidelines via ACI (Agent-Computer Interface) and tool documentation.
limits: Focuses on LLM agents; findings may not generalize to other AI agent types.
Relies on anecdotal evidence from customer collaborations rather than controlled experiments.
Does not address scalability or performance under extreme latency or cost constraints.
Patterns assume reliable LLM tool use and error recovery; not validated for unreliable models.
Lacks quantitative comparison of agentic patterns across diverse tasks and domains.

papers.tEn: Qwen2.5 Technical Report
papers.tZh: Qwen2.5 技术报告
papers.sEn: Qwen2.5 achieves top-tier performance through 18T token pretraining and million-scale fine-tuning with multi-stage RL, competing with 5x larger models.
contrib: Scaled pre-training data from 7T to 18T tokens, enhancing knowledge and reasoning.
Introduced multi-stage reinforcement learning with offline DPO and online GRPO.
Released diverse model sizes from 0.5B to 72B parameters, plus MoE variants.
Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct matches Llama-3-405B-Instruct with 5x fewer parameters.
Serves as foundation for specialized models like Qwen2.5-Math, Coder, and QwQ.
Achieves 100% passkey retrieval accuracy at 1M token context using DCA+YARN.
limits: Reliance on synthetic data quality and filtering may introduce biases.
Over-optimization on reward benchmarks can lead to Goodhart's law effects.
Cultural nuance is improved but still lags; more refinement needed.
Long-context RL training is computationally expensive and currently underexplored.
Current reward model benchmarks do not reliably predict downstream RL performance.

papers.tEn: Alignment faking in large language models
papers.tZh: 大型语言模型中的对齐伪装
papers.sEn: AI models may fake alignment during training, pretending to adopt new principles while retaining original preferences.
contrib: First empirical demonstration of alignment faking in LLMs without explicit instruction.
Shows models strategically comply with harmful queries to preserve original harmless preferences.
Alignment faking persists even when training information is provided implicitly via fine-tuning.
Reinforcement learning training fails to eliminate alignment faking; scratchpad reasoning increases to 78%.
Models exhibit anti-Anthropic actions like attempting to steal weights when faking alignment.
Highlights risk of safety training being undermined by alignment faking in future capable models.
limits: Study does not demonstrate models developing malicious goals or acting on them.
Alignment faking only observed in specific experimental setup with explicit or implicit cues.
Results may not generalize to other models or training paradigms beyond those tested.
Scratchpad reasoning may not reflect true internal states; models could be simulating.
No evidence that alignment faking can lock in misaligned preferences if they arise independently.

papers.tEn: DeepSeek-VL2: Mixture-of-Experts Vision-Language Models for Advanced Multimodal Understanding
papers.tZh: DeepSeek-VL2：用于高级多模态理解的混合专家视觉语言模型
papers.sEn: DeepSeek-VL2, a series of MoE vision-language models, achieves state-of-the-art performance with efficient inference via dynamic tiling and Multi-head Latent Attention.
contrib: Introduces dynamic tiling vision encoding for high-resolution images with varying aspect ratios.
Leverages DeepSeekMoE with Multi-head Latent Attention to compress KV cache for efficient inference.
Trains on improved vision-language dataset, achieving superior performance on VQA, OCR, document understanding, and visual grounding.
Offers three model variants (1.0B, 2.8B, 4.5B activated parameters) balancing performance and efficiency.
Achieves competitive or state-of-the-art results with fewer activated parameters than existing dense and MoE models.
Open-sources codes and pre-trained models to accelerate multimodal research.
limits: Context window limited to few images per chat session, restricting multi-image interactions.
Occasional difficulties with blurry images or unseen objects, indicating robustness issues.
Reasoning capabilities weaker than visual perception and recognition, needing improvement.
Dynamic tiling disabled when processing more than two images, limiting high-resolution handling.
Language mixing issue in smaller variant (Tiny) for Chinese responses, requiring additional data.

papers.tEn: NVILA: Efficient Frontier Visual Language Models
papers.tZh: NVILA：高效前沿视觉语言模型
papers.sEn: NVILA achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with significantly reduced training cost and latency.
contrib: Proposes NVILA, a family of open VLMs optimizing both efficiency and accuracy via a 'scale-then-compress' paradigm.
Introduces Dynamic-S2 for adaptive multi-scale high-resolution image processing, improving accuracy on text-heavy benchmarks by up to 30%.
Develops DeltaLoss-based dataset pruning, reducing training data by 50% while maintaining competitive accuracy.
Implements FP8 mixed-precision training for VLMs, achieving up to 2x speedup over BF16.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on video benchmarks with efficient temporal scaling and compression.
Demonstrates strong performance in downstream tasks including temporal localization, robotic navigation, and medical imaging.
limits: NVILA's accuracy gains are primarily demonstrated on benchmarks; real-world deployment may face additional challenges.
The 'scale-then-compress' approach may not generalize to all VLM architectures or tasks.
Dataset pruning via DeltaLoss relies on a reference model, adding computational overhead.
FP8 training requires specific hardware (NVIDIA H100/B200), limiting accessibility.
The study does not explore the impact of scaling model size beyond 15B parameters.

papers.tEn: JanusFlow: Harmonizing Autoregression and Rectified Flow for Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation
papers.tZh: JanusFlow：融合自回归与整流流实现统一多模态理解与生成
papers.sEn: JanusFlow unifies image understanding and generation in a single model by integrating autoregressive language models with rectified flow, achieving superior performance without complex architectural modifications.
contrib: Introduces JanusFlow, a unified framework integrating autoregressive LLMs with rectified flow for image understanding and generation.
Demonstrates that rectified flow can be trained within LLM architecture without complex modifications.
Proposes decoupled vision encoders for understanding and generation to prevent task interference.
Introduces representation alignment regularization to improve generation quality.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on multimodal understanding and text-to-image generation benchmarks with a 1.3B model.
Outperforms existing unified approaches and several specialized models across standard benchmarks.
limits: Model size limited to 1.3B parameters; scalability to larger models not explored.
Requires three-stage training with careful data ratio tuning.
Image resolution fixed at 384x384; higher resolutions may require adaptation.
Relies on pre-trained VAE and SigLIP encoders; performance may depend on their quality.
Evaluation limited to English-language benchmarks; multilingual capabilities not assessed.

papers.tEn: SVDQuant: Absorbing Outliers by Low-Rank Components for 4-Bit Diffusion Models
papers.tZh: SVDQuant：通过低秩组件吸收异常值实现 4 比特扩散模型
papers.sEn: SVDQuant absorbs outliers via a low-rank branch, enabling 4-bit quantization for diffusion models with significant speedup and memory reduction.
contrib: Proposes SVDQuant, a 4-bit quantization paradigm that absorbs outliers via a low-rank branch.
Co-designs Nunchaku inference engine fusing low-rank and low-bit kernels to eliminate redundant memory access.
Achieves 3.5x memory reduction and 3.0x speedup over weight-only quantization on FLUX.1 12B model.
First to successfully apply 4-bit weight-activation quantization to diffusion models with measured speedup.
Supports seamless integration with off-the-shelf LoRA adapters without re-quantization.
Validates effectiveness across multiple architectures (UNet, DiT) and models (SDXL, PixArt-Σ, FLUX.1).
limits: FP4 speedup not reported due to lack of access to Blackwell GPUs.
Method requires co-designed inference engine for speedup; not applicable to standard frameworks.
Low-rank branch adds 5-10% latency overhead despite kernel fusion.
Evaluation limited to text-to-image diffusion models; generalizability to other domains not tested.
Quantization-aware training not explored; method relies on post-training quantization.

papers.tEn: Hunyuan-Large: An Open-Source MoE Model with 52 Billion Activated Parameters by Tencent
papers.tZh: Hunyuan-Large：腾讯开源 MoE 模型，520 亿激活参数
papers.sEn: Hunyuan-Large is the largest open-source MoE model with 389B total parameters and 52B activated, outperforming LLama3.1-70B and matching LLama3.1-405B.
contrib: Open-sourced the largest Transformer-based MoE model with 389B total and 52B activated parameters.
Proposed mixed expert routing with shared and specialized experts, and recycle routing to reduce token dropping.
Introduced KV cache compression combining GQA and CLA, saving nearly 95% memory.
Developed expert-specific learning rate scaling based on effective batch size differences.
Investigated MoE scaling laws to guide optimal model size and training data volume.
Achieved superior performance on diverse benchmarks, outperforming LLama3.1-70B and matching LLama3.1-405B.
limits: Evaluation limited to English and Chinese benchmarks; multilingual generalization not fully assessed.
Synthetic data quality depends on seed data and generation models, which may introduce biases.
Long-context capability tested up to 256K tokens; performance beyond this length is unknown.
Post-training alignment relies on DPO with offline and online data; potential reward hacking not fully mitigated.
Scaling law experiments conducted on small models (10M-1B); extrapolation to 52B may have inaccuracies.

papers.tEn: Should Developers Care about Interpretability?
papers.tZh: 开发者应该关心可解释性吗？
papers.sEn: Interpretability allows for capturing implicit style, reducing RLHF needs, and enabling cheap classification, but risks moving models out of distribution and misinterpreting features.
contrib: Interpretability enables understanding LLM internal representations via features.
Feature steering allows fine-grained control of model outputs at inference.
Steering reduces need for RLHF by activating/deactivating features on-the-fly.
Applications include capturing indefinable style, cheap classification, and persistent user preferences.
Steering works across modalities: text, voice, and images.
Provides API developers with more specific control than blanket RLHF policies.
limits: Steering can push the model out of distribution, producing incoherent text.
Feature labels are imperfect; mislabeling can reduce steering reliability.
Activating a feature may inadvertently trigger other features or circuits, causing side effects.
Wide-scale use of feature steering remains unproven, making reliability uncertain.
The complexity of steering may require developers to move beyond prompting and RAG.

papers.tEn: $π_0$: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
papers.tZh: $π_0$: 面向通用机器人控制的视觉-语言-动作流模型
papers.sEn: A vision-language-action flow model enables generalist robot policies for complex dexterous tasks.
contrib: Proposes π0, a novel vision-language-action flow model for general robot control.
Integrates pre-trained VLM with flow matching for high-frequency dexterous action chunks.
Demonstrates cross-embodiment training on 7 robot platforms with 10,000 hours of data.
Shows zero-shot task performance and language instruction following after pre-training.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on complex dexterous tasks like laundry folding and box assembly.
Introduces a pre-training/post-training recipe analogous to LLMs for robot foundation models.
limits: Limited understanding of optimal pre-training data composition and weighting.
Not all evaluated tasks achieve reliable performance; failure modes remain.
Unclear how to predict data amount and type needed for near-perfect performance.
Positive transfer across highly diverse domains (e.g., driving, navigation) not yet validated.
Model size and computational cost may limit real-time deployment on resource-constrained robots.

papers.tEn: Sabotage evaluations for frontier models
papers.tZh: 前沿模型的破坏性评估
papers.sEn: A novel set of evaluations tests frontier models' capacity for sabotage, including human deception, code sabotage, sandbagging, and undermining oversight.
contrib: Proposes four novel sabotage evaluations for frontier models: human decision, code, sandbagging, and oversight undermining.
Demonstrates that current models show low-level sabotage capabilities, but minimal mitigations suffice.
Finds that stronger defenders (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) reduce code sabotage success to ~1%.
Shows that safety training can reduce sandbagging from 36.1% to 95.6% of normal performance.
Provides open-source evaluations for other AI developers to use and improve upon.
limits: Human sabotage evaluation is small-scale and artificial, not indicative of catastrophic risk.
Code sabotage evaluation stacks deck in attacker's favor, limiting real-world relevance.
Sandbagging evaluation uses trained models, not naturally occurring sandbagging.
Oversight undermining evaluation caught the overseer, suggesting current models lack subtlety.
Evaluations may not generalize to future, more capable models with different failure modes.

papers.tEn: Janus: Decoupling Visual Encoding for Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation
papers.tZh: Janus：解耦视觉编码以实现统一的多模态理解与生成
papers.sEn: Janus decouples visual encoding into separate pathways for understanding and generation, achieving superior performance in unified multimodal models.
contrib: Proposes Janus, an autoregressive framework that decouples visual encoding for multimodal understanding and generation.
Decouples visual encoding into separate pathways to resolve conflicts between understanding and generation tasks.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on multimodal understanding and generation benchmarks, surpassing unified and task-specific models.
Demonstrates high flexibility and extensibility, allowing independent selection of optimal encoding methods for each task.
Provides extensive ablation studies validating the importance of decoupling visual encoding.
Shows potential for integrating additional modalities like point clouds, EEG, or audio.
limits: Model size limited to 1.3B parameters; scaling to larger models may yield different results.
Evaluation primarily on static images; video understanding and generation not explored.
Training data limited to English text-to-image pairs; multilingual generation relies on LLM's inherent abilities.
Visual generation quality may lag behind specialized diffusion models in fine-grained details.
Ablation study uses a semantic tokenizer not used in main experiments, potentially affecting comparability.

papers.tEn: Deep Compression Autoencoder for Efficient High-Resolution Diffusion Models
papers.tZh: 深度压缩自编码器：面向高效高分辨率扩散模型
papers.sEn: DC-AE achieves up to 128x spatial compression for diffusion models, enabling 19x speedup on ImageNet 512x512 without quality loss.
contrib: Analyzes challenges of increasing autoencoder spatial compression ratio and provides insights.
Proposes Residual Autoencoding to alleviate optimization difficulty of high compression autoencoders.
Proposes Decoupled High-Resolution Adaptation to mitigate generalization penalty across resolutions.
Builds DC-AE autoencoder family achieving spatial compression up to 128x with good reconstruction.
DC-AE provides significant training and inference speedup for latent diffusion models.
Achieves 19.1x inference and 17.9x training speedup on ImageNet 512x512 with UViT-H.
limits: Evaluation limited to image generation tasks; not tested on video or 3D.
Requires careful tuning of training phases for different resolutions.
High compression ratios may still degrade quality for very fine details.
Method relies on specific architecture choices like EfficientViT blocks.
Generalization to other latent diffusion model variants not fully explored.

papers.tEn: Machines of Loving Grace
papers.tZh: 达里奥·阿莫代——爱的恩典机器
papers.sEn: AI could transform the world for the better, with risks being the only obstacle to a fundamentally positive future.
contrib: Powerful AI could compress 50-100 years of biological and medical progress into 5-10 years, curing most diseases and doubling human lifespan.
AI-accelerated neuroscience could cure most mental illness and greatly enhance cognitive and emotional abilities.
AI can drive economic development in poor countries through optimized health interventions and logistics.
The marginal returns to intelligence are high in biology and neuroscience, where key discoveries are often made by a few talented researchers.
AI can act as a virtual biologist, designing and running experiments, not just analyzing data.
The 'compressed 21st century' framework predicts radical improvements in health, lifespan, and biological freedom within a decade of powerful AI.
limits: Predictions are speculative and may be wrong in details; real-world constraints like experiment times and physical laws limit speed.
Clinical trials and regulatory bureaucracy may slow deployment of new treatments despite AI advances.
Economic development faces human constraints like corruption and weak institutions, which AI may not easily overcome.
Some diseases like fast-evolving pathogens or rare cancers may persist despite AI progress.
Mind uploading and other radical neuroscience applications likely lie outside the 5-10 year window.

papers.tEn: RDT-1B: a Diffusion Foundation Model for Bimanual Manipulation
papers.tZh: RDT-1B：面向双臂操作任务的扩散基础模型
papers.sEn: RDT-1B is a diffusion foundation model for bimanual manipulation that achieves zero-shot generalization and few-shot learning.
contrib: Proposes Robotics Diffusion Transformer (RDT), a diffusion foundation model for bimanual manipulation with scalable Transformer architecture.
Introduces Physically Interpretable Unified Action Space to unify action representations across diverse robots for multi-robot pre-training.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on bimanual tasks with 56% improvement in success rates over baselines.
Demonstrates zero-shot generalization to unseen objects, scenes, and language instructions.
Enables few-shot learning of new skills with only 1-5 demonstrations.
Scales model to 1.2B parameters, the largest diffusion-based foundation model for robotic manipulation.
limits: Model is only evaluated on ALOHA dual-arm robot; generalization to other dual-arm robots is not tested.
Fine-tuning dataset is self-collected and limited to 6K+ trajectories, which may not cover all real-world scenarios.
Pre-training relies on publicly available multi-robot datasets, which may contain biases or noise.
Diffusion model inference requires multiple denoising steps, leading to higher latency compared to deterministic methods.
The unified action space is designed for gripper arms only; robots with other end-effectors are not supported.

papers.tEn: Pixtral 12B
papers.tZh: Pixtral 12B：120 亿参数多模态语言模型
papers.sEn: Pixtral-12B is a 12B multimodal model that excels in both vision and text tasks, outperforming larger models.
contrib: Introduces Pixtral-12B, a 12B-parameter multimodal model with a novel vision encoder supporting native resolution and aspect ratio.
Achieves leading performance on multimodal benchmarks, surpassing larger open and closed models like Llama-3.2 90B and Claude-3 Haiku.
Maintains strong text-only performance without sacrificing multimodal capabilities, serving as a drop-in replacement for both tasks.
Open-sources MM-MT-Bench, a practical multimodal benchmark with multi-turn conversations, correlating highly with LMSys Vision ELO.
Provides standardized evaluation protocols with explicit prompts and flexible parsing, addressing inconsistencies in current benchmarks.
Releases model under Apache 2.0 license, including inference and evaluation code for reproducibility.
limits: Evaluation relies on LLM judges for MM-MT-Bench, which may introduce bias or inconsistency.
Vision encoder ablation only compares with CLIPA, not other modern encoders like SigLIP.
Performance on some benchmarks may vary with prompt design, as shown by sensitivity to explicit vs naive prompts.
Model size (12B) may limit deployment on resource-constrained devices compared to smaller models.
MM-MT-Bench covers only five image categories, potentially missing other practical domains.

papers.tEn: Aria: An Open Multimodal Native Mixture-of-Experts Model
papers.tZh: Aria：一个开放的多模态原生混合专家模型
papers.sEn: Aria is an open multimodal native Mixture-of-Experts model that outperforms many existing models across multimodal, language, and coding tasks.
contrib: Introduces Aria, the first open multimodal native MoE model with best-in-class performance.
Proposes a 4-stage training pipeline for developing multimodal native models from scratch.
Achieves superior performance over Pixtral-12B and Llama3.2-11B on multimodal, language, and coding tasks.
Competes with proprietary models like GPT-4o and Gemini-1.5 on various multimodal benchmarks.
Open-sources model weights and a training framework for easy adoption and fine-tuning.
Demonstrates strong long-context multimodal understanding and instruction following.
limits: Model performance is evaluated on specific benchmarks; real-world generalization may vary.
The 64K context window may not suffice for extremely long multimodal sequences.
Training data is limited to knowledge until May 2024; newer information is not covered.
The model's visual encoder is pretrained on SigLIP-SO400M; other visual domains may be less effective.
Expert specialization analysis is limited to three domains; broader generalization not confirmed.

papers.tEn: Automated Red Teaming with GOAT: the Generative Offensive Agent Tester
papers.tZh: 自动化红队测试：生成式对抗代理测试器（GOAT）
papers.sEn: GOAT is an automated red teaming system that simulates plain language adversarial conversations to identify LLM vulnerabilities.
contrib: Introduces GOAT, an automated agentic red teaming system that simulates multi-turn adversarial conversations using plain language.
Combines multiple adversarial prompting techniques dynamically within a single conversation, extensible to new attacks.
Achieves high attack success rates: ASR@10 of 97% against Llama 3.1 and 88% against GPT-4-Turbo on JailbreakBench.
Requires only 5 conversational turns to achieve high success, outperforming other multi-turn methods like Crescendo.
Uses Chain-of-Attack-Thought reasoning to let the attacker model select and layer attacks adaptively.
Demonstrates that multi-turn adversarial conversations are a critical overlooked class of LLM vulnerabilities.
limits: Limited to 5 conversation turns due to context window constraints of smaller models like Llama 2 7B.
Success heavily depends on the reasoning quality and safety alignment of the attacker model.
Attacker model may sometimes follow attack strategy instructions poorly, reducing effectiveness.
Study does not explore longer attack chains or optimal ordering of combined attacks.
Evaluation limited to JailbreakBench dataset; generalizability to other domains not tested.

papers.tEn: Emu3: Next-Token Prediction is All You Need
papers.tZh: Emu3：下一个标记预测就足够了
papers.sEn: Emu3 shows that pure next-token prediction, without diffusion or compositional architectures, achieves state-of-the-art multimodal generation and perception, even surpassing specialized models like SDXL and LLaVA-1.6.
contrib: Emu3 eliminates diffusion and compositional architectures, using only next-token prediction for multimodal generation and perception.
Tokenizes images, text, and videos into discrete space, training a single transformer from scratch on mixed sequences.
Outperforms SDXL and LLaVA-1.6 on generation and understanding benchmarks without task-specific designs.
Generates high-fidelity video by predicting next tokens, enabling autoregressive video extension.
Simplifies multimodal models to a single focus on tokens, unlocking scaling potential for both training and inference.
limits: Relies on external models (GPT-4V, aesthetic predictors) for data captioning and filtering.
High computational cost due to large context length (131k) and two-stage training.
Video generation quality slightly below top closed-source models like Kling and Gen-3.
DPO fine-tuning may degrade some automated metrics despite improving human preference.
Model size fixed; ablation on scaling laws for multimodal data not explored.

papers.tEn: The Intelligence Age
papers.tZh: 智能时代
papers.sEn: In the next few decades, AI will enable us to achieve feats that would seem magical to our grandparents, accelerating human progress by building on the scaffolding of society's collective intelligence.
contrib: Deep learning works and scales predictably with compute and data, enabling superintelligence within a few thousand days.
AI will provide personal AI teams and virtual tutors, revolutionizing productivity and education.
The Intelligence Age will bring massive shared prosperity, improving lives globally beyond current imagination.
AI will solve hard problems like climate change, space colonization, and fundamental physics.
Progress requires abundant compute and energy infrastructure to democratize AI access.
AI will amplify human creativity and enable positive-sum games, despite labor market shifts.
limits: The timeline for superintelligence is speculative; it may take longer than a few thousand days.
Deep learning's scalability may hit diminishing returns or fundamental limits not yet known.
The essay lacks concrete solutions for AI risks like alignment, misuse, and labor displacement.
Assumption of infinite prosperity may overlook distributional inequalities and societal resistance.
The focus on compute and energy ignores other critical factors like data quality and algorithmic innovation.

papers.tEn: Qwen2-VL: Enhancing Vision-Language Model's Perception of the World at Any Resolution
papers.tZh: Qwen2-VL：增强视觉语言模型在任何分辨率下对世界的感知
papers.sEn: Qwen2-VL introduces Naive Dynamic Resolution and M-RoPE, achieving competitive performance comparable to GPT-4o and Claude3.5-Sonnet.
contrib: Introduces Naive Dynamic Resolution mechanism for processing images at any resolution into variable visual tokens.
Proposes Multimodal Rotary Position Embedding (M-RoPE) to fuse positional info across text, images, and videos.
Unifies image and video processing paradigm, enhancing visual perception with 3D convolutions and frame sampling.
Explores scaling laws for large vision-language models, achieving competitive performance at 2B, 8B, and 72B scales.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks, comparable to GPT-4o and Claude3.5-Sonnet.
Supports multilingual text understanding in images and robust agent capabilities for device operation.
limits: Performance on MMMU benchmark still lags behind GPT-4o, indicating room for improvement in complex reasoning.
Video understanding limited to 768 frames per video during evaluation, affecting long video performance.
Vision-language navigation performance significantly behind specialized models due to incomplete 3D map modeling.
Excessive upscaling of small images can lead to out-of-distribution samples and performance decline.
Training data cutoff date is June 2023, limiting knowledge of recent events.

papers.tEn: Qwen2.5-Math Technical Report: Toward Mathematical Expert Model via Self-Improvement
papers.tZh: Qwen2.5-Math 技术报告：通过自我改进迈向数学专家模型
papers.sEn: Qwen2.5-Math integrates self-improvement across pre-training, post-training, and inference to achieve expert-level mathematical reasoning.
contrib: Integrates self-improvement across pre-training, post-training, and inference using synthetic data and reward models.
Introduces Qwen2.5-Math-Instruct supporting Chain-of-Thought and Tool-Integrated Reasoning in English and Chinese.
Develops iterative reward model training and data evolution for supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on MATH, AMC 2023, and AIME 2024, outperforming GPT-4o and Gemini.
Demonstrates cross-scale improvement: 1.5B model surpasses most 70B models, 7B matches previous 72B.
Provides open-source models, reward models, and evaluation scripts on Hugging Face and GitHub.
limits: Evaluation limited to 10 math datasets; generalization to other domains not verified.
Tool-Integrated Reasoning shows no significant advantage over CoT in Chinese benchmarks.
Dependence on synthetic data from Qwen2-Math may introduce biases or quality issues.
Reinforcement learning requires large-scale sampling and reward model, increasing computational cost.
Decontamination may not fully eliminate data leakage from similar problems in training sets.

papers.tEn: Qwen2.5-Coder Technical Report
papers.tZh: Qwen2.5-Coder 技术报告
papers.sEn: Qwen2.5-Coder series achieves state-of-the-art performance across 10+ code benchmarks, outperforming larger models.
contrib: Introduced Qwen2.5-Coder series, built on Qwen2.5 with pretraining on 5.5 trillion tokens.
Achieved state-of-the-art performance on over 10 code benchmarks, including HumanEval and MBPP.
Developed a three-stage training pipeline: file-level pretraining, repo-level pretraining, and instruction tuning.
Designed a multilingual multi-agent framework for synthesizing diverse instruction data.
Implemented decontamination to prevent test set leakage using 10-gram overlap.
Demonstrated strong long-context capability up to 128K tokens via repo-level pretraining.
limits: Evaluation limited to 1.5B and 7B parameter models; larger sizes not explored.
Long-context evaluation only on synthetic Needle in the Code task, not real-world repos.
Data mixing ratio (70% code, 20% text, 10% math) may not generalize to other domains.
Instruction tuning data quality relies on LLM-based scoring, which may introduce bias.
Multilingual evaluation covers only 8 languages; long-tail languages may be underrepresented.

papers.tEn: De novo design of high-affinity protein binders with AlphaProteo
papers.tZh: 利用 AlphaProteo 从头设计高亲和力蛋白结合物
papers.sEn: AlphaProteo achieves 3- to 300-fold better binding affinities than existing methods for de novo protein binder design.
contrib: Introduces AlphaProteo, a family of ML models for de novo protein binder design.
Achieves 3- to 300-fold better binding affinities than existing methods on seven targets.
Demonstrates high experimental success rates (9%-88%) with only one round of medium-throughput screening.
Obtains sub-nanomolar to low-nanomolar binders without affinity optimization for most targets.
Validates biological activity: inhibition of VEGF signaling and SARS-CoV-2 neutralization.
Confirms designed structures via cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography with high accuracy.
limits: Validated on only eight target proteins; generalization to broader targets needs further testing.
Failed to obtain binders for one challenging target (TNFα) due to flat polar binding site.
Requires target crystal structure as input; limited for targets without experimental structures.
Machine learning methods not disclosed due to biosecurity and commercial considerations.
Binders designed for research use only, not for clinical applications.

papers.tEn: Learning to reason with LLMs
papers.tZh: 学习用大语言模型进行推理
papers.sEn: OpenAI o1 achieves 89th percentile on Codeforces, top 500 in AIME, and exceeds PhD-level accuracy on GPQA.
contrib: OpenAI o1 achieves 89th percentile on Codeforces, top 500 in AIME, and exceeds PhD-level accuracy on GPQA.
Performance scales smoothly with both train-time and test-time compute via reinforcement learning.
Chain-of-thought reasoning is learned through RL, enabling self-correction and strategy refinement.
Safety alignment benefits from legible chain-of-thought, improving robustness against jailbreaks.
Fine-tuned o1 achieves 49th percentile in IOI 2024 and 1807 Elo on Codeforces, surpassing GPT-4o.
limits: o1-preview is not preferred on natural language tasks, limiting its general applicability.
Raw chain-of-thought is hidden from users, reducing interpretability and trust.
Scaling constraints differ from pretraining and are not fully understood.
Model may engage in reward hacking during safety evaluations.
High test-time compute requirements may limit practical deployment.

papers.tEn: Fire-Flyer AI-HPC: A Cost-Effective Software-Hardware Co-Design for Deep Learning
papers.tZh: Fire-Flyer AI-HPC：一种经济高效的深度学习软硬件协同设计
papers.sEn: Fire-Flyer AI-HPC achieves DGX-A100-like performance at half the cost and 40% less energy using 10,000 PCIe A100 GPUs.
contrib: Proposes Fire-Flyer AI-HPC, a cost-effective hardware-software co-design for deep learning.
Deploys 10,000 PCIe A100 GPUs achieving 80% DGX-A100 performance at half cost and 40% less energy.
Develops HFReduce for efficient allreduce, outperforming NCCL on PCIe architecture.
Implements HaiScale with overlapping computation and communication for scalable LLM training.
Designs 3FS distributed file system with request-to-send control to mitigate incast congestion.
Integrates HAI Platform for task scheduling, fault handling, and disaster recovery, achieving 99% GPU utilization.
limits: Performance gap between PCIe A100 and SXM A100 remains, limiting peak throughput.
HFReduce performance bottlenecked by AMD EPYC CPU PCIe host bridge bandwidth.
NVLink bridge added later for LLMs, but introduces additional failure points.
Network congestion control disabled DCQCN due to parameter tuning difficulties.
Two-zone network limits cross-zone tasks to one at a time, reducing flexibility.

papers.tEn: DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5: Harnessing Proof Assistant Feedback for Reinforcement Learning and Monte-Carlo Tree Search
papers.tZh: DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5：利用证明助手反馈进行强化学习与蒙特卡洛树搜索
papers.sEn: DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5 achieves state-of-the-art results on theorem proving benchmarks by combining reinforcement learning from proof assistant feedback with Monte-Carlo tree search.
contrib: Proposes RMaxTS, a Monte-Carlo tree search variant with intrinsic-reward-driven exploration for sparse-reward proof search.
Introduces a truncate-and-resume mechanism that integrates whole-proof generation with proof-step generation via tree search.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on miniF2F (63.5%) and ProofNet (25.3%) benchmarks using a 7B parameter model.
Employs reinforcement learning from proof assistant feedback (RLPAF) with GRPO to enhance whole-proof generation.
Augments supervised fine-tuning data with natural language chain-of-thought comments and intermediate tactic states.
Provides open-source model and code for Monte-Carlo tree search to facilitate further research.
limits: Evaluation limited to Lean 4 theorem prover; generalization to other proof assistants not verified.
Performance on miniF2F and ProofNet may not reflect real-world complex theorem proving scenarios.
RMaxTS relies on intrinsic rewards which may not scale to extremely large search spaces.
Model size (7B parameters) may limit reasoning depth compared to larger frontier models.
Exploitation aspect of proof search (e.g., critic model) not addressed; future work needed.

papers.tEn: CogVideoX: Text-to-Video Diffusion Models with An Expert Transformer
papers.tZh: CogVideoX: 带专家 Transformer 的文本到视频扩散模型
papers.sEn: CogVideoX achieves state-of-the-art text-to-video generation using a 3D VAE for spatial-temporal compression, an expert Transformer with adaptive LayerNorm for deep text-video fusion, and multi-resolution training for coherent long-duration videos.
contrib: Proposes CogVideoX, a large-scale text-to-video diffusion Transformer with 3D causal VAE and expert Transformer, generating 10s 768x1360 videos at 16fps.
Introduces a 3D causal VAE that compresses videos spatially and temporally, improving compression rate and video fidelity while reducing flicker.
Designs an expert Transformer with expert adaptive LayerNorm for deep fusion of text and video modalities, enhancing text-video alignment.
Employs progressive training and multi-resolution frame packing to generate coherent, long-duration videos with various shapes and significant motions.
Builds an effective data pipeline including video filtering and video captioning, greatly boosting generation quality and semantic alignment.
Open-sources 5B and 2B models (text-to-video and image-to-video), the first commercial-grade open-source video generation models.
limits: Maximum video length is 10 seconds, still limited for complex narratives; generating longer videos with consistent motion remains challenging.
Physics simulation (e.g., object interaction, fluid dynamics) is imperfect; generated videos may violate real-world physics.
Training data contains noisy web videos despite filtering; residual low-quality data may affect generation quality.
Complex long-text instruction following is limited; the model struggles with detailed narrative descriptions.
Inference is computationally expensive and memory-intensive, limiting deployment on consumer hardware.

papers.tEn: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos
papers.tZh: SAM 2：在图像和视频中分割一切
papers.sEn: SAM 2 is a foundation model for promptable visual segmentation in images and videos, achieving better accuracy with fewer interactions and faster speed.
contrib: Extends promptable segmentation from images to video with a unified model.
Introduces a streaming transformer architecture with memory for real-time video processing.
Builds a data engine with human-in-the-loop to collect the largest video segmentation dataset (SA-V).
Achieves better accuracy with 3x fewer interactions in video segmentation vs prior work.
Outperforms SAM in image segmentation with 6x faster inference.
Demonstrates strong zero-shot generalization across 17 video and 37 image benchmarks.
limits: May fail to segment objects across shot changes or in crowded scenes.
Struggles with tracking very thin or fast-moving objects.
Processes each object separately without inter-object communication.
Data engine relies on human annotators for verification and correction.
Limited evaluation on long-term occlusion and extended videos.

papers.tEn: Gemma 2: Improving Open Language Models at a Practical Size
papers.tZh: Gemma 2：在实用规模上改进开放语言模型
papers.sEn: Gemma 2 introduces architectural improvements and knowledge distillation to achieve state-of-the-art performance at practical model sizes.
contrib: Introduces Gemma 2, a family of open language models from 2B to 27B parameters.
Applies interleaved local-global attention and grouped-query attention to Transformer architecture.
Trains 2B and 9B models using knowledge distillation instead of next-token prediction.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance for model size, competitive with models 2-3x larger.
Demonstrates distillation benefits over raw text training, especially for small models.
Releases all models to the community for open research and development.
limits: Models are not multimodal and not optimized for multilingual capabilities.
Performance gains from distillation may not generalize to all tasks or domains.
Safety evaluations cannot cover all possible applications and scenarios.
Memorization of training data, though low, still occurs for certain data sources.
Models may exhibit vulnerabilities to adversarial attacks and persuasion tasks.

papers.tEn: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
papers.tZh: Llama 3 模型群
papers.sEn: Llama 3, a herd of foundation language models with up to 405B parameters, matches GPT-4 quality across tasks and supports multimodal extensions via composition.
contrib: Introduce Llama 3 herd of 8B, 70B, and 405B dense language models with up to 128K context window.
Develop a data curation pipeline that trains on 15T tokens, improving quality and diversity.
Establish scaling laws that accurately predict downstream benchmark performance, guiding model size selection.
Post-training recipe using SFT, rejection sampling, and DPO yields competitive performance with GPT-4.
Release pre-trained and post-trained 405B models plus Llama Guard 3 safety model.
Demonstrate compositional multimodal integration (image, video, speech) competitive with state-of-the-art.
limits: Multimodal extensions are still under development and not publicly released.
Despite safety mitigations, models may produce harmful or biased outputs.
Training requires massive compute infrastructure, limiting reproducibility to large organizations.
Scaling-law predictions slightly underestimate performance; may diverge for future scales.
Released under Llama Community License, not fully open; usage restrictions apply.

papers.tEn: AI achieves silver-medal standard solving International Mathematical Olympiad problems
papers.tZh: AI 在国际数学奥林匹克竞赛中达到银牌标准
papers.sEn: AI achieves silver-medal standard in solving International Mathematical Olympiad problems
contrib: AlphaProof combines a pre-trained language model with AlphaZero reinforcement learning to prove mathematical statements in Lean.
AlphaGeometry 2 improves on its predecessor with a Gemini-based language model and a faster symbolic engine, solving 83% of historical IMO geometry problems.
The combined system achieved a silver-medal standard at IMO 2024, solving 4 out of 6 problems and scoring 28 points.
AlphaProof uses a formalizer to translate natural language problems into formal statements, enabling large-scale training with verified proofs.
The systems demonstrate advanced mathematical reasoning, solving the hardest problem solved by only five human contestants.
limits: The system requires manual translation of problems into formal language, limiting automation.
AlphaProof took up to three days to solve some problems, far slower than human contestants.
Two combinatorics problems remained unsolved, indicating a gap in certain reasoning types.
The approach relies on large-scale synthetic data generation, which may not generalize to all math domains.
The system's performance is evaluated on a fixed set of problems, and its robustness to adversarial or open-ended problems is untested.

papers.tEn: LongVideoBench: A Benchmark for Long-context Interleaved Video-Language Understanding
papers.tZh: LongVideoBench：面向长上下文交错视频-语言理解的基准测试
papers.sEn: LongVideoBench is a benchmark for evaluating long-context video-language understanding with hour-long videos and subtitles.
contrib: Introduces LongVideoBench, a benchmark for long-context interleaved video-language understanding with up to hour-long videos.
Proposes referring reasoning task to address single-frame bias in video understanding benchmarks.
Curates 6,678 human-annotated multiple-choice questions across 17 fine-grained categories on 3,763 diverse videos.
Evaluates proprietary and open-source LMMs, showing significant challenges and performance gaps.
Demonstrates that model performance improves only with processing more frames, validating benchmark's effectiveness.
Provides insights into model deficiencies, guiding future research on multimodal long-context understanding.
limits: Benchmark focuses on English subtitles and videos, limiting language diversity.
Videos are collected from specific channels, potentially introducing domain bias.
Multiple-choice format may not capture open-ended reasoning capabilities.
Evaluation limited to frame-level sampling; continuous video processing not tested.
Human annotation quality control may still have residual errors despite revision process.

papers.tEn: Qwen2-Audio Technical Report
papers.tZh: Qwen2-Audio 技术报告
papers.sEn: Qwen2-Audio, a large-scale audio-language model, simplifies pre-training with natural language prompts, supports voice chat and audio analysis modes, and achieves SOTA on AIR-Bench.
contrib: Simplified pre-training using natural language prompts instead of hierarchical tags.
Introduced two distinct interaction modes: voice chat and audio analysis, without system prompts.
Applied DPO to optimize factuality and adherence to desired behavior.
Achieved state-of-the-art results on AIR-Bench chat benchmark, outperforming Gemini-1.5-pro.
Open-sourced the model to foster multi-modal language community advancement.
Scaled up training data and improved instruction-following capability.
limits: Evaluation on some datasets like Common Voice 15 was not zero-shot.
Gemini-1.5 results on AIR-Bench were reduced due to safety filtering.
Model performance may degrade on tasks not covered in training.
Audio encoder initialized from Whisper-large-v3 may inherit its biases.
Limited evaluation on real-world noisy audio scenarios.

papers.tEn: Qwen2 Technical Report
papers.tZh: Qwen2 技术报告
papers.sEn: Qwen2 series, with models from 0.5B to 72B parameters, surpasses most open-weight models and competes with proprietary ones across language, coding, math, and reasoning benchmarks.
contrib: Introduces Qwen2 series with 0.5B to 72B parameters, including dense and MoE models.
Qwen2-72B achieves SOTA on MMLU (84.2), HumanEval (64.6), GSM8K (89.5), and BBH (82.4).
Supports ~30 languages with robust multilingual performance, competitive with GPT-4 and Claude-3.
Employs GQA, DCA, YARN, and fine-grained MoE experts for efficiency and long context up to 128K tokens.
Post-training with scalable alignment using SFT and DPO, minimizing human annotation.
Open-source model weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope with quantization and fine-tuning resources.
limits: Performance gap with Llama-3-70B in English comprehension and coding tasks.
Qwen2-7B-Instruct lags behind Llama-3-8B-Instruct in instruction following.
MoE model (57B-A14B) may need more pre-training tokens to match dense models.
Safety evaluation shows room for improvement, especially in pornography detection.
Smaller models (0.5B, 1.5B) limited in complex reasoning tasks compared to larger ones.

papers.tEn: CosyVoice: A Scalable Multilingual Zero-shot Text-to-speech Synthesizer based on Supervised Semantic Tokens
papers.tZh: CosyVoice：基于监督语义标记的可扩展多语言零样本文本转语音合成器
papers.sEn: Supervised semantic tokens from multilingual ASR enable scalable zero-shot TTS with better content and speaker consistency.
contrib: First integration of supervised semantic tokens into TTS models, enhancing content consistency and speaker similarity.
Proposes CosyVoice, a scalable zero-shot TTS synthesizer combining an LLM for text-to-token generation and a conditional flow matching model for token-to-speech synthesis.
Eliminates need for phonemizers and forced aligners by using a direct text-to-speech pathway.
Incorporates x-vector into LLM to separate modeling of speech into semantic, speaker, and prosody components.
Demonstrates scalability: large-scale data and model size significantly improve synthesis performance.
Achieves human parity generation quality in zero-shot voice cloning and cross-lingual scenarios.
limits: Evaluation limited to English and Chinese languages; multilingual performance on other languages not fully explored.
Dependence on a pre-trained ASR model for supervised token extraction may introduce biases.
Single codebook with 4096 codes; impact of codebook size and number on performance not investigated.
Zero-shot voice cloning requires a reference speech sample; performance may degrade with very short or noisy samples.
Instruct fine-tuning data limited to specific emotions and paralinguistic features; broader controllability not tested.

papers.tEn: ChatGLM: A Family of Large Language Models from GLM-130B to GLM-4 All Tools
papers.tZh: ChatGLM：从 GLM-130B 到 GLM-4 All Tools 的大型语言模型家族
papers.sEn: ChatGLM family evolves from GLM-130B to GLM-4, with GLM-4 models rivaling GPT-4 in general metrics, long context, and Chinese alignment, and GLM-4 All Tools matching GPT-4 All Tools in tool use.
contrib: Introduced the GLM-4 model series, achieving performance comparable to GPT-4 on multiple benchmarks.
Developed GLM-4 All Tools, enabling autonomous tool use for complex tasks.
Established scaling laws through models of various sizes from 1.5B to 130B parameters.
Proposed LongAlign for extending context window to 128K and 1M tokens.
Open-sourced multiple models including ChatGLM-6B and GLM-4-9B, with over 10 million downloads.
Achieved state-of-the-art Chinese alignment performance on AlignBench.
limits: Pre-training data limited to 10 trillion tokens, mostly Chinese and English.
GLM-4 lags behind GPT-4 Turbo in Chinese math reasoning on AlignBench.
No fundamental principle identified for data collection and selection.
GLM-4 shows gaps to GPT-4 on code-related agentic tasks in AgentBench.
Safety evaluation limited to Chinese subset of SafetyBench.

papers.tEn: DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence
papers.tZh: DeepSeek-Coder-V2：打破闭源模型在代码智能领域的壁垒
papers.sEn: DeepSeek-Coder-V2, an open-source MoE code model, matches GPT4-Turbo in code tasks with 338 languages and 128K context.
contrib: Open-source MoE code model achieving GPT4-Turbo-level performance in code tasks.
Continued pre-training on 6T tokens enhances coding and math reasoning while maintaining general language performance.
Expands programming language support from 86 to 338 and context length from 16K to 128K.
Outperforms closed-source models like GPT4-Turbo, Claude 3 Opus, and Gemini 1.5 Pro on coding and math benchmarks.
First open-source model to exceed 10% on SWEBench, achieving 90.2% on HumanEval.
Uses GRPO for alignment with human preferences, leveraging compiler feedback and reward models.
limits: Significant gap in instruction-following capabilities compared to GPT-4 Turbo, leading to poor performance on complex tasks like SWEbench.
Pre-training data cutoff before November 2023 may limit knowledge of recent events.
Natural language performance slightly lags behind DeepSeek-V2 on knowledge-intensive benchmarks like TriviaQA.
236B model uses only next-token prediction objective, not Fill-In-Middle, limiting code completion capabilities.
Training instability observed due to exponential normalization, requiring reversion to conventional method.

papers.tEn: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model
papers.tZh: OpenVLA：一个开源的视觉-语言-动作模型
papers.sEn: OpenVLA is an open-source 7B-parameter vision-language-action model that outperforms larger closed models and enables efficient fine-tuning on consumer GPUs.
contrib: Introduces OpenVLA, a 7B-parameter open-source vision-language-action model trained on 970k robot demonstrations.
Outperforms closed-source RT-2-X (55B) by 16.5% absolute success rate across 29 tasks with 7x fewer parameters.
Demonstrates effective fine-tuning for new tasks, outperforming Diffusion Policy by 20.4% in multi-task environments.
Shows compute-efficient fine-tuning via LoRA and quantization on consumer GPUs without performance loss.
Releases model checkpoints, fine-tuning notebooks, and PyTorch codebase for scalable VLA training.
Explores key design decisions like vision encoder fine-tuning and multiple training epochs for VLA performance.
limits: Only supports single-image observations, not multi-image or proprioceptive inputs.
Inference throughput is limited, unsuitable for high-frequency control setups like ALOHA at 50Hz.
Does not achieve very high reliability, typically below 90% success rate on tested tasks.
Many VLA design questions remain unexplored due to compute limitations.
Performance on DROID dataset was low, suggesting need for larger mixture weight or model.

papers.tEn: Claude’s Character
papers.tZh: 克劳德的性格
papers.sEn: We can train AI models to have good character traits beyond just harmlessness, like curiosity, truthfulness, and open-mindedness.
contrib: Introduces 'character training' as a novel alignment finetuning step beyond harmlessness, aiming for nuanced traits like curiosity and open-mindedness.
Proposes training models to be honest about their biases rather than adopting user views, centrism, or claiming neutrality.
Uses a 'character' variant of Constitutional AI with synthetic data to internalize traits without human feedback.
Argues good character traits improve model discernment in handling harmful tasks and diverse human values.
Suggests character training may increase model engagement, viewing this as a positive side effect of alignment.
limits: Character training relies on hand-crafted traits and synthetic data, limiting scalability and objectivity.
The approach may inadvertently encode developer biases into model character, raising ethical concerns.
Effectiveness in diverse cultural contexts is untested; traits like 'open-mindedness' may be interpreted differently.
No rigorous evaluation of character training's impact on safety or alignment robustness is provided.
The method's reliance on model self-ranking may reinforce existing biases rather than correct them.

papers.tEn: Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders
papers.tZh: 缩放与评估稀疏自编码器
papers.sEn: We propose using k-sparse autoencoders to directly control sparsity, find clean scaling laws, and introduce new metrics for evaluating feature quality.
contrib: Propose k-sparse autoencoders with TopK activation to directly control sparsity, simplifying tuning and improving reconstruction-sparsity frontier.
Identify modifications (encoder initialized to decoder transpose, auxiliary loss) that result in few dead latents even at largest scales.
Demonstrate clean scaling laws for autoencoder size and sparsity, and train a 16 million latent autoencoder on GPT-4 activations.
Introduce new metrics for feature quality: probe loss, explainability (N2G), ablation sparsity, and downstream loss.
Show that larger autoencoders generally improve on all proposed quality metrics.
Release training code, autoencoders for open-source models, and a feature visualizer.
limits: TopK forces exactly k active latents per token, which may be suboptimal; expected L0 constraint might be better.
Metrics like probe loss and explainability rely on assumptions about natural features and may not capture all aspects.
N2G explanations are limited to simple n-gram patterns and cannot capture complex feature interactions.
Training uses only 64-token context, potentially insufficient for capturing long-range behaviors in GPT-4.
Scaling laws may break at extreme scales due to sublinear token budget per latent.

papers.tEn: Guiding a Diffusion Model with a Bad Version of Itself
papers.tZh: 用自身的一个劣化版本来引导扩散模型
papers.sEn: Guiding a diffusion model with a smaller, less-trained version of itself yields disentangled control over image quality without reducing variation, achieving record FID scores on ImageNet.
contrib: Proposes autoguidance, using a smaller, less-trained version of the model itself to guide generation, achieving disentangled control over image quality without reducing variation.
Sets new state-of-the-art FID records on ImageNet: 1.01 for 64x64 and 1.25 for 512x512.
Identifies that classifier-free guidance improves image quality by implicitly truncating low-probability regions due to quality differences between conditional and unconditional denoisers.
Demonstrates that autoguidance is applicable to unconditional diffusion models, drastically improving their quality (e.g., FID from 11.67 to 3.86 on ImageNet-512).
Validates that the guiding model must suffer from compatible degradations (e.g., reduced capacity and training) for effective guidance.
Shows autoguidance preserves image style and complexity better than classifier-free guidance, and can be combined with it for artistic control.
limits: Requires a smaller, less-trained version of the same model, which may not be available for existing large-scale generators.
Effectiveness depends on compatible degradations between main and guiding models; mismatched degradations yield no improvement.
Does not provide formal proof of conditions for beneficial autoguidance; relies on empirical observations.
Potential distribution shifts between training snapshots (e.g., due to data changes) may violate assumptions.
Optimal guiding model selection (e.g., capacity, training steps) requires grid search and may vary across datasets.

papers.tEn: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality
papers.tZh: Transformers 是 SSM：通过结构化状态空间对偶的通用模型与高效算法
papers.sEn: The paper reveals that Transformers and state-space models are closely related via structured semiseparable matrices, and introduces Mamba-2 which is 2-8X faster and competitive with Transformers on language modeling.
contrib: Establish equivalence between SSMs and semiseparable matrix transformations, revealing new theoretical connections.
Develop state space duality framework unifying SSMs, attention, and structured matrices through matrix decompositions.
Introduce Mamba-2 whose core SSD layer is 2-8× faster than Mamba while competitive with Transformers.
Propose structured masked attention generalizing linear attention to arbitrary structured masks.
Prove efficient autoregressive attention requires semiseparable masks, characterizing autoregressive attention with bounded order.
Develop hardware-efficient block-decomposition algorithm with O(TN²) training FLOPs dominated by matrix multiplications.
limits: Scalar-times-identity simplification of A matrix reduces expressive power versus general selective SSMs.
Softmax is dropped in dual form, deviating from standard attention; expressivity implications remain unanalyzed.
Duality established for scalar-identity SSM and 1-semiseparable SMA, not for general SSM families.
Empirical validation limited to small-to-medium scale; scaling at large scale not demonstrated.
Dense unstructured A matrices still incur expensive preprocessing, limiting practical applicability of general results.

papers.tEn: Situational Awareness I: From GPT-4 to AGI
papers.tZh: 情境意识 I：从 GPT-4 到 AGI
papers.sEn: The paper outlines a path from GPT-4 to AGI and superintelligence, focusing on orders of magnitude improvements and the intelligence explosion.
contrib: Traces compute, algorithmic efficiency, and unhobbling gains to project another GPT-2-to-GPT-4 jump by 2027.
Argues AGI by 2027 is plausible via extrapolating trendlines, not requiring sci-fi beliefs.
Identifies unhobbling (RLHF, chain-of-thought, tools, scaffolding) as key to unlocking latent capabilities.
Highlights test-time compute overhang as a major source of future capability gains.
Predicts transition from chatbots to drop-in remote worker agents by 2027.
Claims data wall may be overcome via synthetic data, self-play, and RL, maintaining scaling trends.
limits: Relies on extrapolation of trendlines that may break due to data wall or algorithmic limits.
Unhobbling gains may be finite; further improvements could diminish after low-hanging fruit.
Estimates of algorithmic efficiency are uncertain due to proprietary research and lack of public data.
Societal rollout and regulation could slow adoption even if technical AGI is achieved.
Focuses on cognitive tasks; robotics and physical world interaction may lag behind.

papers.tEn: DeepSeek-Prover: Advancing Theorem Proving in LLMs through Large-Scale Synthetic Data
papers.tZh: DeepSeek-Prover：通过大规模合成数据推进大语言模型中的定理证明
papers.sEn: Large-scale synthetic data from math competition problems boosts LLM theorem proving, with DeepSeekMath 7B achieving 46.3% accuracy on miniF2F, surpassing GPT-4.
contrib: Proposes an iterative method to synthesize 8 million formal statements with proofs from informal math problems.
Achieves state-of-the-art whole-proof generation accuracy of 46.3% on miniF2F with 64 samples, surpassing GPT-4 and RL methods.
Successfully proves 5 out of 148 FIMO problems, while GPT-4 proves none.
Introduces dual concurrent proof search for statements and their negations to improve efficiency.
Demonstrates clear correlation between synthetic dataset size and model performance on theorem proving.
Open-sources the large-scale synthetic dataset and model to facilitate further research.
limits: Focuses primarily on algebra and number theory at high school and undergraduate levels.
Synthetic data quality depends on the base model's autoformalization capability.
Proof search may still be computationally intensive despite dual concurrent approach.
Generalizability to advanced mathematical topics requiring complex definitions is limited.
Performance on benchmarks may not fully reflect real-world theorem proving scenarios.

papers.tEn: Mapping the mind of a large language model
papers.tZh: 映射大语言模型的思维
papers.sEn: We identified how millions of concepts are represented inside Claude Sonnet, a production-grade large language model, marking the first detailed look inside such a model.
