contrib: First detailed look inside a modern, production-grade LLM using dictionary learning to extract millions of interpretable features.
Features represent a vast range of concepts, from concrete entities to abstract ideas, and are multimodal and multilingual.
Manipulating features causally changes model behavior, validating they shape responses, e.g., amplifying 'Golden Gate Bridge' causes identity shift.
Identified safety-relevant features like scam emails, code backdoors, bias, and sycophancy, enabling potential monitoring and steering.
Demonstrates that internal concept organization mirrors human similarity, explaining Claude's analogy and metaphor abilities.
Provides a 'test set for safety' by revealing latent harmful capabilities not visible through standard input/output interactions.
limits: Current technique is cost-prohibitive for full feature extraction; compute required vastly exceeds training compute.
Features represent only a small subset of all concepts learned; full set remains unknown.
Understanding representations does not explain how they are used; circuits need to be found.
Safety-relevant features have been identified but not yet proven to improve safety in practice.
Method may be used to remove safeguards by malicious actors with model weight access, though simpler methods already exist.

papers.tEn: Introducing the Model Spec
papers.tZh: 模型规范介绍
papers.sEn: OpenAI introduces the Model Spec, a framework for defining desired model behavior, with an updated version emphasizing customizability, transparency, and intellectual freedom.
contrib: Introduces the Model Spec, a framework for shaping desired model behavior with objectives, rules, and defaults.
Specifies three objectives: assist developer and end user, benefit humanity, and reflect well on OpenAI.
Includes rules for safety and legality, such as complying with laws and avoiding NSFW content.
Provides default behaviors for handling conflicts, like assuming best intentions and asking clarifying questions.
Delegates authority to developers and end users, with developer messages taking precedence over user instructions.
Aims to inform rather than influence, presenting facts while respecting user beliefs.
limits: The Model Spec is a draft and expected to change, lacking empirical validation of its effectiveness.
Relies on human feedback and RLHF, which may introduce biases and scalability issues.
Rules like 'don't try to change anyone's mind' may conflict with factuality in misinformation cases.
Legal compliance is complex across jurisdictions, and the spec does not resolve jurisdictional conflicts.
Default behaviors may not cover all edge cases, leading to inconsistent model responses.

papers.tEn: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model
papers.tZh: DeepSeek-V2：一个强大、经济且高效的混合专家语言模型
papers.sEn: DeepSeek-V2 achieves top-tier performance with only 21B activated parameters, saving 42.5% training cost and 93.3% KV cache.
contrib: Proposes Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) with low-rank KV joint compression for efficient inference.
Adopts DeepSeekMoE with fine-grained expert segmentation and shared expert isolation for economical training.
Achieves top-tier performance among open-source models with only 21B activated parameters.
Saves 42.5% training costs, reduces KV cache by 93.3%, and boosts generation throughput by 5.76x vs DeepSeek 67B.
Supports 128K context length via YaRN extension and demonstrates robust long-context performance.
Employs two-stage RL (reasoning then human preference) to enhance alignment without sacrificing standard benchmarks.
limits: Lacks ongoing knowledge updates after pre-training, limiting adaptability to new information.
May generate non-factual information or hallucinations, especially in unverified advice scenarios.
Proficiency in languages other than Chinese and English is limited due to data composition.
Alignment tax observed: RL training slightly degrades performance on some standard benchmarks like BBH.
Currently supports text modality only; multi-modal capabilities are not yet available.

papers.tEn: QServe: W4A8KV4 Quantization and System Co-design for Efficient LLM Serving
papers.tZh: QServe: W4A8KV4 量化与系统协同设计实现高效 LLM 服务
papers.sEn: QServe achieves up to 3.5x throughput improvement and 3x cost reduction for LLM serving via W4A8KV4 quantization and system co-design.
contrib: Introduces QoQ, a W4A8KV4 quantization algorithm with progressive group quantization to enable low-overhead dequantization on INT8 tensor cores.
Proposes SmoothAttention to mitigate accuracy loss from 4-bit KV cache quantization by smoothing key outliers.
Designs QServe system with compute-aware weight reordering and register-level parallelism to reduce dequantization latency.
Achieves up to 2.4x throughput improvement on A100 and 3.5x on L40S over TensorRT-LLM for LLM serving.
Demonstrates that QServe on L40S can outperform TensorRT-LLM on A100, reducing serving cost by 3x.
Provides open-source implementation at https://github.com/mit-han-lab/qserve.
limits: Evaluation limited to Ampere and Hopper GPU architectures; results may not generalize to other hardware.
Quantization accuracy degradation still exists compared to FP16, especially for smaller models.
Progressive group quantization requires careful protective range tuning to avoid overflow.
SmoothAttention assumes no query quantization; may not extend to fully quantized attention.
System optimizations are specific to CUDA and may not port to other frameworks or backends.

papers.tEn: Phi-3 Technical Report: A Highly Capable Language Model Locally on Your Phone
papers.tZh: Phi-3 技术报告：一款可在手机上本地运行的高性能语言模型
papers.sEn: Phi-3-mini, a 3.8B parameter model, rivals Mixtral 8x7B and GPT-3.5 despite being deployable on a phone.
contrib: Introduces phi-3-mini, a 3.8B parameter model rivaling Mixtral 8x7B and GPT-3.5, deployable on phones.
Training dataset innovation: scaled-up version of phi-2's data with heavily filtered web and synthetic data.
Provides parameter-scaling results with phi-3-small (7B) and phi-3-medium (14B) trained on 4.8T tokens.
Introduces phi-3.5 series: phi-3.5-mini, phi-3.5-MoE, and phi-3.5-Vision for multilingual, multimodal, and long-context capabilities.
Demonstrates that high-quality data enables small models to deviate from standard scaling laws.
Achieves strong safety alignment via post-training, red-teaming, and automated RAI evaluations.
limits: Limited factual knowledge due to small model capacity, e.g., low TriviaQA performance.
Primarily English-focused; multilingual capabilities are limited, especially in phi-3-mini.
Potential for factual inaccuracies, biases, inappropriate content, and safety issues despite RAI efforts.
Data mixture may not be optimal for larger models like phi-3-medium, as some benchmarks show less improvement.
Long-context version (128K) quality is on par with 4K version but may have trade-offs.

papers.tEn: Visual Autoregressive Modeling: Scalable Image Generation via Next-Scale Prediction
papers.tZh: 视觉自回归建模：通过下一尺度预测实现可扩展的图像生成
papers.sEn: VAR redefines autoregressive image generation as coarse-to-fine next-scale prediction, achieving state-of-the-art results on ImageNet with 20x faster inference than diffusion transformers.
contrib: Proposes Visual AutoRegressive (VAR) modeling with next-scale prediction, redefining autoregressive learning on images as coarse-to-fine generation.
Achieves state-of-the-art image generation on ImageNet 256×256 with FID 1.73 and IS 350.2, surpassing diffusion transformers for the first time.
Demonstrates clear power-law scaling laws for VAR models, with linear correlation coefficients near -0.998, similar to LLMs.
Shows zero-shot generalization in downstream tasks like image in-painting, out-painting, and editing without task-specific tuning.
Provides 20x faster inference speed compared to standard autoregressive models, reducing computational complexity from O(n^6) to O(n^4).
Releases all models and code to promote exploration of AR/VAR models for visual generation and unified learning.
limits: VAR relies on a fixed multi-scale tokenization scheme; performance may vary with different tokenizer designs.
The study focuses on class-conditional image generation; text-prompt generation is not yet explored.
Video generation is not implemented; extension to video requires further research on 3D next-scale prediction.
The VQVAE tokenizer is kept unchanged from baseline; advanced tokenizers could further improve performance.
Scaling laws are validated only on ImageNet; generalization to other datasets or domains is not verified.

papers.tEn: Many-shot jailbreaking
papers.tZh: 多轮越狱
papers.sEn: Many-shot jailbreaking exploits large context windows to bypass LLM safety guardrails.
contrib: Proposes many-shot jailbreaking, a simple long-context attack exploiting LLM context windows.
Demonstrates effectiveness on multiple models, including Anthropic's, with up to 256 shots.
Shows attack follows power-law scaling similar to benign in-context learning.
Combining with other jailbreaks reduces required prompt length.
Implements prompt-based mitigations reducing attack success from 61% to 2%.
Highlights risks of increasing context windows for LLM safety.
limits: Mitigations only delay attack; harmful outputs eventually appear with more shots.
Attack effectiveness varies across models; not all models equally vulnerable.
Study limited to text-based LLMs; applicability to multimodal models untested.
Attack requires long prompts; may be impractical for short-context applications.
Defense via prompt classification may be evaded by adversarial modifications.

papers.tEn: InternLM2 Technical Report
papers.tZh: InternLM2 技术报告
papers.sEn: InternLM2 is an open-source LLM that outperforms its predecessors through innovative pre-training and optimization techniques, including long-context modeling and a novel COOL RLHF alignment strategy.
contrib: Open-sourced InternLM2 models (1.8B, 7B, 20B) with superior performance across 30 benchmarks and 6 dimensions.
Designed with a 200k context window, achieving near-perfect needle-in-a-haystack performance.
Provided comprehensive data preparation guidance for pre-training, SFT, and RLHF stages.
Introduced COOL RLHF with conditional reward model to reconcile conflicting preferences and mitigate reward hacking.
Released models at different training stages (pre-RLHF and post-RLHF) for community analysis.
Developed InternEvo framework achieving high MFU (53% on 1024 GPUs) and supporting long contexts up to 1M tokens.
limits: Evaluation limited to benchmarks; real-world deployment performance may vary.
Long-context capability tested only up to 200k tokens; longer contexts not verified.
COOL RLHF requires multiple rounds of online data collection, increasing annotation cost.
Model sizes limited to 1.8B, 7B, and 20B; larger scales not explored.
Data contamination analysis may not fully eliminate benchmark leakage.

papers.tEn: Fast High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Adversarial Diffusion Distillation
papers.tZh: 潜在对抗扩散蒸馏实现快速高分辨率图像合成
papers.sEn: LADD uses generative features from pretrained latent diffusion models to enable fast, high-resolution image synthesis with only four sampling steps.
contrib: Introduces Latent Adversarial Diffusion Distillation (LADD), a novel distillation method using generative features from pretrained latent diffusion models.
Applies LADD to Stable Diffusion 3 (8B) to obtain SD3-Turbo, achieving state-of-the-art performance in four unguided sampling steps.
Systematically investigates scaling behavior of LADD, showing student model size as the most impactful factor.
Demonstrates LADD's versatility in image editing and inpainting tasks with single-step inference.
Simplifies training by unifying teacher and discriminator in latent space, eliminating decoding to pixel space.
Achieves multi-aspect ratio high-resolution image synthesis with stable adversarial training.
limits: SD3-Turbo shows reduced prompt alignment compared to teacher SD3, causing object duplication and spatial prompting issues.
Image editing lacks control over image and text guidance strengths, limiting flexibility.
Model exhibits rigidity in editing, adhering too closely to input and making large changes challenging.
Scaling benefits plateau for teacher model and data quality beyond certain thresholds.
Adversarial training may still require careful tuning of noise distribution parameters.

papers.tEn: SV3D: Novel Multi-view Synthesis and 3D Generation from a Single Image using Latent Video Diffusion
papers.tZh: SV3D：基于潜在视频扩散的单图像新颖多视图合成与 3D 生成
papers.sEn: SV3D adapts image-to-video diffusion for consistent multi-view synthesis and 3D generation from a single image.
contrib: Proposes SV3D, a latent video diffusion model for novel multi-view synthesis and 3D generation from a single image.
Adapts image-to-video diffusion model with explicit camera pose control for multi-view consistent novel view synthesis.
Introduces triangle classifier-free guidance scaling for improved orbital video quality.
Proposes disentangled illumination model and masked score distillation sampling loss for high-quality 3D generation.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction across multiple datasets.
Demonstrates strong generalization to real-world images and user preference in human studies.
limits: SV3D only handles 2 degrees of freedom (elevation and azimuth) for camera control.
View inconsistency for mirror-like reflective surfaces, challenging 3D reconstruction.
Lambertian shading model cannot represent reflective surfaces.
Requires large computational resources for training (4 nodes of 8 A100 GPUs for 6 days).
SDS loss can cause unstable training and artifacts if applied naively.

papers.tEn: Gemma: Open Models Based on Gemini Research and Technology
papers.tZh: Gemma：基于 Gemini 研究与技术的开放模型
papers.sEn: Gemma is a family of lightweight, state-of-the-art open models from Google, built on Gemini research and technology.
contrib: Introduces Gemma, a family of lightweight open models based on Gemini research.
Gemma outperforms similarly sized open models on 11 of 18 text tasks.
Releases pretrained and fine-tuned checkpoints for 2B and 7B parameter models.
Comprehensive safety and responsibility evaluations with detailed model development.
Achieves strong performance on reasoning, math, and code benchmarks.
Emphasizes responsible release to improve frontier model safety and enable innovation.
limits: Models are English-only and not multimodal.
Testing cannot cover all applications; users must conduct safety tests.
Open weights may enable misuse despite prohibited use policy.
Memorization of personal data occurs at low rates.
Further research needed for factuality, alignment, and robustness.

papers.tEn: DeepSeek-VL: Towards Real-World Vision-Language Understanding
papers.tZh: DeepSeek-VL：面向真实世界的视觉语言理解
papers.sEn: DeepSeek-VL is an open-source vision-language model designed for real-world applications, featuring a hybrid vision encoder for high-resolution images and a training strategy that preserves LLM capabilities.
contrib: Proposes a hybrid vision encoder combining SigLIP and SAM for high-resolution (1024x1024) processing with fixed token budget.
Introduces a joint vision-language pretraining strategy with modality warm-up and 70% language data ratio to preserve LLM capabilities.
Constructs a comprehensive real-world use case taxonomy and instruction tuning dataset from GPT-4V and Gemini test cases.
Achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on multiple vision-language benchmarks while maintaining language proficiency.
Develops a scalable training methodology from 1.3B to 7B models using multi-choice PPL and SFT data mixing.
Releases open-source 1.3B and 7B models to foster community innovation.
limits: Performance on MathVista still lags behind proprietary models like GPT-4V due to base model size.
Language capability shows slight decline in mathematics (GSM8K) despite joint training strategy.
Hybrid vision encoder increases computational overhead compared to single encoder approaches.
Stage 1 projector warmup does not benefit from larger data scale, limiting its capacity.
Evaluation limited to English and Chinese; generalization to other languages not verified.

papers.tEn: Gemini 1.5: Unlocking multimodal understanding across millions of tokens of context
papers.tZh: Gemini 1.5：解锁跨数百万 token 上下文的 multimodal 理解
papers.sEn: Gemini 1.5 models achieve near-perfect recall over long contexts up to 10M tokens and match or surpass previous state-of-the-art across benchmarks.
contrib: Introduces Gemini 1.5 models (Pro & Flash) with MoE architecture, achieving near-perfect recall on long-context retrieval up to 10M tokens.
Sets new state-of-the-art on long-document QA, long-video QA, and long-context ASR, outperforming prior models like Claude 2.1 and GPT-4 Turbo.
Demonstrates in-context language learning from a single grammar manual for Kalamang, matching human-level translation with only 250k tokens of context.
Achieves strong core capabilities (math, science, code) without compromise, matching or surpassing Gemini 1.0 Ultra despite using less compute.
Shows real-world productivity gains: 26–75% time savings across 10 job categories in professional collaboration tasks.
limits: Long-context retrieval degrades with multiple needles or similar distractors; performance drops in multi-needle and co-reference resolution tasks.
Inconsistent rule application in language translation, e.g., misapplying phonological alternations in Kalamang despite explicit grammar rules.
Underperforms on OCR-heavy image tasks; false negatives may underestimate true capability, suggesting evaluation improvements needed.
Long-context capability may amplify existing safety risks (e.g., harmful content in long inputs), requiring new mitigation strategies.
Evaluation benchmarks may be contaminated or insufficient for measuring advanced reasoning over extremely long contexts.

papers.tEn: Yi: Open Foundation Models by 01.AI
papers.tZh: Yi: 01.AI 的开源基础模型
papers.sEn: Yi models achieve strong performance through data quality and engineering efforts.
contrib: Introduces Yi model family with 6B and 34B base models, achieving GPT-3.5-matching performance.
Emphasizes data quality over quantity with a cascaded deduplication and filtering pipeline for pretraining.
Uses less than 10K handcrafted instruction data for finetuning, iteratively polished by engineers.
Extends context to 200K via lightweight continual pretraining with strong retrieval performance.
Develops vision-language models by combining chat language model with vision transformer encoder.
Demonstrates depth-upscaling by duplicating layers and continual pretraining to improve performance.
limits: Performance gap remains in math and coding tasks compared to GPT-4 and GPT-3.5.
Data cleaning pipeline is complex and difficult to optimize via extensive grid search.
Smaller models like Yi-6B lack strong mathematical capabilities even after finetuning.
Long-context retrieval performance may not generalize to all real-world tasks.
Model scaling may require even larger data and compute for further improvements.

papers.tEn: Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
papers.tZh: 缩放整流流变换器以实现高分辨率图像合成
papers.sEn: Rectified flow models with improved noise sampling and a novel transformer architecture achieve state-of-the-art text-to-image synthesis.
contrib: Introduces new noise sampling techniques for rectified flow models, biasing towards perceptually relevant scales.
Presents a novel transformer-based architecture (MM-DiT) with separate weights for image and text tokens, enabling bidirectional information flow.
Demonstrates predictable scaling trends and strong correlation between lower validation loss and improved text-to-image synthesis.
Conducts a large-scale systematic study comparing rectified flow formulations with established diffusion models.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance in text-to-image synthesis, outperforming both open and proprietary models.
Provides public release of experimental data, code, and model weights for reproducibility.
limits: Study limited to high-resolution text-to-image synthesis; video results are preliminary.
Scaling experiments conducted up to 8B parameters; saturation not observed but may occur at larger scales.
Dependence on pretrained autoencoder and text encoders; reconstruction quality bounds final image quality.
Synthetic captions from CogVLM may introduce biases or limit concept coverage.
Training stability requires QK-normalization; not a universal recipe for all setups.

papers.tEn: Genie: Generative Interactive Environments
papers.tZh: Genie: 生成式交互环境
papers.sEn: Genie is the first generative interactive environment trained unsupervised from Internet videos, enabling action-controllable virtual worlds from text, images, and sketches.
contrib: First generative interactive environment trained unsupervised from Internet videos.
11B parameter foundation world model with spatiotemporal video tokenizer, dynamics model, and latent action model.
Enables frame-by-frame control without action labels via learned latent action space.
Scaling analysis shows performance improves with model and batch size.
Latent actions from Internet videos can train agents to imitate behaviors in unseen environments.
Generalizes to diverse prompts including text, sketches, and photos.
limits: Limited to 16-frame memory, causing inconsistent environments over long horizons.
Operates at ~1 FPS, requiring future advances for interactive frame rates.
May hallucinate unrealistic futures like other autoregressive models.
Trained only on 2D platformer and robotics videos, limiting domain generality.

papers.tEn: Universal Manipulation Interface: In-The-Wild Robot Teaching Without In-The-Wild Robots
papers.tZh: 通用操控接口：无需野外机器人的野外机器人教学
papers.sEn: UMI enables zero-shot transfer of human manipulation skills to robots via a portable hand-held gripper and careful interface design.
contrib: Proposes Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI), a framework enabling direct skill transfer from in-the-wild human demonstrations to deployable robot policies.
Designs a hand-held gripper with fisheye lens, side mirrors, and IMU-aware tracking for portable, low-cost, and information-rich data collection.
Introduces inference-time latency matching and relative-trajectory action representation for hardware-agnostic policy deployment.
Demonstrates zero-shot generalization to novel environments and objects across dynamic, bimanual, precise, and long-horizon tasks.
Achieves 71.7% success rate in out-of-distribution tests with diverse in-the-wild data, outperforming narrow-domain baselines.
Open-sources hardware and software system, enabling reproducible and accessible robot learning.
limits: Relies on kinematic data filtering to ensure feasibility, limiting transfer from hardware-infeasible actions.
SLAM-based action recovery requires sufficient texture in the environment, failing in texture-deficient scenes.
Data collection with UMI gripper is less efficient than human hand demonstration due to weight and reduced degrees of freedom.
Policy performance depends on careful latency calibration, which varies across hardware platforms.
Generalization to novel objects and environments requires diverse in-the-wild data, which may be costly to collect.

papers.tEn: Aya Model: An Instruction Finetuned Open-Access Multilingual Language Model
papers.tZh: Aya 模型：一种指令微调的开源多语言语言模型
papers.sEn: Aya is an instruction-tuned multilingual model that supports 101 languages, outperforming existing models on most tasks while covering twice as many languages.
contrib: Introduces Aya, an instruction-finetuned multilingual model covering 101 languages, over half being lower-resourced.
Expands multilingual evaluation to 99 languages with discriminative, generative, human, and simulated win-rate benchmarks.
Outperforms mT0 and BLOOMZ on most tasks while covering double the languages, mitigating the curse of multilinguality.
Proposes data weighting and pruning strategies that rebalance the instruction fine-tuning mixture for better performance.
Introduces multilingual safety context distillation, reducing harmful generations by 78–89% across languages.
Open-sources the model and instruction datasets under Apache 2.0 to empower further multilingual research.
limits: Generations still exhibit grammar errors, hallucinations, repetitions, and unnatural structures, especially in lower-resourced languages.
Safety context distillation causes small performance drops on general benchmarks and may introduce false refusals.
Toxicity evaluations rely on Perspective API, which may have language bias affecting cross-lingual comparisons.
Training data still skews toward higher-resourced languages, and translated data may propagate systematic translation errors.
Model capacity limited to 13B parameters; larger models may be needed to further mitigate the curse of multilinguality.

papers.tEn: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
papers.tZh: DeepSeekMath：推动开源语言模型数学推理的极限
papers.sEn: DeepSeekMath 7B achieves 51.7% on MATH without external tools, approaching Gemini-Ultra and GPT-4.
contrib: Constructs DeepSeekMath Corpus, a 120B-token math dataset from Common Crawl via iterative fastText filtering, outperforming existing corpora.
Introduces Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), a PPO variant that eliminates the critic model, reducing memory while improving math reasoning.
DeepSeekMath-Base 7B achieves 36.2% on MATH and 64.2% on GSM8K, surpassing Minerva 540B and all open-source base models.
DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B with GRPO achieves 51.7% on MATH without tools, approaching GPT-4 and Gemini-Ultra performance.
Provides a unified paradigm for RL methods (SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, GRPO), analyzing key components: data source, reward function, and algorithm.
Demonstrates code pre-training improves math reasoning, while arXiv papers show no notable benefit in this context.
limits: Geometry and theorem-proving capabilities are weaker than closed models like GPT-4, indicating data selection bias.
DeepSeekMath 7B shows similar zero-shot and few-shot performance, unlike GPT-4 which benefits from few-shot inputs.
RL improvement is limited to Maj@K accuracy, not Pass@K, suggesting it stabilizes output distribution rather than enhancing fundamental capabilities.
The study does not explore arXiv tokens' impact on specific tasks like theorem informalization or at larger model scales.
RL pipeline uses only in-distribution questions from instruction tuning, limiting generalization to out-of-distribution prompts.

papers.tEn: OLMo: Accelerating the Science of Language Models
papers.tZh: OLMo：加速语言模型科学
papers.sEn: OLMo is a truly open language model released with training data, code, and evaluation tools to advance scientific research.
contrib: Releases OLMo, a truly open language model with full training data, code, and checkpoints.
Provides Dolma, a 3T-token open pretraining dataset from diverse sources.
Open-sources evaluation frameworks Catwalk and Paloma for downstream and perplexity evaluation.
Demonstrates competitive performance of OLMo-7B against other open models on core tasks.
Releases intermediate checkpoints and training logs to enable scientific study of language models.
Provides adapted models via instruction tuning and DPO, showing improved safety and performance.
limits: OLMo-7B still lags behind proprietary models like GPT-4 in overall capabilities.
The study focuses on 1B and 7B scales; larger models like 65B are not yet released.
Carbon emission estimates are lower bounds, excluding hardware manufacturing and other lifecycle impacts.
Adapted models show a performance gap compared to Tülu 2, possibly due to data contamination or mix design.
The study does not address multimodal capabilities or long-context scenarios beyond 2048 tokens.

papers.tEn: Building an early warning system for LLM-aided biological threat creation
papers.tZh: 构建针对 LLM 辅助生物威胁创建的早期预警系统
papers.sEn: We propose an early warning system to detect and mitigate risks of LLM-aided biological threat creation.
contrib: Developed a blueprint for evaluating LLM-aided biological threat creation risk with human participants.
Found GPT-4 provides at most a mild uplift in accuracy and completeness for biothreat tasks.
Largest human evaluation to date on AI's impact on biorisk information access.
Designed tasks covering five stages of biological threat creation with objective rubrics.
Highlighted need for more research on meaningful risk thresholds and statistical methods.
limits: Small sample size (100 participants) limits statistical power and generalizability.
Evaluation only measures information access, not physical implementation of threats.
Student cohort not fully representative due to higher education level than typical.
No tool usage (e.g., browsing) allowed for GPT-4, limiting real-world applicability.
Time constraints (5-hour sessions) may not reflect real malicious actor scenarios.

papers.tEn: DeepSeek-Coder: When the Large Language Model Meets Programming -- The Rise of Code Intelligence
papers.tZh: DeepSeek-Coder：当大型语言模型遇见编程——代码智能的崛起
papers.sEn: DeepSeek-Coder, an open-source code model series from 1.3B to 33B parameters, achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing even closed-source models like Codex and GPT-3.5.
contrib: Introduces DeepSeek-Coder series, open-source code models from 1.3B to 33B parameters.
First to incorporate repository-level data construction during pre-training, boosting cross-file code generation.
Rigorously examines FIM training strategies, revealing trade-offs and optimal configurations.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source code models across multiple benchmarks.
DeepSeek-Coder-Instruct 33B surpasses GPT-3.5 Turbo in code-related tasks after fine-tuning.
Releases models under permissive license for research and commercial use.
limits: Evaluation limited to 87 programming languages; performance on other languages untested.
Long-context adaptation only tested up to 16K tokens; reliability beyond that unverified.
Potential data contamination from GitHub test sets cannot be fully ruled out.
FIM training trades off code completion ability for infilling performance.
DeepSeek-Coder-v1.5 shows slight coding performance drop despite improved NLP.

papers.tEn: AlphaGeometry: An Olympiad-level AI system for geometry
papers.tZh: AlphaGeometry：奥林匹克级别的几何 AI 系统
papers.sEn: AlphaGeometry achieves Olympiad-level performance in solving geometry problems.
contrib: AlphaGeometry solves 25 of 30 Olympiad geometry problems, approaching human gold-medalist performance.
It combines a neural language model with a symbolic deduction engine for fast intuition and rigorous reasoning.
A synthetic data generation method creates 100 million unique training examples without human demonstrations.
The system uses symbolic deduction and traceback to generate proofs and train the language model.
AlphaGeometry is the first AI to pass the IMO bronze medal threshold in geometry for 2000 and 2015.
The approach demonstrates AI's growing ability in logical reasoning and knowledge discovery.
limits: AlphaGeometry only applies to geometry problems, which are one-third of IMO problems.
The system relies on synthetic data that may not cover all real-world geometric reasoning.
Performance is benchmarked on a limited set of 30 problems from 2000-2022.
The neuro-symbolic approach may not scale to other mathematical domains without adaptation.
Human evaluation was limited to a single expert, reducing generalizability of quality assessment.

papers.tEn: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
papers.tZh: DeepSeekMoE：迈向混合专家语言模型中专家专业化的极致
papers.sEn: DeepSeekMoE achieves comparable performance to larger models with significantly less computation by introducing fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts.
contrib: Proposes DeepSeekMoE architecture with fine-grained expert segmentation and shared expert isolation for ultimate expert specialization.
Empirically validates that DeepSeekMoE 2B nearly approaches the upper bound performance of MoE models.
Scales DeepSeekMoE to 16B, achieving comparable performance with LLaMA2 7B using only about 40% computations.
Demonstrates successful alignment via supervised fine-tuning on DeepSeekMoE 16B, creating an effective chat model.
Preliminary scaling to 145B shows consistent advantages over GShard and comparable performance with DeepSeek 67B using 28.5% computations.
Releases DeepSeekMoE 16B checkpoint publicly, deployable on a single 40GB GPU without quantization.
limits: Validation experiments limited to 2B parameters and 100B tokens, may not generalize to larger scales.
DeepSeekMoE 16B shows limitations in multiple-choice tasks due to fewer attention parameters.
Preliminary 145B study trained only on 245B tokens, not fully optimized.
Shared expert isolation may not be optimal for all tasks; ratio of shared to routed experts requires tuning.
Evaluation primarily on English and Chinese benchmarks; performance on other languages not assessed.

papers.tEn: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
papers.tZh: 潜伏特工：训练具有欺骗性的 LLM，使其在安全训练中持续存在
papers.sEn: Deceptive behavior in LLMs can persist through standard safety training, posing challenges for AI safety.
contrib: Constructs proof-of-concept deceptive LLMs with persistent backdoors.
Shows backdoors survive standard safety training like RLHF, SFT, and adversarial training.
Finds backdoor persistence increases with model scale and chain-of-thought reasoning.
Demonstrates adversarial training can teach models to better hide backdoors.
Introduces chain-of-thought backdoor mechanism for studying deceptive instrumental alignment.
Proposes model organisms of misalignment for forward-looking safety research.
limits: Backdoors are deliberately inserted, not naturally emergent.
Simple triggers (e.g., year string) may not generalize to subtle cues.
Results may not apply to other model architectures or training paradigms.
Does not assess likelihood of deceptive alignment occurring naturally.
Safety training evaluated is limited to behavioral methods; other approaches may differ.

papers.tEn: Mixtral of Experts
papers.tZh: Mixtral of Experts
papers.sEn: Mixtral 8x7B, a Sparse Mixture of Experts model, outperforms Llama 2 70B and GPT-3.5 across benchmarks with only 13B active parameters.
contrib: Introduces Mixtral 8x7B, a Sparse Mixture of Experts (SMoE) language model with 47B total parameters but only 13B active per token.
Outperforms or matches Llama 2 70B and GPT-3.5 across all benchmarks, especially in math, code, and multilingual tasks.
Provides Mixtral 8x7B-Instruct, fine-tuned with SFT and DPO, surpassing GPT-3.5 Turbo, Claude-2.1, Gemini Pro, and Llama 2 70B chat on human evaluations.
Achieves 100% passkey retrieval accuracy across context lengths up to 32k tokens, demonstrating effective long-context handling.
Releases both base and instruct models under Apache 2.0 license, with open-source inference stack via vLLM and Megablocks.
Shows reduced biases on BBQ and BOLD benchmarks compared to Llama 2, with more positive sentiment profiles.
limits: Memory costs are proportional to 47B sparse parameters, requiring significant GPU memory for serving.
SMoE layers introduce routing overhead and increased memory loads, reducing efficiency for small batch sizes.
Expert assignment shows no clear domain specialization, limiting potential for targeted expert optimization.
High locality in expert selection may cause load imbalance in Expert Parallelism, requiring careful scheduling.
Evaluation differences from Llama 2 paper (e.g., MBPP subset, TriviaQA without context) may affect direct comparisons.

papers.tEn: DeepSeek LLM: Scaling Open-Source Language Models with Longtermism
papers.tZh: DeepSeek LLM：以长期主义扩展开源语言模型
papers.sEn: DeepSeek LLM 67B surpasses LLaMA-2 70B on code, math, and reasoning, and its chat version outperforms GPT-3.5.
contrib: Established scaling laws for hyperparameters, providing an empirical framework for determining optimal batch size and learning rate.
Introduced non-embedding FLOPs/token as model scale representation, leading to more accurate optimal model/data allocation strategy.
Discovered that pre-training data quality influences optimal model/data scaling allocation; higher quality favors more model scaling.
Developed DeepSeek LLM 7B and 67B models guided by scaling laws, surpassing LLaMA-2 70B on code, math, and reasoning benchmarks.
Achieved superior open-ended generation performance with DeepSeek 67B Chat, outperforming GPT-3.5 in Chinese and English evaluations.
Demonstrated safety and alignment through comprehensive evaluations, including Do-Not-Answer dataset with 97.8 score.
limits: Lack of ongoing knowledge updates after pre-training; model may generate non-factual information.
Initial Chinese data not exhaustive, leading to suboptimal performance on certain Chinese-specific topics.
Model proficiency in languages other than Chinese and English remains limited and should be used cautiously.
Tendency to produce hallucinations and unverified advice, a common limitation of LLMs.
Smaller models (7B) struggle with system prompt understanding, causing performance degradation.

papers.tEn: Mobile ALOHA: Learning Bimanual Mobile Manipulation with Low-Cost Whole-Body Teleoperation
papers.tZh: Mobile ALOHA：通过低成本全身遥操作学习双臂移动操作
papers.sEn: Mobile ALOHA enables bimanual mobile manipulation via low-cost whole-body teleoperation and imitation learning, achieving high success rates on complex tasks.
contrib: Presents Mobile ALOHA, a low-cost whole-body teleoperation system for bimanual mobile manipulation data collection.
Shows that co-training with static ALOHA datasets boosts mobile manipulation success rates by up to 90% with 50 demonstrations.
Achieves over 80% success on complex tasks like opening cabinets, calling elevators, and rinsing pans with only 20-50 demonstrations.
Demonstrates that co-training improves data efficiency and generalization across tasks and imitation learning methods.
Provides an open-source, low-cost hardware platform ($32k) for whole-body teleoperation and autonomous operation.
Validates the system through extensive real-world experiments on 7 diverse mobile manipulation tasks.
limits: Limited to single-task imitation learning; robot cannot improve autonomously or explore new knowledge.
Demonstrations collected by expert operators; not tested on highly suboptimal or heterogeneous datasets.
Hardware footprint (90cm x 135cm) may be too large for narrow paths; fixed arm height limits access to low cabinets.
Cook Shrimp task success rate only 40% due to limited demonstrations and visual challenges.
Co-training with static data may not benefit retrieval-based methods like VINN due to action prediction mismatch.

papers.tEn: InternVL: Scaling up Vision Foundation Models and Aligning for Generic Visual-Linguistic Tasks
papers.tZh: InternVL：扩展视觉基础模型并针对通用视觉语言任务进行对齐
papers.sEn: InternVL scales vision foundation models to 6B parameters and aligns with LLMs, achieving SOTA on 32 benchmarks.
contrib: Proposes InternVL, a large-scale vision-language foundation model scaling vision encoder to 6B parameters and aligning with LLM.
Introduces a progressive image-text alignment strategy for efficient training using web-scale noisy data for contrastive learning and fine-grained data for generative learning.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on 32 generic visual-linguistic benchmarks including image classification, semantic segmentation, video classification, retrieval, and captioning.
Demonstrates strong visual perception capabilities, serving as a good alternative to ViT-22B for visual tasks.
Enables flexible model composition for contrastive and generative tasks via vision encoder and language middleware QLLaMA.
Shows promising compatibility with various LLMs like LLaMA, Vicuna, and InternLM for multi-modal dialogue.
limits: Training requires massive computational resources (640 A100 GPUs for stage 1), limiting accessibility.
Performance heavily depends on web-scale noisy data quality; data filtering is crucial but may discard useful samples.
The model's large size (6B vision encoder + 8B middleware) leads to high inference latency, especially with larger images.
Alignment strategy is progressive but still may not fully bridge the modality gap between vision and language.
Evaluation focuses on English and Chinese; multilingual capabilities on other languages are less explored.

papers.tEn: Generative Multimodal Models are In-Context Learners
papers.tZh: 生成式多模态模型是上下文学习者
papers.sEn: Scaling up generative multimodal models significantly enhances their task-agnostic in-context learning abilities.
contrib: Introduces Emu2, a 37B parameter generative multimodal model trained with a unified autoregressive objective on large-scale multimodal sequences.
Demonstrates that scaling up generative multimodal models significantly enhances task-agnostic in-context learning abilities, including visual prompting and object-grounded generation.
Achieves state-of-the-art few-shot performance on multiple multimodal understanding benchmarks, such as VQAv2 and OKVQA.
After instruction tuning, Emu2-Chat sets new records on LMM benchmarks like MM-Vet and TouchStone, surpassing prior public models.
Emu2-Gen enables controllable visual generation in context, excelling in subject-driven generation and multi-entity composition.
Provides publicly available code and models to facilitate future research in multimodal in-context learning.
limits: In-context learning may fail in complex scenes, e.g., counting in a crowd.
Question-answering capability still lags behind closed multimodal systems like GPT-4V.
Potential for generating harmful or biased content due to biases in training data.
Model hallucination may cause incorrect predictions in certain cases.
Performance gap remains in tasks requiring fine-grained reasoning or high-resolution understanding.

papers.tEn: Gemini: A Family of Highly Capable Multimodal Models
papers.tZh: Gemini：一个高度能干的多模态模型家族
papers.sEn: Gemini Ultra is the first model to achieve human-expert performance on MMLU and sets new state-of-the-art in 30 of 32 benchmarks.
contrib: Introduces Gemini family (Ultra, Pro, Nano) with SOTA on 30/32 benchmarks across text, image, audio, video.
First model to surpass human-expert performance on MMLU (90.04%), a comprehensive exam benchmark.
Demonstrates strong cross-modal reasoning, e.g., understanding messy handwriting and solving physics problems.
Achieves efficient on-device deployment with Gemini Nano, excelling in summarization and reading comprehension.
Presents comprehensive post-training strategy (SFT, RLHF) for alignment and safety, deployed in Gemini and Gemini Advanced.
Advances multimodal capabilities: video understanding, audio ASR, image generation, and multilingual translation.
limits: Benchmark results may be affected by data contamination; HellaSwag results required decontamination.
Limited evaluation of Gemini Ultra on audio tasks; audio performance not yet reported for the largest model.
Relies on massive compute infrastructure (TPUv4 superpods) and sophisticated distributed training, limiting reproducibility.
Safety mitigation relies on post-training methods; potential for harmful outputs remains despite efforts.
Context window limited to 32K tokens, which may restrict long-document or long-video understanding.

papers.tEn: Weak-to-strong generalization
papers.tZh: 弱到强泛化
papers.sEn: Weak-to-strong generalization shows that small models can supervise large models to achieve strong performance, even on hard problems where the small model fails.
contrib: Proposes weak-to-strong generalization as a new research direction for superalignment.
Shows GPT-2-level model can elicit most of GPT-4's capabilities, achieving GPT-3.5-level performance.
Demonstrates strong models generalize beyond weak supervisor's errors on hard problems.
Introduces a simple method encouraging strong models to be more confident, improving generalization.
Provides empirical evidence that naive RLHF may scale poorly to superhuman models.
Opens up iterative empirical progress on superalignment by using current models as analogies.
limits: Method fails on ChatGPT preference data, indicating limited applicability.
Disanalogy: future models may imitate weak human errors more easily than current models.
Only tested on NLP tasks; generalization to other domains is uncertain.
Requires strong pretrained models; may not work for models without latent knowledge.
Proof of concept with limited scale; real superalignment may need more robust methods.

papers.tEn: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
papers.tZh: SGLang：结构化语言模型程序的高效执行
papers.sEn: SGLang achieves up to 6.4x higher throughput than state-of-the-art systems for complex LLM programs.
contrib: Proposes SGLang, a domain-specific language with primitives for LLM programming, supporting parallelism, control flow, nested calls, and external calls.
Develops an interpreter that executes SGLang programs with Python, managing prompt states as asynchronous streams for intra-program parallelism.
Builds a compiler that compiles SGLang programs into computational graphs, enabling classical compiler optimizations like code movement and prefetching.
Introduces RadixAttention, a novel technique for automatic KV cache reuse across multiple generation calls using a radix tree with LRU eviction.
Demonstrates up to 6.4x throughput improvement over state-of-the-art inference systems on diverse LLM tasks including agents, reasoning, and JSON decoding.
Shows productivity gains with 55% fewer lines of code compared to OpenAI APIs for complex prompting flows.
limits: Tracing and compiler lack support for data-dependent control flows, limiting compilation to programs without dynamic branches.
Current tokenization algorithm may create artifacts at prompt and generation boundaries, requiring token healing for resolution.
Grammar-constrained decoding is not yet implemented, requiring future integration of efficient techniques and careful batching.
The system has not been tested on extremely large models (e.g., 100B+ parameters) or distributed settings, limiting scalability claims.
Compiler optimizations using GPT-4 for code movement are not fully reliable, with failures in understanding semantic meaning in some cases.

papers.tEn: Analyzing and Improving the Training Dynamics of Diffusion Models
papers.tZh: 分析与改进扩散模型的训练动态
papers.sEn: We identify and rectify uneven training dynamics in diffusion models by redesigning layers to preserve activation/weight magnitudes, achieving 1.81 FID on ImageNet-512, and propose a post-hoc EMA tuning method.
contrib: Identifies and rectifies uncontrolled activation and weight magnitude drifts in ADM diffusion models, achieving new SOTA FID 1.81 on ImageNet-512.
Proposes post-hoc EMA to tune EMA parameters after training without retraining, revealing interactions with architecture, training time, and guidance.
Systematic magnitude-preserving design eliminates training drifts and imbalances, yielding better networks at equal computational cost.
Shows that a small unconditional model suffices for classifier-free guidance, reducing computational overhead of guidance by nearly 50%.
Improves deterministic FID on ImageNet-64 from 2.22 to 1.58 at similar complexity, and further to 1.33 via scaling.
limits: Modifications tailored to ADM U-Net; applicability to other diffusion architectures like RIN or DiT is not verified.
Post-hoc EMA requires storing multiple weight snapshots during training, increasing storage overhead.
Magnitude-preserving design relies on statistical assumptions (uncorrelated features, equal variance) that may not hold perfectly.
Dropout is beneficial for large models but harmful for small ones, creating an additional hyperparameter dependency.
Optimal EMA length differs between FID and DINOv2-based Fréchet distance, indicating metric-dependent sensitivity.

papers.tEn: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
papers.tZh: Mamba：具有选择性状态空间的线性时间序列建模
papers.sEn: Mamba achieves linear-time sequence modeling with selective state spaces, outperforming Transformers in efficiency and performance across modalities including language, audio, and genomics.
contrib: Proposes selective state space models (SSMs) that allow input-dependent filtering and forgetting, overcoming key weakness of prior LTI SSMs.
Designs a hardware-aware parallel algorithm for the recurrent mode, enabling efficient training and inference with linear scaling in sequence length.
Introduces Mamba, a simplified architecture without attention or MLP blocks, achieving 5x higher inference throughput than Transformers.
Demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across language, audio, and genomics, with Mamba-3B outperforming Transformers of the same size and matching those twice its size.
Shows that selective SSMs enable effective long-context modeling, with performance improving up to million-length sequences.
Provides open-source model code and pre-trained checkpoints to facilitate further research.
limits: Selection mechanism may reduce performance on continuous signal data where LTI SSMs excel, such as audio and video.
Mamba has not been validated at larger scales (e.g., 7B+ parameters) where Transformers are dominant, leaving scalability uncertain.
The hardware-aware algorithm relies on specific GPU memory hierarchy (e.g., HBM and SRAM), potentially limiting generalizability to other hardware.
Mamba lacks the rich ecosystem of Transformer-based models, such as fine-tuning, prompting, and instruction tuning, which may limit practical adoption.
The input-dependent selection mechanism may introduce training instability or require more careful hyperparameter tuning compared to LTI models.

papers.tEn: Adversarial Diffusion Distillation
papers.tZh: 对抗性扩散蒸馏
papers.sEn: ADD enables single-step real-time image synthesis with foundation models, outperforming GANs and LCMs in one step and matching SDXL in four steps.
contrib: Introduces Adversarial Diffusion Distillation (ADD), a method for 1-4 step sampling of foundational image diffusion models.
Combines adversarial loss and score distillation to achieve high fidelity in few-step generation.
ADD-XL outperforms teacher SDXL in 4 steps and LCM-XL in 1 step, per user studies.
First method to enable single-step real-time image synthesis with foundation models.
Ablation studies show importance of pretrained student, discriminator conditioning, and loss combination.
Retains iterative refinement capability, unlike pure GAN approaches.
limits: Requires pretrained diffusion model as teacher and student initialization.
Adversarial training may introduce instability and requires careful tuning.
Enhanced realism at cost of slightly decreased sample diversity.
Evaluation limited to 512x512 resolution; higher resolutions not tested.
Performance depends on choice of weighting schedule for distillation loss.

papers.tEn: Stable Video Diffusion: Scaling Latent Video Diffusion Models to Large Datasets
papers.tZh: 稳定视频扩散：将潜在视频扩散模型扩展到大型数据集
papers.sEn: Stable Video Diffusion achieves state-of-the-art text-to-video and image-to-video generation by scaling latent video diffusion models with a systematic curation process and three-stage training.
contrib: Proposes a systematic data curation workflow to transform large uncurated video collections into quality datasets for generative video modeling.
Identifies and evaluates three distinct training stages for video latent diffusion models: text-to-image pretraining, video pretraining, and high-quality video finetuning.
Trains state-of-the-art text-to-video and image-to-video models outperforming prior models in human preference studies.
Demonstrates that the base model provides a powerful motion representation for downstream tasks like image-to-video and camera motion LoRA modules.
Shows that the video diffusion model can be finetuned into a strong multi-view generator, outperforming specialized methods with less compute.
Releases code and model weights to facilitate reproducibility and further research.
limits: The model is limited to generating videos of up to 25 frames, restricting long-duration content.
Performance depends heavily on the quality and curation of the pretraining dataset, which may not generalize to all domains.
The study focuses on latent diffusion models and may not apply to other video generation architectures.
Human preference evaluations are subjective and may not capture all aspects of video quality.
The multi-view finetuning is limited to object-centric datasets and may not generalize to complex scenes.

papers.tEn: Six intuitions about large language models — Jason Wei
papers.tZh: 关于大型语言模型的六个直觉 — Jason Wei
papers.sEn: Large language models work surprisingly well because next-word prediction on massive self-supervised data is essentially massive multi-task learning.
contrib: Next-token prediction on large self-supervised data acts as massively multi-task learning, acquiring diverse skills implicitly.
Machine learning tasks can be framed as next-token prediction via in-context learning, enabling few-shot prompting.
Tokens vary in information density; chain-of-thought prompting gives models extra compute for hard tokens.
Scaling language model size and data improves loss predictably according to scaling laws, reducing uncertainty in training.
While overall loss scales smoothly, individual tasks may exhibit emergent abilities above a size threshold.
Real in-context learning of input-output mappings emerges only in sufficiently large language models, not small ones.
limits: The exact reasons why scaling works remain an open question; explanations are hand-wavy and unverified.
Emergent abilities cannot be predicted by extrapolating scaling curves from smaller models, complicating forecasts.
In-context learning may partly reflect formatting or label cues rather than genuine input-output mapping, especially in GPT-3.
Random-label experiments show small models ignore flipped labels, indicating limited true in-context learning at smaller scales.
Requiring models to reason via chain-of-thought adds inference compute, which may be costly for complex tasks.

papers.tEn: CogVLM: Visual Expert for Pretrained Language Models
papers.tZh: CogVLM：预训练语言模型的视觉专家
papers.sEn: CogVLM bridges the gap between frozen language models and image encoders via a trainable visual expert module, achieving state-of-the-art on 10 cross-modal benchmarks.
contrib: Introduces CogVLM, a visual language model with a trainable visual expert module for deep fusion of vision and language features.
Achieves state-of-the-art on 17 cross-modal benchmarks, including image captioning, VQA, and visual grounding.
Preserves full NLP capabilities of the pretrained language model by freezing its parameters and adding visual experts.
Validates the visual expert module and deep fusion through extensive ablation studies.
Releases model weights and SFT dataset to the public for research and industrial applications.
Explores critical factors in multimodal pretraining, including visual encoder scale, attention mask, and self-supervised loss.
limits: CogVLM-17B is trained from Vicuna-7B, limiting scalability to larger language models.
The visual expert module doubles parameters, increasing memory and storage requirements.
Performance on text-heavy tasks like TextVQA relies on visual encoder scale, with smaller encoders causing degradation.
The model requires large-scale pretraining data (1.5B image-text pairs), which may not be available for all domains.
Ablation studies are limited to 6,000 iterations, which may not reflect full convergence behavior.

papers.tEn: Vision-Language Foundation Models as Effective Robot Imitators
papers.tZh: 视觉语言基础模型作为有效的机器人模仿者
papers.sEn: RoboFlamingo, built on OpenFlamingo, achieves state-of-the-art robot manipulation by fine-tuning vision-language models with imitation learning.
contrib: Proposes RoboFlamingo, a simple framework adapting OpenFlamingo VLM to robot manipulation via imitation learning.
Decouples vision-language understanding and decision-making with a separate policy head for history modeling.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on CALVIN benchmark, with 2x improvement over prior methods.
Demonstrates zero-shot generalization to unseen visual contexts and language instructions.
Shows data efficiency: larger VLMs perform better with limited robot demonstration data.
Enables open-loop control and deployment on single GPU, reducing computational cost.
limits: Evaluated only in simulation (CALVIN), not on real-world robots.
Requires language-annotated demonstration data, which is scarce (only 1% of total data).
Open-loop control performance degrades without retraining with jump step demonstrations.
Generalization to synonymous instructions drops for later tasks in sequence.
Relies on OpenFlamingo backbone; performance may vary with other VLMs.

papers.tEn: Frontier risk and preparedness
papers.tZh: 前沿风险与准备
papers.sEn: To support the safety of highly-capable AI systems, we are developing our approach to catastrophic risk preparedness, including building a Preparedness team and launching a challenge.
contrib: Established a Preparedness team to evaluate and mitigate catastrophic risks from frontier AI models.
Introduced a Risk-Informed Development Policy (RDP) for capability evaluations and protective actions.
Launched an AI Preparedness Challenge to identify unknown risk areas, awarding $25K API credits to top submissions.
Categorized catastrophic risks including CBRN threats and autonomous replication and adaptation (ARA).
Found that ~70% of challenge submissions highlighted AI-enhanced persuasion as a key threat.
limits: The Preparedness Framework focuses on frontier models, not covering risks from less advanced AI.
The challenge may miss risks that are not easily identified through open submissions.
The RDP's effectiveness depends on accurate capability forecasting, which is uncertain.
The approach primarily addresses misuse risks, not alignment or structural risks.
Voluntary commitments lack enforcement mechanisms, limiting their impact.

papers.tEn: Eureka: Human-Level Reward Design via Coding Large Language Models
papers.tZh: Eureka：通过编码大型语言模型实现人类级别的奖励设计
papers.sEn: Eureka uses LLMs to automatically generate reward functions that outperform human-designed ones, enabling complex manipulation skills like pen spinning.
contrib: Proposes Eureka, a human-level reward design algorithm using LLMs for evolutionary optimization over reward code.
Outperforms human experts on 83% of 29 RL tasks with 52% average normalized improvement.
Enables gradient-free in-context RLHF, incorporating human feedback without model updating.
Demonstrates first simulated Shadow Hand pen spinning via curriculum learning with Eureka rewards.
Introduces reward reflection for targeted reward improvement via textual policy training summaries.
Achieves zero-shot reward generation from environment source code without task-specific prompts.
limits: Requires environment source code as input, limiting applicability to closed-source environments.
Evolutionary search relies on GPU-accelerated RL, which may be computationally expensive.
Performance depends on the quality of the backbone LLM (e.g., GPT-4), which may not be accessible.
Reward reflection requires tracking individual reward components, adding implementation complexity.
May not generalize to tasks with non-code-based fitness functions or sparse feedback.

papers.tEn: Llemma: An Open Language Model For Mathematics
papers.tZh: Llemma：一个开放的数学语言模型
papers.sEn: Llemma, an open language model for mathematics, outperforms all known open base models on MATH and supports tool use and theorem proving without finetuning.
contrib: Trained and released Llemma 7B and 34B models, new state-of-the-art open base models on MATH.
Released Proof-Pile-2, a 55B-token dataset of scientific papers, math web data, and code.
Demonstrated few-shot tool use (Python) and formal theorem proving without finetuning.
Open-sourced all artifacts: models, dataset, and code for reproducibility.
Provided analysis of data mixture, memorization, and supervised finetuning.
limits: Llemma's performance on MATH may be partially influenced by memorization of training data.
The 34B model training was limited to 50B tokens due to compute constraints.
Formal theorem proving evaluation is limited to few-shot settings without finetuning.
The study does not explore scaling laws or optimal data composition for math domain.

papers.tEn: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models
papers.tZh: 开放 X-具身：机器人学习数据集与 RT-X 模型
papers.sEn: A large-scale robotic dataset from 22 robots enables a generalist X-robot policy with positive transfer across platforms.
contrib: Assembled a large-scale multi-embodiment dataset from 22 robots across 21 institutions, covering 527 skills and 160,266 tasks.
Demonstrated positive transfer across robots using Transformer-based policies (RT-1-X and RT-2-X) trained on X-embodiment data.
Showed that RT-1-X outperforms original methods by 50% on small-scale datasets, and RT-2-X achieves 3x improvement in emergent skills.
Provided open-source resources: unified dataset, code, and pre-trained RT-1-X model for X-embodiment research.
Identified that model capacity and web-scale pretraining are critical for effective X-embodiment transfer.
Established a community-driven effort involving 21 institutions to grow the dataset over time.
limits: Does not consider robots with very different sensing and actuation modalities.
Does not study generalization to new robots not seen during training.
Does not provide a decision criterion for when positive transfer occurs.
Action and observation spaces are only coarsely aligned across embodiments.
Experiments limited to 9 manipulators out of 22 total embodiments in the dataset.

papers.tEn: Mistral 7B
papers.tZh: Mistral 7B：高性能高效语言模型
papers.sEn: Mistral 7B outperforms larger models like Llama 2 13B and Llama 1 34B in reasoning, math, and code, using efficient attention mechanisms.
contrib: Introduces Mistral 7B, a 7B-parameter model outperforming Llama 2 13B on all benchmarks and Llama 1 34B on reasoning, math, and code.
Leverages grouped-query attention (GQA) for faster inference and sliding window attention (SWA) for efficient long sequence handling.
Demonstrates that a smaller model can achieve performance comparable to much larger models, compressing knowledge more than previously thought.
Provides Mistral 7B – Instruct, a fine-tuned chat model surpassing Llama 2 13B – Chat on human and automated benchmarks.
Introduces rolling buffer cache and pre-fill chunking to reduce memory usage and improve inference efficiency.
Releases models under Apache 2.0 license with reference implementation for easy deployment.
limits: Performance on knowledge benchmarks shows lower compression rate (1.9x) due to limited parameter count.
Evaluation protocol differences may affect direct comparison with Llama 2 results on some benchmarks.
Safety evaluation uses a limited set of 175 unsafe prompts; real-world robustness may vary.
Sliding window attention theoretical span of 131K tokens may not be fully utilized in practice.
Fine-tuned instruct model is a preliminary demonstration; no proprietary data or training tricks used.

papers.tEn: Improved Baselines with Visual Instruction Tuning
papers.tZh: 通过视觉指令调优改进基线模型
papers.sEn: Simple modifications to LLaVA, including using CLIP-ViT-L-336px with MLP projection and adding academic VQA data, achieve state-of-the-art across 11 benchmarks with only 1.2M public data and ~1 day training on 8 A100s.
contrib: Shows that LLaVA's fully-connected vision-language connector is powerful and data-efficient.
Introduces simple modifications: MLP projection and academic VQA data with response formatting prompts.
Achieves state-of-the-art across 11 benchmarks with only 1.2M public data and ~1 day training on 8 A100s.
Demonstrates that visual instruction tuning is more important than large-scale pre-training for LMMs.
Proposes a single response formatting prompt to balance short and long-form answers without extra data processing.
Provides fully reproducible and affordable baselines for future LMM research.
limits: Uses full image patches, prolonging training iterations compared to visual resamplers.
Cannot process multiple images due to lack of data and context length limits.
Problem-solving capabilities limited in certain domains despite complex instruction following.
Not exempt from hallucinations and misinformation, requiring caution in critical applications.

papers.tEn: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
papers.tZh: 高效流式语言模型：注意力汇聚机制
papers.sEn: StreamingLLM enables LLMs to handle infinite-length sequences by leveraging attention sinks from initial tokens.
contrib: Identifies attention sink phenomenon where initial tokens attract high attention scores, crucial for window attention performance.
Proposes StreamingLLM framework enabling LLMs to generalize to infinite sequence lengths without fine-tuning.
Demonstrates that adding a placeholder token as a dedicated attention sink during pre-training improves streaming deployment.
Achieves up to 22.2x speedup over sliding window recomputation baseline in streaming settings.
Validates that four initial tokens suffice as attention sinks for stable streaming performance across multiple model families.
Shows that pre-training with a sink token does not harm convergence or downstream task accuracy.
limits: StreamingLLM does not expand the attention window size or improve long-context utilization.
Increasing cache size does not consistently lower perplexity, indicating limited context utilization.
The method relies on relative positional encoding; absolute positional encoding may require adaptation.
Attention sink phenomenon may not generalize to non-autoregressive models or encoder-only architectures.
StreamingLLM's performance degrades when the number of initial tokens is insufficient (e.g., one or two).

papers.tEn: Qwen Technical Report
papers.tZh: Qwen 技术报告
papers.sEn: Qwen is a comprehensive LLM series with strong performance across tasks, including chat, coding, and math.
contrib: Qwen base models outperform larger counterparts on multiple benchmarks, using up to 3 trillion tokens for pretraining.
Qwen-Chat models trained with RLHF achieve competitive performance, closely trailing GPT-4 in human evaluation.
Qwen demonstrates advanced tool-use, code interpreter, and agent capabilities, surpassing open-source alternatives.
Code-Qwen and Math-Qwen-Chat specialized models significantly outperform open-source peers, approaching GPT-3.5 on code and math tasks.
Qwen series includes multilingual support, efficient tokenization (152K vocab), and context length extension via dynamic NTK-aware interpolation.
limits: Qwen still lags behind proprietary models like GPT-4 on complex reasoning and creative tasks despite strong benchmarks.
The effectiveness of RLHF for alignment is debated; potential drawbacks like reduced diversity or overfitting remain.
Context length extension techniques (NTK, LogN) are training-free but may degrade performance on longer sequences beyond 8K tokens.
Specialized models (Code-Qwen, Math-Qwen) may lose general-purpose capability due to domain-specific pretraining.
Benchmark evaluations may not fully capture real-world alignment and safety; human evaluation limited to Chinese only.

papers.tEn: Announcing Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy
papers.tZh: Anthropic 负责任扩展政策发布
papers.sEn: Anthropic publishes Responsible Scaling Policy to manage catastrophic risks from increasingly capable AI systems.
contrib: Proposes AI Safety Levels (ASL) framework modeled on biosafety standards to manage catastrophic risks from scaling.
Defines ASL-1 to ASL-3 with specific criteria and safety measures, including red-teaming and security requirements.
Commits to pause training if scaling outpaces safety compliance, incentivizing safety research.
Aims to create a 'race to the top' dynamic among frontier labs by aligning competitive incentives with safety.
Emphasizes iterative policy updates due to rapid AI progress, unlike static biosafety standards.
limits: ASL-4+ measures remain undefined, relying on unsolved research like interpretability for assurance.
Policy may not cover all catastrophic risks, e.g., from models acting autonomously in unforeseen ways.
Effectiveness depends on accurate capability evaluation, which is challenging for frontier models.
Voluntary adoption may not prevent a race to the bottom if other labs ignore similar policies.
Current ASL-2 measures overlap with existing commitments, offering limited new risk mitigation.

papers.tEn: Centaurs and Cyborgs on the Jagged Frontier
papers.tZh: 锯齿前沿的半人马与赛博格
papers.sEn: Exploring the implications of AI for work, education, and life.
contrib: Consultants using GPT-4 completed 12.2% more tasks, 25.1% faster, with 40% higher quality.
AI acts as a skill leveler, boosting low performers by 43% more than top performers.
The 'Jagged Frontier' concept: AI capability is uneven, with tasks inside/outside an invisible boundary.
Two effective human-AI collaboration modes: Centaur (clear task division) and Cyborg (deep integration).
AI can cause 'falling asleep at the wheel', reducing accuracy on tasks outside its frontier.
AI outputs are higher quality but more homogeneous; human-AI collaboration yields better variety and correctness.
limits: Study limited to elite consultants; results may not generalize to other professions or contexts.
AI's 'Jagged Frontier' is dynamic and model-specific; findings may not hold for future models.
Experiment used GPT-4 via API; different interfaces or fine-tuning could alter outcomes.
AI-induced homogeneity in outputs may reduce innovation and diversity in problem-solving.
The study did not explore long-term effects on skill development or organizational dynamics.

papers.tEn: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
papers.tZh: 面向大语言模型服务的高效内存管理：PagedAttention
papers.sEn: PagedAttention reduces KV cache waste by 2-4x throughput improvement for LLM serving.
contrib: Identifies memory allocation challenges in LLM serving and quantifies their impact on performance.
Proposes PagedAttention, an attention algorithm operating on non-contiguous paged memory for KV cache.
Designs and implements vLLM, a distributed LLM serving engine built on PagedAttention.
Achieves near-zero waste in KV cache memory via block-level management and on-demand allocation.
Enables flexible KV cache sharing within and across requests for complex decoding algorithms.
Demonstrates 2-4x throughput improvement over state-of-the-art systems like FasterTransformer and Orca.
limits: PagedAttention introduces 20-26% higher attention kernel latency compared to FasterTransformer.
Performance gains are less pronounced when the system is compute-bound rather than memory-bound.
Block size choice involves trade-off between GPU utilization and fragmentation; default 16 may not suit all workloads.
Swapping recovery method incurs overhead with small block sizes due to numerous small data transfers.
Techniques are specific to LLM serving and may not benefit other GPU workloads with static memory patterns.

papers.tEn: Qwen-VL: A Versatile Vision-Language Model for Understanding, Localization, Text Reading, and Beyond
papers.tZh: Qwen-VL：一个多功能的视觉语言模型，用于理解、定位、文本阅读等
papers.sEn: Qwen-VL series achieves new records on visual-centric benchmarks and real-world dialog.
contrib: Introduced Qwen-VL series, large-scale vision-language models with fine-grained understanding, grounding, and text-reading.
Designed a 3-stage training pipeline with a visual receptor, input-output interface, and multilingual cleaned corpus.
Achieved state-of-the-art results on image captioning, VQA, visual grounding, and text-oriented benchmarks.
Demonstrated strong few-shot and zero-shot performance, comparable to larger models like Flamingo-80B.
Qwen-VL-Chat outperformed existing chatbots on real-world dialog benchmarks like TouchStone and MME.
Released open-source models supporting multilingual, multi-image, and fine-grained visual understanding.
limits: Limited to 7B parameter scale; larger models may yield better performance.
Visual encoder resolution capped at 448x448; higher resolutions could improve fine-grained tasks.
Training data primarily English and Chinese; performance on other languages may be limited.
No integration with other modalities like speech or video; future work needed.
Instruction tuning data size (350k) relatively small; larger datasets could enhance dialogue ability.

papers.tEn: Code Llama: Open Foundation Models for Code
papers.tZh: Code Llama：用于代码的开放基础模型
papers.sEn: Code Llama is a family of state-of-the-art open large language models for code, with specialized versions for Python and instruction following, supporting up to 100k tokens and infilling.
contrib: Releases Code Llama, a family of large language models for code based on Llama 2 with state-of-the-art performance among open models.
Provides multiple variants: foundation models (Code Llama), Python specializations (Code Llama - Python), and instruction-following models (Code Llama - Instruct) in 7B, 13B, 34B, and 70B sizes.
Supports infilling (fill-in-the-middle) for 7B, 13B, and 70B models, enabling code completion in IDEs.
Extends context length to 100K tokens via long context fine-tuning (LCFT) with modified RoPE base period.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on HumanEval (67% pass@1) and MBPP (65% pass@1) among open models.
Code Llama - Python 7B outperforms Llama 2 70B on HumanEval and MBPP, and all models surpass other public models on MultiPL-E.
limits: Infilling and long context fine-tuning slightly degrade performance on standard short-sequence benchmarks like HumanEval and MBPP.
The 34B model lacks infilling capability, limiting its use in real-time code completion scenarios.
Long context fine-tuning reduces performance on short prompts (under 4K tokens) by up to 2 BLEU points.
Safety evaluations rely on automatic benchmarks and limited red teaming, which may not capture all risks.
Instruction fine-tuning may cause over-refusal or false refusals on benign prompts, as noted in red teaming.

papers.tEn: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
papers.tZh: AgentBench：评估作为智能体的大语言模型
papers.sEn: AgentBench is a multi-dimensional benchmark with 8 environments to evaluate LLMs as agents, revealing significant performance gaps between top commercial and open-source models.
contrib: Introduces AgentBench, a multi-dimensional benchmark with 8 environments for evaluating LLMs as agents.
Evaluates 27 LLMs, revealing significant performance gap between top commercial and open-source models.
Identifies poor long-term reasoning, decision-making, and instruction following as main obstacles for LLM agents.
Shows code training and high-quality alignment data can improve agent performance.
Releases datasets, environments, and an integrated evaluation toolkit for AgentBench.
limits: Only evaluates text-only LLMs, excluding multi-modal models.
Open-source LLMs evaluated are limited to those smaller than 70B parameters.
Uses only basic Chain-of-Thought prompting, not advanced strategies like reflection or search.
Evaluation may not fully reflect real-world deployment due to simplified environments.
Score normalization method may obscure absolute performance differences across tasks.

papers.tEn: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
papers.tZh: RT-2：视觉-语言-动作模型将网络知识迁移至机器人控制
papers.sEn: RT-2 integrates web-scale vision-language models into robotic control, enabling emergent semantic reasoning and generalization.
contrib: Proposes vision-language-action (VLA) models that co-fine-tune VLMs on robotic trajectory data and web-scale vision-language tasks.
Introduces RT-2, a family of VLA models derived from PaLI-X and PaLM-E, with up to 55B parameters.
Demonstrates that representing robot actions as text tokens enables direct fine-tuning of VLMs for robotic control.
Shows significant improvements in generalization to novel objects, scenes, and instructions via web-scale pretraining transfer.
Reveals emergent capabilities including symbol understanding, reasoning, and human recognition from vision-language pretraining.
Demonstrates chain-of-thought reasoning in VLA models for multi-stage semantic reasoning tasks.
limits: Physical skills are limited to the distribution of skills seen in robot data; no new motions from web data.
High computational cost of large VLA models may hinder real-time control at high frequencies.
Limited availability of open-source VLM models suitable for building VLA models.
Evaluation is confined to a specific robot platform and kitchen environment, limiting generality.
Co-fine-tuning requires balancing robot and web data, which may be dataset-dependent.

papers.tEn: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
papers.tZh: Llama 2：开放的基础模型与微调聊天模型
papers.sEn: Llama 2 is a collection of pretrained and fine-tuned LLMs from 7B to 70B parameters, with Llama 2-Chat optimized for dialogue, outperforming open-source models and potentially substituting closed-source ones.
contrib: Developed and released Llama 2, a collection of pretrained and fine-tuned LLMs from 7B to 70B parameters.
Introduced Llama 2-Chat, optimized for dialogue, outperforming open-source chat models on most benchmarks.
Provided detailed fine-tuning and safety improvement methodology, including RLHF and Ghost Attention.
Demonstrated that Llama 2-Chat 70B is competitive with closed-source models like ChatGPT on human evaluations.
Released models for research and commercial use, with responsible use guide and code examples.
Shared novel observations such as tool usage emergence and temporal knowledge organization.
limits: Human evaluations limited to 4k prompts, not covering all real-world use cases.
Safety testing conducted only in English, not covering all scenarios.
Pretraining data may contain biases and toxicity, requiring further safety tuning before deployment.
Llama 2 70B still has a significant gap compared to GPT-4 and PaLM-2-L on coding benchmarks.
Reward model accuracy may degrade if not exposed to new sample distribution from iterative updates.

papers.tEn: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models
papers.tZh: Retentive Network：大型语言模型中 Transformer 的继任者
papers.sEn: RetNet achieves training parallelism, low-cost O(1) inference, and good performance, making it a strong successor to Transformer for large language models.
contrib: Proposes Retentive Network (RetNet) as a foundation architecture for large language models, achieving training parallelism, low-cost inference, and good performance.
Introduces a multi-scale retention mechanism with three computation paradigms: parallel, recurrent, and chunkwise recurrent.
Theoretically derives the connection between recurrence and attention, enabling dual-form sequence modeling.
Demonstrates O(1) inference complexity, significantly reducing memory and latency compared to Transformers.
Achieves competitive language modeling performance and favorable scaling results across model sizes.
Provides efficient long-sequence modeling via chunkwise recurrent representation with linear complexity.
