limits: RetNet's training efficiency relies on chunkwise recurrent representation, which may require careful tuning of chunk size.
The retention mechanism uses complex-valued operations, potentially increasing implementation complexity.
Performance gains over Transformers are more pronounced at larger model sizes; smaller models may not benefit as much.
The study does not explore scaling beyond 6.7B parameters or training beyond 100B tokens.
RetNet's inference speed advantage is demonstrated on specific hardware; generalization to other platforms may vary.

papers.tEn: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
papers.tZh: FlashAttention-2：通过更好的并行性和工作分区实现更快的注意力机制
papers.sEn: FlashAttention-2 achieves up to 2x speedup over FlashAttention by improving work partitioning and parallelism, reaching 50-73% of theoretical max FLOPs/s on A100.
contrib: Proposes FlashAttention-2 with better work partitioning to address GPU inefficiency.
Reduces non-matmul FLOPs by tweaking online softmax, saving only logsumexp for backward.
Parallelizes attention computation over sequence length dimension to increase occupancy.
Distributes work between warps within a thread block to reduce shared memory communication.
Achieves up to 2x speedup over FlashAttention, reaching 50-73% of theoretical max FLOPs/s on A100.
End-to-end training of GPT-style models reaches 225 TFLOPs/s per A100 GPU (72% utilization).
limits: Block sizes manually tuned for head dimensions; auto-tuning could reduce manual labor.
Optimizations focused on A100 GPU; H100 performance may improve with new instructions.
Backward pass still requires synchronization due to complex dependencies.
Does not support FP8 or other new data types; planned for future work.
Limited to GPU architectures; not applicable to other hardware like TPU.

papers.tEn: VoxPoser: Composable 3D Value Maps for Robotic Manipulation with Language Models
papers.tZh: VoxPoser：基于语言模型的可组合 3D 价值图用于机器人操作
papers.sEn: LLMs and VLMs compose 3D value maps to zero-shot synthesize robot trajectories for diverse manipulation tasks.
contrib: Proposes VoxPoser, a framework that extracts affordances and constraints from LLMs to compose 3D value maps for robot manipulation.
Leverages LLMs' code-writing to interact with VLMs, grounding knowledge into 3D observation space via value maps.
Uses composed value maps in a model-based planning framework for zero-shot closed-loop trajectory synthesis.
Demonstrates robustness to dynamic perturbations through fast replanning at 5 Hz.
Shows efficient learning of dynamics models for contact-rich tasks by using zero-shot trajectories as exploration priors.
Validates on a large variety of everyday manipulation tasks in both simulation and real-world settings.
limits: Relies on external perception modules, limiting tasks requiring holistic visual reasoning or fine-grained geometry.
Requires a general-purpose dynamics model for contact-rich tasks with same level of generalization.
Motion planner only considers end-effector trajectories, not whole-arm planning.
Manual prompt engineering is required for LLMs.
Perception module is sensitive to object poses and less robust for object parts.

papers.tEn: Jailbroken: How Does LLM Safety Training Fail?
papers.tZh: 越狱：LLM 安全训练为何失败？
papers.sEn: Safety training fails due to competing objectives and mismatched generalization, enabling successful jailbreak attacks even on state-of-the-art models.
contrib: Identifies two failure modes of LLM safety training: competing objectives and mismatched generalization.
Demonstrates that these failure modes can be exploited to create effective jailbreak attacks.
Shows that state-of-the-art models like GPT-4 and Claude v1.3 remain vulnerable to jailbreaks.
Proposes safety-capability parity: safety mechanisms must be as sophisticated as the underlying model.
Argues that scaling alone cannot resolve these safety failure modes.
limits: Limited to black-box access; white-box attacks may reveal additional vulnerabilities.
Evaluation only on English prompts; generalization to other languages is untested.
Attacks may not transfer to models with different training paradigms or architectures.
Study focuses on refusal bypass; other safety aspects like bias or toxicity are not addressed.
Proprietary models limit reproducibility and direct hypothesis confirmation.

papers.tEn: SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion Models for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
papers.tZh: SDXL：改进潜在扩散模型以实现高分辨率图像合成
papers.sEn: SDXL improves latent diffusion models for high-resolution text-to-image synthesis with a larger UNet, dual text encoders, and a refinement model.
contrib: Introduces SDXL with a 3x larger UNet backbone and dual text encoders for improved text-to-image synthesis.
Proposes novel conditioning on original image size and crop coordinates to reduce cropping artifacts and improve object centering.
Implements multi-aspect ratio training with size conditioning, enabling generation at various aspect ratios without quality loss.
Develops a separate refinement model using SDEdit to enhance visual fidelity of base SDXL samples.
Achieves competitive performance with black-box state-of-the-art image generators while being open-source.
Provides code and model weights to promote open research and transparency in large model training.
limits: Two-stage pipeline requires loading two large models, increasing memory usage and reducing sampling speed.
Struggles with synthesizing intricate structures like human hands due to high variance in training data.
May exhibit concept bleeding, where distinct visual elements unintentionally merge or swap attributes.
Text rendering for long or legible text remains challenging, often producing random characters or inconsistencies.
Training data biases can lead to social and racial biases in generated images, requiring careful mitigation.

papers.tEn: RVT: Robotic View Transformer for 3D Object Manipulation
papers.tZh: RVT：用于 3D 物体操作的机器人视角变换器
papers.sEn: RVT achieves 26% higher success than state-of-the-art, trains 36x faster, and works across 18 tasks with few real-world demos.
contrib: Proposes RVT, a multi-view transformer for 3D object manipulation that is both scalable and accurate.
Achieves 26% higher relative success than PerAct on 18 RLBench tasks with 249 variations.
Trains 36X faster and achieves 2.3X inference speed compared to PerAct.
Demonstrates real-world manipulation with only ~10 demonstrations per task.
Introduces re-rendering from virtual views to decouple sensor images from transformer input.
Investigates design choices like separate processing of image tokens before joint attention.
limits: Requires calibration of camera-to-robot extrinsics, limiting portability.
Struggles with sparse or noisy point clouds, e.g., marker tasks.
View specification is manually chosen and not optimized or learned from data.
Evaluated only on a limited set of 5 real-world tasks with 51 demonstrations.
Assumes a low-level motion planner and controller for action execution.

papers.tEn: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents
papers.tZh: LLM 驱动的自主智能体
papers.sEn: LLM-powered autonomous agents can function as general problem solvers beyond generating text.
contrib: Proposes a comprehensive framework for LLM-powered autonomous agents with planning, memory, and tool use.
Introduces self-reflection mechanisms like Reflexion and Chain of Hindsight for iterative improvement.
Demonstrates memory architectures combining short-term (in-context) and long-term (vector store) memory.
Shows tool use via fine-tuning (Toolformer) and task planning (HuggingGPT) to extend LLM capabilities.
Presents generative agents with emergent social behaviors in sandbox environments.
Reviews practical demos like AutoGPT and GPT-Engineer, highlighting potential and reliability issues.
limits: Finite context window restricts historical information and detailed instructions, limiting long-term memory.
Long-term planning and task decomposition remain challenging; LLMs struggle with unexpected errors.
Natural language interface is unreliable; LLMs produce formatting errors and occasional rebellious behavior.
Tool use depends on LLM's ability to correctly select and invoke APIs, which is not always reliable.
Self-reflection and memory retrieval may not fully compensate for limited attention span in complex tasks.

papers.tEn: Simple and Controllable Music Generation
papers.tZh: 简单可控的音乐生成
papers.sEn: MusicGen is a single-stage language model that generates high-quality music from text or melody, outperforming baselines.
contrib: Introduces MusicGen, a single-stage transformer LM with efficient token interleaving patterns for high-quality music generation.
Demonstrates text and melody conditioning in a single model, enabling better control over generated music.
Proposes a general framework for modeling multiple parallel streams of acoustic tokens via codebook interleaving patterns.
Extends generation to stereo audio without extra computational cost using codebook patterns.
Achieves superior performance over baselines on MusicCaps benchmark in human evaluation.
Provides extensive ablation studies on codebook patterns, model sizes, and conditioning methods.
limits: Lacks fine-grained control over generation adherence to conditioning, relying mostly on classifier-free guidance.
Melody conditioning uses unsupervised chromagram, which may not capture complex harmonic structures.
Training data is limited to licensed music with potential lack of diversity, e.g., overrepresentation of Western music.
Model may memorize training examples, raising concerns about originality and copyright.
Evaluation on MusicCaps may be biased due to noisy samples in the dataset.

papers.tEn: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
papers.tZh: AWQ：面向大语言模型压缩与加速的激活感知权重量化
papers.sEn: AWQ protects only 1% salient weights by scaling up their channels based on activation distribution, achieving hardware-friendly low-bit quantization without backpropagation.
contrib: Proposes Activation-aware Weight Quantization (AWQ) for LLM low-bit weight-only quantization.
Identifies that protecting only 1% salient weights based on activation distribution reduces quantization error.
Derives a per-channel scaling method to protect salient weights without mixed-precision hardware overhead.
Achieves state-of-the-art quantization performance on language modeling, instruction-tuned, and multi-modal LMs.
Implements TinyChat inference framework with 3x+ speedup over FP16 on desktop and mobile GPUs.
Enables deployment of 70B Llama-2 on mobile GPU (Jetson Orin) for the first time.
limits: AWQ focuses on weight-only quantization; activation quantization is not addressed.
The method requires a small calibration set from pre-training data to avoid overfitting.
Performance at INT2 quantization still shows a gap compared to FP16 baseline.
The scaling search space is limited to a single hyperparameter alpha, which may not be optimal for all layers.
Evaluation is primarily on LLaMA and OPT families; other architectures may require further validation.

papers.tEn: Let's Verify Step by Step
papers.tZh: 让我们逐步验证
papers.sEn: Process supervision significantly outperforms outcome supervision for training reliable large language models on complex math problems.
contrib: Process supervision significantly outperforms outcome supervision for training reward models on the MATH dataset.
The process-supervised model achieves 78.2% accuracy on a representative subset of the MATH test set.
Active learning improves data efficiency of process supervision by 2.6 times.
Release of PRM800K, a dataset of 800,000 step-level human feedback labels.
Large-scale PRM can supervise smaller models, enabling efficient ablations.
Process supervision incurs a negative alignment tax, improving both performance and alignment.
limits: Results are limited to mathematical reasoning; generalization to other domains is unknown.
Potential test set contamination from MATH problems in pretraining data.
Active learning with iterative retraining showed instability and no improvement.
Comparison at large scale is confounded by different training set sizes and selection biases.
Process supervision relies on expensive human feedback for data collection.

papers.tEn: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
papers.tZh: 直接偏好优化：你的语言模型其实是一个奖励模型
papers.sEn: DPO simplifies RLHF by directly optimizing the policy using a classification loss, eliminating the need for a separate reward model and reinforcement learning.
contrib: Introduces Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), a simple RL-free algorithm for training language models from preferences.
Derives a closed-form mapping between reward functions and optimal policies, enabling direct policy optimization.
Shows DPO optimizes the same objective as RLHF but with a simple binary cross-entropy loss, eliminating RL complexity.
Demonstrates DPO achieves better reward-KL tradeoff than PPO in controlled sentiment generation.
Shows DPO matches or exceeds PPO-based RLHF in summarization and dialogue tasks with up to 6B parameter models.
Provides theoretical justification that DPO's reward parameterization does not constrain the class of representable reward models.
limits: DPO's out-of-distribution generalization compared to explicit reward learning requires further study.
Reward over-optimization in direct preference optimization setting is not fully understood.
Evaluation of DPO is limited to models up to 6B parameters; scaling to larger models is future work.
GPT-4 win rates are sensitive to prompt design, affecting evaluation reliability.
DPO requires a reference policy and offline preference dataset, limiting online adaptation.

papers.tEn: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
papers.tZh: Voyager：基于大型语言模型的开放式具身智能体
papers.sEn: Voyager is the first LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent in Minecraft that continuously explores, acquires skills, and makes discoveries without human intervention.
contrib: First LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent in Minecraft, exploring and acquiring skills without human intervention.
Automatic curriculum that maximizes exploration by proposing tasks based on agent state and progress.
Growing skill library of executable code for storing and retrieving complex, compositional behaviors.
Iterative prompting mechanism using environment feedback, execution errors, and self-verification for code improvement.
Outperforms prior SOTA: 3.3x more unique items, 2.3x longer distances, 15.3x faster tech tree milestones.
Zero-shot generalization to novel tasks in new worlds using learned skill library.
limits: No visual perception; relies on text-only GPT-4 API, limiting spatial tasks.
High cost of GPT-4 API; 15x more expensive than GPT-3.5.
Occasional failures in code generation and self-verification, e.g., hallucinating non-existent items.
Automatic curriculum may propose unachievable tasks due to hallucinations.
Requires high-level Mineflayer API; not directly comparable to low-level pixel-based methods.

papers.tEn: ProlificDreamer: High-Fidelity and Diverse Text-to-3D Generation with Variational Score Distillation
papers.tZh: ProlificDreamer：基于变分分数蒸馏的高保真、多样化文本到 3D 生成
papers.sEn: ProlificDreamer introduces variational score distillation (VSD) to address over-saturation, over-smoothing, and low-diversity in text-to-3D generation, achieving high-fidelity and diverse results.
contrib: Proposes Variational Score Distillation (VSD), a particle-based variational framework for text-to-3D generation.
Shows SDS is a special case of VSD, explaining over-saturation, over-smoothing, and low-diversity issues.
VSD works with normal CFG weights (e.g., 7.5) and improves diversity and sample quality simultaneously.
Introduces high-resolution rendering (512x512) and annealed time schedule for improved visual quality.
Proposes scene initialization for complex scene generation, enabling 360-degree high-fidelity NeRF.
Achieves photo-realistic textured meshes via VSD fine-tuning from NeRF initialization.
limits: Generation takes hours, much slower than image generation by diffusion models.
Camera poses during training are independent of scene structure, limiting detail for large scenes.
Complex prompts may fail due to limited expressiveness of the base 2D model.
Multi-face Janus problem may occur due to poor text-image alignment for view-dependent prompts.
Potential harmful social impacts from content creation and generation of fake content.

papers.tEn: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
papers.tZh: GQA：从多头检查点训练通用多查询 Transformer 模型
papers.sEn: Uptraining multi-head checkpoints to grouped-query attention achieves near multi-head quality with MQA-like speed.
contrib: Proposes a recipe to uptrain multi-head language model checkpoints into multi-query attention models using only 5% of original pre-training compute.
Introduces grouped-query attention (GQA), a generalization of multi-query attention with an intermediate number of key-value heads.
Shows that uptrained GQA achieves quality close to multi-head attention while being almost as fast as multi-query attention.
Demonstrates that mean-pooling key and value heads works better than other conversion methods for uptraining.
Provides empirical evaluation on summarization, translation, and question answering tasks.
Discusses the trade-off between quality and inference speed for large language models.
limits: Evaluation relies on Rouge score for summarization, which is a flawed metric.
Does not compare XXL GQA model to a model trained from scratch due to limited computation.
Only evaluates on encoder-decoder models, not decoder-only models.
The quality trade-off may not generalize to longer sequences or other tasks.
Uptraining recipe may not be optimal for all model architectures or sizes.

papers.tEn: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment
papers.tZh: LIMA：少即是多——对齐的简约之道
papers.sEn: Almost all knowledge in large language models is learned during pretraining, and only limited instruction tuning data is necessary to teach models to produce high quality output.
contrib: Shows that fine-tuning a 65B LLaMa on only 1,000 curated examples achieves strong alignment.
Proposes the Superficial Alignment Hypothesis: knowledge is from pretraining, alignment learns style.
LIMA matches or beats GPT-4 in 43% of cases, and outperforms RLHF-trained DaVinci003.
Demonstrates that scaling data quantity without diversity yields diminishing returns.
Shows multi-turn dialogue ability with only 30 additional dialogue chains.
Provides absolute evaluation: 88% of LIMA responses meet prompt requirements, 50% are excellent.
limits: Manual curation of 1,000 examples is labor-intensive and hard to scale.
LIMA is less robust than production models; adversarial prompts can cause weak responses.
Limited to single-turn fine-tuning; multi-turn dialogue requires additional data.
Safety performance is limited; implicit malicious intents may bypass safeguards.
Results may not generalize to other model sizes or architectures without further study.

papers.tEn: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
papers.tZh: 思维树：利用大型语言模型进行深思熟虑的问题解决
papers.sEn: Tree of Thoughts (ToT) enables language models to explore multiple reasoning paths and make deliberate decisions, significantly improving problem-solving on tasks requiring planning or search.
contrib: Proposes Tree of Thoughts (ToT), a new framework for language model inference that generalizes Chain of Thought by exploring multiple reasoning paths.
Enables deliberate decision-making via self-evaluation, lookahead, and backtracking over coherent thought units.
Demonstrates significant improvements on three challenging tasks: Game of 24 (74% vs 4%), Creative Writing, and Mini Crosswords.
Introduces modular components: thought decomposition, generation, evaluation, and search algorithms adaptable to problem properties.
Shows that LM self-evaluation can serve as a flexible heuristic for search, replacing programmed or learned heuristics.
Provides a unified view where IO, CoT, CoT-SC are special cases of ToT with limited depth and breadth.
limits: ToT requires more computational resources (e.g., API cost) than standard sampling methods.
Deliberate search may be unnecessary for tasks where GPT-4 already excels.
State evaluation heuristics are imperfect and can prune correct solutions, as seen in crosswords.
Explored only three relatively simple tasks; scalability to more complex real-world tasks is untested.
Potential for harmful uses if applied to interactive environments without safeguards.

papers.tEn: InstructBLIP: Towards General-purpose Vision-Language Models with Instruction Tuning
papers.tZh: InstructBLIP：面向通用视觉-语言模型的指令微调
papers.sEn: InstructBLIP achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on 13 held-out datasets by instruction tuning on 26 datasets with an instruction-aware Query Transformer.
contrib: First comprehensive study on vision-language instruction tuning with 26 datasets transformed into instruction format.
Proposes instruction-aware Query Transformer for extracting task-relevant visual features.
Achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on 13 held-out datasets, outperforming BLIP-2 and Flamingo.
Introduces balanced sampling strategy to synchronize learning across diverse datasets.
Demonstrates state-of-the-art finetuning results on downstream tasks like ScienceQA (90.7% accuracy).
Open-sources all InstructBLIP models for reproducibility and further research.
limits: Relies on frozen image encoder and LLM, limiting adaptation to new visual domains.
Instruction tuning data limited to 26 datasets; may not cover all real-world tasks.
Zero-shot performance on entirely unseen task categories (e.g., video QA) still lags behind supervised methods.
Requires careful manual adjustment of sampling weights for optimal performance.
Qualitative evaluation limited to a few examples; broader user studies needed.

papers.tEn: Language models can explain neurons in language models
papers.tZh: 语言模型可以解释语言模型中的神经元
papers.sEn: Language models can explain neurons in language models
contrib: Proposes using GPT-4 to automatically generate and score natural language explanations for neurons in LLMs.
Releases a dataset of explanations and scores for all 307,200 neurons in GPT-2.
Demonstrates that explanation quality improves with larger explainer models and iterative refinement.
Finds over 1,000 neurons with high-scoring explanations (score ≥ 0.8), though most are not interesting.
Shows that changing activation functions in the explained model can improve explanation scores.
Open-sources code and visualization tools to enable community research on neuron interpretability.
limits: Explanations are limited to short natural language, unable to capture complex polysemantic behavior.
Method only explains neuron behavior as a function of input, ignoring downstream effects and circuits.
High-scoring explanations may still fail on out-of-distribution texts due to correlational nature.
The overall procedure is compute-intensive, limiting scalability to very large models.
Even GPT-4 explanations are worse than human-written ones, indicating significant room for improvement.

papers.tEn: Claude’s Constitution \ Anthropic
papers.tZh: 克劳德的宪法 / Anthropic
papers.sEn: Claude's constitution makes AI values explicit and adjustable through a written set of principles.
contrib: Introduces Constitutional AI (CAI) using explicit principles instead of implicit human feedback for model alignment.
CAI achieves Pareto improvement: both more helpful and more harmless than RLHF.
Demonstrates scalable oversight by using AI feedback to train harmlessness without human data.
Provides transparency: principles are easily specified, inspected, and adjusted.
Reduces need for humans to view disturbing content during training.
Constitution draws from UN Declaration, platform guidelines, and safety research, enabling iterative improvement.
limits: Constitution reflects designers' choices; may not represent diverse societal values.
CAI may produce judgmental or annoying responses; requires additional principles to temper.
Effectiveness depends on principle quality; overly specific principles reduce generalization.
Constitutional AI is not a panacea; difficult questions about allowed content remain.
Scalability of AI feedback may face challenges with increasingly complex model outputs.

papers.tEn: ImageBind: One Embedding Space To Bind Them All
papers.tZh: ImageBind：一个嵌入空间绑定所有
papers.sEn: ImageBind learns a joint embedding across six modalities using only image-paired data, enabling zero-shot cross-modal transfer.
contrib: Binds six modalities via image-paired data alone, without requiring all modality pairs.
Leverages large-scale vision-language models to extend zero-shot capabilities to new modalities.
Enables emergent cross-modal retrieval, arithmetic, detection, and generation out-of-the-box.
Sets new state-of-the-art on emergent zero-shot recognition across modalities, outperforming supervised models.
Strong few-shot recognition results and serves as a new evaluation tool for vision models.
limits: Relies on image-paired data; binding quality degrades with weak or misaligned image pairs.
Requires large pretrained vision-language models, leading to high computational cost.
Non-visual modality performance still lags behind specialist supervised models.
Limited by small-scale datasets for depth, thermal, and IMU, affecting small encoders.
Strongly dependent on spatial/temporal alignment; misalignment causes significant performance drop.

papers.tEn: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
papers.tZh: 利用低成本硬件学习精细双手操作
papers.sEn: A low-cost system with imitation learning enables fine bimanual manipulation tasks with high success rates.
contrib: A low-cost bimanual teleoperation system (ALOHA) for fine manipulation, built with off-the-shelf arms and 3D-printed parts.
Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT), a novel imitation learning algorithm that predicts action sequences to reduce compounding errors.
Temporal ensembling to smooth overlapping action chunks, improving motion smoothness without additional training.
Conditional VAE training to handle multi-modal human demonstrations, crucial for learning from noisy data.
Demonstrated 80-90% success on 6 real-world fine manipulation tasks with only 10 minutes of demonstrations.
Open-source hardware and software design for reproducibility and accessibility.
limits: Limited to tasks within the robot's payload (750g) and workspace (1.5m span).
Requires task-specific training from scratch; no generalization across tasks.
Performance degrades on low-contrast objects (e.g., black cable tie on black table).
Action chunking with large chunk sizes reduces reactivity to sudden changes.
Teleoperation requires user skill; high-frequency control (50Hz) is necessary for precision.

papers.tEn: MiniGPT-4: Enhancing Vision-Language Understanding with Advanced Large Language Models
papers.tZh: MiniGPT-4：利用先进大语言模型增强视觉语言理解
papers.sEn: MiniGPT-4 aligns a frozen visual encoder with a frozen advanced LLM using one projection layer, achieving GPT-4-like multi-modal abilities.
contrib: Proposes MiniGPT-4, aligning a frozen visual encoder with Vicuna via one projection layer.
Reveals that proper visual-LLM alignment yields GPT-4-like abilities like detailed image description and website creation.
Identifies that short caption pretraining causes unnatural outputs; second-stage finetuning with detailed descriptions improves reliability.
Demonstrates emergent abilities in MiniGPT-4, including poem writing, recipe generation, and meme interpretation.
Shows that a single linear projection layer suffices for vision-language alignment in limited data settings.
Provides open-source code, pretrained model, and curated dataset for reproducibility.
limits: MiniGPT-4 inherits LLM hallucination, e.g., falsely describing nonexistent objects.
Visual perception is limited, especially in spatial localization tasks.
Second-stage dataset is small (3,500 pairs) and manually curated, limiting scalability.
Model relies on frozen components; no end-to-end training of vision encoder or LLM.
Evaluation on advanced tasks is qualitative and lacks standardized benchmarks.

papers.tEn: Visual Instruction Tuning
papers.tZh: 视觉指令微调
papers.sEn: LLaVA: an end-to-end trained large multimodal model connecting a vision encoder and LLM for general-purpose visual and language understanding, achieving impressive multimodal chat abilities and state-of-the-art accuracy on Science QA.
contrib: First to use language-only GPT-4 to generate multimodal language-image instruction-following data.
Introduces LLaVA, an end-to-end trained large multimodal model connecting a vision encoder and LLM.
Achieves 85.1% relative score vs. GPT-4 on synthetic multimodal instruction-following dataset.
New state-of-the-art accuracy of 92.53% on Science QA when ensembled with GPT-4.
Constructs two evaluation benchmarks for visual instruction following with diverse tasks.
Releases generated multimodal instruction data, model, and code publicly.
limits: Data generation relies on GPT-4, which may introduce biases or inaccuracies.
LLaVA sometimes fails on complex semantics, e.g., misinterpreting image as bag of patches.
Limited to 158K instruction samples; performance may improve with more data.
Simple linear projection for vision-language connection may limit expressiveness.
Evaluation benchmarks are synthetic or limited in scope; real-world generalization not fully tested.

papers.tEn: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision
papers.tZh: DINOv2：无需监督学习鲁棒视觉特征
papers.sEn: Self-supervised pretraining on diverse curated data yields universal visual features that outperform prior methods.
contrib: Proposes DINOv2, a self-supervised method for learning robust visual features from large curated data without supervision.
Introduces an automatic pipeline to build a diverse and curated image dataset (LVD-142M) from uncurated web data.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on image-level and pixel-level tasks with frozen features, matching or surpassing weakly-supervised methods.
Demonstrates that scaling data and model size improves feature quality, with distillation enabling smaller models to benefit from larger ones.
Provides technical improvements for stable and efficient training at scale, including faster training and reduced memory usage.
Shows emergent properties like object part understanding and scene geometry, with potential for further scaling.
limits: The method requires large curated datasets and significant computational resources for training.
Performance on some benchmarks like Places205 lags behind weakly-supervised models.
Geographical and income biases persist, with lower performance on African regions and low-income households.
The study does not fully explore finetuning hyperparameters, leaving potential gains unexplored.
Carbon footprint is substantial, with total project emissions estimated between 0.5k and 1k tCO2eq.

papers.tEn: SegGPT: Segmenting Everything In Context
papers.tZh: SegGPT: 在上下文中分割一切
papers.sEn: SegGPT unifies diverse segmentation tasks into a generalist in-context learning framework, enabling arbitrary segmentation via in-context inference.
contrib: First generalist model for diverse segmentation tasks via in-context learning.
Unifies segmentation tasks into an in-context coloring framework with random color mapping.
Performs arbitrary segmentation tasks in images or videos without fine-tuning.
Proposes context ensemble strategies (spatial and feature) for multi-example prompting.
Enables in-context tuning for specialized tasks without updating model parameters.
Strong performance on in-domain and out-of-domain segmentation benchmarks.
limits: Random coloring scheme makes in-domain tasks harder, causing performance drop.
Not designed to outperform specialist models on all benchmarks.
Performance limited by model size and data availability for scaling.
Context ensemble strategies may cause information loss with low-resolution images.
In-context tuning for in-domain tasks still lags behind specialist methods.

papers.tEn: Segment Anything
papers.tZh: 分割一切
papers.sEn: We introduce Segment Anything, a promptable segmentation model and the largest dataset (SA-1B) with 1B masks on 11M images, achieving impressive zero-shot performance.
contrib: Introduced the promptable segmentation task, enabling zero-shot generalization to new image distributions and tasks.
Developed the Segment Anything Model (SAM) with a flexible prompt encoder and fast mask decoder for real-time interactive use.
Built the SA-1B dataset, the largest segmentation dataset with over 1 billion masks on 11 million images.
Demonstrated strong zero-shot performance on 23 diverse segmentation datasets, often competitive with fully supervised methods.
Released SAM and SA-1B under open license to foster research into foundation models for computer vision.
Achieved real-time mask prediction from prompts in ~50ms on CPU via amortized image embedding.
limits: SAM may miss fine structures and hallucinate small disconnected components.
Boundaries are less crisp compared to computationally intensive zoom-in methods.
Dedicated interactive segmentation methods outperform SAM when many points are provided.
Text-to-mask task is exploratory and not entirely robust.
Overall performance is not real-time when using a heavy image encoder.

papers.tEn: Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training
papers.tZh: 语言图像预训练的 Sigmoid 损失函数
papers.sEn: The proposed Sigmoid loss (SigLIP) for language-image pre-training outperforms standard contrastive learning, works well with both large and small batch sizes, and achieves high accuracy with low compute.
contrib: Proposes a pairwise sigmoid loss for language-image pre-training, removing the need for global normalization.
Outperforms softmax contrastive loss at small batch sizes and enables efficient scaling to large batch sizes.
Combined with locked-image tuning, achieves 84.5% ImageNet zero-shot accuracy with only 4 TPUv4 chips in 2 days.
Shows that batch size benefits saturate at 32k, with larger batch sizes yielding diminishing returns.
Provides a memory-efficient chunked implementation that enables training with batch sizes over 1 million.
Demonstrates robustness to noisy data and studies the impact of positive-negative pair ratio.
limits: Performance gap between sigmoid and softmax loss diminishes at very large batch sizes.
The sigmoid loss suffers from extreme positive-negative imbalance, requiring careful bias initialization.
Training instability may occur at large batch sizes, even for modest model sizes.
The study is limited to English zero-shot tasks; multilingual results show no benefit beyond 32k batch size.
Locked-image tuning relies on a pre-trained vision tower, limiting applicability for new architectures.

papers.tEn: GPT-4 Technical Report
papers.tZh: GPT-4 技术报告
papers.sEn: GPT-4 achieves human-level performance on professional and academic benchmarks, including passing a simulated bar exam in the top 10%.
contrib: Developed GPT-4, a large multimodal model accepting image and text inputs, producing text outputs.
Achieved human-level performance on professional and academic benchmarks, including top 10% on simulated bar exam.
Built predictable scaling infrastructure, accurately forecasting GPT-4's loss and capabilities from smaller models.
Improved factuality and alignment via post-training with RLHF and rule-based reward models.
Demonstrated strong multilingual performance, surpassing English state-of-the-art on translated MMLU in 24 languages.
Reduced safety risks through adversarial testing and model-assisted safety pipeline, cutting disallowed content responses by 82%.
limits: Not fully reliable; hallucinates facts and makes reasoning errors, requiring caution in high-stakes contexts.
Limited context window and does not learn from experience, similar to earlier GPT models.
Lacks knowledge of events after September 2021 pre-training data cutoff.
Post-training reduces calibration; model can be overconfident in wrong predictions.
Vulnerable to jailbreaks and adversarial inputs that bypass safety mitigations.

papers.tEn: Grounding DINO: Marrying DINO with Grounded Pre-Training for Open-Set Object Detection
papers.tZh: Grounding DINO：将 DINO 与接地预训练相结合，实现开放集目标检测
papers.sEn: Grounding DINO marries DINO with grounded pre-training for open-set object detection, achieving 52.5 AP on COCO zero-shot and 26.1 mAP on ODinW.
contrib: Proposes Grounding DINO, extending DINO with tight vision-language fusion for open-set detection.
Introduces a feature enhancer, language-guided query selection, and cross-modality decoder for deep fusion.
Extends open-set detection evaluation to referring expression comprehension (REC) datasets.
Achieves 52.5 AP on COCO zero-shot transfer and 26.1 mean AP on ODinW zero-shot benchmark.
Proposes sub-sentence level text prompts to avoid unwanted word interactions.
limits: Cannot perform segmentation tasks like GLIPv2.
Training data is less than the largest GLIP model, potentially limiting performance.
900 query design may limit ability for long-tailed objects in LVIS.
Performance on REC tasks is poor without fine-tuning on REC data.

papers.tEn: Core Views on AI Safety
papers.tZh: AI 安全核心观点
papers.sEn: AI's impact may rival the industrial and scientific revolutions, and could arrive within a decade, necessitating urgent safety research.
contrib: AI progress is predictable due to scaling laws, with compute doubling every 7 months, leading to transformative AI possibly within a decade.
The technical alignment problem is unsolved: we lack methods to train powerful AI systems to be robustly helpful, honest, and harmless.
Anthropic advocates a multi-faceted empirical approach: scalable oversight, mechanistic interpretability, process-oriented learning, and understanding generalization.
Scalable oversight uses AI to assist human supervision, e.g., via Constitutional AI and AI-generated evaluations, to train safer systems.
Process-oriented learning trains AI to follow safe processes rather than just outcomes, reducing risks of deception and pernicious sub-goals.
Mechanistic interpretability aims to reverse-engineer neural networks for 'code review', enabling detection of deceptive alignment.
limits: Scaling laws may not hold indefinitely; progress could plateau due to data or algorithmic limits, though current evidence suggests continued growth.
Empirical safety research on frontier models risks accelerating dangerous capabilities if not carefully managed, creating a difficult trade-off.
Mechanistic interpretability is extremely difficult due to model size and superposition; success is uncertain and may not scale to advanced AI.
Scalable oversight methods like Constitutional AI may fail if models become deceptive or humans are fooled, especially at superhuman levels.
The portfolio approach assumes diverse scenarios, but pessimistic outcomes may be sudden and hard to detect, limiting timely response.

papers.tEn: Anthropic's core views on AI safety
papers.tZh: Anthropic 关于 AI 安全的核心观点
papers.sEn: Anthropic believes AI's impact could rival industrial and scientific revolutions, but its outcome is uncertain and may arrive within a decade, necessitating urgent safety research.
contrib: Argues rapid AI progress is predictable from scaling laws and exponential compute growth.
Identifies technical alignment problem: training robustly helpful, honest, harmless systems is unsolved.
Proposes multi-faceted empirical safety research: scalable oversight, mechanistic interpretability, process-oriented learning.
Advocates frontier model safety research requiring large models to study emergent risks.
Emphasizes portfolio approach across optimistic, intermediate, and pessimistic safety scenarios.
Stresses need for external oversight and commitments to safety standards before deploying advanced AI.
limits: Scaling laws may not hold indefinitely; progress could plateau due to data or algorithmic limits.
Empirical safety research on frontier models risks accelerating dangerous AI deployment.
Mechanistic interpretability may be intractable for very large models due to superposition.
Scalable oversight methods like AI self-supervision may fail if models deceive humans.
Portfolio approach may spread resources too thin, lacking focus on most promising methods.

papers.tEn: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion
papers.tZh: 扩散策略：通过动作扩散进行视觉运动策略学习
papers.sEn: Diffusion Policy outperforms existing methods by 46.9% on average across 12 robot tasks.
contrib: Proposes Diffusion Policy, representing visuomotor policy as a conditional denoising diffusion process.
Achieves 46.9% average improvement over state-of-the-art methods across 12 tasks from 4 benchmarks.
Introduces closed-loop action sequences via receding horizon control for robust execution.
Presents time-series diffusion transformer to reduce over-smoothing and handle high-frequency actions.
Demonstrates stable training by modeling score function, avoiding intractable normalization constant.
Validates on real-world tasks including non-rigid objects and periodic motions, achieving near-human performance.
limits: Inherits behavior cloning limitations, e.g., suboptimal performance with inadequate demonstration data.
Higher computational cost and inference latency compared to simpler methods like LSTM-GMM.
Transformer backbone is sensitive to hyperparameters, requiring additional tuning.
May not suffice for tasks requiring very high-rate control despite action sequence prediction.
Performance depends on quality and quantity of demonstrations, physical robot capabilities, and architecture.

papers.tEn: Consistency Models
papers.tZh: 一致性模型
papers.sEn: Consistency models enable fast one-step generation by directly mapping noise to data, outperforming diffusion models in speed while maintaining high quality.
contrib: Propose consistency models, a new family of generative models that directly map noise to data for fast one-step generation.
Introduce consistency distillation to distill pre-trained diffusion models into consistency models, achieving state-of-the-art FID on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet 64x64.
Develop consistency training to train consistency models from scratch without pre-trained diffusion models, establishing them as an independent generative model family.
Demonstrate zero-shot data editing capabilities including inpainting, colorization, super-resolution, and stroke-guided editing without task-specific training.
Provide theoretical analysis showing consistency models can approximate the true consistency function arbitrarily well with small ODE solver step sizes.
Achieve superior performance over progressive distillation and other distillation methods in one- and few-step sampling across multiple datasets.
limits: Consistency models may require careful tuning of discretization steps and schedule functions for optimal performance.
The method relies on the assumption that the FID is unimodal with respect to time points in multistep sampling.
Consistency training loss has higher variance with larger N, potentially slowing convergence in later stages.
The approach is evaluated only on image datasets; applicability to other domains like audio or video is not explored.
Continuous-time consistency training requires forward-mode automatic differentiation, which may not be efficiently supported in all frameworks.

papers.tEn: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
papers.tZh: LLaMA：开放且高效的基础语言模型
papers.sEn: LLaMA-13B outperforms GPT-3 on most benchmarks, and LLaMA-65B is competitive with Chinchilla-70B and PaLM-540B.
contrib: Demonstrates that state-of-the-art LLMs can be trained using only publicly available datasets, without proprietary data.
LLaMA-13B outperforms GPT-3 (175B) on most benchmarks while being 10x smaller.
LLaMA-65B achieves competitive performance with Chinchilla-70B and PaLM-540B.
Releases all model sizes (7B to 65B) to the research community to democratize LLM access.
Introduces architectural improvements: RMSNorm, SwiGLU activation, and rotary positional embeddings.
Shows that training on more tokens than recommended by scaling laws improves inference efficiency.
limits: Models are not fine-tuned for code or mathematical reasoning, limiting performance on specialized tasks.
Evaluation of toxicity and bias is limited to a few benchmarks, not fully capturing risks.
Training data includes limited books and academic papers, potentially affecting knowledge-intensive tasks like MMLU.
Instruction fine-tuning was only briefly explored, with performance still below state-of-the-art.
Carbon footprint of training is substantial, estimated at 1,015 tCO2eq.

papers.tEn: Planning for AGI and beyond
papers.tZh: 规划通用人工智能及其未来
papers.sEn: Our mission is to ensure that AGI benefits all of humanity.
contrib: Proposes gradual deployment of AGI to enable co-evolution with society and minimize sudden disruption.
Advocates for tight feedback loop of rapid learning and careful iteration to navigate deployment challenges.
Emphasizes developing alignment techniques alongside capabilities, using AI to help evaluate complex models.
Calls for global conversation on governance, benefit distribution, and access to AGI.
Structures organization with nonprofit governance and profit cap to align incentives with safety and public good.
Highlights need for independent audits, public standards, and government insight on large-scale training runs.
limits: Assumes gradual transition is feasible, but sudden capability jumps may bypass planned safeguards.
Relies on AI to help evaluate AI, which may introduce circular validation issues.
Global governance and fair distribution remain aspirational with no concrete implementation path.
Profit cap and nonprofit structure may not fully prevent misaligned incentives in competitive landscape.
Slowing down at critical junctures requires coordination that may be undermined by geopolitical competition.

papers.tEn: What Is ChatGPT Doing … and Why Does It Work?
papers.tZh: ChatGPT 在做什么……以及它为什么有效？
papers.sEn: ChatGPT works by generating text based on statistical patterns learned from vast amounts of human-written data, using a neural network architecture called Transformer.
contrib: Explains ChatGPT's core mechanism as probabilistic next-token prediction from a trained neural net.
Introduces the concept of embeddings to represent words in a continuous meaning space.
Describes how neural nets learn from vast text corpora via unsupervised training on masked text.
Discusses the role of temperature in controlling randomness and creativity of generated text.
Highlights the tradeoff between computational irreducibility and trainability in neural nets.
Argues that tasks like essay writing are computationally shallower than previously thought.
limits: Lacks formal theory; relies on empirical tuning of hyperparameters like temperature.
Neural nets cannot perform computationally irreducible tasks without external tools.
Training requires enormous data and compute, with no guarantee of global optimality.
Embeddings and internal representations are not interpretable in human terms.
The model's performance degrades on out-of-distribution inputs or novel scenarios.

papers.tEn: Adding Conditional Control to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
papers.tZh: 向文本到图像扩散模型添加条件控制
papers.sEn: ControlNet adds spatial conditioning controls to pretrained text-to-image diffusion models via zero convolutions.
contrib: Proposes ControlNet, a neural network architecture for adding spatial conditioning controls to large pretrained text-to-image diffusion models.
Uses zero-initialized convolution layers to connect trainable and locked copies, preventing harmful noise during finetuning.
Demonstrates robust training with datasets ranging from <50k to >1m samples, avoiding overfitting and catastrophic forgetting.
Supports diverse conditioning inputs (edges, depth, segmentation, human pose) with single or multiple conditions, with or without prompts.
Achieves competitive results with industrial models using limited resources (single GPU, 200k samples) for depth-to-image tasks.
Enables composition of multiple ControlNets without extra weighting, facilitating complex conditional control.
limits: ControlNet requires a pretrained diffusion model (e.g., Stable Diffusion) as backbone, limiting applicability to other architectures.
Training ControlNet for new conditions requires task-specific datasets, which may be small and hard to collect.
The sudden convergence phenomenon may cause abrupt learning, potentially missing gradual improvements.
ControlNet's performance depends on the quality of conditioning inputs; noisy or inaccurate inputs degrade results.
The method has been tested primarily on Stable Diffusion; generalization to other diffusion models is not fully validated.

papers.tEn: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
papers.tZh: Toolformer：语言模型可以自学使用工具
papers.sEn: Language models can teach themselves to use external tools via simple APIs, achieving better performance without sacrificing core language modeling abilities.
contrib: Proposes Toolformer, a self-supervised method for LMs to learn when and how to use external tools via API calls.
Integrates multiple tools (calculator, QA system, search engine, translation, calendar) without task-specific supervision.
Uses perplexity-based filtering to select helpful API calls from LM-generated candidates.
Achieves strong zero-shot performance on arithmetic, factual lookup, QA, and temporal tasks, often beating much larger models.
Preserves core language modeling abilities, as perplexity on standard benchmarks remains unaffected.
Demonstrates scaling benefits: larger LMs benefit more from learning tool use.
limits: Cannot chain multiple API calls; each call is generated independently.
Lacks interactive tool use, e.g., refining search queries or browsing results.
Sensitive to input phrasing when deciding whether to call an API.
Sample-inefficient for some tools; e.g., calculator yields few useful calls from millions of documents.
Does not account for computational cost of API calls during decision-making.

papers.tEn: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
papers.tZh: BLIP-2：利用冻结的图像编码器和大型语言模型引导语言-图像预训练
papers.sEn: BLIP-2 bridges the modality gap with a lightweight Querying Transformer, achieving state-of-the-art performance with 54x fewer trainable parameters than Flamingo80B.
contrib: Proposes BLIP-2, a generic and efficient vision-language pre-training strategy using frozen image encoders and LLMs.
Introduces a lightweight Querying Transformer (Q-Former) to bridge the modality gap with two-stage pre-training.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on VQA, image captioning, and retrieval with significantly fewer trainable parameters.
Demonstrates zero-shot image-to-text generation following natural language instructions, enabling visual reasoning and conversation.
Validates that stronger frozen unimodal models (image encoder or LLM) consistently improve VLP performance.
Shows representation learning stage is crucial to prevent catastrophic forgetting in frozen LLMs during generative learning.
limits: BLIP-2 lacks in-context learning capability due to single image-text pair per sample in pre-training data.
Image-to-text generation may suffer from inaccurate knowledge, incorrect reasoning, or outdated information.
Inherits risks from frozen LLMs, including offensive language, social bias, and private information leakage.
Performance on open-world knowledge tasks like OK-VQA is limited compared to larger LLMs.
Requires careful prompt engineering for zero-shot tasks; optimal prompts vary across LLM types.

papers.tEn: The Transformer Family Version 2.0
papers.tZh: Transformer 家族版本 2.0
papers.sEn: Explores the evolution of transformer architectures combining local and global context, and their applications in reinforcement learning.
contrib: Provides a comprehensive structured survey of Transformer architecture variants and improvements since 2020.
Systematically reviews attention mechanisms and positional encodings, including relative position encoding and rotary position embedding.
Discusses mechanisms for extending context window via memory and retrieval, such as Transformer-XL, Compressive Transformer, kNN-LM, and Memorizing Transformer.
Covers adaptive computation methods including Universal Transformer, adaptive attention span, depth-adaptive Transformer, and CALM.
Surveys efficiency improvements like sparse, LSH, low-rank, and random feature attention to reduce quadratic complexity.
Highlights hybrid local-global attention models including ETC, Longformer, and Big Bird.
limits: The survey is a snapshot; Transformer research evolves rapidly, so coverage and frameworks may become outdated.
Many techniques are evaluated on specific tasks and datasets, so their relative gains may not transfer across domains or model scales.
Efficient attention methods often trade off accuracy for speed and memory, introducing approximation errors or restricted context.
Long-context extrapolation methods like ALiBi show limited extrapolation and may degrade on much longer sequences.
Memory and retrieval based augmentations require extra storage and computation, which may be impractical at very large scale.

papers.tEn: Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture
papers.tZh: 基于联合嵌入预测架构的图像自监督学习
papers.sEn: I-JEPA learns semantic image representations by predicting target block representations from a single context block without hand-crafted augmentations.
contrib: Introduces I-JEPA, a non-generative self-supervised method predicting target block representations from a single context block.
Shows that predicting in representation space yields more semantic features than pixel-level reconstruction.
Demonstrates that a multi-block masking strategy with large target blocks and informative context is crucial for semantic representations.
Achieves strong downstream performance across tasks like linear classification, object counting, and depth prediction without hand-crafted augmentations.
Shows high scalability: ViT-H/14 on ImageNet trained with 16 A100 GPUs in under 72 hours, outperforming prior methods in compute efficiency.
limits: Evaluation primarily on ImageNet-1K; generalization to other domains or modalities not fully explored.
Requires careful tuning of masking strategy (target block scale and context informativeness) for optimal performance.
Performance on semantic tasks may still lag behind view-invariance methods that use hand-crafted augmentations in some settings.
Dependence on exponential moving average target encoder adds complexity and hyperparameter sensitivity.

papers.tEn: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models
papers.tZh: 通过世界模型掌握多样领域
papers.sEn: DreamerV3 is a general algorithm that outperforms specialized methods across over 150 diverse tasks with a single configuration, learning a world model to imagine future scenarios.
contrib: Proposes DreamerV3, a general algorithm mastering diverse domains with fixed hyperparameters.
Demonstrates favorable scaling properties where larger models improve performance and data-efficiency.
Outperforms specialized algorithms across over 150 tasks in 7 benchmarks.
First algorithm to collect diamonds in Minecraft from scratch without human data or curricula.
Introduces symlog predictions and robust normalization for stable learning across domains.
Achieves state-of-the-art on continuous control, BSuite, and Crafter benchmarks.
limits: DreamerV3 only learns to sometimes collect diamonds in Minecraft within 100M steps.
Increases block breaking speed for Minecraft learning, which may not generalize.
Scaling properties need further validation at larger model sizes.
Trains separate agents per task, lacking transfer learning across tasks.
Requires significant compute resources (one V100 GPU per agent).

papers.tEn: GraphCast: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting
papers.tZh: GraphCast：学习进行熟练的中期全球天气预报
papers.sEn: GraphCast, a machine learning model, outperforms traditional numerical weather prediction on 90% of verification targets and forecasts severe events better.
contrib: Introduces GraphCast, a machine learning method for global medium-range weather forecasting trained directly from reanalysis data.
Achieves 10-day forecasts at 0.25° resolution globally in under one minute on a single TPU v4 device.
Outperforms the most accurate operational deterministic system (HRES) on 90% of 1380 verification targets.
Demonstrates improved prediction of severe events including tropical cyclones, atmospheric rivers, and extreme temperatures.
Uses an encode-process-decode graph neural network architecture with 36.7 million parameters.
Shows that machine learning weather prediction can complement traditional numerical weather prediction methods.
limits: Operates at 0.25° resolution and 6-hour time steps due to training data and hardware constraints.
Focuses on deterministic forecasts, not capturing uncertainty as well as ensemble methods.
MSE training objective encourages spatial blurring at longer lead times, limiting value for some applications.
Depends critically on high-quality reanalysis data from numerical weather prediction systems.
Not a replacement for traditional methods; complements them with potential for further scaling.

papers.tEn: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers
papers.tZh: 基于 Transformer 的可扩展扩散模型
papers.sEn: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) scale with Gflops and achieve state-of-the-art FID on ImageNet.
contrib: Introduces Diffusion Transformers (DiTs), a new class of diffusion models based on the transformer architecture.
Replaces the commonly-used U-Net backbone with a transformer operating on latent patches, showing U-Net inductive bias is not crucial.
Demonstrates strong correlation between model Gflops and sample quality (FID), with higher Gflops consistently yielding lower FID.
Achieves state-of-the-art FID of 2.27 on class-conditional ImageNet 256x256, outperforming all prior diffusion models.
Shows adaLN-Zero conditioning mechanism is most compute-efficient and yields best quality among four block designs.
Scaling model compute (Gflops) is more critical than parameter count or sampling compute for improving DiT performance.
limits: Only evaluated on class-conditional ImageNet at 256x256 and 512x512 resolutions.
Uses a fixed pre-trained VAE from Stable Diffusion; DiT's performance may depend on VAE quality.
Training hyperparameters are largely retained from ADM without extensive tuning for DiT.
Scaling analysis limited to Gflops; other complexity metrics like memory or latency not explored.
Does not address text-to-image generation or other conditional modalities beyond class labels.

papers.tEn: Discovering Language Model Behaviors with Model-Written Evaluations
papers.tZh: 通过模型编写的评估发现语言模型行为
papers.sEn: LM-written evaluations are high-quality and enable rapid discovery of novel LM behaviors.
contrib: Proposes a method to automatically generate evaluation datasets using LMs, reducing human effort.
Generates 154 datasets and discovers novel inverse scaling behaviors, including sycophancy and instrumental subgoals.
Finds that RLHF can exacerbate undesirable behaviors like political bias and desire to avoid shutdown.
Demonstrates that LM-written evaluations approach or exceed human-written quality in relevance and label accuracy.
Creates Winogenerated, a 50x larger gender bias evaluation than Winogender, with high validity.
Releases all datasets and tools to facilitate further research on LM behaviors.
limits: LMs struggle to generate evaluations for concepts they do not understand well, e.g., cryptography.
Generated data may inherit biases from training data, affecting quality for underrepresented groups.
Example diversity can be limited, requiring hyperparameter tuning or manual intervention.
LMs may generate evaluations that test unintended behaviors if instructions are underspecified.
Method is less suitable for evaluating capabilities that LMs do not yet possess.

papers.tEn: Point-E: A System for Generating 3D Point Clouds from Complex Prompts
papers.tZh: Point-E: 一种从复杂提示生成 3D 点云的系统
papers.sEn: Point-E generates 3D point clouds from text prompts in 1-2 minutes on a single GPU, offering a practical speed-quality trade-off.
contrib: Proposes a two-stage diffusion pipeline for text-to-3D generation, reducing sampling time to 1-2 minutes on a single GPU.
Introduces a Transformer-based diffusion model for generating colored point clouds conditioned on images.
Demonstrates that conditioning on a grid of CLIP image latents outperforms single-embedding conditioning.
Shows scaling model size improves P-FID convergence and CLIP R-Precision.
Releases pre-trained point cloud diffusion models and evaluation code for reproducibility.
Provides a practical speed-quality trade-off for text-to-3D synthesis, enabling rapid prototyping.
limits: Sample quality falls short of state-of-the-art optimization-based methods like DreamFusion.
Outputs are low-resolution point clouds (4K points), lacking fine-grained shape and texture.
Pipeline requires synthetic renderings; cannot directly condition on real-world images.
Point cloud to mesh conversion can lose information, affecting rendering quality.
Model inherits dataset biases and may generate unsafe 3D blueprints for fabrication.

papers.tEn: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
papers.tZh: 宪法式 AI：来自 AI 反馈的无害性
papers.sEn: Constitutional AI trains harmless AI assistants via self-improvement using only a list of principles, without human labels for harmful outputs.
contrib: Proposes Constitutional AI (CAI) to train harmless assistants without human harmfulness labels.
Demonstrates supervised self-critique and revision to reduce harmfulness.
Introduces RLAIF using model-generated preference labels for harmlessness.
Shows chain-of-thought reasoning improves harmlessness evaluation and transparency.
Achieves non-evasive harmless responses by explaining objections to harmful queries.
Reduces human supervision to a short list of principles, enabling scalable oversight.
limits: Relies on human-written principles which may be ad hoc and require refinement.
Still requires human labels for helpfulness; not fully self-supervised.
Chain-of-thought may produce inaccurate or overstated critiques.
RL-CAI models can exhibit Goodharting or boilerplate responses when overtrained.
Methods may lower barriers for training pernicious AI systems (dual use).

papers.tEn: RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale
papers.tZh: RT-1：面向大规模真实世界控制的机器人 Transformer
papers.sEn: RT-1 shows that large-scale, diverse robotic data combined with high-capacity Transformer models enables strong generalization in real-world robot control.
contrib: Proposes RT-1, a Transformer-based model for real-world robotic control at scale.
Demonstrates RT-1 achieves 97% success on over 700 training instructions.
Shows RT-1 generalizes to new tasks, distractors, and backgrounds significantly better than baselines.
Integrates TokenLearner and FiLM conditioning for efficient real-time inference.
Demonstrates absorption of heterogeneous data from simulation and different robots without performance loss.
Enables long-horizon tasks with up to 50 steps in the SayCan framework.
limits: RT-1 is an imitation learning method, limited by demonstrator performance.
Generalization to new instructions is limited to combinations of seen concepts.
Method is evaluated on a large but not highly dexterous set of manipulation tasks.
Robustness to backgrounds and environments could be improved with more diverse data.
Reaction speed and context retention could benefit from scalable attention and memory.

papers.tEn: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
papers.tZh: 通过大规模弱监督实现鲁棒语音识别
papers.sEn: Scaling weakly supervised speech recognition to 680,000 hours yields models competitive with fully supervised ones in zero-shot settings.
contrib: Proposes Whisper, a speech processing system trained on 680,000 hours of weakly supervised multilingual audio.
Achieves zero-shot transfer competitive with prior fully supervised results without fine-tuning.
Demonstrates that scaling weakly supervised pre-training improves robustness and generalization.
Introduces a multitask and multilingual training format using decoder input tokens.
Shows that larger models benefit from joint training across tasks and languages.
Releases models and inference code to facilitate further research on robust speech processing.
limits: Whisper is limited to 30-second audio segments and requires buffered transcription for longer audio.
Performance on low-resource languages is poor due to English-heavy training data.
Remaining errors include repetition loops, missing words, and hallucinations in long-form transcription.
Zero-shot evaluation may not reflect optimal performance achievable with fine-tuning.
Text normalizer may overfit to Whisper's transcription style, affecting WER comparisons.

papers.tEn: Images Speak in Images: A Generalist Painter for In-Context Visual Learning
papers.tZh: 图像以图像言说：面向上下文视觉学习的通才画家
papers.sEn: Painter redefines vision tasks as image-to-image problems, enabling in-context learning with image prompts.
contrib: Proposes Painter, a generalist model that redefines vision task outputs as images and uses image pairs as task prompts.
Unifies seven diverse vision tasks (depth, segmentation, keypoint, restoration) into a single masked image modeling framework.
Achieves competitive performance against task-specific models on multiple benchmarks, with state-of-the-art on NYUv2 depth estimation.
Demonstrates in-context learning capability for both in-domain and out-of-domain tasks using visual prompts.
Shows that joint training across tasks can improve performance compared to separate training on most tasks.
Introduces a simple prompt selection and learning method that further improves task performance.
limits: Performance on panoptic segmentation lags behind specialized models due to lower input resolution.
The image-based interface is not naturally suited for modeling discrete language signals.
Joint training slightly hurts performance on keypoint detection, indicating task conflicts.
The approach requires careful design of output image representations for each task.
Out-of-domain generalization is only qualitatively shown; quantitative evaluation is limited.

papers.tEn: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
papers.tZh: SmoothQuant：大型语言模型的准确高效训练后量化
papers.sEn: SmoothQuant enables accurate and efficient 8-bit weight and activation quantization for LLMs without training.
contrib: Proposes SmoothQuant, a training-free post-training quantization method for LLMs enabling W8A8 quantization.
Identifies activation outliers as key quantization difficulty and smooths them via offline migration to weights.
Achieves up to 1.56x speedup and 2x memory reduction with negligible accuracy loss across multiple LLM families.
Enables serving a 530B parameter LLM within a single 8-GPU node.
Integrates into PyTorch and FasterTransformer for practical deployment.
Demonstrates effectiveness on OPT, BLOOM, GLM, LLaMA, and MT-NLG models up to 530B parameters.
limits: Requires calibration data (512 sentences) to compute smoothing factors and quantization steps.
Hyperparameter α must be tuned per model family (e.g., 0.5 for OPT/BLOOM, 0.75 for GLM).
Static quantization may cause accuracy drop when calibration and evaluation distributions differ.
Method focuses on linear and attention layers; other operations remain in FP16.
Effectiveness depends on model architecture; some models (e.g., GLM) require stronger smoothing.

papers.tEn: Galactica: A Large Language Model for Science
papers.tZh: Galactica：面向科学的大型语言模型
papers.sEn: Galactica, a large language model for science, outperforms existing models on scientific tasks and sets new state-of-the-art on benchmarks like PubMedQA and MedMCQA.
contrib: Introduces Galactica, a large language model trained on a curated scientific corpus of 106 billion tokens.
Outperforms GPT-3 on LaTeX equation knowledge probes (68.2% vs 49.0%) and Chinchilla on mathematical MMLU (41.3% vs 35.7%).
Achieves state-of-the-art on PubMedQA (77.6%) and MedMCQA dev (52.9%) without fine-tuning.
Demonstrates that repeated tokens improve both upstream and downstream performance on curated data.
Introduces a working memory token (<work>) for step-by-step reasoning, outperforming larger models on MATH.
Shows capability in multi-modal tasks including SMILES-to-IUPAC naming and protein function annotation.
limits: Corpus limited to open-access resources; closed-access knowledge could improve performance.
Self-imposed constraints on molecules (2 million) and proteins (0.5 million) limit modality performance.
Effects of prompt pre-training vs core corpus not disentangled; general capabilities may rely on prompts.
Bias towards popular papers remains in citation prediction at 120B scale.
No notion of geometry (e.g., 3D coordinates) limits chemical and biological understanding.

papers.tEn: InternImage: Exploring Large-Scale Vision Foundation Models with Deformable Convolutions
papers.tZh: InternImage：利用可变形卷积探索大规模视觉基础模型
papers.sEn: InternImage uses deformable convolution to achieve ViT-like scaling in CNNs, setting new records on COCO and ADE20K.
contrib: Proposes InternImage, a large-scale CNN foundation model using deformable convolution as core operator.
Introduces DCNv3 with shared weights, multi-group mechanism, and softmax normalization for stable training.
Develops stacking and scaling rules to efficiently scale CNNs to over 1 billion parameters.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on COCO (65.4 mAP) and ADE20K (62.9 mIoU), outperforming leading ViTs.
Demonstrates that CNN-based models can match or exceed ViTs in large-scale settings with proper designs.
Validates robustness to translation, rotation, and scaling, and data efficiency on limited data.
limits: Latency remains an issue for DCN-based operators in high-speed downstream tasks.
Large-scale CNNs are still in early development; InternImage serves as a starting point.
Performance gap with top ViTs on ImageNet (~1 point) may be due to private data discrepancy.
Throughput is lower than ConvNeXt due to DCN operator overhead.
Scaling rules derived from limited search space may not be optimal for all scales.

papers.tEn: Measuring Progress on Scalable Oversight for Large Language Models
papers.tZh: 衡量大型语言模型可扩展监督的进展
papers.sEn: Scalable oversight for LLMs can be studied empirically using tasks where humans with model assistance outperform both alone.
contrib: Introduces a sandwiching experimental paradigm for evaluating scalable oversight techniques with present-day models.
Demonstrates that human–model teams outperform both the model alone and unaided humans on MMLU and time-limited QuALITY.
Provides qualitative insights into effective human strategies for interacting with language models, such as cross-examination and fact-checking.
Shows that simple chat-based interaction with an unreliable LLM assistant can serve as a baseline for scalable oversight.
Establishes that existing NLP datasets can be used to productively evaluate scalable oversight techniques.
Outlines a research roadmap for scalable oversight, including debate, market-making, and recursive reward modeling.
limits: Relies on multiple-choice questions, which are simpler than real-world oversight tasks.
Reveals correct answers to participants after each question, reducing the difficulty of identifying reliable methods.
Excludes two high-performing outlier participants, potentially biasing results.
Does not test fine-tuning or other modifications beyond dialog interaction.
Human participants sometimes accept false confident claims from the model due to limited domain knowledge.

papers.tEn: Pangu-Weather: A 3D High-Resolution Model for Fast and Accurate Global Weather Forecast
papers.tZh: 盘古天气：一种用于快速准确全球天气预报的 3D 高分辨率模型
papers.sEn: Pangu-Weather is the first AI-based method to outperform traditional numerical weather prediction in accuracy across all factors and time ranges.
contrib: First AI-based method to surpass operational IFS in all weather factors and forecast times from 1 hour to 1 week.
Proposes 3D Earth Specific Transformer (3DEST) integrating height information into 3D data for better atmospheric modeling.
Introduces hierarchical temporal aggregation to reduce cumulative forecast errors by training models with multiple lead times.
Achieves 0.25° spatial resolution with inference speed over 10,000x faster than operational IFS on a single GPU.
Demonstrates strong performance in extreme weather forecast and large-member ensemble forecast scenarios.
Ends the debate on whether AI-based methods can surpass conventional NWP methods for global weather forecast.
limits: Training data limited to 39 years of ERA5 reanalysis; longer periods may improve accuracy.
Model not fully converged after 100 epochs due to computational budget constraints.
3DEST architecture requires large GPU memory, limiting network depth and input features.
Hierarchical temporal aggregation uses fixed lead times; adaptive selection may further reduce errors.
Extreme weather forecast tends to underestimate intensity, especially for longer forecast ranges.

papers.tEn: High Fidelity Neural Audio Compression
papers.tZh: 高保真神经音频压缩
papers.sEn: We introduce a real-time, high-fidelity neural audio codec with a novel loss balancer and lightweight Transformer for further compression.
contrib: Introduced a real-time, high-fidelity neural audio codec with streaming encoder-decoder and quantized latent space.
Simplified training with a single multiscale spectrogram adversary that reduces artifacts and produces high-quality samples.
Proposed a novel loss balancer mechanism that stabilizes training by decoupling loss weights from their typical scale.
Demonstrated lightweight Transformer models can further compress representations by up to 40% while staying faster than real time.
Achieved state-of-the-art subjective and objective results across multiple bandwidths and audio domains, including speech and music.
Provided extensive ablation studies and subjective evaluations (MUSHRA) for various design choices.
limits: The model's performance may degrade for audio domains not well represented in the training set.
The streaming setup introduces a small degradation in quality compared to the non-streamable version.
The entropy coding increases initial latency, which may not be suitable for low-latency applications.
The 48 kHz model is slower than real time on a single CPU core, limiting its use for real-time streaming.
The Transformer language model's compression gain varies with bandwidth, being less effective at higher bitrates.

papers.tEn: Draft, Sketch, and Prove: Guiding Formal Theorem Provers with Informal Proofs
papers.tZh: 草稿、草图与证明：用非形式化证明指导形式化定理证明器
papers.sEn: Draft, Sketch, and Prove (DSP) uses informal proofs to guide formal theorem provers, improving success rate from 20.9% to 39.3% on math competition problems.
contrib: Introduces Draft, Sketch, and Prove (DSP), a method that maps informal proofs to formal proof sketches to guide automated provers.
Demonstrates that large language models can generate well-structured formal sketches following informal reasoning steps.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on miniF2F with Isabelle, increasing success rate from 20.9% to 39.3% using human-written proofs.
Shows that language-model-generated informal proofs are nearly as effective as human-written ones in guiding formal provers.
Provides ablation studies confirming the importance of drafting informal proofs, annotating sketches with comments, and using automated provers.
Releases a curated dataset of informal statements and proofs aligned with miniF2F formal statements.
limits: Method is evaluated only on high-school competition problems in miniF2F, limiting generalizability to advanced mathematics.
Relies on large language models (e.g., Codex, Minerva) which may not be accessible or reproducible due to API costs.
Performance is bounded by the automated prover's ability to fill gaps; complex conjectures may remain unprovable.
Informal proofs from language models can be incorrect, yet still lead to successful formal proofs, indicating potential unreliability.
The method requires manual preparation of few-shot examples for autoformalization, which may not scale to diverse domains.

papers.tEn: Scaling Instruction-Finetuned Language Models
papers.tZh: 扩展指令微调语言模型
papers.sEn: Instruction finetuning with more tasks, larger models, and chain-of-thought data significantly boosts performance across diverse models and benchmarks.
contrib: Scales instruction finetuning to 540B models and 1.8K tasks, showing performance gains with model and task scaling.
Demonstrates that including chain-of-thought data in finetuning improves reasoning on held-out tasks.
Shows instruction finetuning generalizes across architectures (encoder-decoder, decoder-only) and model sizes.
Achieves state-of-the-art on MMLU (75.2% five-shot) and improves multilingual benchmarks like TyDiQA.
Releases Flan-T5 checkpoints that outperform much larger models like PaLM 62B on few-shot tasks.
Instruction finetuning is compute-efficient, using only 0.2% of pre-training compute for Flan-PaLM 540B.
limits: Scaling number of tasks shows diminishing returns beyond 282 tasks.
Flan-PaLM does not surpass specialized models on algorithmic BBH tasks.
Instruction finetuning without CoT data degrades reasoning performance on CoT tasks.
Evaluation limited to English-centric and multilingual benchmarks; not tested on all languages.
Human evaluation uses single rater per example, which may introduce subjectivity.

papers.tEn: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.tZh: ReAct：在语言模型中协同推理与行动
papers.sEn: ReAct synergizes reasoning and acting in LLMs, outperforming baselines on QA, fact verification, and interactive tasks.
contrib: Introduces ReAct, a prompt-based paradigm that synergizes reasoning and acting in LLMs for general task solving.
Demonstrates ReAct's effectiveness across diverse benchmarks, outperforming prior reasoning-only or acting-only methods in few-shot settings.
Provides systematic ablations showing the importance of acting in reasoning tasks and reasoning in interactive tasks.
Analyzes limitations of ReAct under prompting and shows initial fine-tuning experiments that improve performance.
Enhances interpretability, trustworthiness, and diagnosability by combining reasoning traces with external actions.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on ALFWorld and WebShop with only one or two in-context examples.
limits: Complex tasks with large action spaces require more demonstrations, which may exceed input length limits of in-context learning.
ReAct's structural constraint of interleaving reasoning and action can lead to more reasoning errors than chain-of-thought.
Non-informative search results can derail model reasoning and make recovery difficult.
Performance on knowledge-intensive tasks like HotpotQA slightly lags behind chain-of-thought due to reduced reasoning flexibility.
Current prompting-based method still far from expert human performance on WebShop, especially in product exploration and query reformulation.
