papers.tEn: VIMA: General Robot Manipulation with Multimodal Prompts
papers.tZh: VIMA：基于多模态提示的通用机器人操作
papers.sEn: VIMA uses multimodal prompts to unify diverse robot manipulation tasks, achieving strong generalization and data efficiency.
contrib: Proposes multimodal prompting to unify diverse robot manipulation tasks into a single sequence modeling problem.
Develops VIMA-Bench, a simulation benchmark with 17 tasks, 600K+ expert trajectories, and a four-level evaluation protocol.
Designs VIMA, a transformer-based agent with object-centric tokens and cross-attention conditioning for multimodal prompts.
Achieves up to 2.9x task success rate over baselines in zero-shot generalization with same training data.
Demonstrates strong data efficiency: with 10x less data, VIMA still outperforms best competitor by 2.7x.
Provides open-source code, benchmark, and pre-trained models for reproducibility.
limits: Evaluation limited to simulated tabletop tasks; real-world robot deployment not tested.
Relies on pre-trained object detector (Mask R-CNN) which may fail in novel environments.
Behavioral cloning from expert trajectories may not handle suboptimal or noisy demonstrations.
Zero-shot generalization to novel tasks (L4) still shows significant performance drop.
Model scalability tested up to 200M parameters; larger models may have different behaviors.

papers.tEn: GLM-130B: An Open Bilingual Pre-trained Model
papers.tZh: GLM-130B：一个开放的双语预训练模型
papers.sEn: GLM-130B is a 130B bilingual model that outperforms GPT-3 on many benchmarks and achieves INT4 quantization without performance loss.
contrib: Open-sourced a 130B bilingual pre-trained model outperforming GPT-3 on many English benchmarks.
Achieved INT4 quantization without post-training, enabling inference on affordable GPUs like 4×RTX 3090.
Proposed Embedding Gradient Shrink to stabilize training and prevent loss spikes.
Adopted GLM backbone with bidirectional attention and autoregressive blank infilling for superior comprehension.
Introduced Multi-task Instruction Pre-training (MIP) to boost zero-shot performance.
Demonstrated a unique scaling law for INT4 weight quantization in GLM architectures.
limits: Performance growth with few-shot samples is less significant than GPT-3, possibly due to MIP bias.
Training required 96 DGX-A100 nodes and 60 days, limiting reproducibility.
INT4 quantization only applies to weights; activations remain FP16, limiting compression.
Evaluation on Chinese benchmarks is limited to zero-shot; few-shot results not reported.
Potential ethical risks from open-sourcing a powerful LLM, though mitigated by transparency.

papers.tEn: Toy Models of Superposition
papers.tZh: 叠加的玩具模型
papers.sEn: Polysemanticity in neural networks arises from storing sparse features in superposition, as demonstrated by a toy model with phase changes and connections to polytope geometry and adversarial examples.
contrib: Demonstrates superposition in toy ReLU networks, enabling more features than dimensions by tolerating interference.
Reveals a phase change in superposition, with sharp transitions between representational strategies based on sparsity and importance.
Connects superposition geometry to uniform polytopes (e.g., tetrahedrons, pentagons), linking to the Thomson problem.
Finds evidence linking superposition to adversarial examples, suggesting a shared mechanism.
Proposes that superposition explains polysemanticity and has implications for mechanistic interpretability.
limits: Results are from toy models with synthetic sparse features; generalization to real neural networks is unclear.
Uniform superposition assumption (equal importance and sparsity) is unrealistic; real features exhibit non-uniformity.
Phase change demonstration relies on idealized conditions; real models may have smoother transitions.
Linear representation hypothesis, assumed throughout, is debated and may not hold in all cases.
Link to adversarial examples is preliminary, lacking rigorous theoretical proof.

papers.tEn: AudioLM: a Language Modeling Approach to Audio Generation
papers.tZh: AudioLM：一种基于语言建模的音频生成方法
papers.sEn: AudioLM generates high-quality audio with long-term consistency by treating audio generation as a language modeling task.
contrib: Proposes AudioLM, a framework combining semantic and acoustic tokens hierarchically for high-quality audio generation with long-term consistency.
Demonstrates that semantic tokens from w2v-BERT capture linguistic content, while acoustic tokens from SoundStream ensure high-quality synthesis.
Shows AudioLM generates syntactically and semantically coherent speech continuations without text annotations, preserving speaker identity and prosody.
Extends AudioLM to piano music continuation, generating coherent melodies and rhythms without symbolic music representations.
Provides a classifier that detects AudioLM-generated speech with 98.6% accuracy, mitigating misuse risks.
Achieves state-of-the-art lexical and syntactic knowledge in zero-shot metrics sWUGGY and sBLIMP without text supervision.
limits: AudioLM is evaluated only on English speech and piano music; generalization to other audio types is not shown.
The framework requires pre-trained tokenizers (w2v-BERT, SoundStream) and multiple Transformer stages, leading to high computational cost.
Generated speech may reflect societal biases in training data and may not preserve accent/dialect for underrepresented groups.
The model's ability to continue speech with speaker identity preservation poses risks of spoofing biometric identification or impersonation.
Human evaluation shows generated speech is nearly indistinguishable from real speech, raising ethical concerns despite high detection accuracy.

papers.tEn: Our approach to alignment research
papers.tZh: 我们对对齐研究的方法
papers.sEn: Our approach to alignment research focuses on improving AI systems' ability to learn from human feedback and assist humans in evaluating AI, aiming to build a sufficiently aligned AI system that can solve all other alignment problems.
contrib: Proposes a three-pillar approach: training AI with human feedback, assisting human evaluation, and automating alignment research.
Demonstrates that InstructGPT, fine-tuned with RLHF, is preferred over a 100x larger pretrained model with <2% compute cost.
Shows that AI-assisted evaluation increases flaws found in model outputs by 50% on summarization tasks.
Advocates for iterative, empirical alignment research to understand scaling and failure modes.
Aims to build aligned AI systems that can accelerate alignment research, potentially solving the problem recursively.
Emphasizes transparency and open sharing of alignment research to benefit all AGI developers.
limits: RLHF assumes humans can accurately evaluate tasks, which fails for superhuman AI systems.
AI-assisted evaluation may amplify subtle biases or vulnerabilities in the assistant.
Lessons from aligning current models may not transfer if major discontinuities or paradigm shifts occur.
The hardest alignment problems may not be solvable by scalable training signals alone.
Models capable of accelerating alignment research might themselves be dangerous if misaligned.

papers.tEn: Red Teaming Language Models to Reduce Harms: Methods, Scaling Behaviors, and Lessons Learned
papers.tZh: 红队测试语言模型以减少危害：方法、扩展行为与经验教训
papers.sEn: Red teaming language models reveals scaling challenges for RLHF models and provides a dataset of 38,961 attacks.
contrib: Investigated scaling behaviors for red teaming across 3 model sizes and 4 model types.
Released a dataset of 38,961 red team attacks for analysis and learning.
Provided exhaustive descriptions of instructions, processes, and statistical methodologies for red teaming.
Found RLHF models increasingly difficult to red team as they scale, with flat trends for other model types.
Analyzed harmful outputs ranging from offensive language to subtle unethical content.
Proposed policy interventions for developing shared norms and technical standards for red teaming.
limits: Red teaming focused on AI assistant format, not other LM applications.
Crowdworkers may lack domain expertise for evaluating certain attacks.
Data is incomplete due to unbounded space of possible harms.
Reliance on manual red teaming is expensive and slow at scale.
Low inter-annotator agreement on what constitutes a successful attack.

papers.tEn: Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance
papers.tZh: 无分类器扩散引导
papers.sEn: Classifier-free guidance combines conditional and unconditional diffusion models to trade off sample quality and diversity without a separate classifier.
contrib: Proposes classifier-free guidance, a method to trade off sample quality and diversity in diffusion models without a classifier.
Jointly trains conditional and unconditional diffusion models using a single neural network by randomly dropping conditioning.
Demonstrates that classifier-free guidance achieves FID/IS tradeoffs comparable to classifier guidance on ImageNet.
Shows that pure generative models can boost classifier-based metrics without adversarial classifier gradients.
Provides an intuitive explanation: guidance decreases unconditional likelihood while increasing conditional likelihood.
Achieves state-of-the-art FID on 128x128 ImageNet, outperforming classifier-guided ADM-G and BigGAN-deep.
limits: Requires two forward passes per sampling step, reducing sampling speed compared to classifier guidance.
Relies on training an unconditional model, which may be inefficient for high-dimensional conditioning.
Decreased sample diversity may have negative impacts in deployed models, especially for underrepresented data.
Hyperparameter puncond requires tuning; optimal value may vary across datasets.
Method is demonstrated only on ImageNet; generalizability to other modalities is not explored.

papers.tEn: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
papers.tZh: 语言模型（大多）知道它们知道什么
papers.sEn: Language models can self-evaluate the validity of their own claims and predict answerability, with performance improving through self-consistency and context.
contrib: Larger language models are well-calibrated on diverse multiple-choice and true/false questions when formatted appropriately.
Self-evaluation via P(True) shows encouraging performance, calibration, and scaling across tasks.
Providing models with many of their own samples improves self-evaluation performance.
Models can be trained to predict P(IK) and partially generalize across tasks, though calibration on new tasks is challenging.
P(IK) increases appropriately when relevant source materials or hints are provided in context.
Self-evaluation and calibration improve with model size, suggesting verification scales faster than generation.
limits: Study focuses on pretrained language models; RLHF policies require temperature adjustment for calibration.
P(IK) generalization is partial and calibration suffers out-of-distribution.
Self-evaluation is zero-shot poorly calibrated; few-shot prompting is needed for good calibration.
Work does not address intentional deception or distinguish truth from human consensus.
Only five sampling-based datasets were studied, limiting scope of generalization observations.

papers.tEn: MineDojo: Building Open-Ended Embodied Agents with Internet-Scale Knowledge
papers.tZh: MineDojo：利用互联网规模知识构建开放式具身智能体
papers.sEn: MineDojo integrates internet-scale knowledge with Minecraft to train generalist embodied agents on thousands of open-ended tasks.
contrib: Introduces MineDojo, a framework with thousands of open-ended tasks in Minecraft.
Provides an internet-scale knowledge base of 730K+ YouTube videos, 6K+ Wiki pages, and 340K+ Reddit posts.
Proposes MineCLIP, a contrastive video-language model trained on YouTube data for reward learning.
Demonstrates that MineCLIP-based agents achieve competitive performance to hand-engineered rewards on 12 tasks.
Introduces a novel evaluation protocol for creative tasks using a learned video-language model.
Open-sources simulation suite, knowledge bases, algorithms, and pretrained models to promote research.
limits: Agent learning is evaluated on only 12 tasks, limiting generalizability.
MineCLIP reward model may not generalize to tasks outside Minecraft domain.
Creative task evaluation relies on a learned metric, which may not perfectly align with human judgment.
The framework is specific to Minecraft, limiting applicability to other embodied environments.
Computational overhead of MineCLIP requires optimization techniques for practical RL training.

papers.tEn: Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models
papers.tZh: 大型语言模型的涌现能力
papers.sEn: Emergent abilities are unpredictable capabilities that appear only in large language models, not in smaller ones.
contrib: Defines emergent abilities as abilities present in large models but absent in smaller ones, unpredictable via scaling laws.
Documents emergent abilities across few-shot prompting, chain-of-thought, instruction following, and program execution.
Shows emergent abilities appear as phase transitions in scaling curves, with performance jumping from random to above-random at a threshold.
Discusses that emergent abilities are not solely determined by scale; architecture, data quality, and training procedures also matter.
Highlights emergent risks such as bias, toxicity, and memorization that can increase with scale.
Proposes future directions including further scaling, improved architectures, data scaling, and understanding emergence.
limits: Emergent abilities are defined only for pre-trained Transformer language models, not other architectures.
The paper does not propose new methods or models; it surveys existing results.
Emergence may be an artifact of evaluation metrics like exact match, which ignore partial progress.
The scale at which emergence occurs is not fixed; it depends on data quality, architecture, and training.
Some abilities may never emerge due to distributional mismatch or plateauing after emergence.

papers.tEn: DPM-Solver: A Fast ODE Solver for Diffusion Probabilistic Model Sampling in Around 10 Steps
papers.tZh: DPM-Solver：一种用于扩散概率模型快速采样的常微分方程求解器
papers.sEn: DPM-Solver generates high-quality samples in 10-20 steps by analytically solving the linear part of diffusion ODEs.
contrib: Proposes exact formulation of diffusion ODE solutions by analytically computing the linear part.
Simplifies solution to exponentially weighted integral of neural network via change-of-variable.
Develops DPM-Solver, a high-order solver for diffusion ODEs with convergence guarantee.
Achieves high-quality sampling in 10-20 function evaluations, 4-16x speedup over prior methods.
Applies to both discrete-time and continuous-time DPMs without additional training.
Provides theoretical convergence order analysis for first, second, and third-order solvers.
limits: Not suitable for accelerating likelihood evaluations of DPMs.
Still not fast enough for real-time applications compared to GANs.
Potential misuse for generating adverse fake content, amplified by speedup.
Only considers solvers up to third order; higher orders left for future work.

papers.tEn: Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion-Based Generative Models
papers.tZh: 阐明基于扩散的生成模型的设计空间
papers.sEn: We present a clear design space for diffusion-based generative models, yielding new state-of-the-art FID scores on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-64 with faster sampling.
contrib: Presents a modular design space for diffusion-based generative models, decoupling sampling, training, and score-network preconditioning choices.
Develops an improved deterministic sampler using a Heun 2nd-order integrator, optimized noise schedule, and sigma(t)=t, drastically reducing network evaluations.
Proposes a tailored stochastic sampler with explicit noise churn and heuristic controls, correcting earlier sampling errors while noting empirical tuning requirements.
Derives principled preconditioning for inputs, outputs, skip connections, and noise conditioning, plus a log-normal training noise distribution and loss weighting.
Achieves state-of-the-art FID: 1.79 class-conditional and 1.97 unconditional CIFAR-10, and 1.36 ImageNet-64 with only 35 network evaluations for CIFAR-10.
limits: The stochastic sampler relies on heuristic parameters that must be grid-searched per model and dataset, limiting generalization.
Stochasticity is not universally beneficial: with improved CIFAR-10 training it hurts performance, while it helps ImageNet-64, leaving its interaction with training unresolved.
Many proposed parameter values likely need readjustment for higher-resolution datasets and different architectures.
Excessive churn in stochastic sampling causes loss of detail and oversaturation, partly attributed to non-conservative learned score fields.
Training consumed about 250 MWh and advances may amplify misinformation and bias in large-scale deployment.

papers.tEn: EfficientViT: Multi-Scale Linear Attention for High-Resolution Dense Prediction
papers.tZh: EfficientViT：用于高分辨率密集预测的多尺度线性注意力
papers.sEn: EfficientViT achieves global receptive field and multi-scale learning with lightweight, hardware-efficient operations, outperforming prior models in speed and accuracy on high-resolution dense prediction tasks.
contrib: Proposes multi-scale linear attention achieving global receptive field and multi-scale learning with hardware-efficient operations.
First to demonstrate effectiveness of linear attention for high-resolution dense prediction.
Designs EfficientViT model family with significant speedup on diverse hardware platforms.
Achieves up to 13.9x GPU latency reduction on Cityscapes over SegFormer without performance loss.
Delivers 48.9x higher throughput on A100 GPU for Segment Anything with better zero-shot instance segmentation.
Provides up to 6.4x speedup over Restormer for super-resolution with 0.11dB PSNR gain.
limits: Multi-scale linear attention may have limited capacity for local information compared to softmax attention.
Performance on single-point prompt segmentation in LVIS is inferior to SAM-ViT-H, requiring further investigation.
Models are evaluated only on specific tasks (semantic segmentation, super-resolution, Segment Anything) and datasets.
Training requires two-phase process for Segment Anything, adding complexity.
Effectiveness on other vision tasks like video or 3D processing is not explored.

papers.tEn: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
papers.tZh: FlashAttention：快速且内存高效的精确注意力机制，具有 IO 感知能力
papers.sEn: FlashAttention reduces GPU memory reads/writes via tiling, achieving faster training and longer context for Transformers.
contrib: Proposes FlashAttention, an IO-aware exact attention algorithm using tiling to reduce GPU HBM accesses.
Achieves significant wall-clock speedups: 15% on BERT-large, 3x on GPT-2, 2.4x on long-range arena.
Enables longer context in Transformers, improving perplexity by 0.7 on GPT-2 and 6.4 points on long-document classification.
First Transformer to achieve better-than-chance on Path-X (61.4%) and Path-256 (63.1%) via longer sequences.
Extends to block-sparse FlashAttention, faster than all existing approximate attention methods.
Provides IO complexity analysis and proves optimality for exact attention over a range of SRAM sizes.
limits: Requires custom CUDA kernel, limiting portability and ease of use across GPU architectures.
Optimal only for single GPU; multi-GPU IO analysis and parallelization remain unexplored.
Block-sparse attention relies on predefined sparsity patterns, which may not suit all tasks.
Recomputation in backward pass increases FLOPs, though offset by reduced HBM accesses.
Performance gains diminish for very short sequences where memory access is less dominant.

papers.tEn: Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Deep Language Understanding
papers.tZh: 具有深度语言理解能力的逼真文本到图像扩散模型
papers.sEn: Imagen achieves photorealistic text-to-image generation with deep language understanding by leveraging large language models.
contrib: Imagen achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot FID of 7.27 on COCO, outperforming prior methods.
Introduces DrawBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating text-to-image models.
Shows that scaling large language models improves image quality more than scaling diffusion models.
Proposes dynamic thresholding for high guidance weights, improving photorealism and alignment.
Demonstrates that frozen T5-XXL text encoder outperforms CLIP in human evaluation.
Achieves human-level image-text alignment on COCO, with samples rated on par with reference images.
limits: Imagen struggles to generate photorealistic people, as shown by lower preference rates.
Training data contains biases and harmful content, limiting safe public deployment.
Model inherits social biases from language models, e.g., skin tone and gender stereotypes.
Evaluation focuses on English prompts; performance on other languages is unknown.
High computational cost due to large model sizes and cascaded architecture.

papers.tEn: CoCa: Contrastive Captioners are Image-Text Foundation Models
papers.tZh: CoCa: 对比字幕器是图像-文本基础模型
papers.sEn: CoCa jointly pretrains an image-text encoder-decoder with contrastive and captioning losses, achieving SOTA on diverse tasks.
contrib: Proposes Contrastive Captioner (CoCa), a minimalist encoder-decoder foundation model unifying contrastive and captioning losses.
Decouples decoder into unimodal and multimodal layers, enabling both aligned unimodal embeddings and fused multimodal representations.
Achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on ImageNet (86.3%), crossmodal retrieval, and multimodal understanding tasks.
Pretrains end-to-end from scratch on web-scale alt-text and annotated images, treating all labels as text.
Introduces task-specific attentional poolers to customize visual representations for different objectives and downstream tasks.
Sets new state-of-the-art on ImageNet finetuning (91.0%) and NoCaps captioning (120.6 CIDEr).
limits: Model performance depends on large-scale pretraining data (JFT-3B, ALIGN), which may contain biases.
Zero-shot evaluation may not reflect robustness to all real-world image corruptions beyond current benchmarks.
Requires significant computational resources (2048 TPUv4 chips for 5 days) for pretraining.
Decoder design with causal masking limits parallelization for some tasks compared to bidirectional models.
Broader impacts such as fairness, social bias, and potential misuse require further community exploration.

papers.tEn: These are the storytelling lessons I learned from Steve Jobs
papers.tZh: 我从史蒂夫·乔布斯学到的讲故事技巧
papers.sEn: A good product story has three elements: facts, emotion, and a clear narrative.
contrib: Steve Jobs' product storytelling framework combines rational facts with emotional appeal to explain why a product exists.
A good product story simplifies complex concepts, making them accessible to a broad audience.
The narrative should constantly remind users of the problem being solved, focusing on the 'why'.
Jobs' iPhone launch exemplified how a story can drive product adoption and industry change.
The story of a product, company, and vision should guide all strategic decisions.
limits: The framework is based on anecdotal evidence from one individual's experience at Apple.
It may not apply to products in highly technical or regulated industries where emotion is less relevant.
Overemphasis on storytelling could overshadow product functionality and user needs.
The approach assumes a charismatic leader like Jobs, which is not replicable in most organizations.

papers.tEn: OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models
papers.tZh: OPT：开放预训练 Transformer 语言模型
papers.sEn: We release OPT, a suite of decoder-only pre-trained transformers from 125M to 175B parameters, comparable to GPT-3 but with 1/7th the carbon footprint.
contrib: Released OPT, a suite of decoder-only pre-trained transformers from 125M to 175B parameters, fully and responsibly shared with researchers.
Showed OPT-175B is comparable to GPT-3 while requiring only 1/7th the carbon footprint.
Provided detailed logbook of infrastructure challenges and codebase for reproducible research.
Conducted extensive evaluations on 16 NLP tasks, dialogue, bias, and toxicity benchmarks.
Demonstrated parity with GPT-3 on most tasks, with variations in toxicity and hate speech detection.
Enabled broader research community access to large language models for studying limitations and risks.
limits: OPT-175B does not work well with declarative instructions or point-blank interrogatives.
Tends to be repetitive and can get stuck in loops, even with sampling.
Produces factually incorrect statements, especially in critical domains like healthcare.
High propensity to generate toxic language and reinforce harmful stereotypes.
Evaluation results vary with prompting style and number of shots, affecting replicability.

papers.tEn: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
papers.tZh: Flamingo：一种用于少样本学习的视觉语言模型
papers.sEn: Flamingo achieves state-of-the-art few-shot learning on diverse visual tasks by bridging pretrained vision and language models.
contrib: Introduces Flamingo, a family of Visual Language Models for few-shot learning on multimodal tasks.
Proposes architectural innovations: bridging frozen vision and language models, handling interleaved data, and using a Perceiver Resampler.
Achieves state-of-the-art few-shot performance on 16 multimodal benchmarks, often surpassing fine-tuned models.
Demonstrates effective in-context learning for open-ended tasks like captioning and visual question-answering.
Shows that training on interleaved web data is crucial for few-shot capabilities.
Scales model size and number of shots to improve performance, similar to GPT-3.
limits: Inherits weaknesses from pretrained LMs, including hallucinations and poor generalization to long sequences.
Classification performance lags behind contrastive models like CLIP.
In-context learning is sensitive to demonstration selection and scales poorly with many shots.
Training requires large-scale web data, which may contain biases and toxic content.
Freezing the language model prevents catastrophic forgetting but limits adaptation.

papers.tEn: Hierarchical Text-Conditional Image Generation with CLIP Latents
papers.tZh: 基于 CLIP 潜在向量的层次化文本条件图像生成
papers.sEn: Explicitly generating CLIP image embeddings improves image diversity with minimal loss in photorealism and caption similarity.
contrib: Proposes a two-stage model with a prior generating CLIP image embeddings from text and a decoder generating images from embeddings.
Shows that generating image representations explicitly improves diversity with minimal loss in photorealism and caption similarity.
Demonstrates language-guided image manipulations in a zero-shot manner using CLIP's joint embedding space.
Compares autoregressive and diffusion priors, finding diffusion priors more compute-efficient and producing higher-quality samples.
Achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot FID of 10.39 on MS-COCO validation set.
Introduces a bipartite latent representation enabling image variations, interpolation, and text diffs.
limits: unCLIP struggles with binding attributes to objects, e.g., assigning colors to specific cubes.
The model has difficulty generating coherent text within images.
Complex scenes lack fine details due to the 64x64 base resolution and upsampling.
The CLIP embedding may not encode spelling information of rendered text precisely.
The model inherits risks of deceptive and harmful content, with fewer traces of AI generation.

papers.tEn: Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.tZh: 通过人类反馈的强化学习训练有益且无害的助手
papers.sEn: RLHF alignment improves NLP performance and is compatible with specialized skills training.
contrib: Applied RLHF to finetune language models as helpful and harmless assistants, improving NLP evaluations.
Demonstrated compatibility of alignment training with specialized skills like Python coding and summarization.
Explored iterated online training with weekly updates of preference models and RL policies, improving data and models.
Identified a linear relation between RL reward and square root of KL divergence from initial policy.
Conducted peripheral analyses on calibration, competing objectives, and OOD detection.
Compared models with human writers and provided samples from prompts in recent related work.
limits: RLHF may not be the best approach for honesty; other techniques may be more effective.
Preference models become less calibrated and robust at higher scores due to data scarcity.
Online training requires careful handling of distribution shift and entropy reduction.
Harmlessness training can lead to over-optimization and reduced helpfulness if not balanced.
Results may not generalize to real-world tasks or adversarial evaluations.

papers.tEn: Video Diffusion Models
papers.tZh: 视频扩散模型
papers.sEn: We propose a diffusion model for video generation that extends image diffusion, enabling joint training on images and videos, and introduces a conditional sampling technique for spatial-temporal extension.
contrib: Proposes a diffusion model for video generation as a natural extension of image diffusion architectures.
Enables joint training on image and video data, reducing minibatch gradient variance and speeding optimization.
Introduces reconstruction-guided sampling for spatial and temporal video extension, outperforming prior methods.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on video prediction and unconditional video generation benchmarks.
Presents first results on large-scale text-conditioned video generation using diffusion models.
Demonstrates benefits of classifier-free guidance and joint image-video training for video diffusion models.
limits: Model trained on fixed number of frames (e.g., 16) and limited spatial resolution.
Reconstruction guidance relies on Gaussian approximation of conditioning data, which may be inaccurate for large t.
Evaluation metrics (FVD, FID, IS) may not fully capture temporal coherence or perceptual quality.
Text-to-video models inherit biases from training data and may require curation for fair results.
Models not released due to potential for harmful use, limiting reproducibility and further research.

papers.tEn: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
papers.tZh: PaLM：通过 Pathways 扩展语言建模
papers.sEn: PaLM 540B achieves state-of-the-art few-shot learning on hundreds of tasks, outperforming finetuned models on multi-step reasoning and average human performance on BIG-bench.
contrib: Trained PaLM 540B, a densely activated Transformer, using Pathways across 6144 TPU v4 chips, achieving high efficiency.
Achieved state-of-the-art few-shot results on hundreds of language understanding and generation benchmarks.
Demonstrated breakthrough performance on multi-step reasoning tasks using chain-of-thought prompting, outperforming finetuned models.
Observed discontinuous improvements from model scale on many BIG-bench tasks, indicating emergent capabilities.
Showed strong multilingual and code generation capabilities, with PaLM 540B bridging the gap to finetuned models.
Provided comprehensive analysis of bias, toxicity, and memorization, and discussed ethical considerations.
limits: Training loss spikes occurred for the largest model, mitigated by restarting from earlier checkpoints.
Evaluation limited to English and a few multilingual tasks; non-English data proportion was only 22%.
Bias and toxicity analysis showed stereotypes and higher toxicity for larger models, correlating with prompt style.
Chain-of-thought prompting required manual exemplars; performance on some BIG-bench tasks still far from human.
Code generation performance relied on additional finetuning; model size alone did not saturate improvements.

papers.tEn: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
papers.tZh: 做我能做的，而非说我所想的：将语言扎根于机器人能力
papers.sEn: Grounding language models in robotic affordances enables robots to follow high-level instructions by combining semantic knowledge with feasible low-level skills.
contrib: Proposes SayCan, grounding LLMs via pretrained skill value functions for feasible robot actions.
Combines LLM task-grounding with affordance world-grounding to select contextually appropriate skills.
Demonstrates zero-shot long-horizon task execution on a mobile manipulator in real kitchens.
Shows robot performance improves with better LLMs, linking NLP progress to robotics.
Enables easy integration of new skills and handles multilingual queries without retraining.
Integrates chain-of-thought reasoning to handle negation and complex reasoning tasks.
limits: Inherits LLM biases and limitations from training data.
System bottleneck is the range and robustness of underlying low-level skills.
Cannot react to skill failures despite high value function scores; lacks closed-loop feedback.
Struggles with negation and ambiguous references, inherited from underlying LLMs.
Requires manual prompt engineering and predefined skill set; not fully autonomous.

papers.tEn: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
papers.tZh: 训练计算最优的大型语言模型
papers.sEn: Model size and training tokens should be scaled equally for compute-optimal training.
contrib: Proposes three methods to determine compute-optimal model size and training tokens, showing they should scale equally.
Trains over 400 models from 70M to 16B parameters to empirically derive scaling laws.
Demonstrates that current large language models are significantly undertrained due to overemphasis on model size.
Introduces Chinchilla, a 70B parameter model trained on 1.4T tokens, outperforming larger models like Gopher and GPT-3.
Achieves state-of-the-art 67.5% accuracy on MMLU, a 7% improvement over Gopher.
Shows compute-optimal training reduces inference and fine-tuning costs, facilitating downstream usage.
limits: Only two large-scale training runs (Chinchilla and Gopher) are compared, limiting validation at intermediate scales.
Assumes a power-law relationship between compute, model size, and tokens, but observes concavity at high compute budgets.
All training runs use less than one epoch of data; multiple-epoch regime is not explored.
Analysis relies on smoothed training loss as a proxy for test loss, which may not fully capture generalization.
Ethical and privacy concerns from larger datasets are acknowledged but not fully addressed.

papers.tEn: DINO: DETR with Improved DeNoising Anchor Boxes for End-to-End Object Detection
papers.tZh: DINO：通过改进的去噪锚框实现端到端目标检测的 DETR
papers.sEn: DINO achieves state-of-the-art end-to-end object detection with improved denoising training, mixed query selection, and look forward twice scheme.
contrib: Proposes contrastive denoising training with positive and negative samples to improve one-to-one matching.
Introduces mixed query selection to initialize anchor boxes from encoder features while keeping content queries learnable.
Develops look forward twice scheme to leverage later layer gradients for earlier layer parameter updates.
Achieves 49.4 AP in 12 epochs and 51.3 AP in 24 epochs on COCO with ResNet-50, outperforming prior DETR-like models.
Scales to large backbones and data, achieving 63.2 AP on COCO val2017 and 63.3 AP on test-dev with SwinL and Objects365.
First end-to-end Transformer detector to surpass SOTA on COCO leaderboard with reduced model and data size.
limits: Evaluation limited to COCO dataset; generalization to other domains not verified.
Performance depends on pre-training on Objects365; may not hold without large-scale pre-training.
Contrastive denoising requires tuning noise scales λ1 and λ2; sensitivity not fully explored.
Look forward twice adds computational overhead due to extra gradient flow.
Mixed query selection assumes encoder features provide reliable spatial priors; may fail with poor encoder.

papers.tEn: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
papers.tZh: 使用人类反馈训练语言模型遵循指令
papers.sEn: Fine-tuning with human feedback aligns language models with user intent, enabling a 1.3B parameter model to outperform a 175B model.
contrib: Shows fine-tuning with human feedback (RLHF) aligns language models to user intent, with 1.3B InstructGPT preferred over 175B GPT-3.
InstructGPT improves truthfulness on TruthfulQA and reduces toxic outputs by 25% when prompted respectfully.
RLHF alignment cost is modest relative to pretraining; 1.3B InstructGPT outperforms 175B GPT-3 with 100x fewer parameters.
Mixing pretraining gradients (PPO-ptx) mitigates alignment tax on NLP benchmarks like SQuAD and HellaSwag.
InstructGPT generalizes instruction-following to non-English and code tasks despite limited supervision.
Held-out labelers prefer InstructGPT over GPT-3 at similar rates, showing generalization beyond training labelers.
limits: InstructGPT still generates toxic, biased, or false outputs, especially when prompted for harmful content.
Alignment is to specific labeler preferences, not universal human values; labeler demographics are limited.
Performance regressions on some NLP datasets (e.g., SQuAD, DROP) persist even with PPO-ptx mitigation.
Model fails on false premise instructions, over-hedges simple questions, and struggles with multiple constraints.
RLHF may not scale to superhuman systems; method relies on human evaluation which becomes difficult for complex tasks.

papers.tEn: Predictability and Surprise in Large Generative Models
papers.tZh: 大型生成模型中的可预测性与意外性
papers.sEn: Large generative models exhibit predictable loss scaling but unpredictable specific behaviors, creating policy challenges.
contrib: Identifies paradoxical combination of predictable scaling laws and unpredictable specific capabilities in large generative models.
Demonstrates abrupt emergence of harmful capabilities like recidivism prediction with bias at scale via novel experiments.
Analyzes how predictability drives rapid development while unpredictability hinders consequence anticipation.
Documents open-ended inputs and outputs leading to unknown capabilities and harmful outputs like toxicity scaling.
Provides policy interventions including national research clouds, red teaming, and governance structures.
Empirically shows increasing industry-academia gap in large model development and proliferation of deployments.
limits: Focuses on large language models; findings may not generalize to other generative modalities.
Novel experiments limited to recidivism prediction and toxicity; other harms may differ.
Does not address labor, supply chain, or environmental costs of large models.
Policy interventions are speculative and lack empirical validation of effectiveness.
Analysis of motivations and barriers is qualitative and may not capture all factors.

papers.tEn: data2vec: A General Framework for Self-supervised Learning in Speech, Vision and Language
papers.tZh: data2vec：语音、视觉和语言自监督学习的通用框架
papers.sEn: data2vec proposes a unified self-supervised learning framework across speech, NLP, and vision by predicting contextualized latent representations instead of modality-specific targets.
contrib: Proposes data2vec, a unified self-supervised learning framework for speech, vision, and language using the same objective.
Predicts contextualized latent representations from masked input via self-distillation with a standard Transformer.
Achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results on ImageNet-1K, Librispeech, and GLUE benchmarks.
Uses multi-layer target averaging from teacher network, improving over single-layer targets like BYOL.
First NLP model to predict continuous latent targets instead of discrete tokens, enabling open-vocabulary learning.
Demonstrates that contextualized targets from full input outperform local targets in self-supervised learning.
limits: Still uses modality-specific feature encoders and masking strategies, not fully unified.
Requires careful tuning of hyperparameters like learning rate and momentum to avoid representation collapse.
Performance on speech recognition relies on large pre-training data (960 hours) and may not generalize to low-resource languages.
Does not explore multi-modal joint training; only learns representations for each modality separately.
Contextualized targets require full teacher forward pass, increasing computational cost compared to local targets.

papers.tEn: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.tZh: 思维链提示激发大型语言模型的推理能力
papers.sEn: Chain-of-thought prompting significantly improves complex reasoning in large language models.
contrib: Proposes chain-of-thought prompting, a simple method that elicits multi-step reasoning in large language models via few-shot exemplars with intermediate reasoning steps.
Demonstrates that chain-of-thought prompting significantly improves performance on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks, achieving state-of-the-art on GSM8K.
Shows that chain-of-thought reasoning is an emergent ability of model scale, only benefiting models with ~100B parameters or more.
Provides ablation studies isolating the effects of equation-only, variable compute, and chain-of-thought after answer, confirming the importance of sequential natural language reasoning.
Demonstrates robustness of chain-of-thought prompting to different annotators, exemplars, and language models.
Shows that chain-of-thought prompting facilitates length generalization to out-of-distribution inputs with more steps than seen in exemplars.
limits: Does not address whether the neural network is actually reasoning; chain-of-thought emulates human thought processes but does not guarantee reasoning.
Manual annotation of chain-of-thought exemplars is costly for few-shot prompting, and prohibitive for finetuning without synthetic data.
No guarantee of correct reasoning paths; generated chains can lead to both correct and incorrect answers.
Chain-of-thought reasoning only emerges at large model scales, making it costly to serve in real-world applications.
Limited evaluation to arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning; applicability to other domains remains unexplored.

papers.tEn: BLIP: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training for Unified Vision-Language Understanding and Generation
papers.tZh: BLIP：引导语言-图像预训练实现统一视觉-语言理解与生成
papers.sEn: BLIP achieves state-of-the-art on vision-language tasks by bootstrapping captions from noisy web data.
contrib: Proposes BLIP, a unified VLP framework for both understanding and generation tasks.
Introduces multimodal mixture of encoder-decoder (MED) for flexible multi-task pre-training.
Develops CapFilt to bootstrap noisy web data by generating synthetic captions and filtering noise.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on image-text retrieval, captioning, VQA, and zero-shot video tasks.
Demonstrates strong generalization to video-language tasks via zero-shot transfer.
Releases code, models, and bootstrapped datasets to facilitate future research.
limits: CapFilt requires finetuning captioner and filter on human-annotated data like COCO.
Performance gains from CapFilt diminish when using deterministic decoding like beam search.
Zero-shot video transfer ignores temporal information, limiting performance on temporal tasks.
Bootstrapped dataset requires training a new model from scratch; continued training from teacher is ineffective.
Method relies on large-scale web data and computational resources for pre-training.

papers.tEn: Text and Code Embeddings by Contrastive Pre-Training
papers.tZh: 通过对比预训练学习文本和代码嵌入
papers.sEn: Contrastive pre-training on unsupervised data at scale produces high-quality vector representations for text and code, achieving state-of-the-art results in classification and search tasks.
contrib: Shows contrastive pre-training on unsupervised data at scale yields high-quality text and code embeddings.
Achieves state-of-the-art linear-probe classification with 4% relative improvement over prior unsupervised methods.
Attains 23.4%, 14.7%, and 10.6% relative improvement on MSMARCO, Natural Questions, and TriviaQA semantic search.
Code embeddings achieve 20.8% relative improvement on CodeSearchNet code search benchmark.
Demonstrates zero-shot and k-NN classification competitive with supervised methods on SST-2.
Fine-tuned models outperform previous transfer methods by 2.2% on NLI tasks.
limits: Underperforms on sentence similarity tasks compared to prior state-of-the-art.
Requires large batch sizes and substantial computational resources for training.
Code embeddings show no performance gain with increased model size from 300M to 1.2B parameters.
Potential biases in training data may cause representational harms in downstream applications.
Sentence similarity and search tasks may have conflicting objectives, limiting joint optimization.

papers.tEn: A ConvNet for the 2020s
papers.tZh: 面向 2020 年代的卷积神经网络
papers.sEn: Modernizing standard ResNet with Vision Transformer design principles yields ConvNeXt, a pure ConvNet family that matches or outperforms Transformers on ImageNet, COCO, and ADE20K.
contrib: Proposes ConvNeXt, a pure ConvNet family that competes favorably with Transformers in accuracy and scalability.
Systematically modernizes a standard ResNet towards vision Transformer design, identifying key performance components.
Achieves 87.8% ImageNet top-1 accuracy and outperforms Swin Transformers on COCO detection and ADE20K segmentation.
Demonstrates that pure ConvNets can match hierarchical vision Transformers across multiple benchmarks.
Shows ConvNeXt maintains simplicity and efficiency of standard ConvNets while achieving state-of-the-art performance.
Provides detailed ablation study on design choices like large kernel size, inverted bottleneck, and normalization.
limits: ConvNeXt may be less suited for multi-modal learning requiring cross-attention across modalities.
Transformers may be more flexible for tasks requiring discretized, sparse, or structured outputs.
Large model variants require significant compute resources, increasing carbon emissions.
Robustness and fairness of ConvNeXt vs. Transformers require further investigation.
ConvNeXt benefits from large-scale pre-training, which may raise data bias concerns.

papers.tEn: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
papers.tZh: 基于潜在扩散模型的高分辨率图像合成
papers.sEn: Latent diffusion models achieve high-quality image synthesis with reduced computational cost by operating in the latent space of pretrained autoencoders.
contrib: Propose Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs) that apply diffusion in latent space of pretrained autoencoders, reducing computational cost while maintaining quality.
Achieve near-optimal balance between complexity reduction and detail preservation via latent space training, boosting visual fidelity.
Introduce cross-attention layers into UNet backbone for flexible conditioning on text, bounding boxes, etc., enabling high-resolution synthesis.
Set new state-of-the-art on image inpainting and competitive performance on unconditional generation, semantic synthesis, and super-resolution.
Significantly reduce training and inference costs compared to pixel-based diffusion models, e.g., 2.7x speedup in inpainting.
Release pretrained models for reuse across multiple tasks, democratizing access to powerful diffusion models.
limits: Sequential sampling process is still slower than GANs, limiting real-time applications.
Reconstruction capability of autoencoder can bottleneck tasks requiring fine-grained pixel accuracy, e.g., super-resolution.
Potential for misuse in creating deepfakes, spreading misinformation, and revealing sensitive training data.
Two-stage training may exacerbate biases present in data, though mode coverage is better than GANs.
Performance on some tasks (e.g., LSUN-Bedrooms) slightly below specialized models like ADM despite lower resource use.

papers.tEn: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback
papers.tZh: WebGPT：基于浏览器辅助的问答系统与人类反馈优化
papers.sEn: WebGPT fine-tunes GPT-3 to answer questions by browsing the web, achieving human-preferred answers 56% of the time over human demonstrators.
contrib: Fine-tunes GPT-3 to answer long-form questions using a text-based web-browsing environment.
Collects human demonstrations and comparisons to train via imitation learning and human feedback.
Requires models to collect references during browsing to aid factual accuracy evaluation.
Achieves human-level performance on ELI5, with answers preferred 56% over human demonstrators and 69% over Reddit top answers.
Outperforms GPT-3 on TruthfulQA, achieving 75% truthful and 54% truthful and informative answers.
Analyzes scaling trends with dataset size, parameter count, and inference-time compute for rejection sampling.
limits: Struggles with out-of-distribution questions, as shown by lower performance on TruthfulQA compared to humans.
May cherry-pick references to appear convincing, not reflecting fair evidence assessment.
Perpetuates biases from GPT-3 and existing sources, potentially reinforcing confirmation bias.
Risk of overreliance due to authoritative appearance with citations, despite occasional falsehoods.
Requires careful human oversight for safety, especially with more capable models accessing the web.

papers.tEn: A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment
papers.tZh: 通用语言助手作为对齐研究的实验室
papers.sEn: Simple alignment techniques like prompting improve with model scale and generalize across evaluations without harming performance.
contrib: Shows that prompting improves alignment evaluations with model size, with negligible alignment tax on large models.
Finds ranked preference modeling outperforms imitation learning and scales more favorably with model size.
Introduces preference model pre-training (PMP) to improve sample efficiency when finetuning on human preferences.
Demonstrates that binary discrimination performs similarly to imitation learning, unlike ranked preference modeling.
Shows context distillation can transfer prompt benefits into model weights without performance loss on large models.
Provides evidence that PMP with binary data transfers better than ranked data for downstream alignment tasks.
limits: Alignment evaluations are limited to helpfulness, honesty, and harmlessness criteria, which are subjective.
Prompting may not scale to more complex alignment challenges beyond simple imitation.
PMP benefits are mainly observed for models larger than 1B parameters; small models show little improvement.
The study does not address alignment of advanced AI systems with superhuman capabilities.
Human evaluation data may have biases and limited scalability due to annotator expertise and cost.

papers.tEn: A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment
papers.tZh: 通用语言助手作为对齐研究的实验室
papers.sEn: Simple alignment techniques like prompting improve with model scale and generalize across evaluations without harming performance.
contrib: Shows that prompting improves alignment evaluations with model size, with negligible alignment tax on large models.
Finds ranked preference modeling outperforms imitation learning and scales more favorably with model size.
Introduces preference model pre-training (PMP) to improve sample efficiency when finetuning on human preferences.
Demonstrates that binary discrimination performs similarly to imitation learning, unlike ranked preference modeling.
Shows context distillation can transfer prompt benefits into model weights without performance loss on large models.
Provides evidence that PMP with binary data transfers better than ranked data for downstream alignment tasks.
limits: Alignment evaluations are limited to helpfulness, honesty, and harmlessness criteria, which are subjective.
Prompting may not scale to more complex alignment challenges beyond simple imitation.
PMP benefits are mainly observed for models larger than 1B parameters; small models show little improvement.
The study does not address alignment of advanced AI systems with superhuman capabilities.
Human evaluation data may have biases and limited scalability due to annotator expertise and cost.

papers.tEn: SimMIM: A Simple Framework for Masked Image Modeling
papers.tZh: SimMIM：一种简单的掩码图像建模框架
papers.sEn: SimMIM simplifies masked image modeling with random masking, raw pixel regression, and a linear prediction head, achieving strong results.
contrib: Proposes SimMIM, a simple framework for masked image modeling without special designs like block-wise masking or discrete VAE tokenization.
Shows random masking with large patch size (e.g., 32) and raw pixel regression via ℓ1 loss yields strong representations.
Demonstrates a linear prediction head suffices, achieving 83.8% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K with ViT-B.
Scales to 3B-parameter SwinV2-G, achieving state-of-the-art on four vision benchmarks with 40× less data.
Systematically studies masking strategy, prediction target, and head design, revealing simple designs are optimal.
Provides code and models publicly at https://github.com/microsoft/SimMIM.
limits: Evaluation primarily on ImageNet-1K; generalization to other domains not extensively validated.
Requires large masked patch size (e.g., 32) and high masking ratio (e.g., 60%) for best performance.
Pre-training on ImageNet-1K only; performance on other datasets may vary.
Heavier prediction heads or higher target resolutions do not improve fine-tuning performance.
Limited analysis on why simple designs outperform complex ones; relies on empirical observations.

papers.tEn: iBOT: Image BERT Pre-Training with Online Tokenizer
papers.tZh: iBOT：基于在线分词器的图像 BERT 预训练
papers.sEn: iBOT achieves masked image modeling with an online tokenizer via self-distillation, eliminating the need for pre-trained tokenizers and achieving state-of-the-art results on ImageNet-1K.
contrib: Proposes iBOT, a self-supervised framework for masked image modeling with an online tokenizer.
Achieves state-of-the-art linear probing (82.3%) and fine-tuning (87.8%) accuracy on ImageNet-1K.
Eliminates multi-stage training by jointly learning the tokenizer and target model via self-distillation.
Discovers emerging part-level semantics in patch tokens, enhancing robustness and dense task performance.
Outperforms prior methods on object detection, instance segmentation, and semantic segmentation.
Demonstrates scalability to larger models and datasets, with consistent gains over DINO.
limits: Requires more data to train larger models, as ViT-L/16 underperforms BEiT on 1K data.
Performance depends on the shared projection head design; separate heads yield worse results.
Limited evaluation on datasets beyond ImageNet; transfer learning results may vary.
Online tokenizer may not capture semantics as effectively as offline tokenizers in some domains.
Computational cost of self-distillation with momentum update may be high for very large models.

papers.tEn: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners
papers.tZh: 掩码自编码器是可扩展的视觉学习器
papers.sEn: Masked autoencoders (MAE) are scalable self-supervised learners for computer vision, achieving high accuracy and efficient training.
contrib: Proposes masked autoencoders (MAE) as scalable self-supervised learners for vision.
Introduces asymmetric encoder-decoder design: encoder only on visible patches, lightweight decoder reconstructs pixels.
Shows high masking ratio (75%) creates a challenging self-supervisory task that reduces redundancy.
Achieves 87.8% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K with vanilla ViT-Huge, outperforming prior methods.
Demonstrates transfer learning gains over supervised pre-training on detection and segmentation.
Observes promising scaling behavior: larger models yield better performance with MAE pre-training.
limits: Method relies on random patch masking, which may not capture semantic structure like object boundaries.
Reconstruction target is pixels, which are low-level and may limit high-level semantic learning.
Linear probing accuracy is lower than contrastive methods, indicating less linearly separable features.
Requires long pre-training schedules (e.g., 1600 epochs) for optimal performance.
Model may reflect dataset biases and generate inexistent content, raising societal concerns.

papers.tEn: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces
papers.tZh: 使用结构化状态空间高效建模长序列
papers.sEn: S4 model achieves strong results on long-range sequence tasks, including solving Path-X of length 16k, while being efficient.
contrib: Proposes S4, a structured state space model for efficient long-range sequence modeling.
Introduces NPLR parameterization enabling stable diagonalization and O(N+L) computation.
Reduces SSM convolution kernel computation to Cauchy kernel, enabling fast algorithms.
Achieves 91% accuracy on sequential CIFAR-10 without data augmentation, matching ResNet.
Solves Path-X task of length 16K, where all prior models fail, with 88% accuracy.
Sets state-of-the-art on Long Range Arena benchmark, outperforming Transformers by 20+ points.
limits: S4 is primarily evaluated on 1-D sequence tasks; extension to 2-D data is limited.
The NPLR parameterization is specific to HiPPO matrices; general SSMs may not benefit.
S4's performance on very large-scale language models is not fully explored.
The model assumes linear time-invariance, limiting adaptability to non-stationary signals.
Numerical stability issues may arise with eigenvalues on the right half-plane, requiring fixes.

papers.tEn: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems
papers.tZh: 训练验证器解决数学应用题
papers.sEn: Training verifiers to judge model outputs significantly improves multi-step math reasoning performance.
contrib: Introduces GSM8K, a dataset of 8.5K high-quality grade school math word problems with high linguistic diversity.
Proposes training verifiers to judge correctness of model-generated solutions, improving multi-step reasoning.
Demonstrates verification scales more effectively with increased data than finetuning baseline.
Shows verification provides performance boost equivalent to 30x model size increase on GSM8K.
Finds token-level verifiers outperform solution-level verifiers and benefit from language modeling auxiliary objective.
Demonstrates dropout regularization significantly improves both finetuning and verification performance.
limits: Verification performance degrades when generating too many candidate solutions due to adversarial examples.
Verification requires a sufficiently large dataset to outperform finetuning baseline.
Study limited to grade school math problems; generalization to more complex reasoning not verified.
Verifier may rely on coarse heuristics rather than thorough reasoning, especially when smaller than generator.
Generator overconfidence reduces solution diversity, limiting verifier effectiveness after many training epochs.

papers.tEn: Can Machines Learn Morality? The Delphi Experiment
papers.tZh: 机器能学会道德吗？德尔斐实验
papers.sEn: Teaching morality to AI is challenging, but the Delphi experiment shows promise and limitations.
contrib: Introduces Delphi, a large-scale neural framework for commonsense moral reasoning trained on 1.7M ethical judgments.
Demonstrates strong generalization to novel ethical situations, outperforming GPT-3 by 16.1% in accuracy.
Shows that explicit teaching of moral sense is necessary, as off-the-shelf models exhibit poor judgment and biases.
Validates a bottom-up, descriptive approach to machine ethics, grounded in Rawls' decision procedure.
Demonstrates positive downstream impact via hate speech detection and ethically-informed text generation.
Reveals that compositional training data is more critical than scale for learning nuanced moral reasoning.
limits: Delphi is susceptible to pervasive social biases and inconsistencies inherited from crowd-sourced data.
The model is descriptive, not prescriptive, and does not provide normative guidance for moral action.
Generalization is limited to everyday situations; performance on complex moral dilemmas remains untested.
The bottom-up approach may encode systemic biases of crowdworkers, requiring top-down constraints.
Delphi's moral knowledge is culturally bound to the training data, limiting cross-cultural applicability.

papers.tEn: Train Short, Test Long: Attention with Linear Biases Enables Input Length Extrapolation
papers.tZh: 短训练，长测试：线性偏置注意力实现输入长度外推
papers.sEn: ALiBi enables efficient extrapolation to longer sequences by biasing attention scores with distance-based penalties, outperforming sinusoidal embeddings with 11% faster training and less memory.
contrib: Introduces ALiBi, a simple position method that biases attention scores with linear penalties proportional to distance.
Shows ALiBi enables transformer LMs to extrapolate to sequences longer than training length, e.g., 1.3B model trained on 1024 tokens extrapolates to 2048.
Demonstrates ALiBi trains 11% faster and uses 11% less memory than sinusoidal embeddings for equivalent perplexity on long sequences.
Finds that extrapolation ability depends heavily on position method; sinusoidal and rotary methods have limited extrapolation, while T5 bias is computationally costly.
Shows ALiBi outperforms multiple strong position methods on WikiText-103, improving perplexity up to 3x training length.
Validates ALiBi on large-scale 1.3B parameter model with 461GB dataset, achieving similar perplexity to sinusoidal baseline with less memory.
limits: ALiBi's extrapolation performance peaks at around 2x training length; beyond that, gains diminish.
Method tested primarily on language modeling; applicability to other tasks like translation or classification not explored.
ALiBi requires a small memory increase (up to 100MB) due to per-head bias masks, though offset by shorter training sequences.
The fixed slope hyperparameter set may not be optimal for all model sizes or domains, though robust across tested settings.
Extrapolation beyond 10,000 tokens shows strong but not perfect performance; further improvements may require additional techniques.

papers.tEn: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
papers.tZh: 评估基于代码训练的大型语言模型
papers.sEn: Codex, a GPT model fine-tuned on GitHub code, achieves 28.8% on HumanEval, with repeated sampling boosting performance to 70.2%.
contrib: Introduces Codex, a GPT model fine-tuned on GitHub code, achieving 28.8% pass@1 on HumanEval.
Demonstrates repeated sampling with 100 samples solves 70.2% of HumanEval problems.
Releases HumanEval dataset of 164 hand-written programming problems with unit tests.
Shows supervised fine-tuning (Codex-S) improves pass@1 by 6.5 points and pass@100 by 15.1 points.
Finds BLEU score unreliable for functional correctness; functional correctness is preferred.
Discusses broader impacts including safety, security, economics, and alignment issues.
limits: Codex struggles with long chains of operations in docstrings and binding operations to variables.
Codex is not sample efficient; requires huge training data compared to human programmers.
Codex can generate syntactically incorrect, undefined, or insecure code, and may be misaligned with user intent.
Codex performance degrades exponentially with increasing docstring length in synthetic tasks.
Codex may produce biased or harmful outputs as code comments, reflecting stereotypes.

papers.tEn: SoundStream: An End-to-End Neural Audio Codec
papers.tZh: SoundStream: 一种端到端神经音频编解码器
papers.sEn: SoundStream is a neural audio codec that efficiently compresses speech, music, and general audio at low bitrates, outperforming traditional codecs like Opus and approaching EVS quality.
contrib: Proposes SoundStream, a neural audio codec trained end-to-end with adversarial and reconstruction losses for superior audio quality.
Introduces a residual vector quantizer with quantizer dropout for bitrate scalability from 3 to 18 kbps.
Demonstrates that learning the encoder significantly improves coding efficiency over fixed mel-spectrogram features.
Shows SoundStream outperforms Opus and EVS across a wide range of bitrates in subjective evaluations.
Supports streamable inference with low latency, running in real-time on a smartphone CPU.
Enables joint compression and enhancement without additional latency, demonstrated via background noise suppression.
limits: Evaluation limited to 24 kHz sampling rate; performance at higher rates not explored.
Subjective tests use crowd-sourced MUSHRA methodology, which may introduce variability.
Joint compression and enhancement only demonstrated for background noise suppression; other enhancements not tested.
Model complexity and memory requirements may limit deployment on very low-resource devices.
Bitrate scalability relies on quantizer dropout; performance at extreme bitrates (e.g., below 3 kbps) not evaluated.

papers.tEn: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
papers.tZh: 评估基于代码训练的大型语言模型
papers.sEn: Codex, a GPT model fine-tuned on GitHub code, achieves 28.8% on HumanEval, with repeated sampling boosting performance to 70.2%.
contrib: Introduces Codex, a GPT model fine-tuned on GitHub code, achieving 28.8% pass@1 on HumanEval.
Demonstrates repeated sampling with 100 samples solves 70.2% of HumanEval problems.
Releases HumanEval dataset of 164 hand-written programming problems with unit tests.
Shows supervised fine-tuning (Codex-S) improves pass@1 by 6.5 points and pass@100 by 15.1 points.
Finds BLEU score unreliable for functional correctness; functional correctness is preferred.
Discusses broader impacts including safety, security, economics, and alignment issues.
limits: Codex struggles with long chains of operations in docstrings and binding operations to variables.
Codex is not sample efficient; requires huge training data compared to human programmers.
Codex can generate syntactically incorrect, undefined, or insecure code, and may be misaligned with user intent.
Codex performance degrades exponentially with increasing docstring length in synthetic tasks.
Codex may produce biased or harmful outputs as code comments, reflecting stereotypes.

papers.tEn: PVT v2: Improved Baselines with Pyramid Vision Transformer
papers.tZh: PVT v2：改进的金字塔视觉 Transformer 基线
papers.sEn: PVT v2 improves PVT v1 with linear attention, overlapping patch embedding, and convolutional FFN, achieving SOTA on vision tasks.
contrib: Proposes linear spatial reduction attention (SRA) layer with average pooling, reducing complexity to linear.
Introduces overlapping patch embedding to model local continuity of images.
Adds convolutional feed-forward network with zero-padding to capture local continuity and remove fixed position encoding.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on ImageNet classification, COCO detection, and ADE20K segmentation.
Provides a family of models (B0-B5) with varying sizes, outperforming Swin Transformer and Twins.
limits: Evaluation limited to image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks.
Performance may degrade on tasks requiring very high-resolution inputs beyond tested scales.
Ablation studies only on PVT v2-B2 variant; other sizes may show different trade-offs.
Does not explore integration with other advanced architectures like MLP-based backbones.

papers.tEn: Alias-Free Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.tZh: 无别名生成对抗网络
papers.sEn: We identify that aliasing in GAN generators causes unhealthy dependence on absolute pixel coordinates, and propose small architectural changes to achieve translation and rotation equivariance.
contrib: Identified aliasing in GAN generators as root cause of texture sticking to pixel coordinates.
Proposed continuous signal interpretation and architectural changes to eliminate aliasing.
Achieved full translation and rotation equivariance at subpixel scales in StyleGAN3.
Matched FID of StyleGAN2 while dramatically altering internal representations.
Paved way for generative models better suited for video and animation.
Introduced practical approximations like 2x upsampling for nonlinearities and Kaiser-windowed filters.
limits: Assumes training data is properly antialiased; aliased data (e.g., pixel art) causes difficulties.
Rotation equivariance requires 1x1 convolutions and radially symmetric filters, limiting capacity.
Equivariance metrics may not fully capture perceptual quality; FID trade-offs exist.
Generator modifications only; discriminator not made equivariant, potentially limiting performance.
Higher computational cost due to custom CUDA kernels and larger filters.

papers.tEn: BEiT: BERT Pre-Training of Image Transformers
papers.tZh: BEiT：图像 Transformer 的 BERT 预训练
papers.sEn: BEiT introduces masked image modeling for self-supervised vision Transformer pre-training, achieving competitive results on image classification and segmentation.
contrib: Proposes masked image modeling (MIM) to pretrain vision Transformers in a self-supervised manner.
Provides a theoretical explanation of MIM from the perspective of variational autoencoder.
Pretrains BEiT and conducts extensive fine-tuning on image classification and semantic segmentation.
Shows self-attention in BEiT learns to distinguish semantic regions and object boundaries without human annotation.
Achieves competitive results: BEiT-Base 83.2% top-1 on ImageNet-1K, outperforming DeiT (81.8%).
Large-size BEiT achieves 86.3% on ImageNet-1K, surpassing ViT-L with supervised pre-training on ImageNet-22K (85.2%).
limits: Pre-training requires a separate image tokenizer (dVAE) trained on additional data.
Masked image modeling may still focus on low-level details despite using discrete tokens.
Performance gains are demonstrated mainly on ImageNet and ADE20K; generalizability to other tasks is not fully explored.
The method relies on blockwise masking strategy; other masking strategies may yield different results.
Pre-training is computationally expensive (500k steps on 16 GPUs for 5 days).

papers.tEn: HuBERT: Self-Supervised Speech Representation Learning by Masked Prediction of Hidden Units
papers.tZh: HuBERT：通过隐藏单元的掩码预测进行自监督语音表示学习
papers.sEn: HuBERT uses offline clustering to provide target labels for masked prediction, achieving state-of-the-art performance on speech benchmarks.
contrib: Proposes HuBERT, a self-supervised speech representation learning method using masked prediction of hidden units from offline clustering.
Applies prediction loss only on masked regions, forcing the model to learn combined acoustic and language models.
Shows that target consistency matters more than correctness, enabling robust learning from simple k-means clusters.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on Librispeech and Libri-light benchmarks, matching or outperforming wav2vec 2.0.
Demonstrates iterative refinement of cluster assignments using learned representations improves representation quality.
Scales to a 1B parameter model, achieving up to 19% relative WER reduction on challenging subsets.
limits: Requires offline clustering step, adding computational overhead and dependency on clustering quality.
Performance relies on iterative refinement of targets, which may not converge optimally in all settings.
Evaluated only on English audiobook data; generalization to other languages or noisy conditions is not verified.
Fine-tuning requires careful hyperparameter tuning for each subset, limiting practical deployment.
Model size up to 1B parameters demands significant computational resources for pre-training and fine-tuning.

papers.tEn: Diffusion Models Beat GANs on Image Synthesis
papers.tZh: 扩散模型在图像合成上击败 GAN
papers.sEn: Diffusion models achieve superior image quality to GANs with classifier guidance.
contrib: Demonstrates diffusion models surpass GANs in image sample quality on unconditional and conditional synthesis.
Proposes improved UNet architecture with multi-resolution attention, BigGAN blocks, and adaptive group normalization.
Introduces classifier guidance for trading off diversity for fidelity using classifier gradients.
Achieves state-of-the-art FID scores on ImageNet at multiple resolutions with few sampling steps.
Shows classifier guidance combines with upsampling diffusion models for further FID improvements.
Provides open-source code for guided diffusion models.
limits: Sampling is slower than GANs due to multiple forward passes.
Classifier guidance requires labeled datasets; no effective strategy for unlabeled data.
Metrics like FID are imperfect proxies for human judgment.
Guidance scale tuning is needed for optimal trade-off between diversity and fidelity.
Architecture improvements may not transfer to other domains without tuning.

papers.tEn: VICReg: Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization for Self-Supervised Learning
papers.tZh: VICReg：用于自监督学习的方差-不变性-协方差正则化
papers.sEn: VICReg explicitly avoids collapse in self-supervised learning by regularizing embedding variance and covariance.
contrib: Introduces VICReg, a self-supervised method with variance, invariance, and covariance regularization to explicitly prevent collapse.
Variance term maintains embedding variance above a threshold, preventing norm collapse.
Covariance term decorrelates embedding dimensions, maximizing information content.
VICReg does not require weight sharing, batch normalization, or memory banks, enabling multi-modal applications.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on ImageNet linear evaluation and transfer tasks.
Variance regularization stabilizes training and improves performance when added to other methods.
limits: Performance on detection tasks slightly behind top methods like SwAV and BYOL.
Requires careful tuning of hyperparameters λ and μ for optimal performance.
Covariance regularization may hinder optimization when combined with stop-gradient.
VICReg's expander architecture adds computational overhead during pretraining.
Limited evaluation on multi-modal tasks beyond image-text retrieval.

papers.tEn: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
papers.tZh: 自监督视觉 Transformer 中的涌现特性
papers.sEn: Self-supervised ViTs reveal explicit semantic segmentation and strong k-NN performance, leading to DINO method achieving 80.1% top-1 on ImageNet.
contrib: Self-supervised ViT features explicitly encode semantic segmentation information, unlike supervised ViTs or convnets.
Self-supervised ViT features achieve 78.3% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet with a simple k-NN classifier.
The DINO method, a form of self-distillation with no labels, achieves 80.1% top-1 on ImageNet linear evaluation with ViT-Base.
Momentum encoder, multi-crop training, and small patches are crucial for high-quality self-supervised ViT features.
Self-supervised ViT features outperform supervised ones in nearest neighbor retrieval and copy detection tasks.
DINO with ViT achieves competitive performance on dense tasks like video instance segmentation without fine-tuning.
limits: The study focuses on ImageNet; generalization to other datasets is not fully explored.
Small patches improve performance but significantly reduce throughput and increase memory usage.
DINO requires careful tuning of centering and sharpening to avoid collapse, which may be sensitive to hyperparameters.
The method is evaluated on ViT and ResNet; applicability to other architectures is not verified.
Performance gains from multi-crop diminish with more views, suggesting diminishing returns.

papers.tEn: Geometric Deep Learning: Grids, Groups, Graphs, Geodesics, and Gauges
papers.tZh: 几何深度学习：网格、群、图、测地线与规范
papers.sEn: Deep learning's success stems from exploiting structural regularities in data, which can be unified through geometric principles to understand and design neural architectures.
contrib: Proposes Geometric Deep Learning as an Erlangen-style unification: deriving neural architectures from symmetry and invariance principles.
Defines five geometric domains—grids, groups, graphs, geodesics, gauges—as a common structure underlying data and signals.
Shows CNNs, RNNs, GNNs, and Transformers are instances of the same geometric priors: symmetry, stability, and scale separation.
Introduces a blueprint combining symmetry, deformation stability, and scale separation to learn stable high-dimensional representations.
Provides a constructive approach to incorporate physical prior knowledge and to design future neural architectures.
Highlights that nonlinear equivariant maps compose with nonlinearities to build expressive invariant representations without trivial averaging.
limits: Focuses on representation learning, excluding self-supervised learning, generative modelling, and reinforcement learning pipelines.
Does not aim to fully summarise all geometric deep learning research; selected architectures illustrate principles.
Exact symmetry assumptions are often unrealistic; deformation stability is approximate and difficult to quantify on complex domains.
The geometric blueprint may not fully capture all modern designs, notably attention-based Transformers beyond permutation equivariance.
Little discussion of computational cost or practical scaling of equivariant architectures across large-scale problems.

papers.tEn: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
papers.tZh: RoFormer: 增强型 Transformer 与旋转位置嵌入
papers.sEn: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) encodes absolute positions with rotation matrices and captures relative position dependencies, improving Transformer performance on long texts.
contrib: Proposes Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) that encodes absolute position via rotation matrix and relative position via inner product.
Achieves long-term decay property where inter-token dependency decreases with increasing relative distance.
Enables compatibility with linear self-attention, allowing relative position encoding without quadratic complexity.
Demonstrates faster convergence in pre-training compared to baseline models with other position encoding methods.
Outperforms alternatives on long text classification benchmarks, including English and Chinese datasets.
Provides theoretical analysis explaining the properties and effectiveness of RoPE.
limits: Lacks thorough explanation for faster convergence compared to other position encoding strategies.
No faithful explanation for superior long-text performance despite long-term decay property.
Requires significant hardware resources for pre-training due to Transformer-based infrastructure.
Theoretical analysis limited to 2D subspaces, generalization to higher dimensions relies on linearity assumption.
Experimental validation primarily on classification tasks; other NLP tasks not extensively evaluated.

papers.tEn: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows
papers.tZh: Swin Transformer：使用移位窗口的分层视觉 Transformer
papers.sEn: Swin Transformer achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple vision tasks with a hierarchical architecture and shifted windows.
contrib: Proposes Swin Transformer, a hierarchical vision Transformer with shifted windows for general-purpose backbone.
Achieves linear computational complexity relative to image size via local window self-attention.
Introduces shifted window partitioning to enable cross-window connections efficiently.
Outperforms previous state-of-the-art on COCO object detection (+2.7 box AP, +2.6 mask AP) and ADE20K segmentation (+3.2 mIoU).
Demonstrates strong performance on ImageNet-1K classification (87.3% top-1 accuracy).
Shows hierarchical design and shifted windows benefit all-MLP architectures as well.
limits: Requires careful tuning of window size and shift pattern for different tasks.
Performance on video or 3D tasks not explored in this paper.
Relative position bias may not generalize well to very large window sizes.
Computational efficiency relies on fixed window size; adaptive windows not considered.
Pre-training on large datasets (ImageNet-22K) needed for best results.

papers.tEn: GLM: General Language Model Pretraining with Autoregressive Blank Infilling
papers.tZh: GLM：基于自回归空白填充的通用语言模型预训练
