papers.sEn: GLM outperforms BERT, T5, and GPT across NLU, conditional and unconditional generation tasks with a single pretrained model.
contrib: Proposes GLM, a general language model based on autoregressive blank infilling.
Introduces 2D positional encodings and span shuffling to improve blank filling pretraining.
Unifies NLU, conditional, and unconditional generation tasks under a single pretraining framework.
Outperforms BERT, T5, and GPT on NLU and generation tasks with similar model sizes.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on text infilling tasks like Yahoo Answers.
Demonstrates effective parameter sharing across diverse downstream tasks.
limits: Requires manual crafting of cloze patterns for NLU tasks.
Multi-task pretraining may slightly degrade NLU performance compared to single-task.
Language modeling perplexity lags behind GPT without bidirectional context.
Evaluation limited to English and specific datasets like SuperGLUE.
Scaling to larger models requires more computational resources.

papers.tEn: GPT Understands, Too
papers.tZh: GPT 也能理解：P-Tuning——用可训练的连续提示嵌入提升自然语言理解性能
papers.sEn: P-Tuning uses trainable continuous prompt embeddings to stabilize and improve NLU performance across various tasks and settings.
contrib: Proposes P-Tuning, using trainable continuous prompt embeddings with discrete prompts to stabilize and improve NLU performance.
Shows P-Tuning reduces performance variance across different discrete prompts, enhancing training stability.
Achieves significant gains on LAMA knowledge probing (20+ points over manual prompts) and SuperGLUE under both full-supervised and few-shot settings.
Demonstrates effectiveness for both frozen and tuned language models, and compatibility with existing discrete prompts.
Introduces a prompt encoder (LSTM/MLP) to model dependencies among continuous prompt embeddings, improving performance.
Provides analysis on prompt token location and number, offering practical guidelines for optimal configuration.
limits: P-Tuning requires additional trainable parameters for continuous prompts, increasing model complexity.
Performance gains are less pronounced on high-resource tasks (e.g., WiC, MultiRC) compared to low-resource tasks.
The method involves searching over prompt patterns and token numbers, which may be task-specific and time-consuming.
Effectiveness depends on the choice of prompt encoder (LSTM/MLP/EMB), with EMB being unstable on some tasks.
Not directly applicable to tasks without discrete prompts (e.g., ReCoRD in SuperGLUE).

papers.tEn: Moore's Law for Everything
papers.tZh: 万物摩尔定律
papers.sEn: AI will reshape the economy, requiring a new social contract that taxes capital to distribute wealth fairly.
contrib: Proposes 'Moore's Law for Everything' where AI-driven automation halves costs every two years.
Advocates taxing capital (companies and land) instead of labor to distribute AI-generated wealth.
Introduces the American Equity Fund, giving every citizen annual dividends from taxes on companies and land.
Predicts AI will replace most human labor within decades, causing massive socioeconomic shifts.
Argues that inclusive capitalism with broad ownership can align incentives and reduce inequality.
Emphasizes that policy must adapt proactively to the imminent AI revolution to avoid societal harm.
limits: Assumes continuous exponential growth in AI capabilities without considering potential plateaus or risks.
Tax proposal may face political feasibility issues and unintended consequences like capital flight.
Relies on accurate valuation of land and companies, which is difficult and prone to manipulation.
Does not address potential negative impacts of AI, such as job displacement or ethical concerns.
The plan's success hinges on global cooperation, but unilateral implementation may be ineffective.

papers.tEn: Barlow Twins: Self-Supervised Learning via Redundancy Reduction
papers.tZh: Barlow Twins: 通过冗余减少实现自监督学习
papers.sEn: Barlow Twins avoids collapse by making the cross-correlation matrix close to identity, reducing redundancy between embedding components.
contrib: Proposes Barlow Twins, a self-supervised learning method using redundancy reduction to avoid trivial constant solutions.
Objective function measures cross-correlation matrix between twin network outputs and makes it close to identity matrix.
Does not require large batches, predictor networks, stop-gradients, or momentum encoders, simplifying implementation.
Benefits from very high-dimensional output vectors, unlike contrastive methods that saturate.
Outperforms prior methods on ImageNet semi-supervised classification with 1% labels (55% top-1 accuracy).
Matches state-of-the-art on ImageNet linear classification and transfer tasks for classification and object detection.
limits: Performance degrades when certain data augmentations are removed, unlike BYOL which is more robust.
Requires careful tuning of the trade-off parameter λ for optimal performance.
High-dimensional embeddings increase memory requirements, limiting scalability beyond 16,000 dimensions.
Method is evaluated only on computer vision tasks; applicability to other domains like NLP is unexplored.
Theoretical connection to Information Bottleneck is heuristic; alternative implementations may yield different results.

papers.tEn: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
papers.tZh: 从自然语言监督中学习可迁移的视觉模型
papers.sEn: Predicting which caption goes with which image is an efficient and scalable way to learn SOTA image representations from scratch.
contrib: Proposes CLIP, a contrastive language-image pre-training method that learns visual representations from natural language supervision at scale.
Demonstrates zero-shot transfer to over 30 datasets, matching ResNet-50 on ImageNet without any training examples.
Shows that zero-shot CLIP models exhibit significantly higher effective robustness to natural distribution shifts than supervised ImageNet models.
Introduces a new dataset of 400 million (image, text) pairs collected from the internet for pre-training.
Finds that zero-shot CLIP matches the performance of 4-shot logistic regression on the same feature space, highlighting the efficiency of natural language supervision.
Demonstrates that CLIP learns a wide range of tasks during pre-training, including OCR, geo-localization, and action recognition.
limits: Zero-shot CLIP underperforms on specialized tasks like satellite image classification and lymph node tumor detection.
The study focuses on zero-shot and linear probe evaluation, not end-to-end fine-tuning.
The pre-training dataset may contain biases from internet sources, affecting model fairness.
CLIP's zero-shot performance is limited by polysemy and lack of context in class names.
The study does not explore the combination of zero-shot and few-shot learning methods.

papers.tEn: Pyramid Vision Transformer: A Versatile Backbone for Dense Prediction without Convolutions
papers.tZh: 金字塔视觉 Transformer：无需卷积的密集预测通用骨干网络
papers.sEn: PVT is a pyramid vision transformer backbone for dense prediction tasks, outperforming CNNs without convolutions.
contrib: Proposes Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT), the first pure Transformer backbone for dense prediction tasks.
Introduces progressive shrinking pyramid to generate multi-scale feature maps, enabling flexible adaptation to dense prediction.
Designs spatial-reduction attention (SRA) to reduce computational and memory costs for high-resolution features.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on object detection, instance segmentation, and semantic segmentation with fewer parameters.
Demonstrates that PVT can replace CNN backbones in various vision tasks without convolutions.
Builds first convolution-free object detection pipeline by combining PVT with DETR.
limits: PVT has higher computational cost than ResNet for large input scales (e.g., >640x640).
Inference speed of PVT-based RetinaNet is slower than ResNet50-based model on COCO (800px short side).
Specific CNN modules like SE, SK, dilated convolution, and NAS are not integrated into PVT.
PVT is still in early development stage compared to well-engineered CNN backbones like EfficientNet.
Position embeddings pre-trained on ImageNet may require interpolation for arbitrary input sizes in downstream tasks.

papers.tEn: Zero-Shot Text-to-Image Generation
papers.tZh: 零样本文本到图像生成
papers.sEn: A simple transformer-based approach for zero-shot text-to-image generation achieves competitive results with domain-specific models when scaled with sufficient data.
contrib: Proposes a simple transformer-based approach for zero-shot text-to-image generation by modeling text and image tokens as a single data stream.
Demonstrates that scaling data and model size (12-billion parameters) yields high-fidelity, flexible image generation competitive with domain-specific models.
Introduces a two-stage training procedure with a discrete VAE for image compression and an autoregressive transformer for joint text-image modeling.
Achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on MS-COCO, preferred by human evaluators 90% of the time over prior work.
Shows emergent capabilities like zero-shot image-to-image translation and combinatorial generalization from a single generative model.
Develops practical techniques for stable training of large-scale transformers, including per-resblock gradient scaling and PowerSGD compression.
limits: Heavy image compression via dVAE limits high-frequency detail generation, reducing FID/IS on specialized datasets like CUB.
Zero-shot performance on specialized distributions (e.g., CUB birds) is significantly worse than domain-specific models.
Model requires massive computational resources (12-billion parameters, 250M image-text pairs), limiting reproducibility.
Inconsistent performance on complex compositional tasks like variable binding (e.g., hedgehog in sweater walking dog).
Training instability in 16-bit precision required custom gradient scaling and parameter sharding to avoid underflow.

papers.tEn: Scaling Up Visual and Vision-Language Representation Learning With Noisy Text Supervision
papers.tZh: 利用噪声文本监督扩展视觉和视觉-语言表示学习
papers.sEn: Scaling up visual and vision-language representation learning with noisy text supervision achieves state-of-the-art results.
contrib: Leverages a noisy dataset of over one billion image alt-text pairs without expensive filtering.
Simple dual-encoder architecture with contrastive loss aligns visual and language representations.
Achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot image classification on ImageNet with 76.4% top-1 accuracy.
Sets new state-of-the-art results on Flickr30K and MSCOCO image-text retrieval benchmarks.
Enables cross-modality search with complex text and text + image queries.
Shows that data scale can compensate for noise, outperforming curated datasets with 4x size.
limits: Model may reinforce harmful stereotypes from noisy web alt-text data.
Data balancing needed to prevent skewed performance across demographic groups.
Potential misuse for surveillance or nefarious purposes should be prohibited.
Additional testing required for sensitive religious or cultural items to mitigate mislabeling.
Model performance may degrade on tasks requiring fine-grained visual reasoning beyond retrieval.

papers.tEn: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
papers.tZh: Switch Transformers：通过简单高效的稀疏性扩展到万亿参数模型
papers.sEn: Switch Transformers simplify MoE routing, reduce communication and training instability, enabling trillion-parameter models with up to 7x speedup.
contrib: Simplifies MoE routing to top-1 expert, reducing computation and communication costs.
Achieves up to 7x pre-training speedup over T5 with same FLOPs per token.
Introduces selective precision (bfloat16) training for large sparse models.
Demonstrates scaling to trillion parameters with 4x speedup over T5-XXL.
Shows universal improvements across 101 languages in multilingual setting.
Proposes expert dropout and distillation to preserve 30% quality gain with 99% compression.
limits: Training instability persists for largest models like Switch-XXL.
Downstream gains do not fully match upstream perplexity improvements.
Fine-tuning quality depends on FLOPs per token and parameter count in unclear ways.
Expert capacity factor introduces trade-off between token dropping and efficiency.
Distillation preserves only ~30% of sparse model quality gain.

papers.tEn: RepVGG: Making VGG-style ConvNets Great Again
papers.tZh: RepVGG：让 VGG 风格的卷积网络再次伟大
papers.sEn: RepVGG achieves over 80% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet with a simple VGG-like architecture, running 83% faster than ResNet-50.
contrib: Proposes RepVGG, a VGG-style plain architecture with only 3x3 conv and ReLU for inference.
Introduces structural re-parameterization to decouple training-time multi-branch and inference-time plain topology.
Achieves over 80% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet with a plain model for the first time.
Demonstrates favorable speed-accuracy trade-off compared to state-of-the-art models like EfficientNet and RegNet.
Shows effectiveness in semantic segmentation with higher speed and accuracy than ResNet backbones.
Provides simple and practical ConvNets suitable for GPU and specialized hardware.
limits: RepVGG is less parameter-efficient than mobile-regime models like MobileNets for low-power devices.
The structural re-parameterization requires careful handling of batch normalization and branch conversion.
The method is primarily designed for GPU and may not be optimal for all hardware platforms.
The ablation studies show that removing identity or 1x1 branches significantly reduces accuracy.
The dilated convolution implementation in segmentation is inefficient, slowing inference.

papers.tEn: AlphaFold: a solution to a 50-year-old grand challenge in biology — Google DeepMind
papers.tZh: AlphaFold：生物学 50 年重大挑战的解决方案——Google DeepMind
papers.sEn: AlphaFold solves a 50-year grand challenge in biology by predicting protein structures with high accuracy.
contrib: AlphaFold achieves median GDT score of 92.4, rivaling experimental methods.
Solves the 50-year grand challenge of protein structure prediction.
Uses attention-based neural network trained end-to-end on ~170,000 structures.
Predicts structures in days, enabling high-throughput biology.
Provides internal confidence measure for predicted structures.
Demonstrates AI's potential to accelerate scientific discovery.
limits: Not all predicted structures are perfect; accuracy varies.
Does not predict protein complexes, interactions with DNA/RNA or small molecules.
Cannot determine precise side chain conformations.
Requires evolutionary information (MSA) which may be lacking for novel proteins.
Computational cost may limit accessibility for some research groups.

papers.tEn: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
papers.tZh: 基于随机微分方程的分数生成建模
papers.sEn: We present a unified SDE framework for score-based generative modeling, enabling new sampling procedures, exact likelihood computation, and record-breaking image generation.
contrib: Unified score-based generative modeling framework via stochastic differential equations (SDEs).
Predictor-corrector (PC) samplers combining numerical SDE solvers with score-based MCMC.
Probability flow ODE enabling exact likelihood computation and efficient sampling.
Controllable generation for inverse problems using unconditional score models.
Record-breaking unconditional image generation on CIFAR-10 (Inception 9.89, FID 2.20).
First high-fidelity 1024x1024 image generation from a score-based model.
limits: Sampling slower than GANs on same datasets.
Many hyper-parameters for different samplers require tuning.
Likelihood computation limited to affine drift SDEs.
Conditional generation requires known forward process gradient.
Framework assumes continuous state spaces and Gaussian perturbations.

papers.tEn: Scaling Laws for Autoregressive Generative Modeling
papers.tZh: 自回归生成建模的缩放定律
papers.sEn: Scaling laws for autoregressive transformers show power-law improvements in cross-entropy loss across diverse domains, enabling predictions of optimal model size and performance.
contrib: Identifies empirical scaling laws for cross-entropy loss across four domains: image, video, multimodal, and math.
Shows that optimal model size scales as a power-law with compute budget, with exponent ~0.7 across all domains.
Interprets loss as entropy plus KL divergence, enabling prediction of irreducible loss and model size for target reducible loss.
Demonstrates that generative image models finetuned for classification show smooth scaling of loss and error rate with model size.
Finds scaling laws for mutual information in multimodal models, quantifying information gain between images and text.
Shows that math problem extrapolation performance depends mainly on training distribution loss, not model size.
limits: Scaling laws may break down at very large scales due to optimization inefficiencies or data constraints.
Results are limited to autoregressive Transformer models; other architectures may exhibit different scaling.
The interpretation of irreducible loss as entropy assumes infinite data and compute limits, which are not fully realized.
Extrapolation of scaling trends beyond tested ranges may be unreliable, especially for downstream tasks.
Mutual information estimates may be biased due to out-of-distribution inputs like blank captions or images.

papers.tEn: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
papers.tZh: 一张图片等价于 16x16 个词：用于大规模图像识别的 Transformer
papers.sEn: A pure transformer applied directly to image patches can match or exceed state-of-the-art CNNs on image classification, with less training compute.
contrib: Shows pure Transformer applied to image patches achieves strong image classification performance.
Demonstrates Vision Transformer (ViT) matches or exceeds state-of-the-art CNNs on large-scale pre-training.
Reveals large-scale training overcomes lack of inductive biases in ViT.
Provides controlled scaling study showing ViT's favorable performance-to-cost ratio.
Analyzes ViT internal representations, showing global attention and learned position embeddings.
Explores self-supervised pre-training for ViT, showing potential for future improvement.
limits: ViT underperforms CNNs on small datasets due to lack of inductive biases.
Requires large-scale pre-training (e.g., JFT-300M) to achieve state-of-the-art results.
Self-supervised pre-training still lags behind supervised pre-training by 4% on ImageNet.
ViT has not been applied to other vision tasks like detection and segmentation.
Position embeddings require interpolation for higher resolution fine-tuning.

papers.tEn: Deformable DETR: Deformable Transformers for End-to-End Object Detection
papers.tZh: 可变形 DETR：用于端到端目标检测的可变形 Transformer
papers.sEn: Deformable DETR achieves better performance than DETR with 10x fewer training epochs by using attention modules that only attend to a small set of key sampling points.
contrib: Proposes Deformable DETR with deformable attention modules that attend to a small set of key sampling points.
Achieves better performance than DETR, especially on small objects, with 10× fewer training epochs.
Introduces multi-scale deformable attention to aggregate multi-scale features without FPN.
Explores iterative bounding box refinement and two-stage Deformable DETR for improved detection.
Reduces computational complexity from quadratic to linear in spatial size for encoder attention.
Demonstrates effectiveness on COCO benchmark with extensive experiments.
limits: Deformable attention still involves unordered memory access, slightly slower than traditional convolution.
Performance relies on hyperparameters like number of sampling points K and attention heads M.
Two-stage variant adds complexity and may not always improve over single-stage.
Method is evaluated only on COCO; generalization to other domains is not verified.
Deformable attention requires bilinear interpolation for fractional sampling locations, adding overhead.

papers.tEn: Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models
papers.tZh: 去噪扩散隐式模型
papers.sEn: DDIMs accelerate sampling from diffusion models by 10-50x while maintaining high image quality.
contrib: Proposes denoising diffusion implicit models (DDIMs) for faster sampling.
Constructs non-Markovian diffusion processes with same training objective as DDPMs.
Achieves 10× to 50× speedup in wall-clock time for high-quality image generation.
Enables trade-off between computation and sample quality via step count adjustment.
Demonstrates semantically meaningful image interpolation directly in latent space.
Shows deterministic generation process allows encoding and reconstruction of observations.
limits: Sample quality may degrade with very few steps compared to full-step DDPM.
Deterministic process may reduce diversity compared to stochastic DDPM.
Reconstruction error increases with fewer steps in encoding-decoding.
Method assumes same training objective as DDPM, limiting architectural changes.
Empirical validation limited to image generation tasks.

papers.tEn: Rethinking Attention with Performers
papers.tZh: 重新思考注意力机制：Performer
papers.sEn: Performers achieve linear complexity for full-rank attention with provable accuracy.
contrib: Introduces Performers, linear Transformer architectures that estimate softmax full-rank attention with provable accuracy using linear space and time complexity.
Proposes FAVOR+ mechanism using positive orthogonal random features for unbiased, low-variance softmax kernel approximation.
Provides theoretical guarantees: unbiased estimation, uniform convergence, and lower variance for attention matrix approximation.
Demonstrates competitive performance on diverse tasks including pixel prediction, text modeling, and protein sequence modeling.
Enables backward compatibility with pre-trained Transformers via fine-tuning.
Extends attention beyond softmax to other kernelizable mechanisms, enabling large-scale kernel comparison.
limits: Requires periodic redrawing of random features for optimal training, adding minor overhead.
Approximation errors may propagate through multiple layers, requiring tight approximation for deep models.
Orthogonal random features require m ≤ d, limiting the number of features to the embedding dimension.
Performance on very long sequences beyond tested lengths (e.g., >12k tokens) is not fully validated.
The method assumes isotropic distributions for orthogonalization, which may not hold for all kernels.

papers.tEn: Learning to summarize from human feedback
papers.tZh: 从人类反馈中学习摘要生成
papers.sEn: Training summarization models with human feedback significantly improves summary quality over traditional methods.
contrib: Shows training with human feedback significantly improves summary quality over supervised learning.
Demonstrates human feedback models generalize to new domains without task-specific fine-tuning.
Collects and releases a large dataset of 64,832 human summary comparisons.
Conducts extensive analysis of reward model performance and over-optimization.
Finds reward models outperform automatic metrics like ROUGE in predicting human preferences.
Highlights the importance of aligning training objectives with desired model behavior.
limits: High time and cost for training and data collection, e.g., 320 GPU-days for 6.7B model.
Reward model over-optimization can lead to anti-correlation with human preferences.
Models trained on Reddit TL;DR may generate biased or offensive content.
Summary length bias in reward models affects preference judgments.
Method requires human evaluators, limiting scalability for tasks where evaluation is difficult.

papers.tEn: Transformers are RNNs: Fast Autoregressive Transformers with Linear Attention
papers.tZh: Transformer 是 RNN：具有线性注意力的快速自回归 Transformer
papers.sEn: Transformers can be reformulated as linear dot-products of kernel feature maps, reducing complexity from O(N^2) to O(N) and enabling iterative computation akin to RNNs.
contrib: Proposes linear attention via kernel feature maps, reducing complexity from O(N^2) to O(N).
Derives causal masking with linear time and constant memory for autoregressive transformers.
Reveals transformers as recurrent neural networks, enabling constant-time inference per step.
Achieves up to 4000x faster autoregressive inference on long sequences with comparable performance.
Provides constant-memory gradient computation for causal linear attention via cumulative sums.
Validates on image generation and speech recognition, showing linear scaling and competitive accuracy.
limits: Feature map choice (e.g., elu) may not match softmax attention in all tasks.
Linear attention requires finite-dimensional feature maps, limiting exact softmax approximation.
Performance on very short sequences may not benefit from linear complexity due to overhead.
The method assumes non-negative similarity functions, which may restrict attention expressiveness.
Empirical evaluation is limited to image and speech domains; generalizability to other tasks is unverified.

papers.tEn: wav2vec 2.0: A Framework for Self-Supervised Learning of Speech Representations
papers.tZh: wav2vec 2.0：一种自监督学习语音表示的框架
papers.sEn: wav2vec 2.0 outperforms semi-supervised methods by learning from raw audio alone, achieving state-of-the-art results with minimal labeled data.
contrib: Proposes wav2vec 2.0, a self-supervised framework for learning speech representations from raw audio.
Jointly learns discrete speech units and contextualized representations via a contrastive task.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on Librispeech with only 10 minutes of labeled data.
Outperforms previous semi-supervised methods while being conceptually simpler.
Demonstrates feasibility of ultra-low resource speech recognition with 53k hours of unlabeled pre-training.
Sets new state of the art on TIMIT phoneme recognition and full Librispeech benchmark.
limits: Evaluation limited to English speech datasets (Librispeech, TIMIT, LibriVox).
Requires large amounts of unlabeled data (53k hours) for best performance.
Fine-tuning still needs transcribed speech; zero-shot recognition not explored.
Model size and compute requirements are high (Large model uses 128 GPUs).
Character-based vocabulary may limit performance compared to word pieces.

papers.tEn: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.tZh: 去噪扩散概率模型
papers.sEn: We present high quality image synthesis using diffusion probabilistic models, achieving state-of-the-art FID scores on CIFAR10 and LSUN datasets.
contrib: Established connection between diffusion models and denoising score matching with Langevin dynamics.
Proposed epsilon-prediction parameterization for reverse process, improving sample quality.
Achieved state-of-the-art FID score of 3.17 on unconditional CIFAR10.
Demonstrated progressive lossy decompression scheme generalizing autoregressive decoding.
Showed diffusion models as lossy compressors with inductive bias for imperceptible details.
Provided open-source implementation for reproducibility.
limits: Log-likelihoods not competitive with other likelihood-based models.
Sample quality limited to image data; other modalities not explored.
Training on simplified objective yields better samples but worse codelengths.
Reverse process variances fixed as constants, limiting expressiveness.
Potential for malicious use in generating fake images or reinforcing biases.

papers.tEn: Unsupervised Learning of Visual Features by Contrasting Cluster Assignments
papers.tZh: 通过对比聚类分配进行视觉特征的无监督学习
papers.sEn: SwAV achieves unsupervised learning by contrasting cluster assignments instead of pairwise features, enabling efficient scaling and strong performance.
contrib: Proposes SwAV, an online clustering algorithm that avoids explicit pairwise feature comparisons.
Introduces a swapped prediction mechanism that predicts cluster assignments across different views.
Develops multi-crop augmentation strategy using mixed-resolution views without extra memory or compute.
Achieves 75.3% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet with ResNet-50, surpassing supervised pretraining on transfer tasks.
Demonstrates online clustering scales to large datasets and works with small batches.
Shows multi-crop consistently improves multiple self-supervised methods by 2-4% top-1 accuracy.
limits: SwAV requires additional Sinkhorn-Knopp iterations for code computation, adding overhead.
Multi-crop may not benefit supervised models and requires careful tuning of crop sizes.
Method assumes equipartition of prototypes in each batch, which may fail for very small batches.
Performance depends on number of prototypes and temperature parameter, requiring tuning.
Online clustering may not converge as stably as offline methods on extremely noisy data.

papers.tEn: Bootstrap your own latent: A new approach to self-supervised Learning
papers.tZh: 自举你的潜在表示：一种新的自监督学习方法
papers.sEn: BYOL achieves state-of-the-art self-supervised learning without negative pairs.
contrib: Introduces BYOL, a self-supervised learning method achieving state-of-the-art ImageNet linear evaluation without negative pairs.
Demonstrates BYOL outperforms prior art on semi-supervised and transfer benchmarks.
Shows BYOL is more robust to batch size and augmentation changes than contrastive methods.
Provides theoretical hypothesis on why BYOL avoids collapse via predictor and slow-moving target network.
Achieves 79.6% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet with a larger ResNet, narrowing gap to supervised learning.
Releases implementation and pretrained models on GitHub for reproducibility.
limits: BYOL still relies on handcrafted image augmentations specific to vision, limiting generalization to other modalities.
The method requires careful tuning of target decay rate and predictor architecture to avoid collapse.
Performance depends on large batch sizes and compute resources (e.g., 512 TPU v3 cores).
Theoretical understanding of collapse avoidance is incomplete; only empirical evidence is provided.
BYOL may replicate biases present in training datasets, raising dual-use concerns.

papers.tEn: The Scaling Hypothesis
papers.tZh: 规模假设
papers.sEn: Neural networks absorb data and compute, generalizing and becoming more Bayesian as problems get harder, manifesting new abilities even at trivial scale.
contrib: The scaling hypothesis posits that larger neural networks trained on more data and compute yield emergent capabilities without architectural changes.
GPT-3 demonstrates meta-learning and few-shot learning purely from next-token prediction on diverse text, without fine-tuning.
Scaling laws show predictable power-law improvements in loss with model size, data, and compute, with no saturation observed.
Blessings of scale: larger models exhibit better stability, generalization, and meta-learning, solving harder problems more easily.
The pretraining thesis argues that achieving human-level language prediction requires true understanding and reasoning.
GPT-3's agentic capabilities emerge from imitation learning on human-generated text, enabling role-playing and planning.
limits: Scaling may hit diminishing returns beyond current compute budgets, though curves have not bent yet.
GPT-3's performance is hampered by poor prompts, tokenization issues, and limited context windows.
The scaling hypothesis is contested; many researchers believe better algorithms are needed for AGI.
Large models are extremely expensive to train and deploy, raising questions of economic feasibility.
The pretraining thesis is logically compelling but lacks empirical proof that scaling alone yields true intelligence.

papers.tEn: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
papers.tZh: 语言模型是少样本学习者
papers.sEn: Scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic few-shot performance, sometimes reaching competitiveness with prior fine-tuning approaches.
contrib: Demonstrates that scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic few-shot performance, sometimes matching fine-tuned models.
Trains GPT-3, a 175 billion parameter autoregressive model, and tests its few-shot, one-shot, and zero-shot performance on diverse NLP tasks.
Achieves strong results on translation, question-answering, cloze tasks, and on-the-fly reasoning tasks like arithmetic and word unscrambling.
Identifies tasks where few-shot learning struggles, such as natural language inference and some reading comprehension datasets.
Finds that GPT-3 can generate news articles indistinguishable from human-written ones by human evaluators.
Shows smooth scaling of performance with model size across most tasks, with larger models benefiting more from in-context learning.
limits: Few-shot performance on natural language inference tasks like ANLI remains near random chance even for GPT-3.
GPT-3 struggles with tasks requiring comparing two sentences, such as WiC, RTE, and CB in SuperGLUE.
Data contamination from training on web corpora may inflate results on some datasets, though impact is minimal overall.
GPT-3's performance on reading comprehension datasets like RACE and QuAC is weak, far behind state-of-the-art fine-tuned models.
The model requires large computational resources for training and inference, limiting accessibility and reproducibility.

papers.tEn: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
papers.tZh: 语言模型是少样本学习者
papers.sEn: Scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic few-shot performance, sometimes reaching competitiveness with prior fine-tuning approaches.
contrib: Demonstrates that scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic few-shot performance, sometimes matching fine-tuned models.
Trains GPT-3, a 175 billion parameter autoregressive model, and tests its few-shot, one-shot, and zero-shot performance on diverse NLP tasks.
Achieves strong results on translation, question-answering, cloze tasks, and on-the-fly reasoning tasks like arithmetic and word unscrambling.
Identifies tasks where few-shot learning struggles, such as natural language inference and some reading comprehension datasets.
Finds that GPT-3 can generate news articles indistinguishable from human-written ones by human evaluators.
Shows smooth scaling of performance with model size across most tasks, with larger models benefiting more from in-context learning.
limits: Few-shot performance on natural language inference tasks like ANLI remains near random chance even for GPT-3.
GPT-3 struggles with tasks requiring comparing two sentences, such as WiC, RTE, and CB in SuperGLUE.
Data contamination from training on web corpora may inflate results on some datasets, though impact is minimal overall.
GPT-3's performance on reading comprehension datasets like RACE and QuAC is weak, far behind state-of-the-art fine-tuned models.
The model requires large computational resources for training and inference, limiting accessibility and reproducibility.

papers.tEn: End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers
papers.tZh: 端到端目标检测与 Transformer
papers.sEn: DETR simplifies object detection by treating it as a direct set prediction problem, eliminating hand-designed components like NMS and anchor generation.
contrib: Proposes DETR, a transformer-based end-to-end object detector that treats detection as a direct set prediction problem.
Eliminates hand-designed components like non-maximum suppression and anchor generation via bipartite matching loss.
Achieves competitive accuracy and runtime on COCO compared to Faster R-CNN, with superior performance on large objects.
Extends naturally to panoptic segmentation with a unified mask head, outperforming strong baselines.
Provides a simple and flexible architecture that can be implemented with standard CNN and transformer libraries.
limits: Requires extra-long training schedule (300-500 epochs) and auxiliary losses for convergence.
Performs worse on small objects compared to Faster R-CNN, especially without dilated backbone.
Inference speed is slower than some optimized detectors due to transformer self-attention cost.
Fixed number of object queries limits maximum detections per image, potentially missing many objects.

papers.tEn: Conformer: Convolution-augmented Transformer for Speech Recognition
papers.tZh: Conformer: 用于语音识别的卷积增强 Transformer
papers.sEn: Conformer combines CNNs and Transformers to capture both local and global dependencies, achieving state-of-the-art speech recognition results.
contrib: Proposes Conformer, combining convolution and Transformer for speech recognition.
Achieves state-of-the-art WER of 1.9%/3.9% on LibriSpeech test/testother.
Introduces a sandwich structure with two feed-forward modules around attention and convolution.
Demonstrates convolution module is critical for performance via ablation studies.
Shows parameter efficiency: 10M model achieves competitive 2.7%/6.3% WER.
Studies effects of attention heads, kernel size, activation, and module placement.
limits: Evaluation only on LibriSpeech; generalizability to other datasets unverified.
Requires careful tuning of hyperparameters like kernel size and attention heads.
Performance with external language model may vary with LM quality.
Computational cost of depthwise convolution may limit deployment on resource-constrained devices.
Study limited to speech recognition; applicability to other domains not explored.

papers.tEn: Jukebox: A Generative Model for Music
papers.tZh: Jukebox：一种生成音乐的生成模型
papers.sEn: Jukebox generates music with singing in raw audio using multi-scale VQ-VAE and autoregressive Transformers.
contrib: Introduces Jukebox, a generative model for music with singing in raw audio domain.
Uses multi-scale VQ-VAE to compress raw audio into discrete codes.
Models compressed codes with autoregressive Transformers for long-range coherence.
Enables conditioning on artist, genre, and unaligned lyrics for controllable generation.
Demonstrates high-fidelity and diverse song generation with coherence up to multiple minutes.
Releases model weights, code, and thousands of samples for reproducibility.
limits: Generated songs lack traditional large-scale musical structures like repeating choruses.
Audio quality suffers from noise and scratchiness at small time scales.
Model trained only on English-language songs, limiting language and style diversity.
Slow sampling and upsampling process (hours per minute of audio).
Lyrics alignment remains imperfect for fast-paced genres like hip-hop.

papers.tEn: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
papers.tZh: Longformer: 长文档 Transformer
papers.sEn: Longformer introduces a linear-scaling attention mechanism for processing long documents, achieving state-of-the-art results on multiple tasks.
contrib: Introduces Longformer with linear-scaling attention for long documents.
Combines local windowed attention with task-specific global attention.
Achieves state-of-the-art on text8 and enwik8 character-level language modeling.
Pretrains Longformer and fine-tunes on downstream tasks, outperforming RoBERTa on long documents.
Sets new state-of-the-art on WikiHop and TriviaQA.
Introduces Longformer-Encoder-Decoder (LED) for long-document seq2seq tasks.
limits: Attention pattern requires task-specific global attention configuration.
Pretraining from RoBERTa checkpoint may limit adaptation to new patterns.
Dilated attention not compatible with pretrained RoBERTa weights.
Performance on short documents similar to baselines, limited gain.
Custom CUDA kernel implementation complexity for dilated attention.

papers.tEn: ELECTRA: Pre-training Text Encoders as Discriminators Rather Than Generators
papers.tZh: ELECTRA：将文本编码器预训练为判别器而非生成器
papers.sEn: ELECTRA proposes a more sample-efficient pre-training task called replaced token detection, outperforming BERT and matching RoBERTa/XLNet with less compute.
contrib: Proposes replaced token detection, a more sample-efficient pre-training task than masked language modeling.
Trains a discriminative model on all input tokens, not just a masked subset, improving compute efficiency.
Demonstrates ELECTRA outperforms BERT, GPT, RoBERTa, and XLNet under same compute or model size.
Shows strong gains for small models, e.g., ELECTRA-Small beats GPT on GLUE with 30x less compute.
Achieves state-of-the-art on SQuAD 2.0 with ELECTRA-Large while using less compute than prior methods.
Introduces weight sharing and smaller generators to further improve efficiency and performance.
limits: Evaluation limited to English text; multilingual applicability not explored.
Generator trained with maximum likelihood, not adversarially, limiting potential gains.
Two-stage training and adversarial training underperform joint training, showing limited improvement.
Large-scale comparisons not fully apples-to-apples due to different training data and hyperparameters.
Parameter efficiency not fully explained; more analysis needed for complete understanding.

papers.tEn: Benchmarking Graph Neural Networks
papers.tZh: 图神经网络基准测试
papers.sEn: We present an updated benchmark for graph neural networks with a new molecular dataset and demonstrate its utility in exploring positional encoding.
contrib: Released an open-source GNN benchmarking framework with diverse datasets, fair comparison protocols, and modular code.
Added AQSOL, a medium-sized molecular dataset with real-world experimental solubility targets.
Demonstrated the framework's utility by studying graph positional encoding, spurring further research.
Enabled fair model comparison with fixed parameter budgets of 100k and 500k.
Provided 12 datasets covering graph, node, and edge-level tasks from diverse domains.
Facilitated reproducible research with standardized training and evaluation pipelines.
limits: Medium-scale datasets may not capture challenges of very large graphs.
Fixed parameter budgets limit exploration of optimal hyperparameters for each model.
WL-GNNs face scalability issues due to O(n^2)/O(n^3) complexity.
Benchmark does not cover dynamic or temporal graph tasks.
Results may not generalize to domains outside those represented in datasets.

papers.tEn: GLU Variants Improve Transformer
papers.tZh: GLU 变体改进 Transformer
papers.sEn: Variants of Gated Linear Units improve Transformer quality over ReLU or GELU.
contrib: Proposes GLU variants (GEGLU, SwiGLU) for Transformer FFN layers.
Shows GLU variants improve perplexity on denoising pre-training objective.
Demonstrates better downstream task performance on GLUE and SuperGLUE.
Maintains parameter count by reducing hidden size by 2/3 for three-matrix layers.
Finds no dropout during pre-training yields superior results.
Provides simple implementation with no computational drawbacks.
limits: Only tested on encoder-decoder Transformer with T5-style pre-training.
No theoretical explanation for why GLU variants improve performance.
Fine-tuning done on a single mixture of tasks, not per-task.
Results may not generalize to other architectures or training setups.
Limited to feed-forward sublayers; other Transformer components unchanged.

papers.tEn: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
papers.tZh: 神经语言模型的缩放定律
papers.sEn: Language model performance scales as a power-law with model size, dataset size, and compute, enabling optimal compute-efficient training with very large models on modest data.
contrib: Language model cross-entropy loss follows power-law scaling with model size, dataset size, and compute over seven orders of magnitude.
Optimal compute-efficient training uses very large models trained on modest data, stopping before convergence.
Performance depends weakly on architectural details like depth or width compared to scale factors.
Overfitting and training speed are governed by simple equations relating model size and dataset size.
Larger models are more sample-efficient, requiring fewer data points to reach the same loss.
The critical batch size for training follows a power-law in the loss, independent of model size.
limits: Scaling laws may break down at extreme scales due to non-zero entropy of natural language.
Results are based on Transformer architecture; may not generalize to other architectures.
The study uses a single dataset (WebText2); transfer to other distributions incurs a constant loss penalty.
Optimal compute allocation assumes fixed batch size and may not hold for varying hardware constraints.
The power-law fits are empirical and lack a theoretical derivation from first principles.

papers.tEn: Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt
papers.tZh: 深度双重下降：更大的模型和更多的数据反而有害
papers.sEn: Double descent shows that increasing model size or training epochs can first hurt then help performance, and more data can sometimes worsen test results.
contrib: Identifies double descent in modern deep learning tasks as model size increases.
Shows epoch-wise double descent where test error peaks then drops with training time.
Defines Effective Model Complexity (EMC) to unify model-wise and epoch-wise double descent.
Demonstrates that increasing training samples can hurt test performance in critical regimes.
Provides extensive empirical validation across architectures, datasets, and optimizers.
Reconciles classical bias-variance trade-off with modern overparameterized deep learning.
limits: Double descent is most pronounced with label noise; less clear in noiseless settings.
Effective Model Complexity is defined heuristically with no principled choice of epsilon.
Theoretical understanding of double descent in deep networks remains incomplete.
Optimal early stopping may mitigate double descent, but its interaction is not fully explored.
Results are empirical; formal specification of 'sufficiently smaller/larger' is lacking.

papers.tEn: Analyzing and Improving the Image Quality of StyleGAN
papers.tZh: 分析并提升 StyleGAN 的图像质量
papers.sEn: We analyze artifacts in StyleGAN and propose improvements to generator normalization, progressive growing, and regularization, achieving state-of-the-art unconditional image quality.
contrib: Redesigns generator normalization to remove droplet artifacts via weight demodulation.
Introduces path length regularizer to encourage smooth latent-to-image mapping, improving quality and invertibility.
Replaces progressive growing with skip generator and residual discriminator, eliminating related artifacts.
Identifies capacity issue in high-resolution layers and increases feature maps to improve detail.
Proposes lazy regularization to reduce computational cost of regularizers without harming effectiveness.
Demonstrates improved source attribution via latent space projection with StyleGAN2.
limits: Path length regularizer introduces tradeoff between FID and PPL on less structured datasets.
Demodulation relies on statistical assumptions about signal, not actual feature map contents.
FID and P&R metrics are biased towards texture over shape, potentially missing quality aspects.
Increased capacity leads to higher computational cost and training time.
Method still requires large datasets for training, limiting applicability in data-scarce scenarios.

papers.tEn: Dream to Control: Learning Behaviors by Latent Imagination
papers.tZh: 梦想控制：通过潜在想象学习行为
papers.sEn: Dreamer learns behaviors by imagining future trajectories in a learned world model, achieving state-of-the-art performance on visual control tasks.
contrib: Proposes Dreamer, a model-based RL agent that learns long-horizon behaviors purely by latent imagination in a compact latent space.
Introduces an actor-critic algorithm that propagates analytic gradients of multi-step value estimates through learned latent dynamics.
Demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on 20 visual control tasks, exceeding prior methods in data efficiency, computation time, and final score.
Shows that learning a value model in imagination makes the agent robust to the imagination horizon, enabling long-horizon tasks.
Compares representation learning objectives (pixel reconstruction, contrastive estimation, reward prediction) and finds pixel reconstruction most effective.
Validates Dreamer on discrete action tasks and early termination scenarios, showing broad applicability.
limits: Relies on a learned world model that may not generalize to unseen environments or high visual complexity.
Requires differentiable dynamics and reparameterized sampling, limiting applicability to discrete actions without straight-through gradients.
Performance depends on the quality of representation learning; pure reward prediction alone was insufficient.
Imagination horizon and value model hyperparameters may need tuning for different tasks.
Evaluation limited to simulated environments; real-world deployment may face additional challenges.

papers.tEn: Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model
papers.tZh: 通过规划掌握雅达利、围棋、国际象棋和将棋：基于学习模型的方法
papers.sEn: MuZero achieves superhuman performance in Atari, Go, chess, and shogi by combining tree-based search with a learned model, without knowing the environment dynamics.
contrib: Proposes MuZero, combining tree-based search with a learned model for planning without environment dynamics.
Achieves superhuman performance in Go, chess, shogi, and state-of-the-art on 57 Atari games.
Learns a model predicting reward, policy, and value function directly relevant to planning.
Introduces value-equivalent model learning without reconstructing observations or true state.
Demonstrates scalability of planning with learned model matching perfect model in Go.
Shows search-based policy improvement provides stronger learning signal than model-free Q-learning.
limits: Model is deterministic; extension to stochastic transitions left for future work.
Performance in Atari plateaus with search simulations, suggesting model inaccuracy.
Requires significant compute for training (1 million mini-batches, 800 simulations in board games).
Not directly applicable to imperfect information games like Poker.
Limited to environments with discrete actions and rewards; continuous domains not addressed.

papers.tEn: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning
papers.tZh: 动量对比：用于无监督视觉表示学习
papers.sEn: MoCo enables building a large and consistent dynamic dictionary for contrastive learning, achieving competitive results and even surpassing supervised pre-training in downstream tasks.
contrib: Proposes Momentum Contrast (MoCo) for unsupervised visual representation learning.
Builds a dynamic dictionary with a queue and a momentum-updated encoder for contrastive learning.
Achieves competitive results on ImageNet linear classification and outperforms supervised pre-training on 7 detection/segmentation tasks.
Introduces shuffled batch normalization to prevent cheating in contrastive learning.
Demonstrates that MoCo scales to billion-image datasets and closes the gap between unsupervised and supervised representation learning.
limits: MoCo's improvement from ImageNet to Instagram-1B is relatively small, suggesting limited exploitation of larger-scale data.
The pretext task is simple instance discrimination; more advanced pretext tasks may further improve performance.
MoCo lags behind supervised pre-training on VOC semantic segmentation, indicating task-specific limitations.
The method requires careful tuning of momentum coefficient and dictionary size for optimal performance.

papers.tEn: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
papers.tZh: 探索迁移学习的极限：基于统一的文本到文本转换器
papers.sEn: A unified text-to-text framework enables systematic study of transfer learning techniques, achieving state-of-the-art results on multiple NLP benchmarks.
contrib: Proposes a unified text-to-text framework for NLP transfer learning.
Systematically compares pre-training objectives, architectures, and data sets.
Introduces the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus (C4) for pre-training.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple NLP benchmarks via scaling.
Releases pre-trained models, code, and data to facilitate future research.
Explores architectural variants including encoder-decoder and prefix LM.
limits: Study limited to English-language tasks and benchmarks.
Pre-training only on English data; multilingual tasks require additional data.
Computational cost of large-scale experiments is high.
No combinatorial exploration of all factors due to cost.
Results may not generalize to non-text modalities or low-resource languages.

papers.tEn: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations
papers.tZh: ALBERT：一种用于语言表示自监督学习的轻量级 BERT
papers.sEn: ALBERT introduces parameter-reduction techniques to lower memory consumption and increase training speed, achieving state-of-the-art results with fewer parameters than BERT-large.
contrib: Proposes two parameter-reduction techniques: factorized embedding parameterization and cross-layer parameter sharing.
Introduces a self-supervised loss for sentence-order prediction (SOP) to model inter-sentence coherence.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on GLUE, SQuAD, and RACE benchmarks with fewer parameters than BERT-large.
Demonstrates that parameter sharing acts as regularization, stabilizing training and improving generalization.
Shows that dropout can hurt performance in large Transformer-based models, leading to its removal for better results.
limits: ALBERT-xxlarge is computationally more expensive than BERT-large due to larger structure.
The study is limited to English language and specific benchmarks (GLUE, SQuAD, RACE).
The proposed SOP loss may not capture all dimensions of discourse coherence.
The effect of removing dropout may not generalize to other Transformer architectures.

papers.tEn: Emergent Tool Use From Multi-Agent Autocurricula
papers.tZh: 多智能体自动课程中的涌现工具使用
papers.sEn: Multi-agent competition in hide-and-seek leads to emergent tool use and coordination through self-supervised autocurricula.
contrib: Demonstrates six emergent phases of strategy in hide-and-seek via multi-agent autocurricula.
Shows that multi-agent competition leads to sophisticated tool use and coordination.
Provides evidence that multi-agent autocurricula scale better with environment complexity than intrinsic motivation.
Proposes transfer learning and fine-tuning as a quantitative evaluation method for targeted capabilities.
Introduces a suite of domain-specific intelligence tests for evaluating agent capabilities.
Open-sources environments and code to encourage further research in physically grounded multi-agent autocurricula.
limits: Strategy space is inherently bounded and may not surpass six emergent modes.
Agents require enormous experience to progress through stages due to misaligned reward functions.
Transfer results are mixed due to entangled skill representations that are hard to fine-tune.
Agents exploit environment design inaccuracies, such as physics simulation flaws.
Sample complexity is high; reducing it is an important direction for future research.

papers.tEn: Once-for-All: Train One Network and Specialize it for Efficient Deployment
papers.tZh: 一次训练，处处可用：训练一个网络，专用于高效部署
papers.sEn: Train one network that supports diverse architectural settings and quickly specialize sub-networks for different devices without retraining.
contrib: Proposes once-for-all (OFA) network decoupling training and search for efficient deployment across many devices.
Introduces progressive shrinking algorithm to train OFA network supporting over 10^19 sub-networks.
Achieves state-of-the-art 80.0% ImageNet top-1 accuracy under mobile setting (<600M MACs).
Reduces GPU hours and CO2 emission by orders of magnitude compared to conventional NAS methods.
Outperforms SOTA NAS methods on diverse edge devices with up to 4.0% accuracy gain or 2.6x speedup.
Wins 3rd and 4th Low Power Computer Vision Challenge (LPCVC) in classification and detection tracks.
limits: OFA network training requires 1,200 GPU hours on V100 GPUs, a one-time cost.
Progressive shrinking algorithm may not generalize to non-CNN architectures like Transformers.
Accuracy predictor and latency lookup table require 16K sub-network samples for training.
OFA focuses on convolutional neural networks and may not apply to other model types.
The method assumes hardware cost models are available and accurate for each target platform.

papers.tEn: Deep High-Resolution Representation Learning for Visual Recognition
papers.tZh: 用于视觉识别的深度高分辨率表示学习
papers.sEn: HRNet maintains high-resolution representations throughout the process, achieving richer semantics and higher spatial precision.
contrib: Proposes HRNet that maintains high-resolution representations throughout the entire process via parallel multi-resolution convolutions.
Introduces repeated multi-resolution fusion to exchange information across parallel streams, enhancing semantic richness and spatial precision.
Demonstrates superior performance on human pose estimation, semantic segmentation, and object detection compared to state-of-the-art methods.
Provides two versions: HRNetV1 for pose estimation and HRNetV2 for segmentation, with HRNetV2p for detection, showing versatility.
Establishes connection between multi-resolution fusion and regular convolution, justifying exploration of all resolutions.
Achieves state-of-the-art results with comparable model size and lower computation complexity on multiple benchmarks.
limits: Memory cost during training for object detection is slightly larger than state-of-the-art methods.
Training time for pose estimation is a little larger on PyTorch, though comparable on MXNet with static graph.
Performance gain from HRNetV2 over HRNetV1 is minor for large models in Cityscapes segmentation.
The study does not explore resolutions higher than 1/4 of input, leaving potential for further improvement.
Combination with ASPP or PPM did not improve Cityscapes segmentation, limiting certain fusion strategies.

papers.tEn: On the Variance of the Adaptive Learning Rate and Beyond
papers.tZh: 自适应学习率的方差及其改进
papers.sEn: Warmup reduces early-stage variance of adaptive learning rates; RAdam rectifies this variance for better performance.
contrib: Identifies large variance of adaptive learning rate in early training as root cause of convergence issues.
Provides theoretical justification for warmup heuristic as variance reduction technique.
Proposes RAdam, a new Adam variant that rectifies adaptive learning rate variance.
Demonstrates RAdam's effectiveness and robustness across image classification, language modeling, and NMT.
Shows RAdam reduces sensitivity to learning rate and warmup length hyperparameters.
limits: Analysis assumes gradients are i.i.d. Gaussian with zero mean, which may not hold in practice.
Approximation of exponential moving average by simple moving average may introduce error.
First-order approximation of variance may be inaccurate for very small sample sizes.
RAdam's rectification term relies on hyperparameter β2, requiring tuning for optimal performance.

papers.tEn: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
papers.tZh: RoBERTa：一种稳健优化的 BERT 预训练方法
papers.sEn: RoBERTa shows that BERT was significantly undertrained and achieves state-of-the-art results by carefully optimizing hyperparameters and training data size.
contrib: Shows BERT was significantly undertrained and proposes RoBERTa with improved training recipe.
Demonstrates that removing the next sentence prediction objective matches or improves performance.
Introduces dynamic masking, large mini-batches, and byte-level BPE for better pretraining.
Collects CC-News dataset and shows more data improves downstream task performance.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on GLUE, RACE, and SQuAD without multi-task finetuning.
Releases models and code for pretraining and finetuning.
limits: Study focuses on BERT architecture; architectural changes not explored.
Results may not generalize to other pretraining objectives or model sizes.
Data size and diversity effects are conflated; not disentangled.
Large batch training limits not fully explored; further scaling possible.
Comparison with other methods may be affected by hyperparameter tuning differences.

papers.tEn: Generative Modeling by Estimating Gradients of the Data Distribution
papers.tZh: 通过估计数据分布的梯度进行生成建模
papers.sEn: We propose a generative model using Langevin dynamics with score matching, achieving state-of-the-art results on CIFAR-10.
contrib: Proposes score-based generative modeling using Langevin dynamics with score matching.
Introduces Noise Conditional Score Networks (NCSN) to estimate scores at multiple noise levels.
Develops annealed Langevin dynamics for sampling, gradually reducing noise levels.
Achieves state-of-the-art inception score of 8.87 on CIFAR-10 for unconditional generation.
Demonstrates effective image inpainting without specialized architectures.
Provides a tractable objective for principled model comparisons.
limits: Requires multiple noise levels and annealed sampling, increasing computational cost.
Score estimation may be inaccurate in low-density regions despite noise perturbation.
Langevin dynamics mixing can be slow for highly multimodal distributions.
Model performance depends on careful tuning of noise levels and step sizes.
Primarily evaluated on image data; generalization to other domains is not explored.

papers.tEn: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining for Language Understanding
papers.tZh: XLNet：面向语言理解的广义自回归预训练
papers.sEn: XLNet outperforms BERT on 20 tasks by learning bidirectional contexts via permutation language modeling and integrating Transformer-XL.
contrib: Proposes XLNet, a generalized autoregressive pretraining method that learns bidirectional contexts via permutation language modeling.
Overcomes BERT's pretrain-finetune discrepancy by avoiding input corruption with masks.
Integrates Transformer-XL's segment recurrence and relative encoding for improved long-text handling.
Introduces two-stream self-attention to resolve target prediction ambiguity in permutation modeling.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on 20 NLP tasks, including QA, NLI, sentiment analysis, and document ranking.
Demonstrates that permutation LM and Transformer-XL both contribute to XLNet's superiority over BERT.
limits: Permutation language modeling increases optimization difficulty, requiring partial prediction for convergence.
XLNet's performance gain is partly due to more training data and compute, not solely the objective.
The two-stream attention mechanism adds architectural complexity and memory overhead.
Ablation shows next-sentence prediction does not consistently improve XLNet, unlike BERT.
XLNet's reliance on Transformer-XL may limit applicability to tasks with very short sequences.

papers.tEn: COMET: Commonsense Transformers for Automatic Knowledge Graph Construction
papers.tZh: COMET：用于自动知识图谱构建的常识变换器
papers.sEn: Generative models can automatically construct commonsense knowledge graphs with near-human precision.
contrib: Proposes COMET, a generative model for commonsense knowledge base construction using pre-trained transformers.
Achieves 77.5% and 91.7% top-1 precision on ATOMIC and ConceptNet, approaching human performance.
Demonstrates transfer of implicit knowledge from pre-trained language models to explicit commonsense generation.
Shows high novelty and diversity in generated knowledge, with over 75% novel tuples having significant edit distance from training data.
Provides a framework adaptable to different commonsense knowledge bases and relation types.
Conducts comprehensive human evaluation and ablation studies validating model effectiveness.
limits: Novel generations sometimes simplify training tuples, e.g., 'doctor CapableOf save life' vs 'save person life'.
Performance drops significantly with only 1% training data, indicating data dependency.
Model may produce incorrect commonsense due to ambiguous word senses, e.g., 'dove SymbolOf submarine'.
Evaluation limited to English; applicability to other languages is unexplored.
Requires seed knowledge tuples; cannot generate from scratch without existing KB.

papers.tEn: FastSpeech: Fast, Robust and Controllable Text to Speech
papers.tZh: FastSpeech: 快速、鲁棒且可控的文本到语音合成
papers.sEn: FastSpeech achieves 270x speedup in mel-spectrogram generation and 38x in end-to-end speech synthesis while maintaining quality and robustness.
contrib: Proposes FastSpeech, a feed-forward Transformer for parallel mel-spectrogram generation in TTS.
Introduces a length regulator with phoneme duration prediction for robust alignment.
Achieves 270x speedup in mel-spectrogram generation and 38x in end-to-end synthesis.
Nearly eliminates word skipping and repeating issues in hard cases.
Enables smooth voice speed control from 0.5x to 1.5x.
Uses sequence-level knowledge distillation to improve speech quality.
limits: Speech quality only matches, not surpasses, autoregressive models.
Requires a pre-trained autoregressive teacher model for duration extraction.
Limited to single-speaker LJSpeech dataset; multi-speaker not tested.
Prosody control is limited to adjusting breaks between words.
Dependence on external vocoder (WaveGlow) for final audio synthesis.

papers.tEn: A Recipe for Training Neural Networks
papers.tZh: 训练神经网络的秘诀
papers.sEn: A recipe to avoid common neural net mistakes by following a systematic training process.
contrib: Proposes a systematic, iterative recipe for training neural networks, emphasizing debugging and verification rather than ad-hoc tuning.
Stresses thorough data inspection before writing any model code, treating the dataset as the ultimate source of truth.
Recommends building a reliable training and evaluation skeleton with fixed seeds, simple baselines, and loss/accuracy sanity checks.
Advocates overfitting a single batch to verify pipeline correctness before scaling up model complexity.
Introduces a two-stage development strategy: first make a large model overfit, then regularize to improve validation performance.
Shares practical tips such as Adam for early baselines, random search, ensembles, and letting models train for longer.
limits: Based on personal anecdotal experience rather than systematic empirical study; findings may not generalize across all domains.
Focuses mainly on supervised computer vision with small-scale CNNs, offering limited guidance for modern pre-training, NLP, or RL.
Advice such as “don't be a hero” and “Adam is safe” may be too simplistic or outdated in current deep learning practice.
Provides no theoretical guarantees; success relies heavily on human patience, visual intuition, and manual inspection.
Assumes a single-model training pipeline and does not address distributed training, large-scale compute, or complex agentic systems.

papers.tEn: Generating Long Sequences with Sparse Transformers
papers.tZh: 利用稀疏 Transformer 生成长序列
papers.sEn: Sparse Transformers reduce attention complexity to O(n√n), enabling modeling of sequences up to tens of thousands of timesteps with hundreds of layers.
contrib: Introduced sparse factorizations of the attention matrix reducing complexity to O(n√n).
Proposed architectural and initialization changes to train deeper networks.
Introduced recomputation of attention matrices to save memory during training.
Developed fast GPU kernels for sparse attention operations.
Achieved state-of-the-art density modeling on Enwik8, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet-64.
Demonstrated self-attention can model sequences of length one million or more.
limits: Sparse patterns may not capture all data-dependent attention patterns.
Performance degrades for very long sequences due to reduced model capacity.
Fixed attention patterns require careful hyperparameter tuning for different data types.
Strided attention fails on data without periodic structure like text.
Training very deep networks still requires careful initialization and architecture modifications.

papers.tEn: The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration
papers.tZh: 神经文本退化的奇特案例
papers.sEn: Decoding strategies significantly affect machine text quality, and Nucleus Sampling improves diversity and fluency.
contrib: Reveals surprising distributional differences between human and machine text.
Finds that decoding strategies alone dramatically affect machine text quality.
Proposes Nucleus Sampling, a simple and effective decoding method.
Shows maximization-based decoding leads to bland, repetitive text.
Demonstrates that Nucleus Sampling yields diverse and coherent text.
Uses HUSE evaluation to show Nucleus Sampling as the best decoding strategy.
limits: Focuses on open-ended generation, not directed tasks like translation.
Experiments limited to GPT-2 Large model; may not generalize.
Nucleus Sampling requires tuning threshold p for optimal performance.
Does not address training-time solutions for text degeneration.
Human evaluation limited to 200 generations per method.

papers.tEn: On the Convergence of Adam and Beyond
papers.tZh: 论 Adam 及其变体的收敛性
papers.sEn: Adam and related algorithms may fail to converge due to exponential moving averages; adding long-term memory of past gradients fixes the issue.
contrib: Identifies that exponential moving average in Adam and RMSprop causes non-convergence in convex optimization.
Provides explicit convex example where Adam fails to converge to optimal solution.
Proposes AMSGrad algorithm with long-term memory of past gradients to fix convergence issues.
Proves regret bound for AMSGrad in convex setting, similar to Adagrad.
Shows that any constant β1, β2 with β1 < √β2 leads to non-convergence for Adam.
Empirically demonstrates AMSGrad outperforms Adam on logistic regression and neural networks.
limits: Non-convergence examples are carefully constructed and may not reflect typical practical scenarios.
Theoretical analysis focuses on convex settings; non-convex convergence is not guaranteed.
AMSGrad requires tuning of hyperparameters like β1 and β2, similar to Adam.
Empirical evaluation is limited to MNIST and CIFAR-10; broader benchmarks are needed.
Proposed fixes increase memory slightly due to storing maximum of past squared gradients.

papers.tEn: Large Batch Optimization for Deep Learning: Training BERT in 76 minutes
papers.tZh: 大规模批量优化用于深度学习：76 分钟训练 BERT
papers.sEn: LAMB optimizer enables BERT training in 76 minutes with large batch sizes up to 32868.
contrib: Proposes LAMB optimizer with layerwise adaptive learning rates for large-batch training.
Provides convergence analysis for LAMB and LARS in nonconvex settings.
Reduces BERT training time from 3 days to 76 minutes using batch size up to 64K.
Demonstrates LAMB achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on ResNet-50 with large batches.
Shows LAMB outperforms LARS and AdamW on BERT and ResNet-50 tasks.
Introduces mixed-batch training with re-warm-up for stable large-batch optimization.
limits: Convergence analysis assumes bounded gradients and smoothness per layer.
Empirical results limited to BERT and ResNet-50; generalizability to other models unverified.
LAMB requires minimal tuning but optimal hyperparameters may vary across tasks.
Large batch training requires significant hardware resources like TPUv3 Pod.
Theoretical analysis simplified with β1=0 and λ=0; general case not fully covered.

papers.tEn: Semantic Image Synthesis with Spatially-Adaptive Normalization
papers.tZh: 语义图像合成与空间自适应归一化
papers.sEn: We propose spatially-adaptive normalization for photorealistic image synthesis from semantic layouts, outperforming previous methods in visual fidelity and layout alignment.
contrib: Proposes spatially-adaptive normalization (SPADE) to preserve semantic information in normalization layers.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on COCO-Stuff, ADE20K, and Cityscapes datasets.
Enables multi-modal synthesis by using random noise as generator input.
Supports style-guided image synthesis via an image encoder.
Simplifies generator architecture by removing encoder, reducing parameters.
Demonstrates that SPADE outperforms feature concatenation for semantic conditioning.
limits: Requires paired segmentation masks and images for training.
Performance depends on quality of input segmentation masks.
Multi-modal synthesis limited by diversity of training data.
Computationally expensive due to multi-scale discriminators and spectral normalization.
Style transfer may not generalize to unseen styles outside training distribution.

papers.tEn: The Bitter Lesson
papers.tZh: 苦涩的教训
papers.sEn: The key lesson from 70 years of AI research is that general methods leveraging computation are ultimately most effective, due to Moore's law and the exponential decrease in computation cost.
contrib: General methods leveraging computation are ultimately the most effective in AI, by a large margin.
Search and learning are the two key techniques that scale with increased computation.
Human-knowledge-based approaches often plateau and inhibit long-term progress.
Breakthrough progress in AI comes from scaling computation via search and learning, not from encoding human knowledge.
The actual contents of minds are irredeemably complex; we should build meta-methods that discover complexity.
Examples from chess, Go, speech recognition, and computer vision confirm the bitter lesson.
limits: The lesson may not apply to domains with extremely limited computation or no clear scaling path.
Human knowledge can still be valuable in the short term or for specific narrow tasks.
The approach may overlook the importance of data quality and algorithmic innovation beyond scaling.
It does not address ethical or safety concerns that arise from purely computation-driven AI.
The historical examples may not fully represent future AI paradigms like AGI or superintelligence.

papers.tEn: Deep High-Resolution Representation Learning for Human Pose Estimation
papers.tZh: 深度高分辨率表示学习用于人体姿态估计
papers.sEn: Our network maintains high-resolution representations throughout the whole process, leading to more accurate keypoint heatmaps.
contrib: Proposes High-Resolution Net (HRNet) that maintains high-resolution representations throughout the whole process.
Connects high-to-low resolution subnetworks in parallel instead of series, enabling spatially precise heatmap prediction.
Introduces repeated multi-scale fusion across parallel subnetworks to enrich high-resolution representations.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on COCO keypoint detection, MPII Human Pose, and PoseTrack datasets.
Demonstrates superior efficiency with lower computational cost and model size compared to prior methods.
Validates effectiveness through ablation studies on multi-scale fusion and resolution maintenance.
limits: Focuses on single-person pose estimation; multi-person scenarios rely on external person detectors.
Performance on MPII dataset saturates; larger model does not improve results.
Requires careful tuning of network depth and width for different tasks.
Multi-scale fusion increases memory and computation during training.
Evaluation limited to human pose estimation; generalization to other dense prediction tasks not fully explored.

papers.tEn: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context
papers.tZh: Transformer-XL：超越固定长度上下文的注意力语言模型
papers.sEn: Transformer-XL enables learning longer-term dependency beyond fixed-length context with segment-level recurrence and novel positional encoding.
contrib: Proposes Transformer-XL with segment-level recurrence for long-term dependency learning.
Introduces a novel relative positional encoding scheme enabling state reuse.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on five language modeling benchmarks.
Resolves context fragmentation problem, improving performance on short sequences.
Demonstrates up to 1,800+ times faster evaluation than vanilla Transformers.
Generates coherent long text articles with thousands of tokens.
limits: Recurrence mechanism requires additional memory for caching hidden states.
Training still uses fixed-length segments, limiting theoretical context length.
Relative positional encoding may not generalize to extremely long sequences.
Performance on small datasets relies on regularization techniques.
Evaluation speed advantage diminishes with very large memory sizes.

papers.tEn: An Empirical Model of Large-Batch Training
papers.tZh: 大规模批量训练的实证模型
papers.sEn: A simple statistic called the gradient noise scale predicts the largest useful batch size across many domains.
contrib: Proposes gradient noise scale as a simple statistic to predict the largest useful batch size across diverse domains.
Derives a theoretical framework linking noise scale to the compute-time tradeoff curve in large-batch training.
Empirically validates predictions across 8 tasks including supervised learning, RL, and generative models.
Shows noise scale increases during training and is larger for complex tasks, with weak dependence on model size.
Provides a practical method to measure noise scale with minimal overhead in data-parallel training.
Demonstrates efficiency gains from adaptive batch-size training based on noise scale.
limits: Theory relies on local quadratic approximation and may not capture global optimization dynamics.
Noise scale prediction accuracy varies across tasks; ratio to critical batch size can differ by an order of magnitude.
Assumes optimal learning rate tuning; noise scale depends on learning rate via training temperature.
Does not address generalization gap; focuses solely on training loss optimization.
Empirical validation limited to specific architectures and optimizers; may not generalize to all settings.

papers.tEn: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.tZh: 一种基于风格的生成对抗网络生成器架构
papers.sEn: A style-based generator architecture for GANs enables unsupervised separation of high-level attributes and stochastic variation, improving quality and disentanglement.
contrib: Proposes a style-based generator architecture for GANs, enabling unsupervised separation of high-level attributes and stochastic variation.
Introduces an intermediate latent space that improves disentanglement and linearity of factors of variation.
Achieves state-of-the-art FID scores on CelebA-HQ and FFHQ datasets, improving by nearly 20%.
Develops two new automated metrics—perceptual path length and linear separability—for quantifying interpolation quality and disentanglement.
Introduces the FFHQ dataset, a high-quality human face dataset with 70,000 images at 1024x1024 resolution.
Demonstrates scale-specific control of image synthesis through style mixing and noise injection.
limits: The method does not modify the discriminator or loss function, limiting potential improvements from those components.
The proposed metrics rely on pre-trained classifiers and perceptual distances, which may introduce bias.
The truncation trick reduces variation in generated images, limiting diversity.
The approach is evaluated only on face and scene datasets; generalization to other domains is not verified.
The mapping network requires careful tuning of learning rates to avoid training instability.

papers.tEn: Supervising strong learners by amplifying weak experts
papers.tZh: 通过增强弱专家来监督强学习者
papers.sEn: Iterated Amplification trains complex behaviors by combining solutions to easier subproblems without an external reward function.
contrib: Proposes Iterated Amplification, a training strategy that builds training signals by combining solutions to easier subproblems without an external reward function.
Demonstrates that Iterated Amplification can efficiently learn complex behaviors in algorithmic environments, achieving performance close to supervised learning with ground truth.
Shows that Iterated Amplification requires orders of magnitude fewer expert demonstrations than direct supervised learning, reducing sample complexity.
Introduces a human predictor model to reduce the burden on human experts, enabling scalable training with non-stationary distributions.
