Method does not use morphological segmentation, potentially missing some linguistic structures.

papers.tEn: Convolutional Neural Networks on Graphs with Fast Localized Spectral Filtering
papers.tZh: 基于快速局部谱滤波的图卷积神经网络
papers.sEn: We generalize CNNs to graphs using spectral graph theory, achieving linear complexity and universal applicability.
contrib: Proposes a spectral graph CNN formulation using Chebyshev polynomials for fast localized filtering.
Achieves linear computational complexity O(K|E|) and constant learning complexity O(K) like classical CNNs.
Introduces an efficient graph pooling strategy via balanced binary tree rearrangement.
Demonstrates strict localization of spectral filters with K-hop support.
Shows competitive performance on MNIST and 20NEWS datasets.
Provides open-source TensorFlow code for reproducibility.
limits: Spectral filters are isotropic, lacking orientation sensitivity on grids.
Performance heavily depends on the quality of the input graph construction.
Fake nodes from coarsening increase dimensionality and computational cost.
Model not tested on large-scale graphs with millions of nodes.
Graph construction for text uses word2vec embeddings which may not be optimal.

papers.tEn: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
papers.tZh: 人工智能安全中的具体问题
papers.sEn: We identify five concrete research problems in AI safety: avoiding side effects, avoiding reward hacking, scalable supervision, safe exploration, and distributional shift.
contrib: Defines five concrete AI accident problems: negative side effects, reward hacking, scalable oversight, safe exploration, and distributional shift.
Categorizes accident sources: wrong objective function, expensive evaluation, and undesirable learning behavior.
Proposes practical research directions for each problem, including impact regularizers and adversarial reward functions.
Highlights the increasing relevance of safety research due to trends in deep RL, complex agents, and autonomy.
Introduces semi-supervised RL as a scalable oversight method to reduce reliance on expensive reward evaluations.
Emphasizes the need for robust exploration strategies to avoid catastrophic failures in real-world RL systems.
limits: Focuses on technical problems, omitting broader societal, ethical, and policy implications of AI safety.
Proposed solutions like impact regularizers are preliminary and lack empirical validation on complex tasks.
Assumes RL and supervised learning paradigms, limiting applicability to other AI approaches like unsupervised learning.
Does not address adversarial attacks or security vulnerabilities beyond reward hacking and side effects.
Scalable oversight methods like semi-supervised RL may not scale to highly complex or long-horizon tasks.

papers.tEn: Matching Networks for One Shot Learning
papers.tZh: 匹配网络用于单样本学习
papers.sEn: A novel framework combining metric learning with external memories achieves state-of-the-art one-shot learning on vision and language tasks.
contrib: Proposes Matching Networks, a neural architecture combining metric learning with external memory for one-shot learning.
Introduces a training procedure that matches test conditions by sampling episodes from label sets, enabling meta-learning.
Achieves state-of-the-art one-shot accuracy on Omniglot (93.8%) and ImageNet (93.2%), outperforming baselines.
Defines new one-shot benchmarks on ImageNet, miniImageNet, and a language modeling task on Penn Treebank.
Demonstrates that non-parametric attention mechanisms allow rapid adaptation to new classes without fine-tuning.
Shows that Full Contextual Embeddings (FCE) improve performance by encoding support set context.
limits: Computational cost grows linearly with support set size, limiting scalability to large sets.
Performance degrades on fine-grained classification tasks like ImageNet dogs subset due to label bias.
Model assumes support set classes are disjoint from training classes; fails if distributions diverge.
Language modeling results (32-38% accuracy) are far below oracle LSTM, indicating limited one-shot capability in NLP.
Requires careful episode sampling during training to match test distribution, limiting generalization.

papers.tEn: DeepLab: Semantic Image Segmentation with Deep Convolutional Nets, Atrous Convolution, and Fully Connected CRFs
papers.tZh: DeepLab：基于深度卷积网络、空洞卷积和全连接条件随机场的语义图像分割
papers.sEn: DeepLab combines atrous convolution, ASPP, and fully connected CRFs to achieve state-of-the-art semantic segmentation.
contrib: Proposed atrous convolution for dense feature extraction in DCNNs, controlling resolution without increasing parameters.
Introduced Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) to robustly segment objects at multiple scales.
Combined DCNN with fully connected CRF to improve object boundary localization.
Achieved state-of-the-art results on PASCAL VOC 2012, PASCAL-Context, PASCAL-Person-Part, and Cityscapes.
Demonstrated that atrous convolution enlarges filter field-of-view without extra computation.
Showed that CRF post-processing refines segmentation boundaries and removes false positives.
limits: CRF used as post-processing, not jointly trained with DCNN, limiting end-to-end optimization.
Method fails on fine object boundaries like bicycles and chairs due to low unary confidence.
High-resolution images require splitting into overlapped regions due to GPU memory limits.
Multiscale processing increases computation cost by processing multiple image scales.
Model relies on pre-trained ImageNet classifiers, which may not generalize to all domains.

papers.tEn: Perceptual Losses for Real-Time Style Transfer and Super-Resolution
papers.tZh: 用于实时风格迁移和超分辨率的感知损失
papers.sEn: Perceptual loss functions enable feed-forward networks to achieve real-time style transfer and improved super-resolution quality.
contrib: Proposes perceptual loss functions for training feed-forward networks, combining per-pixel and perceptual losses.
Achieves real-time style transfer with quality comparable to optimization-based methods but three orders of magnitude faster.
Demonstrates that perceptual loss improves fine detail reconstruction in single-image super-resolution.
Uses a pretrained VGG-16 network as a fixed loss network to define feature and style reconstruction losses.
Shows that perceptual loss enables semantic knowledge transfer from the loss network to the transformation network.
limits: Perceptual loss may introduce cross-hatch artifacts in super-resolution, harming PSNR and SSIM.
Method requires a pretrained loss network, limiting applicability to tasks without suitable pretrained models.
Style transfer networks are trained per style, not generalizing to unseen styles without retraining.
Super-resolution results are evaluated qualitatively; quantitative metrics like PSNR are lower than per-pixel loss methods.
The method's performance depends on the choice of layers in the loss network, requiring manual tuning.

papers.tEn: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System
papers.tZh: XGBoost：一种可扩展的树提升系统
papers.sEn: XGBoost is a scalable tree boosting system that achieves state-of-the-art results on many machine learning challenges using novel sparsity-aware algorithms and efficient system optimizations.
contrib: Proposes XGBoost, a scalable end-to-end tree boosting system achieving state-of-the-art results on many ML challenges.
Introduces a novel sparsity-aware algorithm for handling sparse data efficiently.
Develops a theoretically justified weighted quantile sketch for approximate tree learning.
Provides insights on cache access patterns, data compression, and sharding to build a scalable system.
XGBoost scales beyond billions of examples using far fewer resources than existing systems.
Achieves over 10x speedup compared to popular solutions on a single machine.
limits: The weighted quantile sketch assumes second-order gradient statistics as weights, which may not be optimal for all loss functions.
Cache-aware prefetching is primarily beneficial for exact greedy algorithm on large datasets; approximate algorithms require careful block size tuning.
Out-of-core computation relies on disk I/O, which can become a bottleneck despite compression and sharding.
The system's performance may degrade on datasets with extremely high dimensionality due to column subsampling overhead.
The paper does not extensively compare with deep learning methods on non-tabular data like images or text.

papers.tEn: Weight Normalization: A Simple Reparameterization to Accelerate Training of Deep Neural Networks
papers.tZh: 权重归一化：一种加速深度神经网络训练的简单重参数化方法
papers.sEn: Weight normalization decouples weight vector length from direction, speeding up SGD convergence without batch dependencies.
contrib: Proposes weight normalization, a reparameterization decoupling weight vector length from direction to improve optimization conditioning.
Demonstrates faster convergence of stochastic gradient descent with weight normalization across supervised, generative, and reinforcement learning tasks.
Shows weight normalization works well with recurrent models like LSTMs and noise-sensitive applications where batch normalization fails.
Introduces mean-only batch normalization combined with weight normalization, achieving state-of-the-art CIFAR-10 test error without data augmentation.
Provides theoretical analysis showing weight normalization projects gradients away from current weight vector, reducing noise and stabilizing learning.
Offers a computationally cheap and deterministic alternative to batch normalization with lower overhead and no minibatch dependencies.
limits: Weight normalization does not fix feature scale across layers, requiring careful data-based initialization for optimal performance.
The method may not be applicable to models where data-based initialization is infeasible, such as recurrent networks without clear minibatch structure.
Empirical results show batch normalization achieves slightly better per-epoch progress early on, though weight normalization compensates with lower computational cost.
The analysis of gradient projection assumes no momentum or adaptive learning rates, which may not hold for modern optimizers like Adam.
Mean-only batch normalization combined with weight normalization introduces additional complexity and may not generalize to all architectures.

papers.tEn: Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations
papers.tZh: Visual Genome：利用众包密集图像标注连接语言与视觉
papers.sEn: We present Visual Genome, a dataset with over 100K images densely annotated with objects, attributes, and relationships to enable cognitive tasks like image description and question answering.
contrib: Introduces Visual Genome, a dataset with 108K images, each annotated with 21 objects, 18 attributes, and 18 relationships on average.
Provides dense region descriptions (42 per image) and 1.7M question-answer pairs, enabling cognitive tasks like reasoning.
Canonicalizes objects, attributes, and relationships to WordNet synsets, enabling consistent cross-image querying.
Constructs scene graphs that formally represent images, combining objects, attributes, and relationships into a structured graph.
Collects data via crowdsourcing with diversity enforcement using BLEU scores and verification via majority voting.
Achieves higher object density and semantic diversity than existing datasets like MS-COCO and ImageNet.
limits: Dataset is biased toward images of people and sports, limiting generalizability to other domains.
Crowdsourced annotations may contain errors despite verification, affecting reliability.
WordNet canonicalization may introduce ambiguity for polysemous words, requiring manual rules.
Scene graph construction relies on heuristic overlap thresholds, potentially merging distinct objects.
Region descriptions and QAs are limited to English, restricting multilingual applicability.

papers.tEn: Asynchronous Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.tZh: 深度强化学习的异步方法
papers.sEn: Asynchronous methods stabilize training and achieve state-of-the-art results on Atari using only CPU.
contrib: Proposes asynchronous gradient descent for deep RL, enabling stable training without experience replay.
Introduces four asynchronous RL algorithms: one-step Q, Sarsa, n-step Q, and advantage actor-critic (A3C).
A3C surpasses state-of-the-art on Atari with half training time on CPU vs GPU.
Demonstrates A3C's effectiveness on continuous control and 3D maze navigation from pixels.
Shows parallel actor-learners stabilize training and enable linear speedup with multiple threads.
Provides robust and scalable framework for deep RL without specialized hardware.
limits: Experiments limited to simulated environments; real-world applicability not tested.
A3C requires careful tuning of entropy regularization and learning rate for stability.
Asynchronous updates may cause gradient staleness, potentially slowing convergence.
Framework does not incorporate experience replay, which could improve data efficiency.
Scalability to very large distributed systems not explored; only single-machine CPU tested.

papers.tEn: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.tZh: 深度残差学习在图像识别中的应用
papers.sEn: Residual networks enable training of substantially deeper networks with improved accuracy and efficiency.
contrib: Proposed residual learning framework to ease training of substantially deeper networks.
Showed deep residual nets are easier to optimize and gain accuracy from increased depth.
Achieved 3.57% top-5 error on ImageNet test set, winning ILSVRC 2015 classification.
Demonstrated 28% relative improvement on COCO object detection due to deep representations.
Introduced identity shortcut connections adding no extra parameters or computation.
Successfully trained networks with over 1000 layers on CIFAR-10.
limits: Residual learning may not generalize to non-vision tasks without further adaptation.
Very deep models (e.g., 1202 layers) can overfit on small datasets like CIFAR-10.
The degradation problem's root cause is not fully explained; only mitigated.
Identity shortcuts assume input and output dimensions match, requiring projections otherwise.
Training very deep ResNets may require careful learning rate warm-up.

papers.tEn: Deep Speech 2: End-to-End Speech Recognition in English and Mandarin
papers.tZh: Deep Speech 2：英语和普通话的端到端语音识别
papers.sEn: End-to-end deep learning achieves competitive speech recognition in English and Mandarin, accelerated by HPC techniques.
contrib: End-to-end deep learning replaces hand-engineered ASR pipelines with neural networks, handling diverse speech.
HPC techniques achieve 7x speedup over prior system, reducing training from weeks to days.
Batch Normalization for RNNs improves convergence and generalization in deep networks.
SortaGrad curriculum learning stabilizes training by ordering examples by length.
System matches or exceeds human transcription accuracy on several benchmarks.
Batch Dispatch with GPUs enables low-latency online deployment at scale.
limits: System requires large labeled datasets (11,940 hours English, 9,400 hours Mandarin).
Bidirectional RNNs hinder low-latency streaming; unidirectional alternatives may lose accuracy.
Performance on noisy real-world data still lags behind human level.
Language model integration requires external text corpora and tuning.
GPU memory constraints limit model depth and batch size for long utterances.

papers.tEn: Rethinking the Inception Architecture for Computer Vision
papers.tZh: 重新思考计算机视觉中的 Inception 架构
papers.sEn: Factorized convolutions and aggressive regularization enable efficient scaling of deep networks, achieving 3.5% top-5 error on ILSVRC 2012.
contrib: Proposes design principles for scaling CNNs efficiently, including avoiding representational bottlenecks and balancing width/depth.
Introduces factorization of large convolutions into smaller ones (e.g., 5x5 into two 3x3) to reduce computation without loss of expressiveness.
Develops asymmetric convolution factorization (e.g., 1xn followed by nx1) for further computational savings on medium grid sizes.
Demonstrates that auxiliary classifiers act as regularizers rather than improving gradient flow, especially with batch normalization.
Proposes label-smoothing regularization to prevent overfitting and improve generalization by softening ground-truth labels.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on ILSVRC 2012 with 21.2% top-1 and 5.6% top-5 error using Inception-v3, while being computationally efficient.
limits: Design principles are speculative and require further experimental validation across diverse tasks.
Factorization techniques may not work well on early layers; effectiveness is limited to medium grid sizes.
Label-smoothing introduces a hyperparameter epsilon that may need tuning for different datasets.
The study focuses on image classification; applicability to other vision tasks like detection or segmentation is not fully explored.
Computational cost savings assume specific architectural choices; naive scaling may still lead to inefficiencies.

papers.tEn: Unsupervised Representation Learning with Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.tZh: 使用深度卷积生成对抗网络的无监督表示学习
papers.sEn: DCGANs learn hierarchical representations from object parts to scenes in an unsupervised manner.
contrib: Proposes architectural constraints for stable training of deep convolutional GANs (DCGANs).
Demonstrates that DCGANs learn hierarchical representations from object parts to scenes.
Shows learned features achieve 82.8% accuracy on CIFAR-10 via linear SVM, outperforming K-means baselines.
Achieves state-of-the-art 22.48% test error on SVHN with only 1000 labeled examples.
Visualizes filters and demonstrates vector arithmetic in latent space for semantic manipulation.
Shows unsupervised learning of object detectors (e.g., windows) in the generator.
limits: Model instability persists; filters may collapse to oscillating modes with longer training.
Performance on CIFAR-10 is lower than Exemplar CNNs, a supervised unsupervised method.
Evaluation limited to image datasets; generalization to video or audio not explored.
Requires careful hyperparameter tuning (e.g., learning rate, momentum) for stability.
No quantitative evaluation using log-likelihood; relies on visual and task-based metrics.

papers.tEn: Prioritized Experience Replay
papers.tZh: 优先经验回放
papers.sEn: Prioritizing important transitions in experience replay improves learning efficiency and achieves state-of-the-art performance in DQN.
contrib: Proposes prioritized experience replay to replay important transitions more frequently, improving learning efficiency.
Introduces stochastic prioritization to balance greedy prioritization and uniform sampling, ensuring diversity.
Uses importance sampling to correct bias introduced by non-uniform sampling, with annealing schedule.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on Atari 2600 benchmark, outperforming DQN and Double DQN on 41 out of 49 games.
Demonstrates faster learning speed, with median normalized performance increasing from 48% to 106% for DQN.
Explores extensions to supervised learning and off-policy RL, showing broad applicability.
limits: Prioritization based on TD error may be suboptimal when rewards are noisy or stochastic.
Greedy prioritization can lead to overfitting due to lack of diversity in sampled transitions.
Importance sampling correction requires careful annealing; full correction may harm performance in non-stationary settings.
Method assumes replay memory contents are fixed; does not address which experiences to store.
Hyperparameters (α, β) require tuning per domain; fixed settings may not generalize across all tasks.

papers.tEn: Deep Compression: Compressing Deep Neural Networks with Pruning, Trained Quantization and Huffman Coding
papers.tZh: 深度压缩：通过剪枝、训练量化和霍夫曼编码压缩深度神经网络
papers.sEn: Deep compression reduces neural network storage by 35x-49x without accuracy loss via pruning, quantization, and Huffman coding.
contrib: Proposes a three-stage pipeline: pruning, trained quantization, and Huffman coding, achieving 35x to 49x compression without accuracy loss.
Reduces AlexNet from 240MB to 6.9MB and VGG-16 from 552MB to 11.3MB on ImageNet, enabling on-chip SRAM storage.
Combines pruning and quantization synergistically, showing pruning reduces connections by 9x-13x and quantization reduces bits per weight to 5.
Demonstrates linear initialization for k-means clustering preserves large weights, improving quantization accuracy.
Achieves 3x-4x layerwise speedup and 3x-7x energy efficiency on CPU, GPU, and mobile GPU.
limits: Quantized network with weight sharing not benchmarked due to lack of library support for indirect lookup.
Pruning advantage diminishes in batched matrix-matrix multiplication due to improved memory locality.
Method focuses on storage compression; inference speedup limited without specialized hardware or custom kernels.
Huffman coding provides marginal gain (e.g., 32x to 40x) compared to pruning and quantization.
Weight sharing across layers not explored; each layer quantized independently.

papers.tEn: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Double Q-learning
papers.tZh: 深度强化学习中的双 Q 学习
papers.sEn: Double Q-learning reduces overestimations in DQN, improving performance on Atari games.
contrib: Shows Q-learning overestimates action values in large-scale deterministic problems due to inherent estimation errors.
Demonstrates DQN suffers substantial overestimations in Atari 2600 games, harming performance.
Generalizes Double Q-learning to large-scale function approximation with deep neural networks.
Proposes Double DQN algorithm, reducing overestimations and improving policy quality.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on Atari 2600 domain with Double DQN.
limits: Evaluation limited to deterministic Atari 2600 games; stochastic environments not tested.
Hyperparameters tuned for DQN, not optimized for Double DQN in main comparison.
Double DQN may not eliminate overestimations entirely; residual bias possible.
Theoretical analysis assumes unbiased estimates; practical violations may affect guarantees.
Results may not generalize to other domains beyond Atari 2600.

papers.tEn: Continuous control with deep reinforcement learning
papers.tZh: 连续控制与深度强化学习
papers.sEn: We adapt Deep Q-Learning to continuous action domains using an actor-critic, model-free algorithm based on deterministic policy gradients, achieving competitive performance on over 20 simulated physics tasks.
contrib: Adapts Deep Q-Learning to continuous action domains via deterministic policy gradient.
Proposes Deep DPG (DDPG) algorithm with actor-critic, replay buffer, and target networks.
Solves over 20 simulated physics tasks with same hyper-parameters and network architecture.
Achieves competitive performance with planning algorithms that have full dynamics access.
Demonstrates end-to-end learning from raw pixel inputs for many tasks.
Combines batch normalization for stable learning across tasks with different units.
limits: Requires large number of training episodes, limiting sample efficiency.
No convergence guarantees due to non-linear function approximators.
Exploration noise must be tuned per environment for effective exploration.
Performance degrades on harder tasks with inaccurate Q-value estimates.
Limited to simulated environments; real-world applicability not tested.

papers.tEn: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
papers.tZh: 基于子词单元的罕见词神经机器翻译
papers.sEn: Encoding rare and unknown words as sequences of subword units enables open-vocabulary translation in NMT, improving BLEU by 1.1 and 1.3 on English-German and English-Russian tasks.
contrib: Proposes encoding rare and unknown words as subword units for open-vocabulary NMT, avoiding back-off dictionaries.
Adapts byte pair encoding (BPE) for word segmentation, enabling open-vocabulary representation with a fixed-size symbol set.
Achieves BLEU improvements of 1.1 (EN-DE) and 1.3 (EN-RU) over back-off dictionary baselines on WMT 2015 tasks.
Shows subword models learn compounding and transliteration, productively generating unseen words.
Joint BPE encoding improves segmentation consistency between source and target, enhancing translation quality.
Demonstrates that reducing subword vocabulary size can improve performance due to less sparsity.
limits: Gains are mainly on rare and unseen words; overall BLEU improvements are modest.
BPE segmentation can produce opaque units that are not translatable independently, potentially harming quality.
Effectiveness varies across language pairs and alphabets; transliteration for different scripts may need extra processing.
Increased sequence length from subword segmentation raises training and inference time.
The number of BPE merge operations is a hyperparameter that requires tuning per task.

papers.tEn: Understanding LSTM Networks
papers.tZh: 理解 LSTM 网络
papers.sEn: LSTM networks address the limitation of traditional neural networks by allowing information to persist through loops, enabling them to use context from previous inputs.
contrib: LSTM networks solve the long-term dependency problem of RNNs via gated cell state.
The cell state acts as a conveyor belt for information flow with minimal linear interactions.
Three gates (forget, input, output) regulate information removal, addition, and output.
LSTMs are explicitly designed to remember information for long periods by default.
Variants like GRU simplify LSTM by merging gates and states, gaining popularity.
Attention mechanisms represent a next step beyond LSTMs for selective information focus.
limits: LSTMs are more complex and computationally expensive than standard RNNs.
Performance varies across tasks; some RNN architectures outperform LSTMs on specific problems.
LSTMs still struggle with very long sequences despite improved memory.
The paper does not address training difficulties like vanishing gradients in deep LSTMs.
Variants like GRU may offer comparable performance with simpler structure.

papers.tEn: Pointer Networks
papers.tZh: 指针网络
papers.sEn: Pointer Networks use attention as a pointer to select input elements as output, enabling solutions to problems with variable-size output dictionaries.
contrib: Proposes Pointer Networks (Ptr-Net), a new neural architecture using attention as a pointer to select input elements as outputs.
Addresses variable-size output dictionaries by using softmax distribution as a pointer, enabling handling of combinatorial problems.
Demonstrates Ptr-Net learns approximate solutions to planar convex hull, Delaunay triangulation, and TSP from training examples alone.
Shows Ptr-Net generalizes to input lengths beyond those seen during training, outperforming sequence-to-sequence with attention.
Provides a purely data-driven approach to computationally intractable discrete problems, encouraging broader exploration.
limits: Ptr-Net's O(n^2) complexity limits scalability to very large inputs compared to exact algorithms.
Model performance degrades for problems requiring complex reasoning, such as TSP beyond n=30.
Input order affects accuracy; points appearing late in the sequence may be missed.
Model struggles with degenerate cases like collinear points in convex hull.
Requires careful output ordering (e.g., triangle sorting) for effective learning; suboptimal ordering reduces performance.

papers.tEn: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
papers.tZh: 你只需看一眼：统一、实时的目标检测
papers.sEn: YOLO frames object detection as a regression problem, enabling real-time processing with a single neural network.
contrib: Frames object detection as a single regression problem from image pixels to bounding boxes and class probabilities.
Unified architecture enables end-to-end training and real-time speeds at 45 fps for YOLO and 155 fps for Fast YOLO.
YOLO reasons globally about the image, reducing background false positives by half compared to Fast R-CNN.
Learns generalizable object representations, outperforming DPM and R-CNN when generalizing from natural images to artwork.
Combining YOLO with Fast R-CNN boosts mAP by 3.2% on VOC 2007 by reducing background errors.
Open-source framework with pretrained models, enabling easy reproduction and deployment.
limits: YOLO makes more localization errors than state-of-the-art detectors, especially for small objects.
Spatial constraints limit the number of nearby objects YOLO can predict, struggling with groups of small objects.
Loss function treats errors equally for large and small boxes, not aligning perfectly with detection performance.
Coarse features from downsampling layers hinder precise bounding box prediction.
YOLO lags behind state-of-the-art in accuracy on standard benchmarks like VOC 2012.

papers.tEn: Visualizing and Understanding Recurrent Networks
papers.tZh: 可视化与理解循环网络
papers.sEn: LSTM networks learn interpretable cells that track long-range dependencies like line lengths and brackets, outperforming n-gram models on structural patterns.
contrib: Reveals interpretable LSTM cells tracking long-range dependencies like line lengths, quotes, and brackets in real-world data.
Demonstrates LSTM outperforms n-gram models on characters requiring long-range reasoning, e.g., closing braces.
Provides error breakdown using oracles, showing 37% errors follow spaces/quotes/newlines, indicating word-level prediction difficulty.
Shows scaling up model size mainly reduces local n-gram errors, leaving other error categories largely unchanged.
Analyzes gate activation statistics, revealing nearly binary saturation in deeper layers but diffuse activations in the first layer.
Trains LSTM training dynamics, showing it progressively models longer dependencies over time.
limits: Analysis limited to character-level language models on two datasets (War and Peace, Linux Kernel).
Error breakdown uses oracles in a fixed order, which may influence results.
Study does not explore architectural innovations beyond LSTM, GRU, and RNN.
Findings on scaling may not generalize to other tasks or larger models.
Interpretability of cells is qualitative and may not capture all learned representations.

papers.tEn: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
papers.tZh: Faster R-CNN: 基于区域提议网络的实时目标检测
papers.sEn: Faster R-CNN introduces a Region Proposal Network that shares convolutional features with the detection network, enabling nearly cost-free region proposals and real-time object detection.
contrib: Introduces Region Proposal Network (RPN) sharing convolutional features with detection network, enabling nearly cost-free region proposals.
Proposes anchor boxes as regression references for multi-scale and aspect ratio prediction without image or filter pyramids.
Develops a 4-step alternating training algorithm to share convolutional layers between RPN and Fast R-CNN, forming a unified network.
Achieves state-of-the-art detection accuracy on PASCAL VOC 2007, 2012, and MS COCO with only 300 proposals per image.
Demonstrates near real-time performance at 5fps on GPU with VGG-16, including all detection steps.
Serves as foundation for 1st-place entries in ILSVRC and COCO 2015 competitions across multiple tracks.
limits: RPN relies on pre-defined anchor scales and aspect ratios, which may not generalize to all object shapes.
Training requires careful handling of cross-boundary anchors to avoid convergence issues.
Non-maximum suppression is needed to reduce proposal redundancy, adding a post-processing step.
Performance depends on pre-trained ImageNet models, limiting applicability to domains with different data distributions.
Joint training of RPN and Fast R-CNN is approximate, ignoring gradients w.r.t. proposal box coordinates.

papers.tEn: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
papers.tZh: U-Net：用于生物医学图像分割的卷积网络
papers.sEn: U-Net achieves state-of-the-art segmentation with few images via strong data augmentation and a symmetric encoder-decoder architecture.
contrib: Proposed U-Net architecture with symmetric contracting and expansive paths for precise localization.
Achieved state-of-the-art segmentation on ISBI EM challenge using only 30 annotated images via elastic deformation augmentation.
Won ISBI cell tracking challenge 2015 with 92% IOU on PhC-U373 and 77.5% on DIC-HeLa, outperforming prior methods by large margins.
Introduced weighted loss to separate touching objects by emphasizing background borders between cells.
Enabled fast segmentation of 512x512 images in under a second on a GPU.
Provided full Caffe-based implementation and trained networks publicly.
limits: Requires careful selection of input tile size to ensure even dimensions for max-pooling layers.
Unpadded convolutions reduce output size by a constant border width, limiting full-context prediction at edges.
Performance depends on data augmentation with elastic deformations, which may not generalize to all biomedical tasks.
Training requires a GPU with sufficient memory (e.g., 6 GB) for large input tiles.
Weight map computation for separation borders relies on morphological operations, adding preprocessing complexity.

papers.tEn: Fast R-CNN
papers.tZh: Fast R-CNN
papers.sEn: Fast R-CNN achieves faster training and testing speeds with higher accuracy for object detection.
contrib: Proposes Fast R-CNN, a single-stage training algorithm for object detection that jointly learns classification and bounding-box regression.
Achieves 9x faster training and 213x faster testing than R-CNN with VGG16, while improving mAP on PASCAL VOC 2012.
Introduces RoI pooling layer for efficient feature sharing and back-propagation through region proposals.
Uses multi-task loss combining softmax classification and robust L1 bounding-box regression.
Demonstrates that fine-tuning convolutional layers is crucial for very deep networks like VGG16.
Shows that sparse object proposals improve detector quality, enabling efficient evaluation.
limits: Relies on pre-computed object proposals, which limits end-to-end training and may miss objects.
Single-scale training and testing may not generalize well to extreme scale variations.
GPU memory constraints limit the use of very deep networks with multi-scale training.
Performance degrades when using dense object proposals instead of sparse ones.
Method is evaluated only on PASCAL VOC and MS COCO datasets; generalization to other domains is not tested.

papers.tEn: End-to-End Training of Deep Visuomotor Policies
papers.tZh: 深度视觉运动策略的端到端训练
papers.sEn: Jointly training perception and control end-to-end yields better performance than separate training for visuomotor policies.
contrib: Develops a guided policy search method that transforms policy search into supervised learning using trajectory-centric RL.
Introduces a novel CNN architecture with spatial soft-argmax for end-to-end visuomotor policy learning from raw images to torques.
Demonstrates end-to-end training of perception and control outperforms separate training on real-world manipulation tasks.
Achieves sample-efficient learning with only tens of minutes of real-world interaction time for complex 7-DoF tasks.
Provides simulated comparisons showing guided policy search outperforms prior methods like REPS, RWR, and PILCO.
Formalizes guided policy search as BADMM, ensuring convergence to a locally optimal solution.
limits: Requires full state observability during training, limiting applicability to instrumented setups.
Assumes low-noise dynamics for linear-Gaussian trajectory optimization, which may not hold in highly stochastic environments.
Uses first-moment constraints on actions, which may be insufficient for tasks requiring precise higher-order statistics.
Pretraining requires ImageNet initialization and pose regression data, adding dependency on external datasets.
Policy architecture with spatial soft-argmax is specialized for visuomotor tasks and may not generalize to other perception problems.

papers.tEn: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics
papers.tZh: 基于非平衡热力学的深度无监督学习
papers.sEn: A novel generative model inspired by non-equilibrium statistical physics that learns to reverse a diffusion process to restore data structure.
contrib: Introduces diffusion probabilistic models inspired by non-equilibrium statistical physics, achieving both flexibility and tractability.
Defines a forward diffusion process that gradually destroys data structure and learns a reverse process to restore it.
Enables exact sampling, log-likelihood evaluation, and multiplication with other distributions for posterior computation.
Demonstrates high log-likelihood on diverse datasets including MNIST, CIFAR-10, and dead leaves images.
Provides entropy bounds for the reverse diffusion process and a lower bound on log-likelihood for training.
Releases open-source reference implementation for reproducibility.
limits: Requires many diffusion steps (thousands) for high-quality samples, increasing computational cost.
Performance depends on the choice of diffusion schedule and noise type (Gaussian or binomial).
The method assumes smooth target distributions; highly multimodal or discontinuous distributions may be challenging.
Training requires careful tuning of hyperparameters like step size and network architecture.
The lower bound on log-likelihood may be loose for finite diffusion steps, affecting model evaluation.

papers.tEn: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
papers.tZh: 神经网络中的知识蒸馏
papers.sEn: Distilling knowledge from an ensemble into a single model improves performance and efficiency.
contrib: Introduces knowledge distillation, transferring ensemble knowledge into a single small model using soft targets with temperature scaling.
Shows distilled model on MNIST achieves 74 errors vs 146 for a regularized small net, even without seeing digit 3 in transfer set.
Demonstrates distillation improves commercial speech recognition: distilled single model matches ensemble performance with 10.9% WER.
Proposes specialist ensemble: one generalist plus many specialists for fine-grained classes, trained in parallel, improving JFT accuracy by 4.4%.
Shows soft targets prevent overfitting with limited data: 3% of speech data yields 57% frame accuracy vs 44.5% with hard targets.
Provides theoretical analysis: high-temperature distillation approximates minimizing squared logit difference.
limits: Distillation requires a pre-trained cumbersome model, which may be computationally expensive to obtain.
Optimal temperature is task-dependent and requires tuning; low temperatures may ignore useful negative logits.
Specialist ensemble relies on clustering of confusable classes, which may not be optimal for all datasets.
Distillation performance degrades when distilled model is too small to capture all knowledge from cumbersome model.
Method assumes soft targets from cumbersome model are reliable; noisy or biased cumbersome models may transfer errors.

papers.tEn: Trust Region Policy Optimization
papers.tZh: 信任区域策略优化
papers.sEn: TRPO is a practical algorithm for optimizing policies with guaranteed monotonic improvement, effective for large nonlinear policies like neural networks.
contrib: Proves a monotonic improvement guarantee for policy optimization with KL divergence penalty.
Develops TRPO, a practical algorithm using a KL divergence constraint for robust updates.
Demonstrates TRPO's effectiveness on simulated robotic locomotion and Atari games.
Unifies policy gradient and policy iteration methods under a trust region framework.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on high-dimensional control tasks with neural network policies.
limits: Assumes exact advantage evaluation, which is unrealistic in practice.
Vine method requires state resets, limiting applicability to simulation.
Theoretical bound uses maximum KL divergence, but practical algorithm uses average KL.
Sample complexity may be high for real-world robotic tasks due to on-policy sampling.
Performance on Atari games is not consistently superior to specialized methods like DQN.

papers.tEn: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
papers.tZh: 批量归一化：通过减少内部协变量偏移加速深度网络训练
papers.sEn: Batch Normalization allows higher learning rates, reduces need for Dropout, and achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with fewer training steps.
contrib: Proposes Batch Normalization to reduce internal covariate shift, enabling higher learning rates and faster training.
Normalizes layer inputs using mini-batch statistics, making normalization part of the model architecture.
Allows use of saturating nonlinearities by preventing saturation, and acts as a regularizer reducing need for Dropout.
Achieves same accuracy with 14x fewer training steps on ImageNet, and sets new state-of-the-art with 4.9% top-5 error.
Introduces learned affine parameters to restore network representation capacity after normalization.
Demonstrates that Batch Normalization improves gradient flow and stabilizes parameter growth.
limits: Normalization depends on mini-batch size; very small batches may lead to inaccurate statistics.
The method assumes that layer inputs have Gaussian-like distribution; non-Gaussian inputs may reduce effectiveness.
Batch Normalization adds computational overhead during training due to per-batch statistics computation.
The theoretical understanding of why Batch Normalization works remains incomplete, especially for gradient propagation.
The method may not generalize well to recurrent networks or tasks with very small batch sizes.

papers.tEn: The AI Revolution: The Road to Superintelligence
papers.tZh: 人工智能革命：通往超级智能之路
papers.sEn: The AI revolution is the most important topic for our future, comparable to the rise of human life on Earth.
contrib: Explains the Law of Accelerating Returns and exponential growth of AI progress.
Defines three AI calibers: ANI, AGI, and ASI, with clear distinctions.
Argues that AGI will quickly lead to ASI via recursive self-improvement.
Highlights that human-level AGI may be achieved by 2040, with ASI soon after.
Emphasizes that ASI could bring either utopia or extinction.
Uses historical analogies to illustrate the difficulty of predicting exponential change.
limits: Relies heavily on Kurzweil's predictions, which may be overly optimistic.
Does not address potential technical barriers to AGI, such as consciousness.
Assumes recursive self-improvement will be stable and safe, which is uncertain.
Lacks detailed discussion of alignment and control of superintelligent AI.
The timeline for AGI and ASI is speculative and contested among experts.

papers.tEn: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
papers.tZh: Adam：一种随机优化方法
papers.sEn: Adam is an efficient stochastic optimization algorithm based on adaptive estimates of lower-order moments.
contrib: Proposes Adam, combining AdaGrad and RMSProp for adaptive learning rates.
Introduces bias correction for moment estimates to prevent large initial steps.
Provides regret bound in online convex optimization, ensuring convergence.
Empirically shows superior performance on logistic regression, MLPs, and CNNs.
Proposes AdaMax variant using infinity norm, simplifying parameter updates.
limits: Theoretical analysis assumes convexity; non-convex convergence lacks guarantees.
Hyperparameters, especially beta2, are sensitive and require careful tuning.
Second moment estimate can be inaccurate in CNNs, slowing convergence.
No rigorous handling of extremely sparse gradients despite claimed suitability.

papers.tEn: Deep Visual-Semantic Alignments for Generating Image Descriptions
papers.tZh: 深度视觉-语义对齐用于生成图像描述
papers.sEn: A model combining CNNs and RNNs with a structured objective aligns visual and language data to generate novel image descriptions.
contrib: Proposes a deep neural network model that infers latent alignments between sentence segments and image regions via a multimodal embedding.
Introduces a Multimodal Recurrent Neural Network architecture that generates novel descriptions of image regions from inferred alignments.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on image-sentence retrieval experiments on Flickr8K, Flickr30K, and MSCOCO datasets.
Demonstrates that generated descriptions significantly outperform retrieval baselines on both full images and region-level annotations.
Simplifies the ranking objective compared to prior work, improving performance without additional hyperparameters.
Uses a Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Network to compute word representations, capturing unbounded context without dependency parsing.
limits: The Multimodal RNN can only generate descriptions for a single input region at fixed resolution, lacking multi-saccade exploration.
Image information is communicated only through additive bias interactions, which are less expressive than multiplicative interactions.
The approach consists of two separate models; end-to-end training from image-sentence pairs to region descriptions remains an open problem.
The model may generate sentences found in training data (60% with beam size 7), limiting novelty.
Performance is sensitive to beam size and word frequency disparity between rare and common words.

papers.tEn: Show and Tell: A Neural Image Caption Generator
papers.tZh: 展示与讲述：一种神经图像描述生成模型
papers.sEn: A neural image caption generator combining computer vision and machine translation achieves state-of-the-art BLEU scores on multiple datasets.
contrib: Proposes an end-to-end neural network (NIC) combining CNN and LSTM for image caption generation.
Achieves state-of-the-art BLEU scores on Pascal (59), Flickr30k (66), and SBU (28).
Demonstrates that the model learns fluent language solely from image descriptions.
Shows transfer learning capability across datasets with different sizes and noise levels.
Provides qualitative and quantitative analysis including human evaluation and diversity of generated captions.
limits: Model performance is limited by small training dataset sizes, leading to overfitting.
BLEU score may not fully capture caption quality; human evaluation shows lower scores.
Transfer learning degrades when source and target domains differ significantly.
Model often retrieves training sentences rather than generating novel ones for the top candidate.
Weakly labeled data (e.g., SBU) reduces performance due to noise and vocabulary mismatch.

papers.tEn: Conditional Generative Adversarial Nets
papers.tZh: 条件生成对抗网络
papers.sEn: Conditional GANs enable controlled data generation by conditioning on additional information like class labels.
contrib: Introduces conditional generative adversarial nets (cGANs) by feeding conditioning data to both generator and discriminator.
Demonstrates MNIST digit generation conditioned on class labels.
Shows multi-modal learning capability via image tagging on MIR Flickr dataset.
Generates descriptive tags not present in training labels using word embeddings.
Provides a framework for one-to-many mapping in probabilistic generative models.
limits: Preliminary results; conditional model underperforms non-conditional adversarial nets on MNIST.
Image tagging experiments use fixed convolutional and language models without joint training.
Only single tags used per image; multi-tag set generation left for future work.
Hyper-parameter search limited; architecture not fully optimized.

papers.tEn: Going Deeper with Convolutions
papers.tZh: 深入卷积网络
papers.sEn: We propose Inception, a deep CNN architecture that achieves state-of-the-art results in ILSVRC 2014 by efficiently using computing resources to increase depth and width.
contrib: Proposed the Inception architecture that improves computing resource utilization by increasing depth and width while keeping computational budget constant.
Introduced dimension reduction using 1x1 convolutions to remove computational bottlenecks.
Achieved state-of-the-art results on ILSVRC 2014 classification and detection with GoogLeNet.
Demonstrated that approximating optimal sparse structure with dense components is viable for improving neural networks.
Showed that increasing network depth and width with efficient design can improve accuracy without proportional computational cost.
Used auxiliary classifiers to encourage discrimination in lower stages and provide regularization.
limits: The Inception architecture was designed specifically for computer vision tasks and may not generalize to other domains.
The architecture relies on manual design and tuning; automated construction of similar topologies remains future work.
The computational efficiency gains are achieved at the cost of increased architectural complexity.
The results are based on a specific competition dataset (ILSVRC 2014) and may not fully represent real-world performance.
The detection pipeline did not use bounding box regression or context, which could further improve accuracy.

papers.tEn: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
papers.tZh: 基于神经网络的序列到序列学习
papers.sEn: A deep LSTM-based end-to-end approach achieves BLEU 34.8 on WMT'14 English-French translation, outperforming a phrase-based SMT system (33.3) and reaching 36.5 when reranking SMT hypotheses.
contrib: Proposes an end-to-end LSTM-based sequence-to-sequence model for general sequence learning.
Achieves BLEU score of 34.8 on WMT'14 English-French translation, outperforming phrase-based SMT baseline.
Reversing source sentences introduces short-term dependencies, improving LSTM performance on long sentences.
LSTM learns sentence representations sensitive to word order and invariant to active/passive voice.
Deep LSTMs with 4 layers significantly outperform shallow LSTMs.
LSTM rescoring of SMT n-best lists achieves BLEU 36.5, close to previous best result.
limits: Limited vocabulary (80k target words) penalizes BLEU for out-of-vocabulary words.
Requires large computational resources (8 GPUs, 10 days training).
Beam search decoder is approximate and may not find optimal translation.
Method assumes monotonic alignment between input and output sequences.
Performance on tasks with very limited training data is not evaluated.

papers.tEn: Recurrent Neural Network Regularization
papers.tZh: 循环神经网络正则化
papers.sEn: We present a simple regularization technique for RNNs with LSTM units, showing that correctly applied dropout substantially reduces overfitting across multiple tasks.
contrib: Shows how to correctly apply dropout to LSTMs by restricting it to non-recurrent connections.
Demonstrates substantial reduction of overfitting in LSTMs across language modeling, speech recognition, image captioning, and machine translation.
Provides empirical evidence that dropout on non-recurrent connections preserves LSTM's long-term memory ability.
Achieves state-of-the-art perplexity on Penn Tree Bank language modeling with a large LSTM.
Improves frame accuracy in speech recognition and BLEU score in machine translation.
Shows that dropout can make a single LSTM model as effective as an ensemble in image captioning.
limits: Dropout is applied only to LSTM; other RNN variants are not tested.
Optimal dropout probability varies across tasks and requires tuning.
Method does not improve performance when combined with ensemble in image captioning.
Experiments are limited to specific datasets and may not generalize to all domains.
Theoretical analysis of why dropout works on non-recurrent connections is limited.

papers.tEn: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
papers.tZh: 用于大规模图像识别的极深卷积网络
papers.sEn: Increasing depth with small 3x3 filters significantly improves accuracy, achieving 16-19 weight layers.
contrib: Systematic evaluation of increasing depth in ConvNets using very small 3x3 filters.
Demonstrated that pushing depth to 16-19 weight layers significantly improves accuracy.
Achieved first and second places in ILSVRC 2014 localization and classification tracks.
Showed that learned representations generalize well to other datasets, achieving state-of-the-art results.
Publicly released two best-performing ConvNet models to facilitate further research.
Confirmed that depth is crucial for visual representation quality.
limits: Evaluation limited to ImageNet dataset; generalization to other domains not fully explored.
Depth beyond 19 layers did not improve performance; saturation observed.
Training required significant computational resources (2-3 weeks on 4 GPUs).
Architecture uses only 3x3 filters; other filter sizes not systematically compared.
Multi-crop evaluation increases computation time without proportional accuracy gain.

papers.tEn: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
papers.tZh: 通过联合学习对齐和翻译的神经机器翻译
papers.sEn: Neural machine translation can be improved by allowing the model to automatically search for relevant parts of the source sentence without encoding it into a fixed-length vector.
contrib: Proposes an attention mechanism that allows soft-search over source sentence parts for each target word.
Eliminates the fixed-length vector bottleneck in encoder-decoder models, improving long sentence translation.
Achieves translation performance comparable to phrase-based SMT on English-to-French WMT'14.
Uses bidirectional RNN encoder to capture both preceding and following context for each word.
Jointly trains alignment and translation in a single neural network via backpropagation.
Visualizes soft-alignments that align with linguistic intuition, handling non-monotonic reordering.
limits: Computes annotation weights for every source word per target word, limiting scalability to very long sequences.
Requires fixed vocabulary with unknown word token, failing to handle rare or out-of-vocabulary words.
Tested only on English-to-French; effectiveness on other language pairs with different reordering patterns is unverified.
Soft alignment is computationally expensive compared to hard alignment used in traditional SMT.
Performance relies on large parallel corpora; may degrade with limited data.

papers.tEn: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge
papers.tZh: ImageNet 大规模视觉识别挑战赛
papers.sEn: The ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge is a benchmark for object category classification and detection, driving advances in computer vision.
contrib: Introduced the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge (ILSVRC), a benchmark for object classification and detection with 1000 categories and millions of images.
Developed scalable crowdsourcing methods for large-scale image annotation, achieving 99.7% precision.
Demonstrated that deep convolutional neural networks (e.g., AlexNet) significantly outperform traditional methods, marking a turning point in object recognition.
Provided a detailed analysis of algorithmic progress over five years, comparing state-of-the-art computer vision accuracy with human accuracy.
Established evaluation metrics for large-scale classification, localization, and detection, including top-5 error and average precision.
Released a publicly available dataset and competition framework that became the standard benchmark for object recognition research.
limits: Dataset annotation only labels one object category per image for classification, causing ambiguity when multiple objects are present.
Evaluation metrics for localization may be inaccurate for images with clustered objects, requiring manual removal of 3.5% of images.
Small object instances pose challenges for localization evaluation; threshold adjustment is needed for objects under 25x25 pixels.
The dataset's 1000 categories are limited to ImageNet synsets and may not cover all real-world object types.
Crowdsourcing annotation quality relies on worker consensus, which may vary across different object categories.

papers.tEn: Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.tZh: 生成对抗网络
papers.sEn: We propose a new framework for estimating generative models via an adversarial process, where a generative model and a discriminative model are trained simultaneously, with the generator aiming to fool the discriminator.
contrib: Proposes adversarial training framework with generator and discriminator networks.
Shows global optimum when generator matches data distribution, discriminator outputs 1/2.
Eliminates need for Markov chains or approximate inference during training or sampling.
Demonstrates competitive sample quality on MNIST, TFD, and CIFAR-10.
Introduces minimax game formulation for generative model estimation.
limits: No explicit representation of probability density p_g(x).
Training requires careful synchronization between G and D to avoid mode collapse.
Theoretical guarantees assume infinite capacity; practical MLPs may have critical points.
Likelihood estimation via Parzen window has high variance and poor high-dimensional performance.
Framework limited to differentiable generator and discriminator functions.

papers.tEn: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
papers.tZh: Microsoft COCO：上下文中的常见物体
papers.sEn: A new dataset for object recognition in context, with 2.5M labeled instances across 91 object types.
contrib: Introduces MS COCO dataset with 91 object categories, 2.5M instances in 328k images.
Focuses on non-iconic images with contextual relationships and precise instance segmentation.
Novel annotation pipeline using hierarchical labeling and crowdsourcing for efficiency.
Provides detailed statistical comparison with PASCAL, ImageNet, and SUN datasets.
Baseline detection and segmentation results using Deformable Parts Model.
Demonstrates dataset difficulty and cross-dataset generalization benefits.
limits: Only includes 'thing' categories, not 'stuff' like sky or grass.
Limited to 91 entry-level categories; fine-grained categories excluded.
Crowd-sourced annotations may have quality variance despite verification.
Baseline models (DPM) may not capture full complexity of dataset.
Dataset split into 2014 and 2015 releases; some categories not segmented.

papers.tEn: Spectral Networks and Locally Connected Networks on Graphs
papers.tZh: 谱网络与图上的局部连接网络
papers.sEn: We propose two generalizations of CNNs to signals on general domains: one via hierarchical clustering and another via graph Laplacian spectrum, enabling efficient deep architectures with input-size-independent parameters for low-dimensional graphs.
contrib: Proposes two generalizations of CNNs to graph-structured data: spatial and spectral constructions.
Shows that spatial construction achieves O(n) parameters using hierarchical clustering and local receptive fields.
Introduces spectral construction using graph Laplacian eigenvectors, achieving O(n) parameters per feature map.
Demonstrates O(1) parameter construction via smooth spectral multipliers, enabling parameter count independent of input size.
Validates both constructions on low-dimensional graph datasets, showing improved efficiency over fully connected networks.
Shows that smooth spectral constraints yield spatially localized filters that generalize across graph locations.
limits: Spatial construction lacks weight sharing across different graph locations.
Spectral construction requires expensive multiplication by eigenvectors and their transpose.
High-frequency eigenvectors may be noisy; spectral construction may not capture meaningful information from them.
Naive multiscale clustering used in spatial construction does not guarantee compatibility with graph Laplacian.
Experiments limited to low-dimensional graphs; scalability to high-dimensional or large-scale graphs not fully explored.

papers.tEn: Rich feature hierarchies for accurate object detection and semantic segmentation
papers.tZh: 用于精确目标检测和语义分割的丰富特征层次结构
papers.sEn: R-CNN combines region proposals with CNNs to achieve a 30% relative improvement in mAP on PASCAL VOC 2012.
contrib: Proposes R-CNN, combining region proposals with CNNs for object detection.
Achieves 30% relative mAP improvement on PASCAL VOC 2012 over prior best.
Shows supervised pre-training on auxiliary task plus domain-specific fine-tuning boosts performance.
Demonstrates R-CNN outperforms OverFeat on ILSVRC2013 detection by large margin.
Extends R-CNN to semantic segmentation with competitive results on PASCAL VOC.
Provides analysis of error modes and bounding-box regression to reduce mislocalizations.
limits: Requires fixed-size CNN input via warping, which may distort aspect ratios.
Region proposal stage (selective search) is a bottleneck for speed and recall.
Fine-tuning and SVM training use different positive/negative definitions, causing inconsistency.
Bounding-box regression only effective for proposals near ground truth, limiting scope.
Performance depends heavily on pre-training dataset (ImageNet) and architecture choice.

papers.tEn: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality
papers.tZh: 词汇与短语的分布式表示及其组合性
papers.sEn: We extend the Skip-gram model with subsampling and negative sampling to learn high-quality word and phrase vectors efficiently.
contrib: Introduced negative sampling as a simple alternative to hierarchical softmax for efficient training.
Demonstrated that subsampling frequent words speeds up training and improves vector quality for rare words.
Extended Skip-gram to learn phrase vectors by treating phrases as single tokens via data-driven phrase detection.
Showed that word vectors exhibit linear structure enabling analogical reasoning via vector arithmetic.
Demonstrated additive compositionality of word vectors, e.g., vec('Russia') + vec('river') ≈ vec('Volga River').
Trained high-quality vectors on billions of words, significantly outperforming prior models on analogy tasks.
limits: Word representations are indifferent to word order, limiting capture of syntactic structure.
Inability to represent idiomatic phrases as compositions of individual word meanings.
Negative sampling does not maximize log probability of softmax, only approximates it.
Phrase detection threshold and subsampling rate are heuristic and task-dependent.
Model performance heavily depends on large training data and careful hyperparameter tuning.

papers.tEn: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
papers.tZh: 词向量空间中的高效估计方法
papers.sEn: Proposed two novel model architectures for computing continuous word vectors from large datasets, achieving higher accuracy with lower computational cost.
contrib: Proposes CBOW and Skip-gram models for efficient learning of high-quality word vectors from large data.
Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on syntactic and semantic word similarity tasks with low computational cost.
Demonstrates that word vectors capture linear regularities, enabling algebraic operations like vector("King") - vector("Man") + vector("Woman") ≈ vector("Queen").
Introduces a comprehensive test set with 8869 semantic and 10675 syntactic questions for evaluating word vectors.
Shows that increasing both vector dimensionality and training data size yields diminishing returns, requiring balanced scaling.
Achieves new state-of-the-art on Microsoft Sentence Completion Challenge (58.9% accuracy) by combining Skip-gram with RNNLM.
limits: Models treat words as atomic units, ignoring morphology; synonyms are counted as mistakes in evaluation.
Performance saturates with increasing vector dimensions or data size, requiring joint scaling for improvement.
Skip-gram model underperforms on syntactic tasks compared to CBOW, limiting its general applicability.
Training on limited in-domain data (e.g., speech recognition) may not benefit from simple scaling, requiring advanced techniques.
Evaluation metric (cosine distance) may not capture all semantic nuances, and 100% accuracy is likely unattainable.

papers.tEn: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.tZh: 使用深度卷积神经网络的 ImageNet 分类
papers.sEn: A deep CNN with 60M parameters achieved state-of-the-art results on ImageNet, using non-saturating neurons, efficient GPU implementation, and dropout to reduce overfitting.
contrib: Trained a large deep CNN on ImageNet with 60M parameters, achieving top-5 error of 17.0% on ILSVRC-2010.
Introduced ReLU nonlinearity to accelerate training, surpassing saturating activations like tanh.
Used dropout regularization to effectively reduce overfitting in large fully connected layers.
Demonstrated depth importance: removing a convolutional layer degrades top-1 accuracy by about 2%.
limits: Network size limited by GPU memory (3GB); requires multiple GPUs and days of training.
Model heavily reliant on large labeled datasets; performance drops without sufficient data.
No unsupervised pre-training used; may improve with additional unlabeled data.
Architecture optimized for ImageNet; transferability to other tasks not extensively validated.
Dropout doubles training iterations; computational cost still high despite optimizations.

papers.tEn: Improving neural networks by preventing co-adaptation of feature detectors
papers.tZh: 通过防止特征检测器的共适应来改进神经网络
papers.sEn: Randomly omitting half of the feature detectors during training prevents co-adaptation and reduces overfitting, leading to significant improvements in neural network performance.
contrib: Proposes dropout, a technique that randomly omits half of feature detectors during training to prevent co-adaptation.
Shows dropout reduces overfitting significantly on small training sets.
Demonstrates dropout as efficient model averaging, approximating exponentially many networks.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on speech (TIMIT) and object recognition (CIFAR-10, ImageNet) benchmarks.
Introduces L2 weight constraints per hidden unit to allow large learning rates and thorough weight-space search.
Connects dropout to evolutionary theory, suggesting robustness through multiple alternative feature sets.
limits: Dropout probability of 0.5 is used throughout; optimal probability may vary per layer or dataset.
Method primarily tested on feedforward neural networks; applicability to recurrent or other architectures not explored.
Performance gains depend on network size and training data amount; may diminish with very large datasets.
Test-time mean network approximation assumes equal importance of all dropout networks; may not hold in all cases.
Dropout increases training time due to stochastic updates and requires careful tuning of learning rate and constraints.

papers.tEn: A Fast Learning Algorithm for Deep Belief Nets
papers.tZh: 一种深度信念网络的快速学习算法
papers.sEn: The paper presents a fast learning algorithm for Deep Belief Networks.
contrib: Proposes complementary priors to eliminate explaining away, enabling efficient inference in deep belief nets.
Derives a fast greedy layer-wise pretraining algorithm that learns one layer at a time via contrastive divergence.
Introduces the up-down algorithm for fine-tuning, a contrastive variant of wake-sleep that avoids mode averaging.
Achieves 1.25% test error on MNIST, outperforming discriminative methods like SVM and backpropagation.
Demonstrates interpretability by generating images from the top-level associative memory's states.
Shows that generative models can learn more parameters without overfitting compared to discriminative models.
limits: Model assumes binary stochastic units, limiting applicability to non-binary or continuous data.
Generative model treats pixel intensities as probabilities, unsuitable for natural images with non-probabilistic values.
Top-down feedback during perception is confined to the associative memory, not full hierarchical inference.
No systematic mechanism for handling perceptual invariances like translation or rotation.
Assumes segmentation is performed beforehand and does not learn sequential attention for difficult discriminations.

papers.tEn: Long Short-Term Memory
papers.tZh: 长短期记忆
papers.sEn: LSTM learns to bridge long time lags by enforcing constant error flow through constant error carousels, solving complex tasks that previous recurrent networks could not.
contrib: Introduces LSTM architecture with constant error carousels to overcome vanishing gradient problem.
Multiplicative gate units learn to control information flow, protecting memory from irrelevant inputs and outputs.
LSTM achieves constant error flow over 1000 time steps, solving long-time-lag tasks unattainable by prior methods.
Computational complexity O(1) per time step and weight, enabling efficient training.
Outperforms BPTT, RTRL, Elman nets, and other recurrent algorithms on multiple benchmarks.
Learns to store precise real values over long intervals with noisy distributed representations.
limits: Internal state drift may occur when inputs are predominantly positive or negative, causing gradient vanishing.
Early learning may abuse memory cells as bias units, slowing release for further learning.
On trivial short-lag tasks, simple random weight guessing can outperform LSTM.
Gate design adds parameters and complexity compared to simpler recurrent architectures.
Performance depends on appropriate initialization of gate biases; poor tuning may hinder learning.

papers.tEn: Learning Internal Representations by Error Propagation
papers.tZh: 通过误差传播学习内部表示
papers.sEn: Error propagation enables learning in multi-layer networks with hidden units.
contrib: Derives the generalized delta rule for training multilayer feedforward networks with semilinear units.
Shows that error signals can be recursively computed by backpropagation through hidden layers.
Demonstrates that the procedure solves nonlinearly separable problems like XOR, parity, and symmetry.
Empirically finds that local minima are rare and can be avoided by adding hidden units or increasing learning rate.
Introduces momentum term and random initial weights to accelerate learning and break symmetry.
limits: The method requires differentiable activation functions, excluding linear threshold units.
Local minima exist, e.g., in binary addition with minimal hidden units, requiring extra units.
Symmetry problem: equal initial weights prevent learning; random weights are necessary.
Learning speed depends on number of hidden units and learning rate; very slow for some tasks.
Hidden units often develop inhibitory connections due to initial error minimization bias.

papers.tEn: A Learning Algorithm for Boltzmann Machines
papers.tZh: 玻尔兹曼机的学习算法
papers.sEn: A parallel search method based on statistical mechanics leads to a learning rule for modifying connection strengths in Boltzmann machines.
contrib: Proposed the Boltzmann Machine, a parallel stochastic search method for constraint satisfaction based on statistical mechanics.
Derived a local learning rule that adjusts connection strengths to model the probability distribution of environmental examples.
Demonstrated that hidden units can automatically form internal representations, such as binary codes in encoder problems.
Showed that annealing and noise injection enable escape from local minima, improving global optimization.
Connected statistical mechanics to parallel computation, influencing later interpretability and learning models.
limits: Learning is extremely slow due to the need for many simulated annealings and equilibrium sampling.
Careful tuning of parameters (e.g., temperature schedule, noise level) is required for stable learning.
Assumes binary units and symmetric weights, limiting applicability to real-valued or asymmetric systems.
Easily trapped in local minima when hidden units create complex error landscapes.
Biologically implausible due to assumptions of symmetric connections and no transmission delays.

papers.tEn: Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities
papers.tZh: 具有涌现集体计算能力的神经网络与物理系统
papers.sEn: Neural networks and physical systems can exhibit useful computational abilities through collective behavior of many simple components.
contrib: Proposes that neural networks as physical systems exhibit emergent collective computational abilities.
Implements a content-addressable memory using asynchronous parallel processing and symmetric connections.
Demonstrates an energy function that monotonically decreases, ensuring convergence to stable states.
Shows capacity to store approximately 0.15N memories with error correction and pattern completion.
Reveals emergent properties: generalization, familiarity recognition, categorization, and time sequence retention.
Suggests robust fault tolerance and suitability for hardware implementation.
limits: Assumes symmetric connections (Tij = Tji), which is biologically unrealistic.
Memory capacity limited to about 0.15N, scaling poorly with network size.
Requires stored memories to be nearly random and uncorrelated for optimal performance.
Unable to reliably encode long sequences of temporal order beyond a few states.
Model omits many neurobiological details such as synaptic delays and stochastic spiking.

papers.tEn: The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model for Information Storage and Organization in the Brain
papers.tZh: 感知器：大脑中信息存储与组织的概率模型
papers.sEn: This paper addresses the fundamental questions of how information is stored and how stored information influences recognition in the brain, proposing the perceptron as a probabilistic model.
contrib: Proposes the perceptron as a probabilistic model for information storage and organization in the brain, based on statistical separability theory.
Establishes a quantitative learning theory from six physical parameters, enabling prediction of learning curves from neurological variables.
Demonstrates that in a differentiated environment, the perceptron achieves above-chance generalization asymptote approaching unity with more association cells.
Analyzes three value dynamics systems (alpha, beta, gamma) and bivalent reinforcement for trial-and-error learning.
Shows distributed memory, spontaneous concept formation, and selective recall capabilities in improved perceptrons.
limits: Fails at relationship abstraction and higher-order cognition, such as recognizing spatial or temporal relations between stimuli.
Requires many parameters (x, y, theta, omega, NA, NR) and independent measurements for verifiability, limiting practical application.
In an ideal random environment, generalization probability remains at chance level, showing no basis for generalization.
Performance degrades with increasing number of mutually exclusive responses unless binary coding is used.
Biological plausibility is limited; the model assumes random connections and specific value dynamics not fully verified in real neurons.

papers.tEn: A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity
papers.tZh: 神经活动中内在思想的逻辑演算
papers.sEn: Neural events and their relations can be treated with propositional logic due to the all-or-none character of nervous activity.
contrib: Formalized neural activity using propositional logic, showing that all-or-none neuron firing can represent logical propositions.
Proved that any logical expression satisfying certain conditions can be realized by a neural net with appropriate structure.
Extended the analysis to nets with circles, using recursion and temporal logic to describe reverberatory activity.
Demonstrated equivalence of different neurophysiological assumptions (e.g., absolute vs. relative inhibition) for net behavior.
Linked the theory to computation, showing nets with circles compute Turing-machine computable numbers.
Applied the calculus to psychology and neurophysiology, arguing that mental events are propositional and intentional.
limits: Assumes all-or-none law and fixed thresholds, ignoring graded potentials, continuous changes, and adaptation.
Model oversimplifies synaptic plasticity, learning, and long-term changes, treating them as equivalent to static nets.
Treatment of cyclic nets is incomplete; necessary and sufficient conditions for realizability remain complex and abstract.
Real neurons exhibit temporal summation, variable conduction delays, and other dynamics not captured by the calculus.
The theory's reduction of psychology to propositional logic may be too narrow for explaining consciousness and qualia.
